doi:10.1001/jama.2026.12556.abstract: Importance Blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer disease, particularly plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217), accurately reflect early Alzheimer disease brain pathology in cognitively unimpaired individuals, but estimates of absolute risk of progression to cognitive impairment across multiple cohorts are needed. Objective To estimate absolute risk of progression to cognitive impairment and rates of cognitive decline based on plasma p-tau217 across cognitively unimpaired older adults. Design, Setting, and Participants Longitudinal cohort study using harmonized data from 2684 cognitively unimpaired older adults (defined within cohort) across 6 observational and clinical trial cohorts based in North America, Japan, and Australia. The earliest enrollment was in 2004, with most recent follow-up in 2025. Exposure Baseline plasma p-tau217. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was time to progression to cognitive impairment (mild cognitive impairment, dementia, or 2 consecutive global Clinical Dementia Rating scores ≥0.5). The secondary outcome was longitudinal change on the latent Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC; higher values indicate better performance). Results Among the 2684 participants (median [IQR] age, 69.6 [66.2-74.2] years; 1697 [63%] female), there were 478 events of progression to cognitive impairment over a median follow-up of 5.4 years (maximum follow-up of 13.5 years). Each 1-SD increase in baseline p-tau217 level was associated with an increased risk of progression to cognitive impairment (hazard ratio, 1.38 [95% CI, 1.30-1.46]), and the association remained significant after adjustment, including β-amyloid positron emission tomography scan Centiloids (hazard ratio, 1.32 [95% CI, 1.24-1.41]). Participants with high (1.1-2.4 SD) and very high (&gt;2.5 SD) baseline p-tau217 had 24% (95% CI, 20%-28%) and 38% (95% CI, 33%-43%) absolute risk of progression over 5 years, respectively, and risk was markedly higher over 10 years, although longer-term estimates were constrained by limited data. Elevated p-tau217 was also associated with faster cognitive decline based on change in latent PACC score. Among the overall sample, baseline latent PACC scores ranged from −0.8 to 2.7. The 5-year annualized decline for the very high p-tau217 group was −0.07 latent PACC units/y (95% CI, −0.10 to −0.05), relative to 0.03 units/y (95% CI, 0.02-0.04) in the low p-tau217 group. Conclusions and Relevance In a pooled sample of multiple selected cohorts of cognitively unimpaired older adults, higher plasma p-tau217 levels were consistently associated with increased risk of clinical progression and accelerated cognitive decline. By providing time-specific absolute risk estimates, these findings support the potential of p-tau217 for prognostic model development, with direct implications for future trial design. Further validation in unselected populations is needed to inform individual prognosis and clinical decision-making in cognitively unimpaired individuals.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.14762.abstract: Importance Antiretroviral therapy (ART), particularly regimens containing tenofovir alafenamide with dolutegravir or bictegravir, is associated with substantial weight gain, potentially exacerbating cardiometabolic risk in people with HIV. Objective To determine whether a regimen with doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate results in less weight gain than a regimen with dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide while maintaining noninferior viral suppression. Design, Setting, and Participants Open-label, noninferiority randomized clinical trial including ART-naive adults (≥18 years of age) with an HIV RNA level greater than 500 copies/mL and no detectable baseline, high-level doravirine resistance. The study was conducted at 2 South African sites and individuals were recruited between October 2023 and March 2025. The final participant visit occurred in February 2026. Interventions A once-daily regimen with 100 mg of doravirine, 300 mg of lamivudine, and 300 mg of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (n = 299) or 50 mg of dolutegravir, 200 mg of emtricitabine, and 25 mg of tenofovir alafenamide (n = 301). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was viral suppression (HIV RNA level &lt;50 copies/mL) at week 48 (prespecified noninferiority margin of −10 percentage points). The key secondary outcomes included changes in body weight, treatment-associated effects on body composition, and safety and adverse events. Results Among 600 participants, 597 (99.5%) were Black African, 413 (68.8%) were assigned female at birth, and the median age was 34 years (IQR, 28-41). At week 48, 266 participants (89.0%) in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group achieved viral suppression (HIV RNA level &lt;50 copies/mL) vs 273 participants (90.7%) in the dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide group (between-group difference, −1.7 percentage points [95% CI, −6.6 to 3.1], meeting the prespecified noninferiority margin of −10 percentage points). The median weight gain was 3.0 kg in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group vs 5.0 kg in the dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide group (between-group difference, −2.0 kg [95% CI, −3.0 to −1.0 kg]; P &lt; .001). Among participants in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group, the median change in hip bone mineral density (BMD) was −2.1% (IQR, −4.1% to −0.5%) and was −3.2% (IQR, −5.4% to −0.8%) for spine BMD vs −0.5% (IQR, −1.9% to 1.2%) for hip BMD and −1.3% (IQR, −3.2% to 0.8%) for spine BMD with dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide ( P &lt; .001 for each between-group comparison). Resistance to doravirine emerged among 7 of 9 participants experiencing virologic failure in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group. Of these 7 participants, 5 of 6 achieved viral suppression after switching to dolutegravir-based therapy and 1 was lost to follow-up. Serious adverse events and deaths (n = 2) were infrequent and not considered treatment-related. Conclusions and Relevance Among predominantly Black African adults initiating ART, a regimen with doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate was noninferior to a regimen with dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide for 48-week viral suppression and was associated with less weight gain. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05924438

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.15278.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03164473.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.17403.abstract: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.17622.abstract: Heart failure affects more than 6 million US adults; approximately 4% to 5% progress to advanced disease despite optimal therapy. Heart transplant is a class I guideline-recommended therapy for select individuals with advanced heart failure. Early referral for heart transplant is guided by the "I NEED HELP" mnemonic, a tool that identifies patients with advanced heart failure based on criteria such as use of inotropes, persistent symptoms (New York Heart Association class III or IV), end-organ dysfunction, left ventricular ejection fraction, defibrillator shocks, hospitalizations for heart failure, persistent edema or escalating use of diuretics, and low blood pressure. Each criterion is associated with higher risk of death or first heart failure hospitalization over a median follow-up of 260 days (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.19 [95% CI, 1.11-1.27] for each additional criterion). Typical absolute contraindications to heart transplant include active systemic infection, malignancy with limited life expectancy, severe and irreversible end-organ dysfunction (eg, cirrhosis, severe pulmonary hypertension), active substance use, major untreated psychiatric illness, inadequate social support, and severe frailty. Approximately 4600 heart transplants are performed annually in the US. The mortality rate was 8.5 deaths/100 patient-years for adults on the transplant waiting list in 2023. Leading causes of early death after transplant include primary graft dysfunction (39.5%), multiorgan failure (18.5%), and infection (13.9%). Among adults, contemporary survival rates after heart transplant are 91.5% at 1 year and 80.3% at 5 years. Lifelong maintenance immunosuppression typically combines a calcineurin inhibitor, antiproliferative agents (typically mycophenolate mofetil or azathioprine) and corticosteroids, with selective use of induction therapy (intensive immunosuppression immediately after transplant). Acute rejection requiring treatment occurs in 20% to 25% of recipients within a year, and may be treated with high-dose corticosteroids, antithymocyte globulin, and B-cell-targeted therapies (such as rituximab or bortezomib). Rejection surveillance with endomyocardial biopsies of the right ventricular septum is performed 5 to 10 times within the first year after transplant. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (chronic rejection that causes diffuse coronary narrowing) affects 29% of heart transplant recipients within 5 years and 46.8% by 10 years and is the leading cause of late mortality. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy is treated with statins, mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitors (such as sirolimus or everolimus), and retransplant for severe cases. Infections (62.5% are bacterial, 30.0% are viral, 6.7% are fungal, and 0.8% are parasitic) and malignancy (10.7% within 5 years after heart transplant) are other leading causes of late mortality. Heart transplant is the definitive therapy for carefully selected patients with advanced heart failure despite receiving optimal, guideline-directed therapy. After heart transplant, lifelong multidisciplinary care is necessary to manage immunosuppression, prevent and treat rejection and cardiac allograft vasculopathy, and monitor for infection and malignancy.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18146.abstract: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups. Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18380.abstract: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation. To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression. Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025. After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support. The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing. Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, -11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs -5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, -5.3 [95% CI, -8.9 to -1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, -12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, -6.2 [95% CI, -10.2 to -2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 76%, 85%, and 73% of participants in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively; most events (99.7%) were mild or moderate. Overall, most participants were deemed ready for discharge within 2 hours post dose (85% for 8 mg and 78% for 12 mg). In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms. Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05870540.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18449.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure that disproportionately affects individuals of predominantly African ancestry, among whom familial clustering of disease is more pronounced relative to those of predominantly European ancestry. Truncating variants in TTN, which encodes the sarcomeric protein titin, are the most common established monogenic cause of DCM. A common CD36 nonsense variant enriched among individuals of African ancestry has also been shown to account for a substantial burden of DCM. To compare the contribution of a CD36 nonsense variant to DCM risk with that of truncating variants in TTN and pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other established genes for DCM. Multicohort genetic association study including participants of African and European ancestry with exome or genome sequence data and DCM case status from the following 4 US datasets: All of Us Research Program (recruitment: 2017-present; last follow-up: August 27, 2024), Million Veteran Program (recruitment: 2011-present; last follow-up: September 30, 2024), Penn Medicine Biobank (recruitment: 2013-present; last follow-up: November 14, 2022), and the DCM Precision Medicine Study (recruitment: 2016-2020; last follow-up: March 15, 2020). Carrier status for TTN truncating variants, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 11 high-confidence genes for DCM, and the nonsense variant CD36 Y325* (0, 1, or 2 copies). Risk of DCM, prevalence of variant carriers among DCM cases, and population attributable fraction of DCM. Among 82 623 individuals of predominantly African ancestry across 4 cohorts, the mean age was 53.4 years (SD, 13.9 years), 47 124 were male, and 1316 had DCM. Individuals who were homozygous for the CD36 Y325* risk allele had a higher risk of DCM (odds ratio [OR], 4.8; 95% CI, 3.1-7.3) as did those who were heterozygous (OR, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.2-1.7). TTN truncating variants also conferred an elevated risk of DCM in participants of African ancestry (OR, 8.5; 95% CI, 5.5-13.0). Among 1316 individuals of African ancestry classified as DCM cases, 33 (2.5%) were homozygous for CD36, 56 (4.3%) had TTN truncating variants, and 16 (1.2%) had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other high-confidence genes for DCM. In population-level analyses incorporating both heterozygous and homozygous CD36 Y325* carriers, the population attributable fraction for CD36 (9.0% [6.2% for heterozygous carriers and 2.8% for homozygous carriers]) surpassed the population attributable fraction for TTN truncating variants (3.7%). In 4 US cohorts, an ancestry-specific CD36 variant contributed more to DCM burden among individuals of African ancestry than established genes for DCM, including TTN truncating variants that are typically considered the most common genetic cause. These findings reshape the known genetic architecture of DCM in individuals of African ancestry and highlight the importance of representation in genomic research.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18471.abstract: Rigorous evidence for inhaled sedation using isoflurane in mechanically ventilated patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is limited. To evaluate whether an inhaled sedation strategy lowers hospital mortality compared with usual care intravenous sedation strategy in mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF. Pragmatic, effectiveness, open-label, superiority, randomized clinical trial in 14 intensive care units (ICUs) in Canada. Adults (≥18 years) receiving sedation for less than 72 hours and receiving mechanical ventilation for AHRF from non-COVID respiratory failure (ratio of partial pressure of arterial oxygen [Pao2] to fraction of inspired oxygen [Fio2] <300 mm Hg) or COVID-19 were enrolled between September 2020 and March 2025 with follow-up through June 2025. Patients were randomized to an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed or to a usual intravenous sedation care strategy. Sedatives were titrated to achieve the desired target sedation score guided by clinical teams and continued until extubation or death. Primary outcome was all-cause hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU- and ventilator-free days at day 30; hospital-free days at day 60; use of refractory hypoxemia adjunctive therapies; delirium- and coma-free days at day 14; and quality-of-life and disability scores at 3 months. Of 786 patients randomized, 780 were included in the primary analysis (mean age, 61.1 years; 34.0% female; 73.7% non-COVID AHRF, mean Pao2:Fio2 ratio, 152.6 mm Hg); 385 in the inhaled sedation and 395 in the intravenous sedation groups. In the inhaled sedation group, 49.9% to 55.4% of patients received concomitant intravenous sedation on any day during the first 14 days after randomization. At hospital discharge, 161 of 379 patients (42.5%) in the inhaled sedation group had died, compared with 171 of 390 patients (43.8%) in the intravenous sedation group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.84 to 1.14]; P = .85). There was no effect modification in prespecified subgroup analyses for age, sex, and COVID-19 status. ICU-, ventilator-, and hospital-free days were similar between groups. The inhaled sedation group received more adjunctive therapies for hypoxemia (239 [63.9%] vs 214 [55.0%]; between-group difference, 8.89% [95% CI, 1.95% to 15.83%]) and had fewer delirium- and coma-free days (between-group difference, -0.95 [95% CI, -1.69 to -0.22]). There was no difference in quality-of-life and disability scores between groups. In mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF, an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed did not reduce hospital mortality compared with an intravenous sedation strategy. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04415060.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18574.abstract: It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index. To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery. This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026. Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring). The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18806.abstract: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18862.abstract: Importance Childhood cancer risk after assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains uncertain, particularly by procedure and cancer type. Objective To examine associations between ART and childhood cancer overall and by ART modality and cancer type. Design, Setting, and Population Nationwide Danish cohort of 1 086 136 live-born children from 1996 to 2012, of whom 37 228 (3.4%) were conceived using ART, with follow-up through 2023. Exposures Maternal ART, classified as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, or frozen embryo transfer. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident childhood cancer. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Poisson models estimated incidence rates. Non-ART births were the primary reference; secondary analyses used children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. Results During a median follow-up of 20 years, 3736 cancers occurred. Compared with non-ART births (incidence rate, 18.3 per 100 000 person-years), children conceived using ART had higher cancer incidence (incidence rate, 23.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 1.07-1.48]). Rates were higher after frozen embryo transfer (incidence rate, 41.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.45-3.29]) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (incidence rate, 27.9 per 100 000; HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.16-1.89]) but not IVF (incidence rate, 18.5 per 100 000; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.79-1.28]). Frozen embryo transfer was associated with leukemia (incidence rate, 11.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.36 [95% CI, 1.06-5.28]), lymphomas (HR, 3.03 [95% CI, 1.13-8.12]), and soft tissue sarcomas (HR, 7.63 [95% CI, 2.82-20.62]); intracytoplasmic sperm injection was associated with lymphomas (incidence rate, 4.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.07-3.54]), soft tissue sarcomas (incidence rate, 3.3 per 100 000; HR, 3.28 [95% CI, 1.54-7.00]), and central nervous system neoplasms (incidence rate, 8.2 per 100 000; HR, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.04-2.57]); no associations were observed for IVF. Findings were similar in secondary analyses using children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. Conclusions and Relevance ART, particularly frozen embryo transfer and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, was associated with increased childhood cancer risk, but absolute risks were low. The consistent results in secondary analyses of children with maternal infertility history or conceived via IVF suggest that procedure-related, rather than infertility-related, factors warrant further investigation.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.19921.abstract: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear. To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026. Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin). A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001). In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.21291.abstract: Fluid therapy is ubiquitous in the intensive care unit (ICU) but carries risks, especially in mechanically ventilated patients. Contemporary global practice across dose, indication, and type is unknown. To characterize ICU fluid practices in mechanically ventilated adults. International prospective observational cohort study between April 2024 and July 2025, across 206 ICUs in 41 countries on 6 continents. Consecutive adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation within 3 days of ICU admission and ventilated 24 hours or more. Exclusion criteria were age younger than 16 years and transfer under mechanical ventilation from another ICU. Fluid volume, indication, and type after intubation. Key measures included (1) total infused volume and daily fluid balance over 7 days after intubation; (2) the indication for fluid therapy over the first 3 days after intubation; (3) the proportion of total administered fluid volume attributable to each fluid type over the first 3 days after intubation. Among 2454 patients analyzed (median age, 63 years [IQR, 49-73 years]; 63.6% [1560] male), median daily fluid input peaked on day 1 at 3.0 L (IQR, 2.2-4.0 L) and declined to 2.6 L (IQR, 1.8-3.5 L) through day 6. Daily fluid balance (median, 0.9 L; IQR, 0.1-1.9 L on day 1) decreased to less than 0.3 L (IQR, -0.5 to 1.2 L) by day 3 and remained near-neutral through day 6. Maintenance and replacement fluids (to meet daily requirements and to correct ongoing losses; 31.9%) and creep fluids (to deliver medications and maintain catheter patency; 30.9%) were the primary indications, whereas resuscitation (to restore circulating blood volume; 16.0%) accounted for a smaller proportion. Isotonic balanced crystalloids (48.9%) and isotonic saline (0.9% sodium chloride) (27.0%) were common; colloids were rare (1.3%). Substantial between-site variation persisted after adjustment for case-mix. In this prospective international cohort study, fluid therapy varied widely among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, with maintenance and creep fluids-rather than resuscitation fluids-accounting for most total volume.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.21322.abstract: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025. Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone. The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention. Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone. Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.21333.abstract: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain. To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock. Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026. Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter. The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics. There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]). In this large, pragmatic clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of 2 hospital-level strategies for second-line vasopressor management in septic shock, a strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower dose of other vasopressors did not reduce 28-day mortality compared with a strategy recommending vasopressin initiation at a higher dose of other vasopressors. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06217562.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.21372.abstract: Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) has demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in a global phase 1 trial involving heavily pretreated patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2)-low metastatic breast cancer. To compare trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer. This open-label, randomized, multicenter phase 3 trial was conducted at 73 hospitals across China. Eligible patients were females aged 18 to 75 years with centrally confirmed ERBB2-low (immunohistochemistry [IHC] 1+ or IHC 2+/in-situ hybridization [ISH]-negative) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received 1 or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor-positive disease. Enrollment began on June 30, 2023, and ended on August 20, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the final analysis for progression-free survival in the current study was March 20, 2026. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab rezetecan (6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks; n = 277) or physician's choice of chemotherapy (n = 274). The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and the overall population. Between June 30, 2023, and August 20, 2025, a total of 551 patients were randomized, with a mean (SD) age of 54.9 (9.9) years. At the data cutoff (March 20, 2026), trastuzumab rezetecan significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with chemotherapy in the chemotherapy-naive patients (median, 16.6 [95% CI, 14.0-19.4] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-7.0] months; hazard ratio, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.19-0.33]; P < .001) and the overall population (median, 16.4 [95% CI, 14.0-16.8] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-6.9] months; hazard ratio, 0.27 [95% CI, 0.21-0.34]; P < .001). The benefit was consistent in hormone receptor-negative disease (median progression-free survival: 16.5 vs 6.8 months; hazard ratio, 0.34, [95% CI, 0.22-0.54]) and hormone receptor-positive disease (median progression-free survival: 16.4 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.18-0.33]). Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events occurred in 84.1% of patients (232/276) with trastuzumab rezetecan and 67.9% (184/271) with chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (180 [65.2%] vs 147 [54.2%]). Trastuzumab rezetecan provided significant progression-free survival benefit over physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer, with benefit observed across all key subgroups. It exhibited the potential as a new treatment option with a distinct safety profile in this setting. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05814354.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.21737.abstract: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

doi:10.1001/jama.2026.21868.abstract: Despite growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, empirical evidence on how clinicians use these tools is limited. To characterize clinician use of an AI-enabled clinical information platform, the distribution of use across the clinical workforce, and the purpose of submitted queries. This cross-sectional study analyzed clinicians with National Provider Identifier-verified accounts of a commonly used AI-enabled clinical information platform, OpenEvidence, from January 1, 2024, through June 30, 2026. A large language model was used to classify the clinical purpose and topic areas of a stratified random sample of 38.8 million queries. The number of active users and clinical queries, the share of queries relative to representation in the national workforce, and the clinical purpose and topic of queries were examined. Overall, 952 008 clinicians (58.5% female), including 556 200 physicians, submitted 271 million queries during the 2.5-year study period. Monthly active users increased from 355 in January 2024 to 703 265 in June 2026, and average monthly queries per active user rose from 18.0 to 39.5. Nurse practitioners (44.5) and physician assistants (44.5) submitted more queries per active user-month than physicians (37.1). A higher share of queries relative to the national workforce was submitted by physicians within a decade of graduation (use ratio, 2.54) and residents and fellows (1.84). Use was also higher than average among physicians specializing in oncology and hematology (use ratio, 2.00), internal medicine (1.88), and family medicine (1.80), but lower in procedural and diagnostic specialties (ophthalmology, 0.23; radiology, 0.24; orthopedics, 0.24). Most queries addressed clinical decision-making (51.9%), particularly treatment and management (33.1%), whereas diagnosis accounted for 13.9% of queries. Queries addressing topics outside physicians' own specialties ranged from 35% among oncologists and hematologists to 88% among emergency department physicians. Over 2.5 years, more than 950 000 US clinicians submitted greater than 270 million queries to an AI-enabled clinical information platform. Use varied across clinician types, specialties, and career stages and was frequently for treatment decisions rather than diagnostic tasks.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.2790.abstract: Importance Metabolic syndrome (MetS) includes obesity, insulin resistance, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. While androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is associated with an increased risk of dyslipidemia, adiposity, and MetS, evidence is limited on the occurrence and timing of metabolic dysfunction among men receiving concurrent androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) therapy and whether patterns vary by age. Objective To characterize the occurrence and rate of MetS during the first year following initiation of ADT-ARPI, examine associations with age and ARPI type, and evaluate component metabolic outcomes (secondary end points). Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study of adult patients from January 2014 to September 2025 with up to 12 months of follow-up per person used data from a national, deidentified health record dataset (Epic Cosmos) and included patients with prostate cancer who initiated treatment with ADT-ARPI (abiraterone acetate, enzalutamide, apalutamide, and darolutamide) without evidence of MetS or its components before treatment. Data were analyzed between October 2025 and January 2026 (further analyses were done with revisions through May 2026). Exposure Concurrent ADT and ARPI use, with index date defined as the first date of overlap between therapies. Main Outcomes and Measures New-onset MetS during the 12 months following the index date. Secondary outcomes included individual metabolic abnormalities. Results The cohort included 16 924 men with prostate cancer (mean [SD] age, 73.1 [9.1] y; 509 [3.0%] Asian individuals, 912 [5.4%] Hispanic individuals, 3562 [21.0%] non-Hispanic Black individuals, and 11 083 [65.5%] non-Hispanic White individuals). Medical ADT use predominated, and enzalutamide was the most frequently used ARPI. During the first year following initiation of concurrent ADT and ARPI therapy, the cumulative incidence of metabolic syndrome increased steadily, reaching nearly 40%, and varied by age group. Hypertension was the most frequently documented component outcome. Metabolic associations varied by age, with the highest incidence of metabolic syndrome among patients aged 70 to 79 years (51.7 events per 1000 person-months; 95% CI, 50.7-53.9). Heterogeneity in metabolic outcomes by ARPI type was observed in exploratory analyses. Conclusions and Relevance This study found that while ARPIs are standard of care for advanced prostate cancer, metabolic abnormalities were frequently documented shortly after initiation of concurrent ADT and ARPI therapy. This suggests that monitoring should extend beyond cancer-specific outcomes to include early detection of metabolic dysfunction, ideally through multidisciplinary care. The early burden of metabolic abnormalities highlights the need to evaluate scalable interventions addressing cardiometabolic risk in men with prostate cancer.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.2833.abstract: Importance Molecular residual disease (MRD) detection has potential to transform the selection of adjuvant therapy. Most evidence is from tumor-informed assays. Tissue-free assays not requiring sequencing of the primary tumor may simplify workflows if they offer accuracy similar to that of tumor-informed assays. Objective To evaluate tissue-free circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis in patients with triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) and compare the tissue-free assay with tumor-informed assay results. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a prognostic and exploratory analysis of patients with TNBC at moderate to high risk of recurrence who were participating in the ctDNA surveillance period of c-TRAK TN, a multicenter phase 2 clinical study. Plasma samples were collected from participants every 3 months for up to 2 years after the completion of adjuvant therapy and analyzed prospectively with digital polymerase chain reaction (dPCR). Data for the analysis were from a database lock on September 28, 2021, with subsequent follow-up through January 18, 2023. Data were analyzed from July 2025 to May 2026. Intervention or Exposure Tissue-free assay leverages cancer differential methylation patterns to detect ctDNA. Main Outcome and Measures Recurrence-free survival by tissue-free ctDNA detection status. Comparison between tissue-free ctDNA detection and both dPCR and whole-exome sequencing−powered multivariant tumor-informed assays. Results The analysis included 1026 plasma samples from 159 patients (mean [SD; range] age, 51.4 [11.4; 25.0-78.0] years; 159 females [100%]). The tissue-free assay detected ctDNA in 54 patients (34.0%), with detection strongly associated with risk of recurrence (HR, 27.2; 95% CI, 13.7-54.2; P &lt; .001). Among patients with ctDNA detected by both the tissue-free assay and dPCR (42 patients [26%]), tissue-free detection occurred at an earlier time point in 14 patients (33.3%); dPCR detection occurred before tissue-free detection in no patients. Median lead time to recurrence was 7.9 (95% CI, 6.1-10.5) months for tissue-free vs 5.8 (95% CI, 3.3-10.0) months for dPCR (HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.34-0.95; P = .03). Concordance between tissue-free and multivariant tumor-informed assays was good. Among patients detected by both assays (41 of 133), 12 of 41 (29.3%) had ctDNA detected earlier by multivariant tumor-informed assay with 1 (2.4%) earlier by the tissue-free assay. Median lead times to recurrence were 7.6 (95% CI, 4.6-10.5) months with tissue-free and 7.1 (95% CI, 5.7-10.0) months with multivariant tumor-informed assay (HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 0.87-2.44; P = .15). Conclusion and Relevance In this prognostic study, tissue-free ctDNA detection during surveillance was strongly prognostic for recurrence in patients with TNBC. Comparable lead times between the tissue-free and multivariant tumor-informed assays support tissue-free MRD detection in a clinical trial setting, permitting ctDNA testing when tissue is not available.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.3918.abstract: Consolidation immunotherapy improves outcomes after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Disease progression remains common, and more effective consolidation strategies are needed. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of benmelstobart with or without anlotinib as consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC. This multicenter double-blind phase 3 randomized clinical trial took place at 42 centers in China from 2020 to 2023 among patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. In stage 1, patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 2 active regimens or placebo; in stage 2, additional patients were randomized 1:1 between the active regimens to power their direct comparison. Data cutoffs were November 30, 2023, for stage 1 and July 8, 2024, for the pooled analysis. Data analysis was performed from January 17 to March 23, 2025. Patients were randomized to receive benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart plus anlotinib placebo, or their matching placebos. Primary end point was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). Of 553 participants (median [IQR] age, 62 [56-67] years; 495 male individuals [89.5%]), 390 were randomized in stage 1 and 163 in stage 2. In stage 1, median PFS was 15.1 months (95% CI, 9.4-21.7) with benmelstobart plus anlotinib, 9.7 months (95% CI, 6.0-34.4) with benmelstobart alone, and 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.2-6.8) with placebo. The hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.49 (95% CI, 0.36-0.66; P < .001) for benmelstobart plus anlotinib vs placebo and 0.53 (95% CI, 0.39-0.72; P < .001) for benmelstobart vs placebo. In the pooled stage 1 and 2 analysis, median PFS was 17.4 (95% CI, 12.5-24.8) months with benmelstobart plus anlotinib and 11.2 (95% CI, 7.0-20.7) months with benmelstobart alone (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.63-1.08; P = .12). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 48.8%, 29.4%, and 19.7% in the benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart alone, and placebo groups, respectively; grade 5 events occurred in 7.2%, 1.4%, and 1.5%, respectively. This randomized clinical trial found that benmelstobart with or without anlotinib significantly improved PFS compared with placebo. Adding anlotinib did not significantly improve PFS compared with benmelstobart alone and increased severe and fatal treatment-related adverse events. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04325763.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4162.abstract: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in localized deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma was evaluated in the NEONIPIGA study. The primary end point of pathological complete response (pCR) was previously reported. To report long-term follow-up results and secondary end points, including event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS), of the NEONIPIGA study. The NEONIPIGA study is a French, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial that included patients with histologically proven cT2-T4NXM0 deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high GEJ adenocarcinoma who were eligible for surgery. Patients were enrolled between October 23, 2019, and June 4, 2021, and the database was locked on November 13, 2025. Neoadjuvant nivolumab, 240 mg, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles plus ipilimumab, 1 mg/kg, every 6 weeks for 2 cycles, followed by surgery 5 weeks after the last nivolumab dose, and adjuvant nivolumab, 480 mg, every 4 weeks for 9 cycles. EFS and OS. A total of 32 patients (median [range] age, 65 [40-80] years; 8 [28%] female and 21 [72%] were male) were included: 16 (50%) with gastric cancer and 16 (50%) with GEJ cancer. Three patients did not undergo surgery (1 with metastatic disease and 2 who refused). Twenty-seven patients (84%) completed neoadjuvant therapy and 14 (44%) received all treatment as planned. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 6 (19%) and 4 patients (17%), respectively. Median follow-up was 48.3 months (95% CI, 44.8-52.0 months). Among the 32 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 4-year OS was 84.1% (95% CI, 65.8%-93.0%). In the 31 patients eligible for surgery, 4-year EFS was 83.5% (95% CI, 64.8%-92.8%). One patient relapsed with cerebral metastases. Six deaths occurred: 2 related to gastric cancer or treatment (1 patient had postoperative complications and 1 cerebral metastases) and 4 unrelated. All patients who did not undergo surgery achieved a clinical complete response after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. One patient subsequently died of causes unrelated to their cancer. Overall, 17 of 29 patients (59%) achieved pCR on surgical specimen. Safety was previously reported, and no additional late toxic effects were observed. In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, the immunotherapy regimen evaluated was associated with sustained long-term survival, but no clear evidence of improved survival over outcomes reported in other studies evaluating surgery alone in this patient population was observed. The high pCR rates and durable responses observed may provide useful information for designing future clinical studies, including randomized trials investigating organ-preserving strategies. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04006262.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4172.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus is associated with substantial perioperative risk and frequent recurrence despite nephrectomy and thrombectomy. No established neoadjuvant local therapy exists for this high-risk population. To evaluate the feasibility, safety, clinical outcomes, and exploratory biomarker effects of neoadjuvant stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) targeting IVC tumor thrombus before nephrectomy and thrombectomy. This single-center prospective phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with newly diagnosed RCC and Mayo level II to IV IVC tumor thrombus eligible for neoadjuvant SABR and definitive surgery from July 2015 to January 2024. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026. Neoadjuvant SABR to the radiographically defined IVC tumor thrombus, delivered as 40 Gy in 5 fractions or 36 Gy in 3 fractions, followed by radical nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy. The primary end point was 1-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared with a prespecified historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7%. Secondary outcomes included 90-day perioperative morbidity and mortality, adverse events, pulmonary embolism, overall survival, and cancer-specific survival. Exploratory analyses included Ki-67 immunohistochemistry and tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA. Of 23 patients who received neoadjuvant SABR, 22 completed surgery, and 21 were included in the primary RFS analysis. Of 21 included patients, 12 (57%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 62.5 (54.0-73.2) years. A total of 19 patients had clear-cell RCC; all tumors were grade 3 or 4, and 3 patients had metastatic disease at enrollment. At a median (range) follow-up of 108.6 (2.0-127.2) months, 1-year RFS was 71.4% (80% CI, 56.6-82.0; 95% CI, 47.2-86.0), meeting the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion based on comparison with the historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7% (P = .09). One-year overall survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3) and cancer-specific survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3). No 90-day perioperative mortality occurred; 4 grade 4 treatment-attributed events occurred, but no grade 4/5 radiation-attributed toxic effects occurred. Ki-67 expression was reduced in patients with irradiated tumor thrombus compared with nonirradiated controls. Tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA was detected in all patients with available plasma and declined after treatment. In this nonrandomized clinical trial, neoadjuvant SABR before nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy appeared feasible with an acceptable safety profile. RFS met the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion but remains exploratory and warrants further evaluation. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02473536.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4196.abstract: Alterations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) pathway, particularly FGFR3, are among the most common genomic events in urothelial carcinoma (UC) and represent a cornerstone of precision oncology. Although FGFR3 alterations predominate, selected FGFR2 fusions also identify patients who may benefit from targeted therapy. This review summarizes the biology, molecular diagnostics, and evolving clinical applications of FGFR alterations in UC. FGFR2/3 alterations are clinically actionable biomarkers across non-muscle-invasive, muscle-invasive, metastatic, and upper-tract UC. Comprehensive genomic profiling, tissue sequencing, plasma circulating tumor DNA, urine-based molecular assays, and molecular residual disease assessment are expanding their roles in diagnosis, treatment selection, surveillance, and disease monitoring. Recent clinical studies support combination strategies, next-generation FGFR inhibitors, and earlier use of FGFR-directed therapy, while emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-assisted pathology and integrated multi-omic biomarkers, may further improve patient selection. FGFR alterations have become integral to the molecular classification and precision management of UC. Continued advances in molecular diagnostics, liquid biopsy, biomarker-guided therapy, and next-generation FGFR inhibitors are expected to further personalize care. This review provides a practical framework for integrating FGFR biomarkers into contemporary management and highlights emerging developments likely to influence future clinical practice.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4258.abstract: The I-SPY2.2 trial tests personalized treatment strategies to improve outcomes while reducing exposure to standard chemotherapy in patients with high-risk early breast cancer (EBC). To evaluate the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd), an antibody drug conjugate targeting low ERBB2 (formerly HER2) expression, combined with rilvegostomig (R), a bispecific antibody targeting programmed cell death 1 protein and T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain as initial therapy in I-SPY2.2 (RT-DXd). This phase 2, multicenter, adaptively randomized neoadjuvant trial enrolled patients with high-risk stage II/III ERBB2-negative EBC (including those with ERBB2 low/ultralow tumors), as stratified by hormone receptor (HR) status and response-predictive subtypes. It was conducted at 30 sites in the US; efficacy data were analyzed continuously during the trial to update probabilities and other analyses before publication. Participants received up to 3 sequential treatment blocks, based on response and subtype: RT-DXd (block A), taxane-based therapy with/without immunotherapy (block B), and doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide (AC) with/without immunotherapy (block C). The primary end point was pathologic complete response (pCR). Safety assessments included adverse events (AEs), with focused monitoring for interstitial lung disease (ILD). A total of 182 individuals (mean [SD] age: RT-DXd, 48.1 [13.1] years; control, 50.9 [12.0] years) participated in the trial. Eighty-eight were randomized to the contemporary control arm, and 108 of 289 remaining participants (37%) were randomized to RT-DXd; 3 participants did not receive block A treatment, and 11 did not receive the assigned control treatment, leaving the intention-to-treat population with 105 and 77 evaluable participants. Among 105 patients treated with RT-DXd in block A, the modeled pCR rate was 54% in immune-positive tumors, which met the predefined threshold for success. Similar pCR rates were observed in HR-positive, immune-positive disease (57%) and HR-negative, immune-positive disease (52%). Across all treatment blocks, overall pCR rates were similar to control regimens; however, among immune-positive patients who experienced pCR, 21 (62%) required only block A, and 33 (97%) avoided anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Enrollment was paused twice to evaluate grade 2 or higher ILD and resumed after data safety monitoring board approval. The most common AEs were fatigue and nausea. Serious AEs included pulmonary embolism and ILD (3 of 105 [2.9%] each). ILD occurred in 13 (12.4%), including 1 grade 3 event, and was identified early with serial chest computed tomography monitoring. This randomized clinical trial found that treatment with RT-DXd demonstrated promising activity, with mostly low-grade toxic effects in immune-positive, ERBB2-negative EBC. Unlike immune-negative patients, many immune-positive patients who experienced pCR avoided standard chemotherapy, including anthracyclines, supporting further evaluation in biomarker-selected populations. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01042379.

doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4274.abstract: Primary bone cancers include multiple histologic types, with survival differing by age and location. Results from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 were analyzed to support policies and initiatives worldwide. To estimate the global burden of bone cancer from 1990 to 2023 and forecast future trends to 2050. This systematic analysis estimated bone cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in 204 countries and territories grouped by GBD super-regions and World Bank income groups from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. Individuals of all ages with bone cancers included in the GBD 2023 study were included in analyses. Data were analyzed from June 2023 to July 2025. The GBD 2023 study used standardized estimation methods to describe bone cancer incidence, mortality, and DALYs in 2023, as well as trends over the past 3 decades and forecasts through 2050. All estimates are presented with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) were calculated using GBD-specific age weights. In 2023, there were 111 000 (95% UI, 81 300-164 000) malignant bone cancer cases, 76 600 (95% UI, 60 700-96 300) deaths, and 3.02 million (95% UI, 2.29 million-3.96 million) DALYs globally. A bimodal age distribution was noted in both incidence (peaking at ages 10 to 14 years and 65 to 69 years) and mortality (peaking at ages 15 to 19 years and 65 to 69 years). The highest ASRs for incidence were in Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania (1.6 per 100 000; 95% UI, 1.1-2.4), while Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASRs for DALYs (51.0 per 100 000; 95% UI, 27.7-79.7). By World Bank income group, upper-middle-income countries had the highest ASRs for incidence, whereas low-income countries exhibited the highest ASRs for both mortality and DALYs. Globally, incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased from 1990 to 2023, while global mortality and DALY ASRs were relatively stable; high-income countries experienced a decline in mortality and DALY ASRs. Forecasts suggest a potential increase in global cases and deaths by 2050. In this systematic analysis, the burden of bone cancer varied by age, geography, and time, underscoring global disparities. These findings provide valuable insights to inform health system planning and resource allocation tailored to different settings.

doi:10.1002/1878-0261.13752.abstract: Lipid metabolism is altered in rapidly proliferating cancer cells, where fatty acids (FAs) are utilized in the synthesis of sphingolipids and glycerophospholipids to produce cell membranes and signaling molecules. Receptor for activated C‐kinase 1 (RACK1; also known as small ribosomal subunit protein) is an intracellular scaffolding protein involved in signaling pathways. Whether such lipid metabolism is regulated by RACK1 is unknown. Here, integrated spatially resolved metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics revealed that accumulation of lipids in cervical cancer (CC) samples correlated with overexpression of RACK1 , and RACK1 promoted lipid synthesis in CC cells. Chromatin immunoprecipitation verified binding of sterol regulatory element‐binding protein 1 (SREBP1) to acetyl‐CoA carboxylase (ACC) and fatty acid synthase (FASN) promoters. RACK1 enhanced de novo FA synthesis by upregulating expression of sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor 1 ( SREBP1 ) and lipogenic genes FASN and ACC1 . Co‐immunoprecipitation and western blotting revealed that RACK1 interacted with protein kinase B (AKT) to activate the AKT/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)/SREBP1 signaling pathway to promote FA synthesis. Cell proliferation and apoptosis experiments suggested that RACK1‐regulated FA synthesis is key in the progression of CC. Thus, RACK1 enhanced lipid synthesis through the AKT/mTOR/SREBP1 signaling pathway to promote the growth of CC cells. RACK1 may become a therapeutic target for CC.

doi:10.1002/1878-0261.13786.abstract: Glioblastoma cells rely on connexin 43 (Cx43)‐based gap junctions (GJs) for intercellular communication, enabling them to integrate into a widely branched malignant network. Although there are promising prospects for new targeted therapies, the lack of clinically feasible GJ inhibitors has impeded their adoption in clinical practice. In the present study, we investigated tonabersat (TO), a blood–brain‐barrier‐penetrating drug with GJ‐inhibitory properties, in regard to its potential to disassemble intercellular connectivity in glioblastoma networks. Fluorescence‐guided measurements of calcein cell‐to‐cell transfer were used to study functional intercellular connectivity. Specific DNA fragmentation rates of propidium iodide‐stained nuclei were measured as a surrogate readout for cell death using flow cytometry. CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated gene editing of Cx43 served as a validation tool of cellular effects related to Cx43 GJ inhibition. 3′ mRNA sequencing was performed for molecular downstream analysis. We found that TO reduced intercellular GJ‐mediated cytosolic traffic and yielded a significant reduction of tumor microtube (TM) length. TO‐mediated inhibition of cellular tumor networks was accompanied by a synergistic effect for temozolomide‐induced cell death. CRISPR/Cas9 Cx43 ‐knockout revealed similar results, indicating that TO‐mediated inhibitory effects rely on the inhibition of Cx43‐based GJs. Gene set enrichment analyses found that GJ‐mediated synergistic cytotoxic effects were linked to a significant upregulation of cell death signaling pathways. In conclusion, TO disrupts TM‐based network connectivity via GJ inhibition and renders glioblastoma cells more susceptible to cytotoxic therapy. Given its previous use in clinical trials for migraine therapy, TO might harbor the potential of bridging the idea of a GJ‐targeted therapeutic approach from bench to bedside.

doi:10.1002/1878-0261.70310.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single‐cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell‐to‐cell communication. However, gene expression alone offers only an indirect view of the regulatory mechanisms governing cellular states. The emergence of spatial epigenomic technologies now enables the investigation of chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and DNA methylation while preserving tissue structure. Here, we discuss the current landscape of spatial epigenomics, including spatial ATAC‐seq, spatial CUT&Tag, emerging spatial CUT&RUN approaches, spatial DNA methylation profiling, and multimodal strategies integrating epigenetic, transcriptional, and proteomic information within the same tissue context. Despite remaining technical and computational challenges, continued advances are expected to establish spatial epigenomics as a powerful tool for studying cancer pathways and their regulation within intact tissues.
