doi:10.1002/hon.70259.abstract: ABSTRACT The effect of geographical accessibility to care and patients' social environment on survival has been little studied for hematological malignancies. The objective was to investigate the influence of these factors on excess mortality for these patients in France. This study included 13 French cancer registries. Hodgkin's lymphomas, myeloid haemopathies, multiple myeloma, chronic lymphatic leukemia, diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma and follicular lymphoma diagnosed between 2013 and 2015 are included ( N = 19,041). Social environment was measured using the European Deprivation Index. The access of secondary care was measured by travel time to the nearest reference care center, and access to primary care was estimated using Spatial Accessibility multiscALar (SCALe) index and Accessibilité Potentielle Localisée (APL). The effects of these indicators on excess mortality were investigated using additive excess hazard models with multidimensional penalized splines. For myeloid haemopathies, only the social environment had a significant effect on excess mortality. For diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma, the travel time to nearest reference care center had an impact on excess mortality. Finally, for follicular lymphoma, an increase of APL index was associated with a decrease of mortality. Our study showed that the social environment and the geographical accessibility to care were prognostic factors for survival in certain hematological malignancies.

doi:10.1002/hon.70261.abstract: ABSTRACT FLT3 ‐ITD occurs in approximately 20%–25% of cases of adult AML and is associated with increased relapse risk and shorter survival. FLT3 ‐ITD status informs AML risk at diagnosis, but its dynamic changes during disease evolution are not well defined. We hypothesized that divergent FLT3 ‐ITD clonal trajectories are shaped by preexisting molecular features detectable at diagnosis. We analyzed 319 intensively treated adults who were newly diagnosed with non‐M3 de novo AML who experienced relapse and had paired FLT3 ‐ITD mutation data at diagnosis and relapse. Patients were classified into four clonal evolution patterns: maintained FLT3 ‐ITD negative ( FLT3 ‐ITD negative ), FLT3 ‐ITD loss ( FLT3 ‐ITD lost ), FLT3 ‐ITD acquisition ( FLT3 ‐ITD acquired ), and maintained FLT3 ‐ITD positive ( FLT3 ‐ITD positive ). The FLT3 ‐ITD positive group was strongly associated with concurrent NPM1 and/or DNMT3A mutations, which were enriched compared with those in other groups ( p < 0.001). ELN 2022 risk categories differed across clonal evolution patterns, with favorable‐risk disease declining progressively from the FLT3 ‐ITD negative to the FLT3 ‐ITD positive group (44.3%–6.1%) while intermediate‐risk disease rose correspondingly (21.2%–73.5%; both p < 0.001). With a median follow‐up of 96.8 months, patients in the FLT3 ‐ITD acquired or FLT3 ‐ITD positive group had significantly inferior relapse‐free and overall survival compared with those in the FLT3 ‐ITD negative group ( p = 0.009 and p = 0.018, respectively, in univariate analyses; p = 0.001 and p = 0.006, respectively, in multivariate analyses adjusted for individual genetic risk features). Transcriptomics showed enrichment of inflammatory pathways in FLT3 ‐ITD positive cases that persisted after adjustment for NPM1 / DNMT3A co‐mutations and FLT3 ‐ITD allelic ratio, together with an inferred monocyte‐rich profile. Overall, FLT3 ‐ITD evolution is associated with distinct genomic and transcriptomic features present at diagnosis. Trial Registration 202203013RSD

doi:10.1002/hon.70262.abstract: ABSTRACT Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T‐cell lymphoma (MEITL) is a rare, aggressive intestinal T‐cell lymphoma with poorly defined prognostic factors and limited therapeutic evidence. This study presents a retrospective, pooled patient‐level analysis of MEITL cases, including those previously classified as type II enteropathy‐associated T‐cell lymphoma, consistent with modern MEITL criteria. Among 299 patients, the median age was 60 years, with a male preponderance. Cases clustered predominantly in East Asia. Abdominal pain was the most frequent presentation, and perforation occurred in 31.9% of cases. The canonical CD3+, CD4−, CD5−, CD8+, CD56+ phenotype was present in 65.9% of fully annotated cases. Median OS was 12 months, and median PFS was 5 months. Elevated LDH ≥ 250 U/L ( p = 0.002), advanced Lugano stage II2/IIE/IV ( p = 0.042), and non‐ileal‐only disease distribution were associated with inferior OS, whereas isolated ileal involvement was favorable ( p = 0.004). In multivariable analysis, advanced Lugano stage, non‐ileal‐only involvement, and failure to achieve complete or partial response remained independently adverse. An exploratory prognostic score incorporating stage, anatomic distribution, and LDH showed preliminary risk group separation in a small subset of patients (C‐index 0.734). Stem cell transplantation (SCT) was associated with improved survival in fixed‐time analyses, but this association was attenuated after accounting for transplant timing; exploratory responder‐restricted and landmark analyses suggested that any potential SCT benefit may be concentrated among patients with chemotherapy‐sensitive disease. MEITL demonstrates poor survival despite multimodality therapy. Disease extent, anatomic distribution, LDH, treatment response, and response‐adapted SCT may inform risk stratification and management.

doi:10.1002/hon.70264.abstract: ABSTRACT Although clinical trials showed outcomes improvement in MCL, their applicability to real‐world practice remains limited. Using the prospective REALYSA registry (NCT03869619), we evaluated contemporary management, highlighting evolving practices and differences by age. Among 295 patients, 63% were ≥ 65 years, 48% had a high‐risk MIPI score with Ki‐67 ≥ 30% in 53% and aggressive morphology in 11%. Younger patients received high‐dose cytarabine (93%) and ASCT (78%). Older patients were treated with bendamustine‐rituximab (28%), R‐CHOP (18%), and low‐dose cytarabine (20%). Two‐year event‐free (EFS‐2y) and overall (OS‐2y) survivals were 80% and 89% in < 65y; 60% and 77% in ≥ 65y. Among 238 patients responders after induction, rituximab maintenance (RM) use was frequent but lower in older patients (88% vs. 76%). In time‐dependent Cox models adjusted for age (< 65 vs. ≥ 65) and MIPI, RM was associated with a lower hazard of EFS events (HR 0.48; 95% CI: 0.25–0.92), although residual confounding related to treatment selection may remain. In the second‐line setting ( n = 72), most patients were POD24 (89%) and 56% received ibrutinib, yet outcomes remained poor (CR 24%, ORR 35%, median EFS and OS of 6.3 and 25.6 months, respectively). These findings underscore the need for improved strategies for older and high‐risk patients. Retrospective landmark analyses suggest a potential association between RM and improved EFS but are limited by baseline differences between groups.

doi:10.1002/hon.70268.abstract: Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) redirect T-cells to tumor antigens in an MHC-independent manner. These universally available, off-the-shelf products have demonstrated unprecedented efficacy in heavily pretreated patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) hematological malignancies (HMs). The indefinite treatment duration associated with most BsAb products, coupled with neutropenia, B-cell aplasia, and hypogammaglobulinemia result in significant immune-related toxicities and infections. Hence, non-relapse mortality (NRM) which represents the cumulative burden of treatment-related toxicities, defined as death from any cause other than disease relapse or progression, is a patient-centric endpoint across cellular therapy platforms. While recent NRM estimates with CAR T-cell therapy have identified infections as major drivers of NRM, real-world NRM estimates remain limited with BsAbs. To mitigate the limitations associated with each of the methods, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of the existing literature, supplemented concurrently by a pharmacovigilance analysis using the FAERS database, to estimate NRM with BsAbs and compare real-world findings between commercially available BsAb products approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) and NHL. The primary endpoint was NRM; secondary endpoints included CRS, ICANS, infections, and death. Teclistamab demonstrated a high toxicity burden across both analytic methods, with the highest ICANS incidences, significantly greater infection rates (particularly grade > 3), and a non-negligible NRM estimate in the SRMA as well in FAERS. Glofitamab was associated with severe toxicities, including increased reporting odds for NRM and overall mortality. Mosunetuzumab showed lower pooled estimates and lower reporting odds, as seen in both analytic approaches. Low pooled incidences of infections, and ICANS were calculated in the SRMA. FAERS analyses also suggested reduced reporting odds for NRM and neurotoxicity. While trial-level data and real-world reporting largely converged for severe toxicities, divergences in other agents underscore the importance of continuous post-marketing surveillance. Given the risks associated with prolonged treatment, future protocols must prioritize infection management and adopt NRM as a standardized endpoint to guide appropriate therapeutic selection and sequencing.

doi:10.1002/hon.70272.abstract: ABSTRACT Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo‐HCT) is the only curative approach for adult T‐cell leukemia‐lymphoma (ATL). However, preventing post‐transplant relapse remains challenging. While pre‐transplant disease status is known to be associated with post‐transplant outcomes, the impact of residual disease (RD) localization at the time of allo‐HCT has not been well described. In this retrospective study of 33 patients with aggressive ATL who underwent allo‐HCT, patients were classified into two risk groups based on RD sites: a low‐risk group (no lymph node [LN] or extranodal [EN] disease, regardless of the presence of peripheral blood disease) and a high‐risk group (presence of LN and/or EN disease). The low‐risk group had significantly superior overall survival (OS) and progression‐free survival (PFS) compared to the high‐risk group, with longer median survival times (OS: 1953 vs. 245 days; PFS: 1177.5 vs. 72 days) and higher 2‐year survival rates (OS: 65.0% vs. 11.3%; PFS: 50.0% vs. 8.3%) ( p = 0.012 and p = 0.013, respectively). Furthermore, even among patients who had not achieved complete response, RD localization stratified the survival outcomes: the 2‐year OS and PFS were 75.0% and 75.0% in the low‐risk group, compared with 11.3% and 8.3% in the high‐risk group, respectively. In conclusion, RD localization at the time of allo‐HCT is a novel prognostic factor, highlighting the need for tailored pre‐transplant management for ATL.

doi:10.1002/hon.70273.abstract: Coexistent chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and BCR::ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are rare. We aimed to evaluate their clinical and therapeutic profiles. We retrospectively evaluated 36 institutional patients with coexistent CML and BCR::ABL1-negative MPN (Cohort A) and systematically reviewed 244 published cases (Cohort B). Patients were categorized by diagnostic sequence: prior CML, prior BCR::ABL1-negative MPN, or concurrent presentation. BCR::ABL1 p210 and JAK2V617 F aberrations predominantly co-occurred. Diagnoses in Cohort A were mostly concurrent (77.8%), whereas Cohort B predominantly featured prior BCR::ABL1-negative MPN (43.0%), followed by concurrent diagnoses (35.7%) and prior CML (21.3%). In Cohort B, myelofibrosis was significantly more prevalent in prior BCR::ABL1-negative MPN compared to those with prior CML or concurrent diagnoses (56.2% vs. 26.9% vs. 35.6%, respectively; p = 0.007). Persistent, unexplained cytosis despite active therapy triggered secondary mutation cross-screening in both cohorts. In Cohort A, exploratory survival analysis suggested a potential trend toward shorter overall survival in prior BCR::ABL1-negative MPN compared to concurrent diagnoses (90.5 months vs. not reached, p = 0.032). Multivariable analysis of Cohort B identified prior BCR::ABL1-negative MPN as an independent adverse predictor for major or deeper molecular responses (OR = 0.412, 95% CI: 0.197-0.861, p = 0.018), while tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)-based therapy was favorable (OR = 9.74, 95% CI: 1.108-85.636, p = 0.040). Addition of JAK2 inhibitors to TKI therapy did not significantly improve molecular responses over TKI monotherapy (67.1% vs. 54.8%, p = 0.193). To summarize, prior BCR::ABL1-negative MPN, the most frequent presentation, predicted inferior molecular responses. Clinicians should screen for coexistent mutations if cytosis persisted despite treatment. TKI remained the therapeutic cornerstone, as combined JAK2 inhibition demonstrated limited additional benefit.

doi:10.1002/hon.70277.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a metabolically heterogeneous malignancy with poor outcomes and limited durable therapeutic options. We investigated NFS1, a key enzyme involved in iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, as a potential metabolic vulnerability in AML. NFS1 was overexpressed in AML samples, and higher expression was associated with inferior overall survival in the TCGA-LAML cohort. Genetic knockdown of NFS1 markedly suppressed AML cell proliferation in vitro and reduced tumor growth in subcutaneous xenograft models. NFS1 knockdown induced disturbances in iron homeostasis accompanied by increased reactive oxygen species production and lipid peroxidation, together with reduced GPX4 expression. Together with the partial restoration of cell viability by ferrostatin-1, deferoxamine, and Z-VAD-FMK, these changes were consistent with concurrent apoptotic and ferroptosis-like cell death. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of type I interferon-related signaling pathways, while experimental validation demonstrated increased STAT1 phosphorylation at Tyr701 and increased expression of the downstream effector IFIT2. IFIT2 knockdown partially reversed the anti-proliferative effects of NFS1 knockdown, supporting an association between the growth-suppressive phenotype induced by NFS1 knockdown and STAT1/IFIT2-associated signaling. NFS1 knockdown was also accompanied by increased expression of PD-L1 and elevated concentrations of inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6 and IL-8, and reduced CD80 expression in THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells in an in vitro co-culture system. These findings indicate that NFS1 depletion is associated with immune-related transcriptional and phenotypic changes in vitro. Furthermore, NFS1 knockdown enhanced the in vitro sensitivity of AML cells to azacitidine, venetoclax, and bortezomib. Collectively, this study suggests that NFS1 may represent a metabolic vulnerability in AML that links its depletion to iron dysregulation, apoptotic and ferroptosis-like cell death, and STAT1/IFIT2-associated signaling, providing a rationale for further investigation of NFS1 as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

doi:10.1002/hon.70278.abstract: We report the first case of using teclistamab, a BCMA × CD3 bispecific antibody, in a 63-year-old male with κ-light chain deposition disease (LCDD) involving the kidneys and probably the heart. The patient initially responded to daratumumab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone but experienced hematologic relapse. Salvage therapy with teclistamab induced a rapid and sustained hematologic complete response without cytokine release syndrome or neurotoxicity. Renal and cardiac functions remained stable. This case provides critical early evidence that BCMA-directed immunotherapy may serve as an effective salvage strategy for this rare plasma cell disorder, addressing a significant unmet therapeutic need.

doi:10.1002/hon.70282.abstract: Treatment of relapsed refractory follicular lymphoma (R/R FL) still remains challenging. Several strategies have been used against R/R FL. Recently, two chemotherapy-free regimens have gained space, epcoritamab-lenalidomide-rituximab (Epco-R2) and tafasitamab-lenalidomide-rituximab (Tafa-R2). Herein, we performed an indirect trial comparison (ITC) between the two regimens using the Bucher method as they both have the common comparator arm R2. The ITC between the two study arms showed an overall response rate (ORR; p = 0.020), and complete remission rates (CR; p < 0.0001), in favor of Epco-R2. Analysis regarding time to next treatment (TTNT) interval also favored Epco-R2 (p = 0.0011). The ITC in the progression free survival (PFS) context showed the anchored comparison favored Epco-R2 over Tafa-R2 [HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.31-0.86)], p = 0.011, a finding more pronounced in patients with progression of disease within 24 months (POD24) negativity. Regarding the safety profile, Epco-R2 was associated with more hematological toxicity and infections, whereas, Tafa-R2 was associated with more COVID-19 infections probably reflecting the pandemic era enrollment timing. In conclusion, Epco-R2 is more effective in terms of treatment outcomes, but comes with greater toxicity. Tafa-R2 seems more suitable for patients with limited bone marrow reserves, patients who wish to avoid hospitalization, patients at a higher risk for cytokine release syndrome, and patients with high-risk infection vulnerability. Finally, this is not a direct comparison of two therapeutic regimens and the results should be cautiously interpreted. Treatment choice should be decided on a case-by-case scenario based on several different variables.

doi:10.1002/hon.70286.abstract: ABSTRACT Monoclonal protein is frequently tested in marginal zone lymphoma, but interpretation is often inconsistent in practice because prior studies used selective testing and rarely linked serologic findings to biology or post‐treatment dynamics. We analyzed 235 adults with newly diagnosed MZL receiving first‐line systemic therapy at a single center (2010–2025). All patients had baseline serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, and free light chain testing. Plasmacytic differentiation was reviewed by hematopathologists. M‐protein response (IMWG criteria) was assessed in patients with post‐treatment data. The primary endpoint was progression‐free survival (PFS). Baseline M‐protein was detected in 117 of 235 patients (49.8%), most commonly immunoglobulin M (IgM) (65.8%). M‐protein positivity was associated with a higher frequency of plasmacytic differentiation (39.6% vs. 16.2%; adjusted OR 3.78). M‐protein‐positive patients had shorter PFS than M‐protein‐negative patients (median, 50.9 months vs. not reached; log‐rank p = 0.044), and this association remained in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio [HR] 1.58). Overall survival (OS), progression of disease within 24 months (POD24), and histologic transformation did not differ significantly by M‐protein status. Among 70 patients with evaluable post‐treatment data, M‐protein response of at least partial response (PR) was highly specific for clinical response and had a high positive predictive value, but response depth did not predict PFS. In uniformly tested MZL patients requiring systemic therapy, baseline M‐protein identifies a subgroup enriched for plasmacytic differentiation and associated with shorter PFS. Post‐treatment M‐protein decline can support response confirmation when present, but it should not be used as a surrogate endpoint for durable disease control without prospective validation.

doi:10.1002/hon.70287.abstract: ABSTRACT Measurable residual disease (MRD) has established itself as an essential post‐treatment biomarker in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). While achieving undetectable MRD (uMRD) reliably predicts prolonged progression‐free survival (PFS) for individual patients across clinical trials, establishing MRD as a universal, trial‐level regulatory surrogate endpoint across contemporary targeted therapies remains a formidable biostatistical hurdle. This perspective addresses the “atomistic fallacy” underlying the apparent erosion of trial‐level surrogacy observed in aggregate meta‐analyses. We demonstrate that the attenuation of trial‐level surrogacy stems from fundamental biological effect modification—specifically the distinction between cytostatic therapies (e.g., continuous Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors) and cytotoxic, deep‐remission regimens (e.g., fixed‐duration venetoclax combinations)—as well as operational confounders introduced by modern adaptive trial designs. Reconciling these individual‐ and trial‐level observations requires transitioning from a binary endorsement model to a mechanism‐dependent, context‐specific framework for surrogate endpoint validation in CLL.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70668.abstract: ABSTRACT Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection has been implicated in vocal fold leukoplakia (VFL), a precancerous laryngeal lesion. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the relationship between H. pylori and VFL, focusing on the NRF2/KEAP1 oxidative stress pathway. Clinicopathological analysis was performed on samples from 64 patients with VFL and 30 patients with vocal cord polyps (controls). The results showed a significantly higher prevalence of H. pylori in the VFL group (48.4%) than in the controls (16.7%, p = 0.003). Among H. pylori ‐positive VFL cases, VacA‐positive strains predominated, accounting for 71.0%. Multivariate logistic regression identified H. pylori as an independent risk factor for VFL (OR = 6.198, 95% CI: 1.580–24.321). VFL tissues exhibited upregulated expression of NRF2, KEAP1, and HO‐1 ( p < 0.001), demonstrating both virulence‐dependent (HO‐1 induction) and virulence‐independent (NRF2 upregulation) pathway activation patterns. In vitro experiments revealed that H. pylori exposure induced NRF2 nuclear translocation and triggered an oxidative stress response. Notably, VFL‐derived cells responded more rapidly to H. pylori stimulation, with pathway activation peaking at 24 h post‐infection, whereas normal cells showed a delayed response, peaking at 48 h ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, VFL‐derived cells displayed more pronounced stress‐induced morphological alterations following H. pylori exposure. These findings suggest that H. pylori may promote VFL progression via NRF2/KEAP1 pathway activation, highlighting the potential clinical value of H. pylori screening in VFL management.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70681.abstract: Historically viewed as a localized gastrointestinal malignancy, colorectal cancer (CRC) is increasingly recognized as a systemic pathology that actively programs distant microenvironments. This review delineates a novel mechanistic framework wherein CRC-driven dysregulation of the brain-gut-microbiota axis (BGMA) acts as a systemic architect of the breast pre-metastatic niche (PMN). We synthesize how localized intestinal oncogenic stress propagates through three convergent conduits: (1) Immune Reprogramming, where gut-derived inflammatory mediators and extracellular vesicles (EVs) recruit myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) to the mammary stroma; (2) Neuro-ecological Conditioning, involving chronic hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activation and sympathetic hyperactivation that drives catecholamine-mediated remodeling of breast tissue; and (3) Humoral-Metabolic Convergence, specifically via the "estrobolome" and secondary bile acids that synchronize systemic hormonal levels with local tissue receptivity. By reframing CRC progression as a systemic pathology that potentially preconditions distant, hormone-sensitive environments, we propose the BGMA as a conceptual framework for prospective "systemic interception", outlining roadmaps to neutralize metastatic cascades at their incipient, reversible stages.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70726.abstract: Early detection of melanoma remains challenging, and minimally invasive diagnostic tools are needed to complement imaging and histopathology. Circulating tumour antigen-specific antibodies (Abs) are promising biomarkers, but their diagnostic value across melanoma stages is not fully established. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs were profiled in plasma from two independent melanoma cohorts, early-stage (n = 65) and advanced-stage (n = 77), alongside healthy controls (n = 86) and individuals with prior cancer in remission (n = 37). A protein microarray containing 263 tumour antigens, predominantly cancer-testis (CT) antigens, was used to measure plasma antibody (Ab) reactivity. Univariate and multivariate ROC analyses identified candidate diagnostic biomarker signatures. Early-stage melanoma was best distinguished by an IgM signature comprising AURKA, BAGE3, BAGE4, CDK7, CEP290, MYBL2, PIAS2, RAD51 and SPANXB1 (AUC = 0.939). An IgG signature including ANKRD45, BCL2L14, CDK2, MAGEA4v3, MAPK3 and RBM46 achieved AUC = 0.827. Advanced-stage melanoma exhibited broader Ab repertoires, including an IgG signature (CTAG1A, DKKL1, PIWIL2, SPANXN1, TSGA10, TSPY1; AUC = 0.865) and an IgM signature (CPXCR1, CSAG2, FMR1NB, FOXR2, LIPI, MAGEA5, TSGA10; AUC = 0.889). Individuals in cancer remission displayed persistent Ab signatures distinct from early melanoma and healthy controls. Overlap between IgG and IgM repertoires was minimal, highlighting complementary discriminatory value. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs against tumour antigens reveal stage-specific signatures that distinguish melanoma from healthy individuals and those in cancer remission, identifying candidate discovery-stage diagnostic biomarker signatures warranting independent validation in larger prospective cohorts to determine clinical utility.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70742.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors such as anti-PD-1 antibodies are essential in cancer therapy. Emerging data suggest that lower doses may be effective and more economical, though further evidence is needed. We conducted a retrospective study at Centre Léon Bérard to assess the efficacy and safety of low-dose nivolumab (20 mg every 3 weeks) in patients with advanced cancer, mainly squamous cell carcinomas (SCC). Between 2023 and 2024, 53 patients were treated, with a median age of 74 years; 39.6% were over 80. Most were male (64%) and had ECOG ≥ 2 (69.9%). Primary tumor sites included cutaneous SCC (34%), head and neck SCC (32%), and soft tissue sarcoma (15%). After a median follow-up of 8.3 months, median overall survival was 7.5 months. The objective response rate (ORR) was 20.8%, driven by the SCC subgroup; no responses were observed in non-SCC histologies, in patients with prior ICI exposure, or beyond the second line of treatment. Among IO-naïve SCC patients treated in first or second line (n = 22), ORR was 50%. Toxicity was manageable: 18.7% experienced immune-related adverse events, with only 3.7% grade 3. Low-dose nivolumab demonstrates encouraging efficacy and tolerability in a frail population, supporting its potential role in resource-limited settings. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm these findings in broader populations.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70753.abstract: We conducted a controlled trial among 5626 early adolescent women vaccinated in 2007-2009 against human papillomavirus (HPV) types 16/18 to evaluate the impact of high-intensity versus low-intensity cervical screening, respectively at ages 22/25/28 and 28 years with squamous-cell intraepithelial lesions (SILs) as the end-point. Over the 16-year follow-up, most of the cytologically and/or histologically confirmed low-grade and high-grade SILs were associated with non-vaccine-targeted, medium oncogenicity HPV types 33/35/52/58 belonging to clade A9. The low-intensity cervical screening was non-inferior to the high-intensity screening in the identification of these lesions. Possibly, the transition from cervical infections with vaccine-covered HPV types to infections with non-vaccine-covered HPV types contributes to more manageable occurrence of the screen-detected cervical lesions. Reduction of cervical screening among vaccinated women to a minimum may be warranted to balance the harm-benefit ratio of screening.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70765.abstract: BRCAness, a phenotype associated with homologous recombination deficiency, has not been fully characterized in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), especially regarding prognosis and regimen-specific postoperative management. We analyzed 137 patients with TNBC who had residual invasive disease after NAC. BRCAness status was assessed in surgical specimens using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA). Its associations with clinicopathological features and survival were evaluated according to NAC regimen, and prognostic models for disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were developed by combining BRCAness with clinicopathological variables. BRCAness was identified in 42.3% of tumors and was associated with high histological grade, high Ki-67, and perineural invasion. Patients with BRCAness-positive tumors had worse survival than those with BRCAness-negative tumors (5-year DFS, 50.0% vs. 68.2%, p = 0.020; 5-year OS, 58.6% vs. 78.1%, p = 0.014). This prognostic effect was evident in patients treated with anthracycline-based NAC, but not in those treated with platinum-based regimens. Models incorporating BRCAness showed good discrimination (DFS C-index, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.62-0.78; OS C-index, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.69-0.81). Among BRCAness-positive patients who had received anthracycline-based NAC, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with better survival (5-year DFS, 55.6% vs. 27.3%, p = 0.035; 5-year OS, 66.7% vs. 36.4%, p = 0.023). BRCAness was associated with poorer outcome in residual TNBC after NAC and may help identify patients with different prognoses and postoperative treatment patterns.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70774.abstract: While current colorectal cancer (CRC) screening guidelines consider family history to determine starting age for screening, they inadequately incorporate other important unmodifiable risk factors, including polygenic risk score (PRS) and biological sex. In 353,118 average-risk UK Biobank participants, we used family history-stratified Cox models to estimate associations of sex and PRS with CRC incidence, metastasis, and CRC-specific mortality. We translated risk differences into risk-adapted initiation screening ages using both risk advancement period (RAP) and absolute 10-year cumulative risk. Men had a higher risk of CRC compared to women, with HRs of 1.41 (95% CI, 1.33-1.50) for those without family history and 1.42 (95% CI, 1.26-1.61) for those with family history. For each one-standard deviation (SD) increase in PRS, the risk was 1.49 times higher (95% CI, 1.45-1.53) in participants without a family history and 1.42 times higher (95% CI, 1.34-1.51) in those with a family history. The increase in PRS was associated with elevated risks of both metastatic CRC at diagnosis and CRC-specific mortality, indicating delayed diagnosis in high-PRS individuals and highlighting the potential benefit of earlier screening. Consequently, risk-adapted initiation ages ranged from before 40 years for men with a family history in the high-PRS group to after 60 years for women without a family history in the low-PRS group. Our findings demonstrate that the integration of PRS, biological sex, and family history identifies substantial heterogeneity in CRC risk and risk-adapted screening initiation ages.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70779.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including esophageal (EC), gastric (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), impose a substantial global burden, with early detection remaining crucial for improving patient outcomes. The oral and gut microbiota are increasingly implicated in cancer development and hold promise as sources of non-invasive biomarkers. However, current evidence on microbiome-based diagnostics remains fragmented, and a systematic comparison of the diagnostic accuracy between oral and fecal sampling across multiple GI cancer types is lacking. To address this gap, a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus up to December 31, 2025, identified 43 case-control studies (59 cohorts) comprising 4452 cancer patients and 5809 controls. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.846 (95% CI: 0.824-0.867), though with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 86.5%). By cancer type, pooled AUCs were 0.746 for EC (5 cohorts), 0.886 for GC (8 cohorts), and 0.850 for CRC (46 cohorts). A bivariate analysis of 20 cohorts comparing sample types found no statistically significant difference in diagnostic performance between oral (sAUC = 0.863) and fecal sampling (sAUC = 0.820; p = 0.369). While these exploratory findings suggest that oral and fecal microbial biomarkers may offer comparable diagnostic accuracy for GI cancers, with oral sampling presenting a more practical option for screening, the results are preliminary. Significant heterogeneity, a limited number of oral cohorts, and the absence of clinical control groups highlight the need for large-scale prospective studies with direct comparisons and real-world validation to validate these biomarkers for clinical translation.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70780.abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in a subset of cases. We previously showed that the incidence of HL in Taiwan increased ~2.5-fold between 2001 and 2020, particularly among young women with the nodular sclerosis (NS) subtype. In this nationwide multicenter study, we evaluated EBV status in HL to determine its impact on clinicopathologic features and survival outcomes. We found that the proportion of EBV-associated HL in Taiwan declined over the past two decades, from 39% to 27%. EBV-positive frequency exhibited a bimodal age distribution, peaking in children 70 years (80%), with the lowest frequency in patients 20-29 years (11%). Compared with EBV-negative patients, EBV-positive patients were older (53.5 vs. 32.9 years; p 60 years), B symptoms, non-NS histology, EBV-positivity, advanced-stage disease (Stage III-IV), and a high International Prognostic Score (IPS, 4-7). On multivariate analysis, older age and a high IPS retained prognostic significance. Large registry datasets from Taiwan and the US further demonstrated that survival outcomes have improved over the past two decades. Female patients and those with the NS and nodular lymphocyte-predominant subtypes had significantly better survival. These findings provide insight into the biological impact of EBV in HL and help inform strategies for disease prevention and management.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70781.abstract: Available epidemiological evidence shows that many cancers share familial risks, and this is increasingly confirmed by data on shared pathogenic germline gene variants between cancers. We decided to harness the world's largest resource on familial cancer to assess discordant familial risks for female breast (BC), prostate (PC), colorectal (CRC), and lung (LC) cancers with any of 22 different cancers in first-degree relatives (proband cancers). Familial relative risk was calculated as standardized incidence ratio (SIR) when either one proband or 2 or more (2+) probands were found in a family to distinguish low- and high-risk associations. Discordant familial associations of BC were significant for 12 1-proband and 5 2+ proband cancers. For PC, the numbers were 11 and 4; for CRC, they were 8 and 4; and for LC, they were 15 and 5. The results with large case numbers showed that BC, CRC, and LC associated with each other, but the familial association between PC and LC was negative. Many known or novel associations with possible genetic causes were found, including lobular BC with stomach cancer, PC with kidney cancer, CRC with squamous cell skin and thyroid cancers, and LC with gallbladder and endocrine tumors, the most common of which were parathyroid adenomas. Also, LC associations with esophageal and cervical cancers were unlikely to be due to smoking alone and require additional explanations. In conclusion, 2/3 of discordant associations could suggest low-risk genetic and environmental causation and 1/3 high-risk genetic causation, both waiting for experimental proof.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70785.abstract: Rising incidence of endometrial cancer among young women has increased the demand for fertility-sparing treatment (FST) in patients with endometrial atypical hyperplasia (EAH) and endometrioid endometrial cancer (EEC). However, approximately 20%-30% of patients exhibit progesterone resistance, and reliable predictive biomarkers remain inadequately defined. Therefore, we aimed to identify biomarkers associated with treatment response and prognosis in patients undergoing FST. In this retrospective study, we analyzed 161 patients undergoing mainly progestin-based FST, including 125 with EAH and 36 with G1 EEC. Molecular classification, pretreatment pathological morphology, hormone receptor expression, oncological outcomes, recurrence, and reproductive outcomes were evaluated. According to molecular classification, the cohort included POLEmut (n = 2), NSMP (n = 143), MMRd (n = 11), and p53abn (n = 5). Over a median treatment duration of 7 months, molecular classification significantly stratified complete response (CR) rates (p = 0.027), with distinct cumulative CR curves (p = 0.034). Patients with EEC showed lower CR rates than those with EAH (p < 0.001). Reduced CR was associated with extensive lesions, larger lesion diameter, proliferative endometrial background, papillary structure, and squamous metaplasia, whereas morular metaplasia and high estrogen receptor (ER)/progesterone receptor (PR) expression predicted higher CR rates. Multivariate analysis identified MMRd and squamous metaplasia as independent predictors of recurrence. Within the NSMP subgroup, pathological morphology and PR expression further refined risk stratification. Pregnancy outcomes were comparable across molecular subtypes. These findings suggested that integrating molecular classification with clinicopathological characteristics can improve prognostic assessment and support individualized management for patients undergoing FST.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70788.abstract: Fifty years ago, Zech et al. in this journal described for the first time the t(8;14) as a recurrent chromosomal aberration in Burkitt lymphoma (BL). Nevertheless, in regions where BL is not endemic, a subset of lymphomas with features of BL lacks the t(8;14)/IG::MYC and instead represents high-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration (HGBCL,11q). As Zech et al. already noted the cell line BJAB to be an exception as BL from a 5-year Kenyan girl in being EBV-negative, lacking the t(8;14) but showing a chromosome 11 aberration, we here revisited and updated the molecular features of BJAB. Genetic analyses confirmed its East African origin and absence of IG::MYC but unraveled complex 11q aberrations, including gains in 11q14.1-q23.1, loss of 11q23.2qter, and, notably, a nonreciprocal 5'KMT2A::CLTC3'-fusion. The mutational landscape contained genes typically mutated in mature B-cell lymphomas but no driver genes restricted to BL. Therefore, we hypothesize that BJAB derives from an African HGBCL,11q. To investigate the presence of this entity in East Africa, we analyzed 24 cases with Burkitt or high-grade morphology diagnosed at Kenyatta National Hospital. Twenty cases fulfilled the morphological and immunophenotypical criteria for the diagnosis of BLs (11 EBV-positive, 9 EBV-negative). Genetic testing in these cases identified one EBV-negative case (20 years) as MYC-nonrearranged but displaying the typical 11q pattern, thus representing HGBCL,11q. Among the four HGBCL with intermediate features, two showed gains in 11q including the region typically deleted in HGBCL,11q. Our findings establish HGBCL,11q as a relevant differential molecular diagnosis to Burkitt lymphoma in sub-Saharan Africa.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70789.abstract: Neoadjuvant therapy has recently become an integral component of multimodal treatment for resectable lung cancer. However, real-world data on perioperative morbidity and treatment adherence remain limited. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of different neoadjuvant treatment approaches applied within daily clinical routine. We retrospectively analyzed patients with resectable stage II-III non-small cell lung cancer undergoing either neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy or chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy followed by curative surgical resection. Treatment groups were compared with respect to perioperative outcomes, radiologic and pathologic downstaging, and pathologic response. A total of 143 patients met the inclusion criteria, of whom 46 (32.2%) received chemoimmunotherapy and 97 (67.8%) were treated with chemotherapy prior to surgery. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in only two patients in the chemoimmunotherapy group and four patients in the chemotherapy group. Chemoimmunotherapy was associated with significantly higher rates of pathologic complete response (37.0% vs. 4.1%) and more pronounced nodal downstaging, with a higher proportion of patients achieving ypN0 status (76.1% vs. 34.0%). High tumoral PD-L1 expression (≥ 50%) and squamous cell carcinoma histology were independently associated with pathologic complete response. Real-world treatment with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy was feasible and resulted in improved response rates compared with chemotherapy, without increasing perioperative morbidity. Histology and high PD-L1 expression may serve as predictors for complete pathologic response, although the predictive value of PD-L1 requires confirmation in larger cohorts with more complete biomarker data.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70790.abstract: Lynch syndrome, a prevalent hereditary cancer predisposition, is frequently caused by pathogenic variants in the MutL homolog 1 (MLH1) mismatch repair gene. However, a significant proportion of MLH1 missense variants remain classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), creating clinical ambiguity. Functional validation assays in vertebrate models are crucial to assess the pathogenicity of these VUS. We previously reported the rare MLH1 NM_000249.4:c.335A>G (p.His112Arg) variant in individuals with cancer histories within the Qatar Genome Program. To assess its functional impact, we established the MLH1 p.His112Arg variant in the human colorectal cancer cell line, COLO205, using CRISPR-Cas9 technology. Isogenic wild-type (WT) and variant-carrying cells were xenotransplanted into the zebrafish. Tumor growth was quantified via fluorescence microscopy at 24 and 72 h post-injection. Zebrafish xenografted with MLH1 p.His112Arg cells exhibited a significant increase in tumor area compared to WT. This accelerated growth was associated with a significant upregulation of the proliferation marker MKI67 in variant-carrying tumors, while cyclin D1 (CCND1) and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) (key regulators of cell cycle progression and DNA replication, respectively) expression remained unchanged, despite a tendency for increased expression. Furthermore, our functional characterization of the MLH1 p.His112Arg variant in COLO205 cells showed an enhanced proliferation capacity compared to the WT cell line, as well as increased cell viability and decreased apoptotic susceptibility when subjected to methylation-induced DNA damage. The MLH1 p.His112Arg variant confers a tumor-promoting phenotype in an in vivo zebrafish model, providing functional evidence that supports its reclassification from VUS to likely pathogenic.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70795.abstract: Evaluation of arterial resection (AR) during pancreatoduodenectomy (PD) remains limited. This study compares PD with AR to PD with venous resection (VR) and no vascular resection (NVR). Patient demographics, outcomes, and changes over 5 years are evaluated. In this study, NSQIP data was analyzed comparing patients undergoing PD with AR to NVR and VR. Demographics and 30-day post-operative outcomes were compared, and multivariable modeling evaluated factors associated with serious complications and mortality. Propensity score matched (PSM) analysis compared AR to NVR, AR to VR, and VR to NVR. We evaluated 28,083 patients with 4.1% having AR and 10.9% having VR. After demographic adjustment, both AR (1.40; p < 0.001) and VR (OR 1.32; p < 0.001) were independently associated with serious complications and mortality (AR: OR 2.03; p = 0.002; VR: OR 1.43; p = 0.043). PSM supported increased serious complications (+4.9% VR, p < 0.001; +5.40% AR, p = 0.008) but not mortality (+0.4% VR, p = 0.323; +1.4% AR, p = 0.067) compared to NVR. AR did not increase the risk of complications or mortality compared to VR following PSM. Evaluating AR/VR from 2017 to 2021 shows consistent demographics but increasing neoadjuvant treatment (40.2%-48.9%; p < 0.001). Length of stay has decreased (12.3-9.6 days; p < 0.001), while serious complications (19.7%-22.1%) and mortality (1.7%-3.1%) remained similar. Results demonstrate that arterial (and venous) resection during PD is independently associated with 30-day serious complications compared to without vascular resection. However, absolute morbidity rates during vascular resection may be acceptable in selected patients and appear to be similar with arterial and venous resection. Future studies evaluating long-term outcomes are needed.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70796.abstract: We examined the associations of parity and breastfeeding with postmenopausal breast density, longitudinal changes in breast density, and breast cancer risk, and assessed the extent to which breast density mediates these relationships. We analyzed a cohort of women who underwent mammography in 2009-2010 and had at least one follow-up mammogram through 2016. Parity and breastfeeding history were self-reported, breast density was classified using Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS), and relative risks (RRs) were estimated using Poisson regression. Mediation analysis evaluated the contributions of baseline breast density and its longitudinal change. Lower parity and shorter breastfeeding duration were associated with higher baseline breast density and less favorable density trajectories over time, including a greater likelihood of increasing density and a lower likelihood of decreasing density. Compared with women with at least two children who breastfed for > 12 months, women with one child who did not breastfeed had a higher breast cancer risk (RR: 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.43-1.64), with a clear dose-response pattern across parity and breastfeeding categories. Parity showed stronger associations than breastfeeding duration with both breast density and breast cancer risk, and these associations were generally stronger among women aged 65 years or older. Baseline breast density and its longitudinal change mediated approximately 10%-15% of the associations between reproductive factors and breast cancer risk. These findings suggest that reproductive history has long-term effects on breast tissue composition and partly explains subsequent breast cancer risk in postmenopausal women.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70797.abstract: Globally, Japan has the largest proportion of individuals aged ≥ 85 years. However, epidemiological studies on cancer in this age group are limited. This study aimed to investigate cancer trends and characteristics among the oldest-old adults (aged ≥ 85 years) in Japan, using population-based national and prefectural cancer registry data on incidence, mortality, trends, stage, and treatment patterns, and compared them with those of young-old adults (aged 65-84 years). From 1995 to 2020, the number of cancer cases among the oldest-old increased more than four-fold, with a significant average annual percent change of +5.9% (confidence interval: 5.4-6.3), surpassing growth in both the overall and young-old populations, and accounting for 15.7% of all cases in 2020. The oldest-old showed higher proportions of skin and gallbladder/bile duct cancers, and rising proportions of breast and prostate cancers. The group was more likely to be diagnosed at unstaged or advanced stages of cancer. Aggressive treatment was less commonly administered to this group, even when the stage at diagnosis was similar to that in the younger-old patients. These findings highlight distinct epidemiological and clinical cancer trends in the oldest-old. Since cancer incidence among the oldest-old will likely continue to rise, targeted healthcare and policy interventions that consider the impact of this age group at both individual and societal levels are urgently needed. To address the needs of an aging population, reconsideration of prevention, detection, and management, including guidelines and specialist availability, is suggested. Moreover, Japan must consider further cancer research in this rapidly increasing population.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70797.title: Cancer in the Oldest-Old in Super-Aging Japan: Trends and Characteristics From National Registry Data.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70798.abstract: Many cervical screening programmes rely on cytology for triage of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) positive women. However, cytological triage has variable and often limited sensitivity, and its availability can be restricted in resource-poor settings. The Women's cancer risk IDentification cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (WID-CIN) test is a DNA methylation test shown to have promising diagnostic accuracy as an alternative triage test. In this case-control study, women were recruited from colposcopy clinics in the UK and Greece. Cases were defined as women with histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia Grade 3 or cancer (CIN3+) (n = 128) and controls (n = 119) had histological and/or cytological evidence of normal cervix. The WID-CIN index's accuracy was assessed, and the quality of the index was appraised using a validated biomarker toolkit. The WID-CIN index achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.898 (95%: CI 0.860-0.936) for diagnosis of CIN3+ in all women (irrespective of hrHPV status). In hrHPV positive women only (N = 108), the AUC was 0.875 (95% CI: 0.793-0.956). In contrast to previous work, the WID-CIN maintained high levels of accuracy in women under 30 (N = 57), reporting an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.762-0.952). Consequently, the WID-CIN index appears to be a highly promising translational biomarker and may provide effective triage to colposcopy clinics. Further validation in large, prospective studies including screening populations and comparison to currently available methods including cytology remain essential next steps.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70801.abstract: Although chemoradiotherapy (CRT) has exhibited activity against locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC), no standard regimen has been established. We previously completed a Phase I trial of CRT with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (GnP) and established the recommended dose. This prospective, single-arm, Phase II study evaluated the safety and efficacy of GnP-based CRT in patients with LAPC. They received the NUPAT-05 trial protocol treatment (UMIN000028116). Conversion surgery (CS) was considered for patients who achieved favorable local disease control and tumor markers normalization. To evaluate the efficacy of multidisciplinary treatment, the primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate, with a predefined threshold of 15%, and the key secondary endpoint was the CS rate. The other secondary endpoints included OS, progression free survival (PFS), time to treatment failure (TTF), and adverse events. Twenty-five patients were enrolled in the trial. The 2-year OS rate was 36.0%, meeting the primary endpoint. The CS rate was 32.0%, and the 2-year OS rate reached 75.0% among patients who underwent CS. Postoperative major complications occurred in 37.5% of patients. The median OS, PFS, and TTF were 20.8, 13.8, and 7.9 months, respectively. Although adverse events (Grade ≥ 3) occurred in 92.0% of patients, no treatment-related Grade 5 events occurred. In conclusion, our findings suggested that GnP-based CRT showed encouraging clinical activity with manageable toxicity in patients with LAPC. Future studies are needed to validate the additional benefits of radiotherapy. Trial Registration: UMIN-CTR: UMIN000028116.

doi:10.1002/ijc.70802.abstract: Clinical data on combined Immunotherapy (IO) and palliative radiotherapy (RT) in HNSCC is scarce. HNSCC Palliative RT differs from curative intent RT as it does not involve elective nodal irradiation; therefore, an immune response may be more likely. We conducted a UK retrospective survey of patients starting palliative RT and IO monotherapy within 3 months of each other. About 75 patients were treated at 16 centres from January 2022 to December 31, 2023. About 89.3% received first-line Pembrolizumab and 10.7% second-line Nivolumab. 13.3% reported ≥ Grade 3 immune-related adverse events and 6.7% ≥ Grade 3 RTOG side effects; overall response rate (ORR) was 41.3%. Median overall survival (OS) was 10.2 months (95% CI: 6.5-16.2) and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 5.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-8.3). OS was significantly better in locally advanced disease non-amenable to radical treatment (OS HR = 0.42 (95% CI: 0.18-0.97), p = 0.043) and de-novo metastatic disease (OS HR = 0.35 (95% CI: 0.16-0.76), p = 0.008) compared to recurrent disease. Compared to starting IO > 6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, OS was significantly better in those starting IO 0-6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (OS HR = 0.40 (95% CI: 0.17-0.95), p = 0.037). The ORR in this cohort is higher than published data of single agent IO alone. Improved survival outcomes in patients receiving IO closer to RT with BED > 70 and alternative fractionation may reflect favourable patient selection but could be influenced by synergy between IO and RT. These findings are from non-randomised cohort data and should be seen as exploratory and hypothesis generating.

doi:10.1002/jso.70388.abstract: Although OBS is a well-established approach, evidence regarding its long-term safety and outcomes in older women remains limited. We performed a retrospective analysis to identify patients ≥ 60 years who underwent OBS for breast cancer between 2001 and 2014. Patients were stratified into two age groups: elderly (60-74 years) and senior (≥ 75 years). Primary endpoints were disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and local recurrence rates. Secondary endpoints included post-operative complication rates and distribution of OBS techniques according to age group. 303 patients were identified, 287 (94.7%) elderly and 16 (5.3%) senior. Most patients (60.7%) had comorbidities. Fifteen patients had bilateral tumors, for a total of 318 operated breasts. Breast cancer was staged as Tis, T0, T1, T2, and T3 respectively in 15.1%, 1.3%, 48.1%, 33.3%, and 0.9% of breasts. Multicentricity and multifocality were reported in 6.6% and 12.3% of cases, respectively. Postoperative complications were recorded in 15.2% of patients. Median follow-up time was 11.4 years. 5-year and 10-year OS were respectively 96.0% and 92.9%; 5-year and 10-year DFS were respectively 94.6% and 89.0%. Our findings support the oncologic safety and feasibility of OBS in elderly patients, demonstrating acceptable complication rates and oncologic outcomes.

doi:10.1002/jso.70391.abstract: The PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6- trial has shown an overall survival (OS) up to 55 months in patients treated with (modified) 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan and oxaliplatin ((m)FOLFIRINOX) chemotherapy after resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The applicability of these results to a real-world patient population is, however, unknown. This study aimed to assess the efficacy of (m)FOLFIRINOX compared to other adjuvant chemotherapy regimens in a real-world cohort. We performed a post-hoc analysis in a prospectively maintained cohort of patients undergoing PDAC resection in the Regional Academic Cancer Centre Utrecht, the Netherlands, from 2016 to 2020. Median OS was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves, primarily stratified by adjuvant chemotherapy regimen and secondarily by eligibility for the PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6- trial. Multivariable Cox regression was used to assess the association between chemotherapy regimen and OS, presented as hazard ratio's (HR) with 95% confidence interval (95%CI). A total of 161 patients with a median follow-up of 51 months (interquartile range (IQR) 43-61) were included. With (m)FOLFIRINOX (n = 30), OS was 29 months (IQR 22-42; [HR 0.26, 95%CI 0.14-0.47, p < 0.01]). Comparing (m)FOLFIRINOX with gemcitabine monotherapy yielded a HR of 0.62 (95%CI 0.33-1.17, p = 0.14), while (m)FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine combination therapy had a HR of 0.66 (95% CI 0.35-1.24 p = 0.20). Patients without adjuvant therapy (n = 71) had a median OS of 13 months (IQR 11-23, reference group). In patients receiving gemcitabine monotherapy (n = 31), median OS was 21 months (IQR 15-31; [HR 0.41 95%CI 0.25-0.69, p < 0.01]); for gemcitabine combination therapy (n = 29), OS was 28 months (IQR 23-43; [HR 0.39, 95%CI 0.23-0.66, p < 0.01]) In patients who received (m)FOLFIRINOX and who did or did not meet trial eligibility criteria, OS was 27 months (IQR 12-NR), compared to 30 months (IQR 21-NR) (p = 0.16), respectively. The survival benefit of (m)FOLFIRINOX observed in the clinical trial setting was not observed in our real-world cohort, not even in the selected subset of patients who would have deemed eligible for inclusion in the PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6- trial. Survival was not different for patients treated with (m)FOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine combination therapy.

doi:10.1002/jso.70406.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare but aggressive carcinoma with rising incidence. This review summarizes key updates in the optimal surgical and medical management of MCC. Surgery remains the cornerstone of treatment for early-stage MCC, and sentinel node biopsy is important for accurate staging. Emerging salvage options represent critical areas of progress. Sensitive surveillance tools enable earlier recurrence detection. Surgeons play a central role in excision, staging, multidisciplinary coordination, and integration of emerging tools.

doi:10.1002/jso.70415.abstract: Hepatic adenomas (HAs) are rare benign liver tumors traditionally associated with young women, yet contemporary epidemiologic trends reveal increasing recognition among men. Historically, universal resection in males has been recommended because of a nearly tenfold increased risk of malignant transformation as reported by Farges et al. in a single-institution surgical series; however, advances in molecular profiling and imaging have challenged this paradigm. β-catenin-activated and inflammatory subtypes account for most cases in men, often associated with anabolic steroid exposure, obesity, or metabolic syndrome. β-catenin-activated adenomas-particularly those harboring CTNNB1 exon 3 mutations-demonstrate the strongest correlation with malignant potential. Magnetic resonance imaging with hepatobiliary contrast agents can suggest subtype but lacks perfect accuracy; biopsy offers improved diagnostic precision and enables molecular confirmation. Current ACG and EASL guidelines still endorse routine resection for all hepatic adenomas in males; however, available retrospective data suggest that malignant transformation appears to be uncommon in small (5 cm) lesions lacking exon 3 CTNNB1 mutations; however, this observation is derived from limited, predominantly retrospective data and does not exclude the possibility of malignant transformation in this subgroup. These data support selective, biopsy-guided surveillance for small, indeterminate tumors within experienced multidisciplinary centers where longitudinal follow-up is reliable. Resection remains the standard recommendation for large or β-catenin-mutated adenomas, with minimally invasive surgery demonstrating excellent outcomes. Modern management of hepatic adenomas in men should be individualized, integrating molecular subtype, size, risk factors, and patient context. A multidisciplinary and molecularly informed strategy is essential to optimize outcomes while avoiding unnecessary intervention.

doi:10.1002/jso.70415.title: Hepatic Adenomas in Men: Diagnostic Considerations and Management in the Modern Era.

doi:10.1002/jso.70419.abstract: Among patient with early-stage breast cancer, breast conservation surgery (BCS) is the most performed surgery, utilized in approximately two-thirds of patients. While 5-year overall-survival rates are strong-typically above 90%-additional re-excisions can occur in up to 25% of patients who undergo index BCS and some patients will require subsequent surgery for new breast cancer or recurrences. As such, these additional procedures can complicate patients' pathway to survivorship, negatively impact quality of life, and lead to excess healthcare costs. This retrospective cohort study used linked claims and an electronic healthcare record database to (1) characterize patients at higher risk for additional breast oncologic surgery (aBOS) following BCS, and (2) quantify the long-term financial impact of aBOS after BCS. In total, 87,190 patients with breast cancer, who had an index BCS between January 1, 2012, to March 31, 2023, were followed for up to 5-years post-operatively. Patients with and without aBOS were analyzed, comparing demographics, tumor characteristics, healthcare utilization, and per-person-per-month (PPPM) costs. Twenty-three percent (n = 20,212) of patients underwent aBOS. These patients were younger, had higher tumor grades and larger tumor sizes, and incurred greater healthcare costs compared to patients who did not undergo a secondary surgery. This study highlights significant factors influencing BCS outcomes and healthcare utilization, underscoring the need for tailored therapeutic strategies for patients with breast cancer.

doi:10.1002/jso.70419.title: Repeat Breast Cancer Surgeries After Segmental Mastectomy Meaningfully Increase Long Term Healthcare Costs.

doi:10.1002/jso.70420.abstract: Goldilocks-based breast reconstruction (GBR) offers an autologous, implant-free option for patients seeking breast mound restoration after mastectomy. It is particularly suited for patients with macromastia, ptosis, or significant comorbidities. Despite its growing adoption, limited studies have examined patient understanding and expectations. We interviewed patients who underwent GBR after mastectomy within our institution. Demographic, oncologic, and perioperative data were collected. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to explore patient understanding, decision making process and post-operative experience based on Ottawa Decision Support Framework. Nine participants were included. Mean age was 58.1 years (range: 41-71), and mean body mass index was 34.9 kg/m2 (range: 24.3-46.1). Most participants demonstrated a good understanding of the procedure and why it was offered. Common reasons for selecting this approach were a desire to avoid implants and additional surgeries. Misunderstandings regarding the amount of residual breast tissue, expected postoperative volume, and the need for post-mastectomy surveillance contributed to dissatisfaction. However, decisional regrets were rare. Motivations for choosing GBR consistently revolve around avoidance of implant placement and desire for single-stage surgery. Common misconceptions regarding the extent of oncological resection and expectations for achievable volume from GBR should be addressed pre-operatively.

doi:10.1002/jso.70422.abstract: Upper extremity soft tissue sarcomas (UE STS) present unique management challenges; existing prognostic nomograms were developed from mixed anatomic cohorts. This study develops anatomically specific machine learning (ML) models to predict UE-STS outcomes and benchmarks them against established tools. Time-to-event models for local recurrence (LR), distant metastasis (DM), and overall survival (OS) were developed in 188 patients treated at a single sarcoma center, treating death as a competing risk. Five survival algorithms were compared within a nested cross-validation framework. Discrimination was benchmarked against the Sarculator, PERSARC, and MSKCC nomograms. Five-year event rates were 24% (LR), 20% (DM), and 13% (death) over a median follow-up of 3.9 years. Best-performing models achieved competing-risks concordance indices of 0.79 (LR), 0.67 (DM), and 0.75 (OS). Parsimonious models performed comparably. Discrimination was similar to Sarculator and PERSARC and higher than the MSKCC nomogram for LR (C-index 0.90 vs. 0.68). Predicted-risk groups separated clearly on cumulative-incidence and survival curves (p < 0.001). These results demonstrate the feasibility and potential value of anatomy-specific, time-to-event risk modeling in UE STS, achieving discrimination comparable to established nomograms despite a smaller cohort. Multicenter cohorts and multidimensional data may strengthen future efforts. External validation is warranted.

doi:10.1002/jso.70423.abstract: Timely medical intervention is critical to achieve optimal outcomes in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, yet numerous patients experience delayed or forgone (D/F) medical care. This study aimed to evaluate the national impact of D/F care on emergency surgical interventions and associated healthcare expenditures among patients with GI cancers. Adults with a self-reported history of GI cancer were identified from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, 2007-2017. Multivariable regression analyzes was performed to assess associations between D/F medical care, ED-associated GI surgery, inpatient utilization, and related healthcare expenditures after adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic variables. Among a weighted sample of 6 517 883 patients with GI cancers, 8.5% (n = 552 751) reported D/F medical care. Patients with D/F care were older (76 years [IQR: 69-82] vs. 68 years [IQR: 58-76]), more frequently male (57.3% vs. 50.6%) and frequently had family income below the poverty line (40.2% vs. 11.3%) (all p < 0.001). Furthermore, individuals reporting D/F care were more likely to have emergency department visits (44.2% vs. 27.4%), hospitalizations (64.6% vs. 34.5%) (both p < 0.05), or undergo ED-associated GI surgery (41.0% vs. 19.1%; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, after adjusting for relevant factors, D/F care was associated with markedly greater odds of ED-associated GI surgery (OR 2.70, 95%CI 1.47-4.95) and higher annual inpatient healthcare costs (β +$31,410, 95% CI $23,592-$39,227) compared with individuals who did not report D/F care. Self-reported D/F medical care was associated with greater acute healthcare utilization, higher odds of ED-associated GI surgery, and greater healthcare expenditures. These findings highlight the importance of understanding barriers to healthcare access among adults with a history of GI cancer.

doi:10.1002/jso.70423.title: Missed Care, Missed Opportunities: Health and Economic Impact of Delayed or Forgone Care Among Adults With a History of Gastrointestinal Cancer.

doi:10.1002/jso.70424.abstract: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) remain underutilized in musculoskeletal oncology, with only 4.9% of tumor-focused articles incorporating them. This review synthesizes current PROM instruments-including Toronto Extremity Salvage Score, PROMIS, and emerging tools such as the Sarcoma Assessment Measure-and identifies barriers unique to this population, including psychological distress, workflow complexity, and disease heterogeneity. Future directions include flexible baseline collection, EHR-integrated dashboards, national registry linkage, wearable technology, and AI-driven processing to increase PROMs utilization.

doi:10.1002/jso.70425.abstract: Adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) following breast-conserving surgery reduces local recurrence but can introduce reconstructive morbidity. Although recent trials support the safe omission of RT in selected patients, its impact on surgical and patient-reported outcomes following oncoplastic breast-conserving surgery (OPBCS) remains poorly defined. We evaluated surgical and long-term patient-reported outcomes in patients undergoing OPBCS, stratified by receipt of RT. We retrospectively studied consecutive patients who underwent OPBCS between 2017 and 2024 for stage 0-3 breast cancer. Patients were stratified based on receipt of RT. Postoperative complications, unplanned reoperation, and revision procedures were compared between cohorts. Long-term patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the validated BREAST-Q Reconstruction Module. Multivariable regression was used to evaluate the independent association between RT status and outcomes. We identified 257 patients; 210 patients received RT (81.7%) and 47 underwent RT de-escalation (18.3%). Surgical site infection (p = 0.100), delayed wound healing (p = 0.300), and skin flap necrosis rates (p = 0.0300) were similar between cohorts. Seroma (30% vs. 13%; p = 0.006) and unplanned reoperation (21% vs. 7.1%; p = 0.006) were more frequent with RT omission. Patients who did not receive RT demonstrated significantly higher mean Satisfaction with Breasts scores compared with those who received RT (57 ± 25 vs. 23 ± 24; p = 0.001). In adjusted models, RT de-escalation was associated with a 36-point increase in Satisfaction with Breasts scores (β = 36.0; 95% CI, 18.0-54.0; p < 0.001). RT omission was independently associated with higher patient-reported satisfaction with breasts, though patients had higher seroma and reoperation rates. These data support balanced shared decision-making for RT de-escalation in appropriately selected patients.

doi:10.1002/jso.70425.title: Association of Adjuvant Radiotherapy De-Escalation With Outcomes Following Oncoplastic Breast-Conserving Surgery.

doi:10.1002/jso.70427.abstract: Core needle biopsy (CNB) is commonly used to diagnose bone tumors, but characteristics of tibial lesions may affect its diagnostic performance. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-guided CNB for tibial lesions, factors associated with diagnostic success, and outcomes of nondiagnostic biopsies. We retrospectively reviewed 272 patients with tibial lesions treated at a quaternary sarcoma referral center from 2016 to 2022, of whom 43 underwent CT-guided CNB. Patient, lesion, and pathologic characteristics were evaluated for associations with diagnostic outcomes. Of 43 biopsies, 58.1% were diagnostic, 79.1% accurate, and 55.8% successful. Accuracy was significantly higher for non-diaphyseal than diaphyseal lesions (27/31 vs. 7/12; p = 0.038). Lesions < 5 cm were less likely to achieve diagnostic success than lesions ≥ 5 cm (OR 0.231, 95% CI 0.064-0.836; p = 0.022). Of 18 nondiagnostic CNBs, 12 underwent subsequent incisional biopsy, identifying five malignancies. CT-guided CNB of tibial lesions has modest diagnostic yield, with lower accuracy in diaphyseal lesions and reduced diagnostic success in lesions < 5 cm. These findings may inform biopsy planning and identify patients more likely to require incisional biopsy for definitive diagnosis.

doi:10.1002/jso.70428.abstract: Recurrence risk after hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs) changes during follow-up, but whether baseline tumor burden remains prognostically relevant with increasing recurrence-free time is unclear. We evaluated the time-dependent prognostic relevance of liver metastasis number. We retrospectively analyzed 226 patients who underwent initial curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLMs between 2007 and 2022. Three-year conditional recurrence-free survival (RFS) was estimated at surgery and after 6, 12, and 24 months without recurrence. Landmark Cox models evaluated liver metastasis number (< 4 vs. ≥ 4), adjusting for RAS status, with supplementary expanded models. Three-year conditional RFS improved from 27.1% at surgery to 33.3%, 49.3%, and 76.6% after 6, 12, and 24 months without recurrence, respectively. However, subsequent RFS remained worse in patients with ≥ 4 liver metastases at the 6-month (adjusted hazard ratio [HR]: 1.83, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.14-2.94; p = 0.012) and 12-month (HR: 2.14, 95% CI: 1.08-4.27; p = 0.030) landmarks. In supplementary expanded models, the associations remained directionally similar but were attenuated. Recurrence risk improved with increasing recurrence-free time, but survivors remained heterogeneous according to baseline tumor burden. Liver metastasis number retained prognostic relevance at early postoperative landmarks.

doi:10.1002/jso.70430.abstract: Incisional hernia is a prevalent long-term complication after open abdominal surgery, with reported rates exceeding 20%-30%. Despite extensive research on abdominal wall failure, evidence regarding incisional hernia after retroperitoneal sarcoma resections is scarce. Retroperitoneal sarcoma frequently requires wide exposure, and combined incisions are often used, yet their effect on incisional hernia risk is unknown. Our aim was to determine the incisional hernia rate in these surgeries and to determine its association with incision type. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 134 patients who underwent primary RPS resection between 2004 and 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients were grouped according to incision type: single midline or combined incisions. Clinicopathologic variables were collected from a prospectively maintained institutional database. Incisional hernia was identified by cross-sectional imaging. Incisional hernia occurred in 33.5% of patients, with no significant difference between simple and combined incision groups (32.7% vs. 37.0%, p = 0.883). Time to hernia development was similar (log-rank p = 0.829). Tumor size was the only independent predictor of incisional hernia in a logistic regression model: larger tumors were associated with reduced hernia risk (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.47-0.98, p = 0.042). Incision type and other known risk factors were not associated with incisional hernia. Combined incisions were not associated with a higher risk of incisional hernia, indicating that the additional exposure required for complex retroperitoneal sarcoma resections does not compromise long-term abdominal wall integrity. These findings support prioritizing optimal oncologic exposure when selecting incision type, without concern for increased hernia risk.

doi:10.1002/jso.70431.abstract: Oncoplastic breast surgery integrates oncologic resection with reconstructive techniques to optimize both tumor control and aesthetic outcomes. The Modified Oncoplastic Lift and Lymphatic Excision and Reconstruction (MOLLER) technique is a reconstructive approach incorporating lymphatic preservation principles while aiming to preserve breast contour. However, perioperative outcomes remain incompletely characterized. A single-center retrospective cohort study included adult women undergoing partial mastectomy or lumpectomy for malignant or benign breast conditions with the MOLLER technique (2011-2021). Primary outcomes were immediate and delayed postoperative complications; secondary outcomes were re-excision and radiation-related complications. A total of 136 patients were included. Median follow-up was 3 years. Immediate complications were infrequent: hematoma and wound dehiscence each occurred in 3 patients (2.2%); seroma, infection, and paresthesia each in 2 (1.5%). Delayed complications were uncommon: arm lymphedema in 5 patients (3.7%); fat necrosis and breast lymphedema each in 4 (2.9%). The re-excision rate was 4.4%. Radiation-related complications were uncommon, most commonly skin discoloration (7.4%) and skin thickening (5.1%); no delayed wound healing occurred. The MOLLER technique is a safe reconstructive approach associated with low rates of postoperative complications, re-excision, and lymphedema. Its lymphatic preservation principles may be associated with reduced lymphatic morbidity. Prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

doi:10.1002/jso.70432.abstract: Gastroesophageal junction cancer is a rising global health concern with variable outcomes. The availability to high-volume cancer centers may influence survival, yet disparities related to geography and socioeconomic status remain poorly defined. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the SEER 21 Research Plus database (2000-2022). A total of 40,273 patients with locoregional gastroesophageal junction cancer were included. Patient-level variables included age, sex, race, histology, stage, and survival. Socioeconomic and geographic variables included county-level median household income and rural-urban residence. State-level volume was defined according to the number of high-volume esophageal cancer centers within each patient's state of residence: high-volume (≥ 2 centers), moderate-volume (1 center), and low-volume (no centers). The primary outcome was overall survival. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations between patient-, socioeconomic-, geographic-, and state-level factors and survival. Residence in states with lower-volume centers was associated with worse outcomes than residence in states with high-volume centers. Each step toward lower-volume categories was associated with an increased hazard of death (HR 0.923, 95% CI 0.899-0.949, p < 0.001). While stage at diagnosis varied significantly across hospital volume categories (p < 0.001), no clear pattern of more advanced stage in lower-volume states was observed. Patients with adenocarcinoma had a 25% lower hazard of death compared to those with squamous cell carcinoma (HR 0.752, 95% CI 0.726-0.780, p < 0.001). Female gender was associated with a statistically significant increase in hazard of death compared to males (HR 1.042, 95% CI 1.013-1.072, p = 0.004). Additionally, higher median household income was associated with improved survival (HR 1.006, p < 0.001 per category increase), and urban residence (HR 1.036, p < 0.001) was independently associated with improved survival. Survival in locoregional gastroesophageal junction cancer is influenced by both tumor biology and healthcare access. Residence in states with high-volume centers, adenocarcinoma histology, higher income, and urban residence were independently associated with improved survival, highlighting disparities tied to regional resource availability within the United States.
