doi:10.1002/jso.70435.abstract: The association between time to treatment initiation (TTI) and metastatic progression in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the association between TTI and subsequent metastasis among patients undergoing curative-intent resection for PDAC. Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries aged ≥ 66 years with nonmetastatic PDAC who underwent curative-intent resection from 2017 to 2021 were identified. TTI was defined as the interval from diagnosis to first cancer-directed treatment and modeled continuously per 30-day increase. Three-year metastatic progression was evaluated using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression, with death before metastasis as a competing event. Each 30-day increase in TTI was independently associated with a 14.2% higher subhazard of metastasis (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.142; 95% CI, 1.119-1.166; p < 0.001). The association persisted across surgery alone (sHR, 1.130), neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery (sHR, 1.187), surgery followed by adjuvant therapy (sHR, 1.144), and trimodality therapy (sHR, 1.125) (all p < 0.001). In sensitivity analysis restricted to TTI ≤ 90 days, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant (sHR, 1.064; 95% CI, 0.964-1.174; p = 0.22). Longer TTI was associated with increased metastatic progression across treatment pathways, although this association was attenuated among patients with TTI ≤ 90 days. Further studies are needed to determine whether treatment timing independently influences metastatic progression.

doi:10.1002/jso.70436.abstract: Transoral robotic thyroidectomy (TORT) is a promising alternative to open thyroidectomy (OT) for managing differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC), especially in select low-risk patients. This study aimed to compare TORT and OT in patients with DTC < 2 cm using propensity score matching. A retrospective analysis of 355 patients who underwent thyroidectomy between April 2020 and August 2024 was conducted. Of these, 100 underwent TORT and 255 underwent OT. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 70 patients per group. Outcomes included operative time, lymph node retrieval, complications, and hospital stay. TORT had significantly longer operative times than OT (151.2 ± 42.1 vs. 48.3 ± 11.1 min; p 0.05). Hospital stay was slightly longer for TORT (2.1 ± 0.7 vs. 1.8 ± 0.7 days; p = 0.011). No recurrences were observed during the median follow-up period of 29 months in the TORT group and 44 months in the OT group (p = 0.238). TORT demonstrated comparable short-term oncologic and surgical outcomes to OT in well-selected patients with DTC < 2 cm. Further studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm long-term oncologic safety.

doi:10.1002/jso.70437.abstract: With ongoing axillary treatment de-escalation in breast cancer, preoperative assessment of axillary tumor burden has become increasingly important. We investigated whether pathological information from preoperative axillary lymph node (LN) core needle biopsy (CNB) could stratify final axillary tumor burden. We included 473 patients who underwent ultrasound-guided CNB of suspicious axillary LNs. Associations of metastatic focus size and extranodal extension (ENE) on CNB with final axillary tumor burden were evaluated. Of 473 patients, 212 had positive and 261 had negative CNB findings. Among 135 CNB-positive patients undergoing upfront surgery, CNB metastatic focus size correlated with the maximum metastatic focus size in resected LNs (ρ = 0.72, p < 0.001) and the number of positive LNs (ρ = 0.269, p = 0.0016). All 21 patients with a CNB metastatic focus ≤ 2 mm had two or fewer positive LNs. ENE independently predicted pN2-3 disease (OR, 3.61; 95% CI, 1.51-8.68; p = 0.004). Among patients receiving primary systemic therapy, CNB metastatic focus size did not independently predict total pathological complete response. None of 244 CNB-negative patients undergoing upfront surgery had pN2 or higher disease. Pathological information from preoperative axillary LN CNB may help stratify axillary tumor burden and support individualized axillary risk assessment in the era of treatment de-escalation.

doi:10.1002/jso.70438.abstract: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (HD) have limited physiologic reserve and high competing cardiometabolic risk, yet surgery remains central to cure for many gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies. Evidence describing oncologic surgery in this population is fragmented across cancer sites and data sources. A PRISMA guided systematic review of adult patients on maintenance HD undergoing resection for GI malignancy was performed. The review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL through March 2026 and included comparative observational studies reporting perioperative or long-term outcomes. In parallel, a propensity-score matched TriNetX cohort of adults undergoing major GI cancer surgery between 2010 and 2025. HD was defined by preoperative ESRD and dialysis dependence codes. Patients were matched 1:1 on age, sex, race, and ethnicity. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes were 30-day sepsis, pneumonia, and acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The review included 20 studies after screening 1,744 deduplicated records and 83 full texts. Colorectal surgery provided the most robust evidence: dialysis was associated with markedly higher mortality and serious morbidity, and a published meta-analysis of colorectal surgery estimated a pooled mortality odds ratio (OR) of 4.12. Gastric, pancreatic, and hepatobiliary reports were smaller but showed the same direction of effect, with frequent infectious and cardiovascular complications and substantial competing non-cancer mortality. In the current TriNetX analysis, 3,757 HD patients were matched to 3757 non-HD controls. Thirty-day mortality was 11.4% in HD patients versus 3.0% in controls (OR: 4.21, 95% CI: 3.40-5.22). HD patients also had higher rates of sepsis (14.1% vs. 3.9%; OR 4.06), pneumonia (8.1% vs. 2.2%; OR: 4.02), and AMI (4.3% vs. 0.9%; OR: 5.18). Across GI cancer operations, maintenance HD identifies a very high-risk surgical phenotype. The dominant short-term pattern is excess death, infection, and cardiopulmonary morbidity; the dominant long-term pattern is competing non-cancer mortality. Surgery remains appropriate for selected patients with resectable disease, but perioperative dialysis timing, multidisciplinary optimization, and treatment in experienced centers are critical.

doi:10.1002/jso.70440.abstract: Colon and rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) have varying disease behaviors, presentations, and outcomes. Rectal NETs are detected early; colonic NETs present later and more aggressively. We compared demographic, tumor, treatment, and survival characteristics of colonic versus rectal NETs. This retrospective cohort study used SEER data (2000-2022) to identify adults with colonic or rectal NETs. Demographic, tumor, and treatment characteristics were compared by tumor site. Five-year overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier statistics and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Additional site-specific analyses evaluated stage and treatment patterns by race, ethnicity, and household income. Twenty-four percent of 30 246 patients had colonic NETs, and 76.0% had rectal NETs. Rectal NET patients were younger (55.7 vs. 62.9 years, p < 0.001) and more often Black, Asian, or Hispanic. Colonic NETs were more frequently poorly differentiated (43.9% vs. 7.0%), larger (median 30 vs. 5 mm), and more likely to have liver metastases (27.7% vs. 3.7%). Rectal NETs underwent local excision (92.1%), colonic NETs required colectomy (72.3%). Rectal NETs demonstrated higher 5-year OS (88.8% vs. 55.8%) and CSS (93.8% vs. 58.2%, p < 0.001). Stage III colonic NETs had higher CSS than rectal NETs (67.3% vs. 53.5%, p < 0.001). Colonic and rectal NETs have distinct clinicopathologic profiles, treatment patterns, and stage-specific outcomes. These findings support site-specific evaluation while emphasizing the importance of stage and tumor biology in prognosis.

doi:10.1002/jso.70442.abstract: Multidisciplinary management of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) has evolved rapidly over the past decade, guided by data from multiple prospective clinical trials. Changes in treatment of cT3-4 or N+ rectal cancer at a comprehensive cancer center between 2015 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. Of 1121 patients who received neoadjuvant therapy, 793 (71%) underwent active surveillance and 328 (29%) underwent surgery within 3 months. Treatments whose use increased from 2015 to 2023 included TNT with consolidation chemotherapy (from 10% to 81%), neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone (from 13% to 21%), immunotherapy or targeted therapy (from 0% to 10%), and oral capecitabine versus intravenous fluorouracil in combination with oxaliplatin (from 4% to 56%). Among patients who received TNT, nonoperative management with sustained clinical complete response rose from 38% to 50%. With more patients undergoing nonoperative management, the rate of pathologic complete response decreased from 22% to 8.3%. Robotic assistance was used in 88% of surgeries. The adoption of new diagnostic and treatment paradigms allows for longer intervals until surgery, more frequent use of active surveillance, and higher rates of organ preservation without compromising safety or oncologic outcomes.

doi:10.1002/jso.70443.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) metastases to retroperitoneal (RP) and lateral pelvic (LP) lymph nodes are functionally classified as stage IV disease. While metastasectomy is established for select hepatic and pulmonary metastases, the role of lymphadenectomy for nodal disease remains uncertain. This study evaluates the safety, indications, and oncologic outcomes of RP/LP lymph node dissection in CRC. A single-center retrospective review identified patients undergoing RP or LP lymphadenectomy for CRC between 2011 and 2024. Patients with peritoneal metastases or incomplete data were excluded. Demographic, operative, and outcome data were analyzed. Associations with nodal positivity, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Fisher's exact test and univariate Cox regression. Forty-nine patients underwent lymphadenectomy, 45% for synchronous and 55% for metachronous nodal metastases. Dissection was selective in 61% and formal in 39%, with 86% undergoing concurrent major abdominal procedures. There was no perioperative mortality and dissection-specific morbidity was low (two lymphatic leaks, both after multivisceral resection). Pathologic nodal metastases were confirmed in 59% of cases. Median RFS and OS were 30.2 and 104.9 months, respectively. Node positivity was associated with initial N2 stage but did not affect RFS or OS. Formal lymphadenectomy was associated with shorter RFS, likely reflecting higher disease burden. RP and LP lymphadenectomy can be safely performed, even with multivisceral resection. Pathologic nodal status did not predict survival, suggesting potential benefit to lymphadenectomy irrespective of final pathology. These findings support its use in carefully selected patients with controlled systemic disease and isolated nodal recurrence.

doi:10.1002/jso.70445.abstract: To evaluate the incidence, timing and anatomical pattern of relapse after cytoreductive surgery (CRS) for pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP), and identify predictors of overall and early (within 12 months) relapse. Retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing curative-intent CRS for appendiceal PMP at a single institution (2016-2025), recording the site of first relapse. Predictors of progression-free survival (PFS) and early relapse were evaluated using Cox and logistic regression. Among 204 patients, CC-0/1 cytoreduction was achieved in 89% and HIPEC in 92%. At 37.1-month median follow-up, 89 patients (44%) relapsed; 3-year PFS and overall survival were 50.2% and 75.6%. Relapse was predominantly intraperitoneal, most often the pelvis and small bowel/mesentery (25% each). Histology and completeness of cytoreduction independently predicted PFS: low-grade (HR 2.18), high-grade (HR 2.79) and signet-ring PMP (HR 4.35) vs acellular mucin, CC-2/3 (HR 2.18), and male sex (HR 1.74). Early relapse occurred in 34 patients (17%), independently predicted by high-grade histology (OR 5.06) and CC-2/3 (OR 3.55). Relapse after CRS for PMP is predominantly intraperitoneal, most often the small bowel/mesentery and pelvis. Histology and completeness of cytoreduction are the principal determinants of overall and early relapse, supporting risk-stratified surveillance and selective repeat cytoreduction.

doi:10.1002/pan.70327.abstract: Non-pharmacological interventions are essential to reduce procedural anxiety in pediatric care. Fidget and sensory toys are widely used for distraction and self-regulation, yet evidence on their effectiveness remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the evidence on fidget and sensory toys across general pediatric settings, with a focus on perioperative outcomes-such as anxiety, distress, and pain-to highlight relevant gaps in care. This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL, complemented by trial registries, gray literature, citation tracking, and reference screening. Studies involving children (0-18 years) evaluating fidget or sensory toys in any setting were eligible. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Fifteen studies published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Fidget spinners were the most frequently investigated device (n = 9), followed by stress balls (n = 3). Studies were conducted in educational (n = 8) and healthcare settings (n = 7). Educational studies generally reported limited or no benefits for attention, engagement, behavior, or academic performance. In contrast, healthcare studies generally suggested reductions in anxiety, pain, fear, and procedural distress, although findings were heterogeneous, and outcome measures varied substantially. Current evidence does not support the routine use of fidget toys to improve attention or academic performance in educational settings. Evidence from healthcare and procedural settings suggests that fidget and sensory toys may be feasible distraction tools for selected pediatric patients, but evidence is insufficient to support routine perioperative use. Further high-quality randomized controlled trials are needed to establish standardized intervention protocols and identify the pediatric populations and clinical settings most likely to benefit.

doi:10.1002/pan.70328.abstract: Induction of anesthesia is one of the most distressing moments for pediatric patients during their perioperative experience. They may consequently refuse induction at the last minute. Anesthesia providers are then placed in a challenging ethical dilemma: they must seek to gain the child's cooperation, force the child to undergo induction using restraint, or delay the case. In the moment, it can be difficult to parse the relevant clinical and ethical factors to determine the most appropriate course of action. The purpose of this perspective paper is to provide a clinical ethics framework to support anesthesia provider decision making during instances of last-minute pediatric refusal of anesthesia induction. Three prominent pediatric ethics concepts support this framework, including the harm principle, best interests, and emerging autonomy. This framework uses the criteria of (1) urgency of intervention, (2) decision-making ability of the patient, and (3) harms to the patient from a forced induction. Each of these criteria is discussed in depth as it relates to last-minute pediatric refusal. Case illustrations are provided to demonstrate the clinical utility of this framework in everyday practice.

doi:10.1002/pan.70329.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring during pediatric anesthesia may improve perioperative safety by optimizing anesthetic titration and reducing adverse outcomes. However, little is known about patient and caregiver perceptions regarding this technology and its implementation into routine anesthesia care. This study evaluates perceived importance, utility, and extent of reassurance provided by intra-operative EEG monitoring among pediatric patients and their parents. Secondary aims include identifying concerns surrounding general anesthesia (GA), concerns surrounding EEG monitoring, cost and willingness to pay, and sociodemographic and medical factors shaping these attitudes. We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional survey at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Singapore between July 2022 and September 2025. Respondents were parents of children aged 1-18 years and children aged 12-18 scheduled for elective procedures under general anesthesia. A 16-item anonymized questionnaire assessed perceptions of intra-operative EEG monitoring, concerns about anesthesia, and attitudes regarding the cost of EEG monitoring. Of 400 respondents (100 children, 300 parents), 83.5% rated intra-operative brain monitoring as "very" or "quite" important and 93% reported feeling more reassured by its use. Children were most concerned about intraoperative awareness and failure to awaken, whereas parents were most concerned about anesthetic side effects and dosage. Parents with higher education and whose children had prior anesthetic exposure reported greater reassurance from EEG monitoring. Cost was the leading concern regarding EEG monitoring, particularly among parents from families residing in public housing. Despite this, most parents (75%) and children (59%) expressed willingness to pay for EEG monitoring. Pediatric patients and parents viewed intra-operative EEG monitoring as important and reassuring, and expressed willingness to support its implementation despite cost concerns. These findings suggest that families are unlikely to be a major barrier to EEG adoption and highlight the need for clinician- and system-level strategies to integrate EEG monitoring into family-centered pediatric anesthesia care.

doi:10.1002/pan.70330.abstract: Women anesthesiologists face unique challenges that threaten their well-being and retention. This includes high rates of imposter phenomenon, higher rates of attrition compared to male colleagues, and high rates of suicide. While group coaching is increasingly recognized as a developmental modality to foster growth in complex work environments, gaps remain in understanding how group coaching supports women who face imposter syndrome or how effective this modality is for women anesthesiologists. This study examines the impact of a pilot group coaching intervention that focused on addressing imposter syndrome in women anesthesiologists participating in the Women's Empowerment and Leadership Initiative (WELI). Fifteen women pediatric anesthesiologists, split across two groups, took part in seven monthly group coaching sessions. A post-coaching survey was then conducted in which participants were asked about their experiences before and after group coaching. Eight of the participants volunteered to participate in semi-structured interviews about their experiences. Qualitative data were coded using an inductive thematic analysis approach. The survey showed that following group coaching, participants demonstrated an increase in self-reported compassion and acceptance of others. They also reported learning more about themselves and how to amend their own behavior in helpful ways compared to pre-intervention. Two overarching themes emerged: a sense of community (fueled by psychological safety, validation, shared experience, and addressing imposter syndrome through the group coaching) and tools gained (including clearer priorities, work/life integration, and proactive social support). Results of this pilot intervention suggest group coaching programs for anesthesiologists have the potential to build resilience in the current work environment, thereby benefiting not only individuals but the anesthesiology workforce as a whole.

doi:10.1002/pan.70331.abstract: This educational review describes the historical development of pediatric congenital cardiac anesthesia and its expanding role in the care of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Over the past eight decades, the specialty has evolved from an era in which few congenital heart defects were surgically treatable and perioperative mortality was high to one in which survival into adulthood is expected for most children with CHD. This transformation has been driven by parallel advances in surgical techniques, cardiopulmonary bypass technology, myocardial protection, monitoring, intensive care, and anesthetic management. From the first successful patent ductus arteriosus ligation in 1938 to the development of fetal cardiac interventions and the many major technological and scientific advances of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, anesthesiologists have played a pivotal role in improving the care of patients with CHD. As survival has improved, the population of adults and elderly patients living with repaired or palliated CHD has grown, and the specialty's focus has expanded beyond reducing perioperative mortality to improving lifelong outcomes. Today, congenital cardiac anesthesiologists are integral members of multidisciplinary teams responsible for perioperative risk assessment, hemodynamic optimization, neuroprotection, coagulation management, mechanical circulatory support, and enhanced recovery. The history of the specialty highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and continued scientific progress in improving patient safety, recovery, and long-term outcomes.

doi:10.1002/pan.70332.abstract: The systemic inflammatory response syndrome to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) affects all organ systems including the brain. Perioperative brain injury in children with congenital heart disease is often clinically silent in the acute perioperative period and may not be detected until patients are older. The plasma biomarkers neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and S100ß protein show potential for detecting neurological injury in the perioperative period. The three objectives of this study were to examine the correlation of NSE and S100ß protein levels with inflammatory cytokines, parameters of CPB, and the development of neurological injury in the intensive care unit following cardiac surgery in children. 50 children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB had blood samples drawn at three time points: after induction of anesthesia, 30 min post-CPB, and 24 h post-CPB. Blood samples were analyzed for NSE, S100ß, and the inflammatory cytokines IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. Data were collected on CPB durations and neurological injury diagnosed in the postoperative period. NSE and S100ß increased significantly following bypass and correlated with increases of IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. There was a significant positive correlation of NSE and S100ß with duration of CPB, and of S100ß with duration of aortic cross clamp. Three patients suffered neurological insult. These patients had greater levels of NSE during the post-CPB period (p = 0.02) and S100ß at 24 h post-CPB (p = 0.02) than patients without neurological deficits. The positive correlation between NSE, S100ß, inflammatory cytokines, and neurological deficits suggests that the systemic inflammatory response to CPB may contribute to neurological injury and that NSE and S100ß may be useful tools to detect neurological injury following CPB.

doi:10.1002/pan.70333.abstract: Scoliosis surgery is complex and associated with significant morbidity. Accurate risk assessment is essential for appropriate resource allocation and improved care. Risk factors for developing complications have been identified; however, structured frameworks to support preoperative assessment are limited. Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) uses a three-tier multidisciplinary team (MDT) traffic-light system to triage patients based on well-defined risk factors and expert clinical judgment. We aimed to describe complications following scoliosis surgery at GOSH and evaluate the relationship between preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment and outcomes such as complication rates, operative times, and length of stay. A retrospective hospital file review was conducted for all patients presenting to GOSH for primary scoliosis surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Institutional approval was obtained, and the need for ethical approval was waived. Preoperative risk is quantified by the MDT using a three-tier traffic-light system categorizing patients as low (green), intermediate (amber), and high-risk (red). Outcomes including 30-day in-hospital complications, operative time, and length of stay were analyzed in relation to preoperative MDT traffic-light score. Of 350 eligible patients, 337 had a documented preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment. Low-risk patients comprised 43.6% (n = 147/337), intermediate-risk 49.3% (n = 166/337), and high-risk 7.1% (n = 24/337). Major complications occurred in 2% (n = 3/147) of low-risk patients compared with 50% (n = 12/24) of high-risk patients, corresponding to an adjusted odds ratio of 11.4 ([95% CI 1.98-65.4], p = 0.006). High-risk patients also had significantly longer operative times (381 min vs. 320 min, p < 0.001) and length of stay (12 days vs. 5 days, p < 0.001) when compared to low-risk patients. Patients classified as high-risk by the MDT demonstrated an increased odds of developing major complications, longer operative time, and extended length of stay when compared to low-risk patients. Similar structured tools, with local adaptations, may be valuable in other centers to support preoperative assessment, shared decision making, and guide resource allocation.

doi:10.1002/path.70127.abstract: Pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant response remains an unresolved challenge in locally advanced rectal cancer, where management is moving towards risk-adapted and response-oriented treatment strategies. Prediction remains difficult because response reflects interacting tumour-intrinsic, immune, stromal, and spatial processes that are incompletely captured by standard clinical and radiological assessment. From a technology-centred perspective, in this Review we assess how molecular, spatial, image-based, and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches are being used to study and predict response to neoadjuvant treatment from pretreatment biopsies and how readily they may be translated into clinical workflows. Genomic profiling has its clearest current clinical role in identifying hypermutated immune-responsive subgroups, whereas broader genomic, epigenomic, and immune-repertoire markers remain largely investigational. Bulk transcriptomics has generated multiple response signatures with variable reproducibility but has consistently highlighted immune activation, interferon signalling, stromal remodelling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition as recurrent response-associated programmes; its most feasible clinical route is likely through targeted expression panels rather than open-ended transcriptome profiling. Higher-resolution approaches such as spatial transcriptomic and proteomic platforms refine these observations by localising signals to tumour, immune, and stromal compartments and capturing therapy-induced tissue reorganisation, but they are currently best positioned for deepening biological understanding and nominating rational treatment combinations for future testing. Established platforms such as digital pathology are closer to routine deployment as they build on clinically embedded workflows, although response-prediction algorithms still require robust external validation, calibration, and regulatory-grade implementation. Patient-derived models provide functional systems for testing candidate biomarkers and resistance mechanisms. Multimodal artificial intelligence may support response prediction by identifying complementary signals across data types and distilling complex signatures into parsimonious models suitable for clinical translation. Progress will depend on harmonised, longitudinal, multi-centre studies that couple biological depth with assay standardisation, model reduction, and prospective evidence that response predictors improve patient management. © 2026 The Author(s). doi:10.1002/path.70136.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) with anaplastic features is a rare and highly aggressive subtype with an extremely poor prognosis. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying anaplastic transformation remain poorly understood. To characterize the anaplastic transformation molecular landscape, we analyzed genomic alterations in 5,997 conventional PDAC and 41 anaplastic carcinoma cases from the Memorial Sloan Kettering-Integrated Mutation Profiling of Actionable Cancer Targets (MSK-IMPACT) cohort. Additionally, four PDAC samples from the Kyorin cohort with both tubular and anaplastic components were subjected to spatial transcriptomics using the Visium platform. Differential gene expression and pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify key molecular drivers. Genomic analysis revealed higher KRAS (90 versus 75%), TP53 (85 versus 60%), and CDKN2A (50 versus 30%) mutation frequencies, but notably fewer SMAD4 mutations (5 versus 20%; p = 0.022), in anaplastic carcinoma than in conventional PDAC. Spatial transcriptomics identified distinct molecular signatures, with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) pathways significantly enriched in anaplastic regions. Levels of ELF3, an epithelial transcription factor, were consistently downregulated in all anaplastic components. Importantly, we detected a strong inverse correlation between SMAD4 and ELF3 expression in both the bulk RNA sequencing cohort and spatial transcriptomic data. Functional validation using the KC-shSmad4 mouse model demonstrated that increased Smad4 suppressed Elf3 expression and promoted mesenchymal reprogramming. Our findings suggest a novel SMAD4-ELF3 regulatory axis that may contribute to anaplastic transformation in PDAC. The retention of SMAD4 functions coupled with ELF3 downregulation may promote EMT and contribute to tumor dedifferentiation. This SMAD4-ELF3 regulatory axis may provide a framework for identifying therapeutic vulnerabilities in this aggressive PDAC variant and further highlight the utility of spatial transcriptomics for understanding tumor heterogeneity. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1002/path.70137.abstract: Forkhead box protein C2 (FOXC2) is frequently overexpressed in osteosarcoma (OS) and has been implicated in tumor proliferation and metastasis; however, its role in regulating the tumor immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. In this study, integrative bioinformatics analyses of the TCGA-SARC (The Cancer Genome Atlas sarcoma cohort) dataset were performed to evaluate the clinical significance of FOXC2 in OS. High FOXC2 expression was significantly associated with poorer overall survival in patients with OS (p < 0.001). Functional experiments demonstrated that FOXC2 knockdown significantly reduced the overall viable cell/metabolic signal, migration, and invasion in U-2 OS and SaOS-2 cells (p < 0.05). Mechanistically, FOXC2 was found to regulate the CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling axis. ELISA, RT-qPCR, and western blotting analyses showed that FOXC2 knockdown decreased CXCL12 expression, whereas FOXC2 overexpression significantly increased CXCL12 levels. ChIP-qPCR analysis demonstrated significant enrichment of FOXC2 at the CXCL12 promoter and detectable enrichment at the CXCR4 promoter in SaOS-2 cells, and dual-luciferase reporter assays further showed that FOXC2 overexpression significantly increased CXCL12 promoter activity whereas FOXC2 knockdown reduced it, supporting direct transcriptional regulation of the CXCL12/CXCR4 axis by FOXC2. In macrophage co-culture experiments, FOXC2 knockdown promoted M1-like macrophage polarization and reduced M2-like macrophage markers, whereas activation of CXCR4 partially reversed these effects. Flow cytometric analysis further confirmed that FOXC2 knockdown significantly increased the M1/M2 macrophage ratio. In vivo, FOXC2 knockdown markedly reduced tumor growth and lung metastases in a xenograft mouse model, with tumor volume and lung metastatic burden reduced by approximately 50% and 43%, respectively. Tumor tissues from FOXC2-knockdown mice exhibited increased M1-like macrophage infiltration and reduced M2-like macrophage markers. Together, these findings demonstrate that FOXC2 regulates macrophage polarization and OS progression through transcriptional modulation of the CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling axis, highlighting FOXC2 as a potential regulator of the tumor immune microenvironment in OS. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1002/path.70138.abstract: Abstract Metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion are hallmarks of cancer metastasis, but how tumor metabolism shapes the immune microenvironment during colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains poorly understood. The role of E‐cadherin (CDH1) beyond cell adhesion is unexplored. We integrated single‐cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime trajectory inference, and in vivo/in vitro functional assays in primary and liver‐metastatic CRC models. CellChat was used to map intercellular communication. Histone lactylation, ADAM10 activation, and CDH1 shedding were validated by biochemical and immunohistochemical assays. PGK1 ‐driven glycolysis is upregulated in liver metastases and promotes metastatic progression. Elevated lactate induces histone H3K18 lactylation, activating ADAM10 expression. ADAM10 cleaves CDH1, releasing its soluble ectodomain. This fragment acts as a ligand for KLRG1 on T cells, driving exhaustion and immunosuppression. Cell–cell communication analysis confirmed CDH1–KLRG1 as a top differentially activated pathway in metastasis. Functionally, targeting PGK1 or blocking CDH1 shedding inhibits liver metastasis and restores T‐cell function. We identify a metabolic–epigenetic–immune axis in which tumor glycolysis reprograms immunity via lactate‐induced CDH1 shedding. Soluble CDH1 functions as an immunomodulatory signal, linking metabolic activity to T‐cell exhaustion. This redefines CDH1 as a dual‐function molecule and reveals actionable targets for metastatic CRC. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1002/path.70141.abstract: Children with germline pathogenic variants of DICER1 have a highly elevated risk of cancers in many different organs, recognized as DICER1-related tumor predisposition (DRTP). DRTP tumors/lesions have one inactivated copy and one 'hotspot' mutated copy of DICER1. All 'hotspot' DICER1 mutations impair 5p microRNA (miRNA) production. MiRNAs are short non-coding RNA molecules that downregulate messenger RNA (mRNA) expression. Mature 5p or 3p miRNAs are produced by the endonuclease DICER1. Mature miRNAs are loaded into AGO2-containing RNA-induced silencing complex where they target mRNAs via a seed sequence in the mRNA's 3' untranslated region (3' UTR). Despite evidence of widespread dysregulation of gene expression in the presence of DICER1 'hotspot' mutations, there is no established immunohistochemistry (IHC) marker to complement sequencing-based strategies for identification of DRTP tumors. AGO2 miR-eCLIP and RNA-seq data from a mouse cell model of DRTP (Dicer1E1705K, referred to here as E1705K cells) identified paternally expressed gene 10 (Peg10) as a diagnostic candidate. Peg10 mRNA and protein expression were tested in control and Dicer1-mutant cells, and de-repression of Peg10 3' UTR was tested using reporter assays. PEG10 IHC staining of a human tumor microarray (TMA, n = 63) was performed and the performance of the PEG10 H-score as a DICER1 classifier was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Peg10 mRNA and protein levels were elevated in E1705K cells. Expression of a reporter gene linked to the Peg10 3' UTR was elevated in mutant but not control cells, consistent with altered miRNA regulation of Peg10 in the mutant cells. A PEG10 H-score cutoff of 35 resulted in a sensitivity of 78.1% and specificity of 90.0% for presence of a DICER1 'hotspot' mutation. PEG10 is a biomarker that is elevated in many DRTP tumors from both sexes bearing a variety of DICER1 'hotspot' variants. PEG10 may act as a cancer-placental antigen/cancer-testis antigen, whose expression could create a possible target for cancer immunotherapies. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1002/path.70142.abstract: Abstract The tumor–stroma percentage (TSP) has been proposed as a prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. When assessed manually by pathologists, the TSP can be subject to significant inter‐rater variability. Automated methods for TSP determination have recently been developed. Existing approaches typically yield a single TSP value for a relatively small region of interest in the slide, introducing bias through region selection and potentially overlooking the TSP distribution across the entire histologically examined area. We present an adaptable deep learning pipeline, efficiently fine‐tuned for ovarian cancer tissue analysis using a few‐shot learning approach, requiring only minimal new training annotations. Instead of calculating a single TSP value, our method quantifies the global TSP distribution across the entire tumor and therefore captures its spatial heterogeneity. To identify a prognostic biomarker, we systematically evaluated a panel of metrics describing this distribution in 98 patients. Our analysis revealed that the mean–median difference of the TSP distribution [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.46–0.79, p < 0.001], a quantitative measure of asymmetry, together with the mean TSP (HR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.43–0.97, p = 0.03), are biomarkers significantly associated with recurrence‐free survival. By successfully adapting a pipeline for ovarian cancer, we demonstrate that automated analysis of the entire TSP distribution provides significant prognostic information superior to that obtained by manual assessment. Spatial heterogeneity of the TSP is a key prognostic factor. © 2026 Fraunhofer IIS and The Author(s). doi:10.1002/path.70143.abstract: Abstract Prostate intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) is a recognized precursor to prostate cancer (PCa) and shares many histological and molecular features with invasive disease. To clarify the relationship between PIN and PCa, we performed integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses on epithelial and stromal laser‐capture microdissected samples in matched PIN ( n = 121), PCa ( n = 217), and adjacent normal (AN, n = 115) prostate tissue from formalin‐fixed paraffin‐embedded (FFPE) samples across three datasets. We identified two epithelial and two stromal transcriptomic clusters, termed ‘invasive‐like’ and ‘normal‐like’, which were present across all datasets. Among PIN samples, 46% of epithelial and 38% of stromal samples were classified as invasive‐like. Whole‐genome sequencing analysis revealed recurrent copy number alterations in PIN and PCa lesions, with recurrent copy number alterations more frequently shared between invasive‐like PIN and PCa. This study provides new insight into PIN biology and the relationship between PIN and invasive PCa and highlights a transcriptional signature in PIN samples that may have prognostic implications. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1002/path.70144.abstract: Endometrial stromal sarcomas (ESSs) comprise a heterogeneous group of uterine mesenchymal tumors characterized by diverse morphological features and recurrent molecular alterations. Although molecular classification has substantially improved ESS diagnosis, the relationship between specific genetic alterations and morphological phenotypes remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated molecular and histopathological analysis of ESS to investigate genotype-phenotype correlations and refine tumor classification. A total of 61 patients with histologically suspected ESSs were initially enrolled, and 51 successfully underwent targeted RNA sequencing, followed by comprehensive morphological reassessment, immunohistochemical evaluation, molecular validation, and clinicopathological correlation. Molecularly confirmed ESSs demonstrated distinct genotype-associated morphological patterns. PHF1-rearranged low-grade ESSs showed a strong association with hypocellular growth and prominent collagenized stroma. Quantitative cellularity analysis further demonstrated significantly lower tumor cellularity in PHF1-rearranged low-grade ESSs compared with JAZF1::SUZ12-rearranged tumors (p < 0.001). High-grade ESSs with YWHAE::NUTM2 and BCOR::ZC3H7B alterations showed higher mitotic activity than low-grade ESSs and demonstrated tongue-like infiltration patterns in both primary and metastatic lesions, indicating that this growth pattern, traditionally emphasized in low-grade ESSs, may represent a broader morphological feature of ESSs. Molecular reassessment led to the reclassification of 10 cases (19.6%, 10/51), identifying tumors with alternative molecular alterations that were initially diagnosed as ESSs based on morphology alone. Among these cases, a uterine sarcoma harboring a novel GATA6::SRF fusion exhibited a low-grade ESS-like morphological phenotype but lacked the characteristic molecular alterations of conventional ESSs, suggesting a potential molecularly defined uterine sarcoma subtype requiring further investigation. Our findings demonstrate that integrated molecular and histopathological analysis extends beyond diagnostic refinement by revealing genotype-phenotype relationships, expanding the molecular spectrum of ESSs and ESS-like uterine sarcomas, and providing new insights into the biological heterogeneity of these rare tumors. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1002/path.70148.abstract: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN), a grossly visible precursor of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, is classified into gastric, intestinal, and pancreatobiliary subtypes, each associated with distinct clinicopathological features and biological aggressiveness. We hypothesised that the tumour microenvironment can explain the association between histological subtypes and clinical outcomes. We first enrolled 116 IPMN resection cases, with or without associated invasive carcinoma, and then sequenced four single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) libraries from those with distinct histological grades and subtypes. The snRNA-seq revealed that fibroblasts were the main source of cell-cell communication, whereas myeloid and mast cells were the main receivers. Therefore, we subclassified fibroblasts into inflammatory (iCAF), myofibroblast (myCAF), and reticular-like (rCAF) subpopulations, and myeloid cells into monocytes, neutrophils, macrophages, and dendritic cell subpopulations. Cell-cell interaction analysis revealed that iCAF and rCAF mainly communicated with SPP1High macrophages via the C3-integrin pathway and with neutrophils via the CXCL12-CXCR4 pathway, whereas myCAF mainly communicated with monocytes and mast cells via ECM-related pathways. Subsequently, we performed two panels of Opal multiplex immunohistochemistry and Elastic van Gieson staining to evaluate fibroblast and myeloid subpopulations and collagen, respectively, in all enrolled cases. Quantitative image analyses revealed that iCAF, neutrophils, and SPP1+ macrophages were associated with higher histological grade, whereas myCAF, collagen, monocytes, and mast cells were associated with lower histological grade. No decrease in myCAF or increase in neutrophils was observed in the invasive intestinal type. Finally, we classified the cases into three groups based on the density of fibroblast and myeloid subpopulations: iCAF/SPP1+ macrophage-rich (I-stroma), neutrophil-rich (N-stroma), and myCAF/mast cell-rich (M-stroma). These stromal groups were associated with distinct clinicopathological features. In conclusion, we revealed that the heterogeneous microenvironment of IPMN, associated with distinct clinicopathological features, may explain the clinical significance of histological subtypes. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

doi:10.1007/s00262-026-04585-8.abstract: Abstract Background Relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), particularly with extramedullary disease (EMD), has a dismal prognosis. The efficacy and durability of allogeneic chimeric antigen receptor T cell (allo-CAR-T) therapy in this setting remain unclear. Methods Fourteen patients with post-transplant relapsed B-ALL received allogeneic anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, including eight with EMD. Clinical responses, survival, CAR-T kinetics, and toxicities were evaluated. Results With a median follow-up of 13.8 months (range, 4.4–52.9 months), the overall complete remission (CR) rate was 92.9% (13/14), with a median duration of remission (DOR) of 12.7 months (range, 3.5–50.3 months). Among patients with EMD, 87.5% (7/8) achieved CR, with a median DOR of 14.7 months (range, 3.5–50.3 months). Of the eight patients with EMD, four were Philadelphia chromosome-positive and received maintenance therapy with tyrosine kinase inhibitors after allo-CAR-T, including dasatinib ( n =1), ponatinib ( n =2), and olverembatinib ( n =1). Median overall survival and event-free survival were not reached in either the overall cohort or EMD subgroup. CAR-T cells persisted in vivo for a median of 5.9 months (range, 1.2–51.6 months). One patient experienced grade 3 cytokine release syndrome and grade 4 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome. One patient developed acute gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease, followed by chronic graft-versus-host disease involving the skin and lungs. Conclusion Allo-CAR-T therapy induces sustained remissions in patients with post-transplant relapsed B-ALL, including patients with EMD, and may serve as an effective backbone for tailored combination strategies. Trial registration ChiCTR2000036350, registered on August 22, 2020; retrospectively registered.

doi:10.1007/s00262-026-04592-9.abstract: Abstract High-dose vitamin C (HDVC) exhibits antitumor and immunomodulatory properties and may enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs); however, its ability to reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in pancreatic cancer, particularly through modulating tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) polarization, remains unclear. In this study, the antitumor activity of HDVC was evaluated in a subcutaneous KPC mouse model, while in vitro models utilizing lipopolysaccharide (LPS) + IFN-γ-stimulated mouse and human macrophages were employed to investigate polarization. Mechanisms were probed by RNA sequencing, western blotting, flow cytometry, pharmacological inhibition, and siRNA-mediated JAK2 knockdown. Macrophage involvement was confirmed in vivo via clodronate liposome-mediated depletion, and the combinatory effect of HDVC with anti-PD-1 therapy was assessed. The results showed that HDVC significantly inhibited pancreatic tumor growth and prolonged survival in vivo. Mechanistically, HDVC enhanced LPS + IFN-γ-induced M1 macrophage polarization, at least in part through activation of the JAK2-STAT1 signaling pathway, without markedly increasing M2-associated features. The antitumor efficacy of HDVC was markedly attenuated upon macrophage depletion, supporting the involvement of macrophage-dependent immune modulation. Furthermore, HDVC enhanced the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, accompanied by increased M1-like macrophages and CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration in the TME. These findings identify HDVC as a potential immunomodulator that remodels the immunosuppressive TME of pancreatic cancer through macrophage-centered immune remodeling, providing a rationale for further investigating HDVC-based combination strategies with ICIs in pancreatic cancer.

doi:10.1007/s00262-026-04594-7.abstract: Abstract Despite growing enthusiasm for immunotherapy in cancer treatment, only a few colorectal cancer (CRC) patients experience lasting therapeutic effect. This limited efficacy is likely driven by different tumor-intrinsic resistance mechanisms, including loss or downregulation of HLA-I molecules, which may impair antigen presentation and cytotoxic T cell recognition. Interestingly, the downregulation of HLA-I can augment tumor susceptibility to natural killer (NK) cell attack. However, NK cell activity may be inhibited by immunosuppressive signals within the tumor microenvironment. This study describes two patients with metastatic CRC and microsatellite instability who showed durable responses to pembrolizumab despite unfavorable prognostic factors (tumor recurrence, BRAF V600E mutation and markedly reduced HLA-I on tumor cells). Tumor samples obtained at surgical resection also revealed PD-L1 expression on tumor cells and a substantial fraction of tumor-infiltrating PD-1 + NK cells. These findings raise the hypothesis that PD-1/PD-L1 blockade may have contributed to NK-cell-mediated antitumor activity in the context of markedly reduced HLA-I expression. Furthermore, assessing PD-L1 and HLA-I expression on tumor cells at diagnosis could help identify patients who could benefit most from pembrolizumab treatment, alone or combined with inhibitors of HLA-I-specific inhibitory NK receptors. These observations provide a rationale for further investigation in larger and multicenter patient cohorts.

doi:10.1007/s00262-026-04595-6.abstract: Abstract Effective therapies remain limited for neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)- and schwannomatosis (SWN)-related nerve sheath tumors, particularly for malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs). Although tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy induces durable responses in multiple solid tumors, its feasibility and optimized manufacturing workflows have not been established for these hereditary neoplasms. Herein, we evaluated T cell infiltration in 109 clinical specimens and detected moderate-to-high CD3⁺ T cell infiltration in most neurofibromas (84.0%), schwannomas (98.3%), and MPNSTs (75.0%), supporting the biological prerequisite for TIL intervention in this disease. We established OM-400, a pre-rapid expansion (pre-REP) protocol utilizing CD3/CD28-bead co-stimulation plus low-dose IL-2 (400 IU/mL) for NF1/SWN-related nerve sheath tumor-derived TILs. Compared with the traditional high-dose-IL-2 method, OM-400 achieved 100% expansion success, shortened culture duration, enriched CD8⁺ effector T cells, showed preliminary evidence of better preservation of original TCR repertoires based on analysis of one representative specimen, and enhanced autologous tumor-reactive cytotoxicity and IFN-γ secretion. Exploratory subgroup analysis across 15 independent patient samples covering NF1, SWN, and NF1-related MPNST revealed no statistically significant differences in TIL performance among subtypes. However, the study was not powered to establish equivalence, and larger cohorts are needed to definitively assess the impact of tumor subtype. Using autologous MPNST patient-derived xenograft models, we confirmed that OM-400-expanded TILs infiltrated tumor tissue and significantly suppressed in vivo tumor growth. In summary, this work provides first preclinical proof of concept for TIL-based immunotherapy against NF1/SWN-related nerve sheath tumors and establishes a reproducible manufacturing platform to facilitate future clinical translation.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06519-4.abstract: Melanoma has a growing incidence, and early and accurate detection can enhance survival rates. However, its complex diagnoses pose challenges that could be overcome by Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the ABCD(E) rule (Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter, and Evolution) is a major screening pattern enabling melanoma detection. This systematic review assessed advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) for melanoma diagnosis, particularly focusing on systems incorporating or informed by ABCD(E) criteria. Guided by Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines, this review included experimental or observational studies indexed on PubMed, LILACS, Latindex, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials platforms. Independent screening and data extraction were performed by two authors. 2,735 records were assessed and 21 studies were included in the final screening, analyzing over 90,000 images/cases. AI systems, notably CNNs and DCNNs, demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, often matching or exceeding human expert evaluation, achieving an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 90.3% for early melanoma differentiation. Patient selection bias was observed, limiting applicability of the findings. AI shows significant and evolving capability in skin lesion diagnosis, increasingly integrating ABCD(E) criteria. While offering enhanced diagnostic consistency, challenges persist, including data limitations, model generalizability, and interpretability.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06555-0.abstract: To prospectively explore efficacy and safety of radiotherapy combined with albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy for locoregional recurrent cervical cancer (CC). Patients with locoregional recurrent CC were enrolled in the analysis. The enrolled patients received radiotherapy and albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety. 99 patients were enrolled. For all patients, the 3-year PFS and 3-year OS were 48.5% and 58.6%. 17.2% of patients achieved CR and 67.7% of patients achieved PR. The ORR was 84.8%. Moreover, 10.1% of patients were confirmed SD. The DCR was 94.9%. Locoregional recurrent CC could benefit from radiotherapy combined with albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06563-0.abstract: Nucleotide excision repair (NER) is a critical DNA repair pathway responsible for removing bulky, helix-distorting DNA lesions, including ultraviolet radiation-induced photoproducts and platinum drug-DNA adducts. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current understanding of NER in cancer, with particular emphasis on its role in therapeutic response. We discuss the molecular mechanisms of DNA repair in cancer, the significance of NER in platinum-based therapies, results from in vitro studies across various cancer types, findings from patient-based studies, and outcomes from clinical trials. Special attention is given to ERCC1, ERCC2/XPD, XPA, and XPC molecules as potential biomarkers of treatment response and therapeutic targets, and incorporating the most recent discoveries regarding NER inhibitors, mutational signatures, and synthetic lethality-based approaches.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06566-x.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are among the most abundant cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME), with M1 and M2 polarization exhibiting anti-tumorigenic and tumorigenic functions, respectively. Originating from both embryonic precursors and circulating monocytes derived from hematopoietic stem cells, TAMs acquire distinct transcriptional, metabolic, and functional identities shaped by the TME. The interactions in the TME among various cells, including cancerous and non-cancerous cells, can determine the polarization and function of TAMs within the tumor. More recently, TAMs have garnered significant interest as a promising therapeutic target in oncology. The TAMs have been shown to enhance proliferation, metastasis, and angiogenesis in human cancers. Notably, cytokines and chemokines, among others, can regulate the infiltration of TAMs in TME. Given the crucial role of macrophages in regulating inflammation and immune responses, targeting these cells has become a significant focus in cancer immunotherapy. Currently, macrophages have been targeted through three strategies, including suppressing macrophage/monocyte recruitment, depletion of TAMs, and re-education of TAMs. Each of these approaches is being investigated in preclinical models and clinical trials, either as monotherapy or in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors. TAMs can also be engineered to act as drug delivery tools, carrying nanoparticles directly into tumors. In the clinic, some types of TAMs, marked by proteins like CD163 and CD204, can help predict patient outcomes in several cancers. This review investigates the origins of TAMs and the mechanisms underlying their polarization and metabolism. Furthermore, we study macrophage-driven tumor progression and devising effective targeting strategies, as well as challenges that remain and where the field may go next in macrophage-based cancer treatment. Going forward, combining single-cell profiling with multi-target therapies may offer the best path toward more effective, TAM-based cancer treatments.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06568-9.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis and complex tumour microenvironment. We previously demonstrated that doublecortin-like kinase 1 (DCLK1) is associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in CCA; however, its biological functions and clinical relevance remain unclear. Herein, we elucidated the role of DCLK1 in CCA progression, focusing on its effects on angiogenesis, and evaluated its potential as a prognostic marker. We analysed bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data to characterise DCLK1 expression and function in CCA. Functional validation was performed using conditioned medium from DCLK1-modified CCA cells, as well as endothelial tube formation, migration, and invasion assays. Tumour vascular density was assessed using a xenograft model. We used a human angiogenesis-related antibody array, western blotting, quantitative real-time PCR, and nuclear translocation assays to examine CXCL5 expression and NF-κB pathway activity. We found that DCLK1 was upregulated in CCA and correlated with advanced disease and poor survival. DCLK1⁺ malignant cells displayed pro-angiogenic features and increased paracrine interaction with endothelial cells. Conditioned medium from DCLK1-overexpressing tumour cells enhanced endothelial tube formation, migration, and invasion, whereas DCLK1 knockout reversed these effects. DCLK1-expressing tumours showed increased vascular density in vivo. Mechanistically, an angiogenesis antibody array and western blotting demonstrated that DCLK1 activated the NF-κB pathway to upregulate CXCL5 expression. Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κB or neutralization of CXCL5 significantly attenuated DCLK1-related pro-angiogenic responses in vitro. DCLK1 activated the NF-κB pathway to upregulate CXCL5 secretion; inhibiting NF-κB or CXCL5 reduced DCLK1-related pro-angiogenic capacity.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06571-0.abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) and lung cancer remain among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, with a high burden reported in the United States. While both conditions often coexist and share risk factors such as smoking and environmental exposure, temporal mortality trends and disparities across demographics remain underexplored. To analyze age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) associated with the co-occurrence of COPD and lung cancer (COPD-LC) in the United States from 1999 to 2020, with a specific focus on temporal shifts and disparities across sex, race/ethnicity, and geographic regions. Mortality data were retrieved from the CDC WONDER database. The underlying causes of death were identified using ICD-10 codes (J40-J44 for COPD and C33-C34 for lung cancer). AAMRs were standardized to the 2000 U.S. Joinpoint regression analysis was used to calculate Annual Percent Changes (APCs) and identify statistically significant shifts in mortality trends. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, race/ethnicity, and census regions. Mortality associated with the co-occurrence of COPD and lung cancer was identified using multiple-cause-of-death coding. A total of 587,762 deaths involving co-occurring chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer were identified in the United States between 1999 and 2020. Overall age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) declined from 8.904 per 100,000 population in 1999 to 7.128 in 2020. Joinpoint regression demonstrated a three-segment trend, including a non-significant decline from 1999 to 2006 (APC: - 0.40), a significant decline from 2006 to 2018 (APC: - 1.77%), and a non-significant increase from 2018 to 2020 (APC: 0.71%). Sex-stratified analysis showed persistently higher mortality among males, although mortality declined more substantially in males than in females over time. Non-Hispanic White individuals demonstrated the highest mortality burden, whereas Asian or Pacific Islander and Hispanic populations had the lowest AAMRs. Regionally, mortality rates remained highest in the Midwest and South, while the West exhibited the steepest decline. Non-metropolitan areas demonstrated persistently elevated mortality rates compared with metropolitan regions. While mortality among individuals with co-occurring COPD and lung cancer has declined significantly over two decades, demographic disparities based on sex, race, and geography persist. These findings highlight the need for equity-driven public health interventions and early detection strategies tailored to high-risk populations.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06577-8.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the anti-tumor effects of the natural flavonoid Isorhamnetin (ISO) on BC and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. We integrated network pharmacology and bioinformatic analysis to predict the core targets and pathways between BC and ISO. In vitro functional assays were performed using the human BC cell line 5637. Cell viability, proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and adhesion were assessed via CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry, Transwell, and adhesion assays. Glycolytic function was evaluated by measuring extracellular acidification rate (ECAR), oxygen consumption rate (OCR), glucose uptake, and lactate production. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were used to validate ISO-SRC binding. Western blot and RT-qPCR analyses were conducted to examine protein and mRNA expression of key signaling and glycolytic components. For the rescue experiments, SRC was overexpressed along with treatment using the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. ISO significantly inhibited BC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, adhesion, and glycolysis while inducing G0/G1 phase arrest and apoptosis. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified SRC as a direct target of ISO, with CETSA confirming their binding. ISO treatment downregulated phosphorylation of SRC and its downstream effectors (PI3K, Akt, mTOR), reduced the expression of glycolytic enzymes (HK2, GLUT1, PFKFB3), and decreased ECAR, OCR, glucose uptake, and lactate production. SRC overexpression reversed the anti-tumor and anti-glycolytic effects of ISO. Furthermore, administration of LY294002 on this basis counteracted the effects induced by SRC overexpression, confirming the critical role of the SRC/PI3K/Akt axis. ISO inhibits the malignant progression of BC by directly targeting SRC to suppress glycolysis mediated by the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for considering ISO as a potential metabolic-targeting agent for BC, warranting further preclinical evaluation.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06579-6.abstract: Extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived RNAs may provide complementary molecular information beyond conventional serum tumor markers for colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of EV-derived SNORD46 and AL592064.2 alone and in combination with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9). An exploratory EV small-RNA microarray was performed using samples from three patients with CRC and three healthy donors. The clinical dataset included 160 patients with CRC and 160 healthy donors and was stratified into a model-development cohort (112 CRC and 112 healthy donors) and a frozen internal hold-out validation cohort (48 CRC and 48 healthy donors). A multivariable logistic regression model integrating SNORD46, AL592064.2, CEA, and CA19-9 was developed. The probability threshold was determined in the development cohort and applied unchanged to the validation cohort. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap validation, stage-specific analysis, reclassification metrics, and exploratory decision-curve analysis. In the internal hold-out validation cohort, the four-marker model achieved an AUC of 0.910 (95% CI 0.846-0.963), with a sensitivity of 77.1% and specificity of 91.7% at the prespecified probability threshold. The clinical reference model based on CEA and CA19-9 achieved an AUC of 0.801, and the four-marker model demonstrated a significant improvement in discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.109; 95% CI 0.032-0.186; DeLong P = 0.0053). For stage I-II and stage I CRC, the AUCs were 0.879 and 0.842, respectively. Model calibration in the validation cohort showed a calibration slope of 0.759 and a Brier score of 0.118. The EV-derived SNORD46 and AL592064.2-based four-marker model improved diagnostic performance beyond conventional CEA and CA19-9 in an internally validated cohort. These findings support the potential value of EV-derived small RNA biomarkers as complementary components of future multimarker diagnostic strategies for CRC, while external validation and evaluation in clinically representative populations remain required.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06635-1.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor-natural killer (CAR-NK) cells combine innate cytotoxicity with antigen-directed killing and promise as an immunotherapy with lower cytokine toxicity than CAR-T approaches. However, clinical translation is limited by challenges in transduction, persistence, tumor infiltration, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed a comprehensive literature review of recent preclinical and early-phase clinical studies, engineering strategies (CAR design, transduction technologies, gene-editing), manufacturing and expansion protocols, and trial outcomes in this review. We noted a reference to the advantages of CAR-NK, like multimodal killing (CAR-dependent and innate pathways), potential for allogeneic "off-the-shelf" use, and favorable early safety profiles. However, NK-specific obstacles persist: lower viral transduction efficiencies, short in vivo persistence, poor infiltration into solid tumors, and TME-mediated suppression (TGF-β, adenosine, metabolic stress). Engineering countermeasures such as IL-15 expression, checkpoint receptor knockout, chemokine receptor co-expression (e.g., CXCR1/4), DAP10/DAP12-based signaling domains, and non-viral delivery (transposons/CRISPR) have shown preclinical promise. CAR-NK therapy has developed from concept to a clinically actionable treatment line for hematologic malignancies and shows emerging potential in solid tumors when combined with TME-modulating strategies. This review provides robust evidence about CAR-NK therapies in hematological and solid tumors, with a great emphasis on the challenges they encounter, strategies, and innovative approaches to overcome these challenges, and forward-looking perspectives to improve future therapeutic CAR-NK designs and clinical outcomes.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06639-x.abstract: Abstract Background Evidence of treatment strategies in frail patients (i.e. not fit for combination therapies) with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is limited to dose-reduced doublet regimens or oral fluoropyrimidines (FP) with bevacizumab. We conducted a systematic review analyzing evidence for oral FPs with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-directed monoclonal antibodies for patients with RAS wild-type (WT) mCRC across treatment lines. Methods We searched PubMed and Cochrane Library for phase II and phase III studies evaluating oral FPs (capecitabine, S-1 or trifluridine/tipiracil (FTD/TPI)) plus EGFR-directed monoclonal antibody (panitumumab or cetuximab) in mCRC. Outcomes included efficacy and safety. Results Seven publications met inclusion criteria (n = 262 patients). First-line data was limited to elderly cohorts receiving capecitabine plus cetuximab or panitumumab with a median progression-free survival (PFS)/median overall survival (OS) of 7.2/17.1 months (cetuximab) and 7.5/23.7 months (panitumumab), respectively. In third-line and beyond, median PFS for the combination of FTD/TPI plus cetuximab or panitumumab ranged from 2.4 (cetuximab) to 5.8 months (panitumumab), and OS from 9.8 (cetuximab) to 14.2 months (panitumumab). S-1 plus cetuximab was associated with a median PFS of 5.5 months and OS of 13.6 months. Conclusion While capecitabine should not be used together with anti-EGFR antibodies, FTD/TPI in combination with an EGFR-directed antibody appears feasible, shows promising activity and manageable toxicity profile in RAS WT mCRC potentially offering an alternative for frail patients; prospective trials are needed.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06642-2.abstract: CT-based staging of the clinically node-negative (cN0) neck in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) has limited sensitivity, and occult nodal metastasis remains common. Whether the CT-to-surgery interval influences pathological nodal outcome is unclear. This retrospective study included 329 patients with primary cN0 OSCC undergoing CT staging and neck dissection (2011-2024). Associations with lymph node positivity, lymph node count, and extranodal extension (ENE) were assessed using logistic and negative binomial regression, with sensitivity analyses (quartiles, exclusion of extreme intervals, lymph node yield adjustment). Median CT-to-surgery interval was 9.0 days (IQR 5.0-15.0), and 53 patients (16.1%) had lymph node metastasis. The interval was associated with lymph node positivity in univariable analysis (OR 1.031, p = 0.035), but not after adjustment for age and smoking (OR 1.027, p = 0.065); lymph node count showed a similar non-significant association (IRR 1.027, p = 0.068). The association with nodal positivity was not robust across interval quartiles (p = 0.969), after excluding intervals >30 days (OR 0.995, p = 0.824), or after adjustment for lymph node yield (OR 1.015, p = 0.334). However, patients with intervals >30 days (n = 13) had higher nodal positivity than those with shorter intervals (53.8% vs. 14.6%). The interval was not associated with ENE (p = 0.740), and tumor localization was not associated with nodal positivity (p = 0.175). An initially significant, unadjusted association was not robust to sensitivity testing and was confined to a small subgroup with substantially prolonged intervals. This offers some reassurance that the CT-to-surgery interval is not strongly associated with occult nodal metastasis in cN0 OSCC, while substantially delayed surgery warrants further investigation.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06646-y.abstract: Following the EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39 study, the combination therapy of enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (EV-P) has been established as a new first-line treatment for metastatic urothelial carcinoma. With increasing use, the documentation and publication of unexpected side effects and complications are essential to systematize procedures. We report on a 56-year-old patient who experienced an extravasation of EV-P during the first cycle due to dislocation of the port catheter from the cephalic vein. Extensive subcutaneous necrosis of the infraclavicular region required surgical debridement and application of a vacuum-assisted closure system, followed by secondary wound healing. The wound healed with a residual scar but no functional impairment or persistent pain. The therapy was resumed via a peripheral venous catheter, and the patient achieved a deep partial response. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of central venous EV-P extravasation (CTCAE grade 3) requiring surgical therapy. Because of its cytotoxic payload, EV in particular may pose a high risk of local complications in the context of extravasations.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06651-1.abstract: Advanced sarcomas remain therapeutically challenging. We evaluated treatment implementation and clinical outcomes after molecular tumor board recommendations. We retrospectively analyzed 125 sarcoma patients discussed in our multidisciplinary Molecular and Familial Tumor Board between 2017 and 2023. Clinical benefit was assessed by treatment implementation and by the ratio of progression-free survival on molecularly guided therapy versus the preceding treatment line (PFS2/PFS1). Overall survival (OS) was measured from first board discussion. A total of 252 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant records across 133 genes were identified. Molecular profiling enabled therapy recommendations in 71 of 125 patients (56.8%), with treatment implementation in 41 (32.8%). PFS2/PFS1 evaluation was feasible in 29 patients, and nine (31.0%) had a documented ratio > 1.3. Median PFS2 was 102 days (95% CI 63-233). Two of seven patients (28.6%) receiving poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor-containing regimens had ratios > 1.3. Median OS in 124 patients was 14.6 months (95% CI 11.7-18.5; global log-rank p = 0.220). Molecular tumor board-guided therapy identified treatment options for selected sarcoma patients. Prolonged disease control in individual PARP-treated cases provides a positive signal that warrants prospective evaluation.

doi:10.1007/s00432-026-06653-z.abstract: Health literacy, physical activity, and complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) are increasingly recognized as important factors influencing coping strategies, quality of life, and well-being in cancer patients. However, empirical evidence on their interrelationships remains limited. We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional study between April and November 2024 at one Comprehensive Cancer Center and eleven oncological sites across Germany. A total of 316 cancer patients completed a standardized questionnaire assessing health literacy, self-reported sport participation, expectations toward physical activity, affective attitudes toward physical activity, CAM use, spirituality, nutrition, and life satisfaction. Descriptive statistics, reliability analyses, t-tests, and Spearman's correlations were performed. Among the 316 participants, health literacy (M = 3.10, SD = 0.44) and life satisfaction (M = 7.03, SD = 2.02) were high. Health literacy did not differ significantly by self-reported pre-diagnosis sport participation. Life satisfaction likewise did not differ by self-reported pre-diagnosis sport participation. In contrast, more positive affective attitudes toward physical activity were significantly correlated with health-related expectations toward physical activity (r = 0.580, p < 0.001), body-related motives (r = 0.471, p < 0.001), and life satisfaction (r = 0.212, p < 0.001). CAM use was frequent, with 44.9% reporting vitamin D supplementation and 37.5% other vitamins or dietary supplements. While self-reported sport participation did not show significant associations with life satisfaction, motivational and cognitive factors-such as positive attitudes and expectations-were linked to health literacy and well-being. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening patient-centered communication, motivational counseling, and health literacy as key elements of integrative oncology.

doi:10.1007/s00540-026-03916-4.abstract: To develop and validate a risk prediction model for postpartum urinary retention (PUR) among parturients receiving epidural analgesia (EA) during vaginal delivery, to support individualized bladder management. This dual-center retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic medical records from two hospitals (2022-2024). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select independent predictors from demographic, labor, and analgesia-related variables. A clinical nomogram was developed. The model underwent internal and external validation; performance was assessed using calibration, discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Among 1019 parturients receiving EA (PUR incidence 16.09%), prolonged analgesia duration and prolonged second-stage labor were independently associated with PUR, whereas higher intermittent catheterization frequency (ICF) was associated with a lower rate of recorded PUR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination, satisfactory calibration, and clinical net benefit across validation cohorts. The validated nomogram provides real-time, individualized estimates of PUR risk during late labor. By identifying parturients at elevated risk, it offers an evidence-based basis for risk-adaptive bladder monitoring and individualized care; however, whether such model-guided management ultimately reduces PUR incidence remains to be established in prospective interventional studies.

doi:10.1007/s00540-026-03921-7.abstract: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose. This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes from 709 adults who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. SHR was calculated as the first ICU glucose divided by HbA1c-derived estimated average glucose. The primary outcome was an unweighted composite of 30-day mortality, stroke, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury, reoperation for bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and deep sternal wound infection. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinically relevant covariates. The composite outcome occurred in 90 surgical episodes (12.3%). SHR was associated with the composite outcome after adjustment (odds ratio [OR], 1.103 per 0.1 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.008-1.208; P = 0.033), whereas ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated (OR, 1.019 per 10 mg/dL increase; 95% CI 0.946-1.096; P = 0.626). SHR at ICU admission was associated with major postoperative complications in the primary analysis, whereas absolute ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated after multivariable adjustment. Confidence intervals for SHR included 1.0 in several sensitivity analyses. SHR warrants prospective evaluation as an early postoperative risk marker after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
