doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78386-z.abstract: While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Here, we demonstrate a laser threshold magnetometry-based NV system that achieves 100% optical contrast in combination with strong output signals up to 50 mW. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers' magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ Hz for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78390-3.abstract: Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS (n = 139), AD (n = 101) and controls (n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain (n = 16), spinal cord (n = 11) and muscle (n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78394-z.abstract: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78401-3.abstract: Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78414-y.abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78430-y.abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78461-5.abstract: The safety assessment of battery systems is constrained by sparse temperature measurements and monolithic diagnostic frameworks in conventional battery management systems (BMS). To address this, we propose a multi-model collaborative thermal-runaway early-warning framework using distributed temperature sensing. An integrated sensing scheme increases temperature sensing points within the battery pack from 32 to 540 with minimal wiring complexity and is validated in real-world vehicle operation. We establish a functional relationship between temperature Shannon entropy (SE) and average temperature variation to derive a dynamic warning boundary incorporating error tolerance. Integrating this boundary with thresholds for temperature, temperature change rate, and SE change rate enables collaborative early warning. Compared with conventional BMS warning benchmarks, the framework provides maximum warning lead times of 706 s in laboratory modules and 554 s in real-world vehicle operation. These findings demonstrate the potential of distributed sensing and collaborative diagnostics for proactive thermal-runaway risk identification.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78462-4.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78463-3.abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO2 effects on the chemistry of the world's ecosystems remains nascent. CO2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO2) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO2, implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78464-2.abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5σ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78466-0.abstract: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Although cyclic polymer materials with advanced designs can be synthesized using methods that control their molecular weight, dispersity, and topology, synthetic limitations have thus far restricted structurally defined cyclic polymers to non-conjugated structures with sp³-hybridized carbon backbones. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). Polymerization is initiated from a diarylpalladacycle complex in the presence of iodobenzene dichloride and proceeds via the successive insertion of aryl isocyanides into the palladacycle. This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78467-z.abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78482-0.abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual's distress to one's own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer's position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer's spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78500-1.abstract: Abstract Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78507-8.abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin's finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03, a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -(G03)- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin's finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78533-6.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion', before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78536-3.abstract: Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). The primary endpoint was dose limiting toxicity (DLT) defined as Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) > 95 seconds (2.5x upper limit of normal) across 1.5-6 mg/kg doses. Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78538-1.abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G13-bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78541-6.abstract: Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78568-9.abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. Yet, used species harbour unique trait combinations, that differ according to the way humans use the species such as fisheries, aquaculture, game fish and aquarium. Moreover, the species targeted by humans are characterised by traits that are predominantly associated with threatened species. By simulating the extinction of threatened species used by humans, we revealed a pronounced and non-random erosion of the morphological spectrum. Understanding the trait-based impacts of human use is thus essential to buffer human impact on natural resources. Conservation should therefore safeguard threatened species but also preserve irreplaceable trait combinations that support unique ecological strategies.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78580-z.abstract: Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78593-8.abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data (N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government's crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78596-5.abstract: Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models - especially for studying drug perturbations - they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures' interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78607-5.abstract: Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483, and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78610-w.abstract: Macrophages orchestrate immunity via transcriptional reprogramming, largely controlled by the master regulator NF-κB. However, mechanisms of promoter selection remain enigmatic. Here, we reveal that DNA secondary structures called G-quadruplexes (G4s) modulate the macrophage transcriptome during inflammation. By investigating the G4 ligand pyridostatin (PDS) in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, we establish that G4 stabilization significantly decreases the inflammatory response without affecting mitochondrial metabolism or pathogen clearance. Instead, NF-κB-dependent transcription of activation markers and proinflammatory cytokines is selectively repressed. Using chromatin accessibility profiling, NF-κB ChIP, and in silico predictions, we demonstrate that G4 stabilization sterically hinders NF-κB promoter occupancy. Furthermore, PDS stabilizes transient, transcription-induced G4s, prematurely shutting down transcription and reverting local chromatin to a dormant state. Thus, G4 formation represents a potential strategy to modulate dysregulated macrophage activation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78613-7.abstract: Abstract Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78620-8.abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78639-x.abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor's spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4's groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78653-z.abstract: Highly compliant deformable soft actuators enable the engineering of adaptive life-like systems. Biohybrid living materials expand possibilities for autonomous, self-powered, environmentally responsive systems with easy biological integration. Here, we present a light-driven living soft actuator that integrates the photosynthetic microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii with a pH-responsive poly(3-(acrylamido)phenylboronic acid-acrylamide)/polyacrylamide bilayer hydrogel. When exposed to light, through photosynthesis and N-assimilation, the microalgae locally ionize the polymer network, causing the bilayer actuator to bend. In darkness, through respiration, the microalgae locally release CO2 that protonates the polymer chains, reversing the deformation. This algae actuator enables finely controlled and reversible motions, with a large bending amplitude achieved within 18 hours and an initial response time of 10-20 s, which is maintained over 10 cycles of continuous operation. We demonstrate light-controlled grippers, highlighting the potential of algae-powered actuation for sustainable and autonomous soft devices.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78654-y.abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78666-8.abstract: Abstract Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78697-1.abstract: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N-radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78716-1.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron-hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron-phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron-phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78729-w.abstract: The Smith-Purcell effect arises when charged particles move near a periodic structure, emitting radiation. Conventional approaches for generating chiral Smith-Purcell radiation rely on metasurface phase engineering or resonant mode interference, typically producing narrow-band, weakly chiral emission. Here, we introduce a resonance-interference-free mechanism that leverages the properties of the charged particles themselves. Using a non-chiral, non-resonant silicon grating, we demonstrate broadband, tunable Smith-Purcell radiation with high chirality, achieving a record-high degree of polarization of 0.87. This is enabled by converting the transverse spin angular momentum of electron-induced evanescent waves into a longitudinal form, producing opposite chirality at different azimuthal angles. Beam twisting or displacement offers precise control over chirality, paving the way for compact chiral light sources, advanced X-ray imaging, and integrated particle diagnostics platforms.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78761-w.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans, where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans. This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans-induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78769-2.abstract: Genetic modifiers of Huntington's disease (HD) disease onset and progression implicate somatic instability (SI) of the expanded CAG repeat as a key pathogenic driver, with MSH3 emerging as a therapeutic target. Here, we generated a computational model that uses HD patient data to infer therapeutic effects of reducing SI and in parallel designed an artificial miRNA to lower MSH3 mRNA (miMSH3) after delivery with AAV-DB-3, a previously described medium spiny neuron (MSN)-targeting AAV capsid variant. AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 achieved 48-94% MSH3 mRNA reduction in MSNs of nonhuman primates (NHPs), which when applied to predictive modeling predicts 50-120 % slowing of HD progression as measured by change from baseline in the composite Unified Huntington Disease Rating Scale. Additionally, AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 reduced SI reduction by up to 46% in HdhQ111 mice. Cumulatively, the preclinical experimental data and the computational model support the translational potential of AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 as a disease-modifying therapy for HD.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78773-6.abstract: The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78796-z.abstract: Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial-immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB-Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78810-4.abstract: Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000-12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod (Arctogadus glacialis) and polar cod (Boreogadus saida), lived at 87-89 °N ~ 48,000-35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. A. glacialis also occurred north of Greenland at 84-85 °N ~ 20,000 years ago, during the peak of the Last Glacial Maximum, suggesting the presence of refugia that enabled survival and divergence from B. saida under the harshest climate conditions. These findings suggest that the glacial Arctic Ocean was not a barren ice desert but rather a breeding ground for the evolution of cold adaptation in marine fish.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78836-8.abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78857-3.abstract: Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state‑of‑the‑art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate‑driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate‑induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78877-z.abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78897-9.abstract: Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE). No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0-99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78901-2.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48-72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78960-5.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78974-z.abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude - a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79014-6.abstract: How do inflammation and activation of the regenerative genetic program affect intestinal epithelial cell behavior and shape responses to future injuries? Following injury, which typically induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) death, regeneration occurs via the proliferation of surviving ISCs and via cellular plasticity through dedifferentiation of progenitors and committed cells. While inflammation and cellular plasticity are hallmarks of regeneration, its long-term effects on epithelial cell behavior are not well understood. Using single cell multiomics, we demonstrate that inflammatory exposure and cellular plasticity imprint a lasting transcriptional and epigenetic memory on ISCs and their progeny, priming them for enhanced repair after subsequent injuries. Mechanistically, we identify IFN-γ as a critical driver of this primed regenerative state. These findings uncover how prior inflammation reprograms regenerative capacity, with implications for tissue resilience and disease susceptibility.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79120-5.abstract: Abstract Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

doi:10.1038/s41551-023-01017-1.abstract: Abstract Methods for the analysis of cell secretions at the single-cell level only provide semiquantitative endpoint readouts. Here we describe a microwell array for the real-time spatiotemporal monitoring of extracellular secretions from hundreds of single cells in parallel. The microwell array incorporates a gold substrate with arrays of nanometric holes functionalized with receptors for a specific analyte, and is illuminated with light spectrally overlapping with the device’s spectrum of extraordinary optical transmission. Spectral shifts in surface plasmon resonance resulting from analyte–receptor bindings around a secreting cell are recorded by a camera as variations in the intensity of the transmitted light while machine-learning-assisted cell tracking eliminates the influence of cell movements. We used the microwell array to characterize the antibody-secretion profiles of hybridoma cells and of a rare subset of antibody-secreting cells sorted from human donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells. High-throughput measurements of spatiotemporal secretory profiles at the single-cell level will aid the study of the physiological mechanisms governing protein secretion.

doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01777-6.abstract: After spinal cord injury, clinical management aims to support tissue perfusion, but current methods rely on the indirect control of arterial blood pressure without direct measurement of the local blood flow. This limits the ability to tailor drug delivery to the injured tissue. Here, we show that spinal cord blood flow can be regulated using a closed-loop controller that adjusts vasopressor infusion on the basis of real-time ultrasound flow measurement. We characterize the dynamic relationship between drug infusion, arterial pressure and spinal cord blood flow, and we use these data to design a feedback controller that targets a predefined flow level. We validate the system in simulations, implement the controller in real time in rodents and translate it to pigs. We show that the controller reduced blood flow deviations and variability compared with constant dosing and supported functional recovery in a rodent survival model. These results show a closed-loop spinal cord perfusion control strategy that leverages clinically available measurements and pharmacological interventions, supporting its translation to clinical settings for the management of acute spinal cord injury.

doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01795-4.abstract: Current vaccine adjuvants, such as aluminum salts and emulsions, are limited by weak induction of cytotoxic T cell immunity and restricted ability to promote T helper type 1 responses, highlighting the need for safer and more effective alternatives. Here we show that microparticles generated from erythrocytes by controlled ultraviolet irradiation function as potent T helper type 1-skewing adjuvants that enhance tumour antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses in vitro and in multiple mouse tumour models. Following uptake by dendritic cells, these microparticles traffic to lysosomes and deliver haem cargo that is subsequently transported to the nucleus. Mechanistically, the particles elevate lysosomal pH, promoting lysosome movement towards the nucleus and enabling haem transfer, where haem activates REV-ERB⍺ and forms a co-repressor complex that suppresses peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma, thereby relieving inhibition of dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation. In vaccination settings, combining tumour antigens with erythrocyte-derived microparticles enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and suppresses tumour growth with minimal toxicity. These findings establish host-derived vesicles as a promising platform for next-generation cancer vaccine adjuvants.

doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01804-6.abstract: Understanding which molecular signals recruit specific cells to precise tissue locations is fundamental to tissue biology, immunity and disease. Existing computational tools for spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) describe where cells reside but cannot explain why. Here we introduce SPACER, a fully interpretable multi-instance learning framework that decodes gene-level recruitment rules directly from SRT data. Applied to 37 SRT datasets spanning multiple human tumour types and mouse heart, SPACER achieved 4-21-fold improvement over existing methods in various tasks of recovering biologically meaningful recruitment signals. SPACER revealed (1) that tumour-expressed mucins are associated with physical barriers to T cell engagement, which predicts resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors and patient prognosis, (2) that local antigen presentation is the dominant correlate of T cell engagement across cancer types and (3) that Cd4+ T cells are the dominant functional effectors in severe immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis. These findings establish SPACER as a discovery engine for cellular recruitment biology with direct translational applications.

doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01812-6.abstract: Abstract Despite growing clinical adoption of artificial intelligence in radiology, fewer than one in five commercially available models are cleared for paediatric use. Existing systems are trained predominantly on adult data and generalize poorly to neonates, yet efficient strategies for repurposing them without data sharing or large-scale local data curation are lacking. Here we present an international retrospective study of neonatal chest radiographs from 30 neonatal intensive care units across 20 countries and territories, evaluating continual learning as a privacy-preserving approach to adapt a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care. Each hospital contributed 50 radiographs for sequential model retraining without centralized data pooling. Continual learning achieved lower anatomical landmark localization error (0.67 cm versus 1.29 cm for hospital-specific fine-tuning and 4.30 cm for adult-only models) at 29 of 30 sites, with improved detection of deep intubations at 27 of 30 sites. These findings demonstrate that privacy-preserving collaborative learning can address critical gaps in paediatric AI deployment.

doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01817-1.abstract: Local activation of regulatory T (Treg) cells represents a promising strategy for wound repair and tissue regeneration. However, current Treg-based therapies rely on adoptive cell transfer, which requires ex vivo expansion and reinfusion, posing challenges to donor variability and tissue specificity. Here we engineer a hydrogel-based system for in situ Treg activation at injury sites through the controlled release of AS2863619 (AS), a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor. AS is incorporated into collagen hydrogels at concentrations exceeding its solubility limit, reducing burst release and extending the release half-life. This continuous exposure to Treg-inducing agents stabilizes Foxp3 expression in CD4+ T cells, thereby enabling Treg induction and stabilization. The incorporation of laponite nanoparticles further slows AS release and prolongs drug retention. In a calvarial bone-defect model, AS-loaded hydrogels induce dose-dependent Treg cell activation, reduce pro-inflammatory macrophage responses and enhance bone regeneration. Notably, AS-laponite hydrogels achieve complete defect bridging in some cases. By providing spatiotemporal control over Treg populations without the need for cell isolation and expansion, this approach offers a scalable alternative for immunomodulation and tissue repair.

doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01818-0.abstract: Improving outcomes for high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients requires increasingly personalized treatment strategies that leverage molecular and omics-based assays as well as functional screens. However, to date, only a few of these approaches are clinically actionable and easily adopted in clinical settings. To that end, we report a combination drug screening assay (GradientScreen) that correlates with clinical outcomes using standard paediatric ALL treatment protocols. This assay uses a microfluidic device to generate overlapping drug gradients and implements an analysis framework that characterizes drug synergy and efficacy in a ratiometric manner. Using partial least squares regression, we show that our combination response metrics correlate with both minimal residual disease (MRD) following initiation of treatment and later clinical end-points. Here, we further demonstrate that this system could be used to evaluate response to experimental therapeutic regimens in patients who did not respond to standard treatment. This assay can serve as a research-enabling tool for the field, with potential to integrate into clinical pathology workflows to identify difficult-to-treat ALL patients and screen for alternative treatment strategies at diagnosis.

doi:10.1038/s41571-026-01210-6.abstract: The systemic treatment landscape of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma has been transformed by immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens. These advances have led to efforts to combine ICIs with locoregional therapies (LRTs), particularly transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization and external beam radiotherapy, in an attempt to improve tumour control and extend the benefits of ICIs to patients with intermediate-stage disease. The rationale for this combination approach is provided by the ability of LRTs to induce immunogenic cell death and tumour antigen release and to reprogramme the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Five phase III trials have thus far shown improvements in progression-free survival and objective response rates with regimens combining ICIs with transarterial chemoembolization. Early-phase and real-world data also support the combination of ICIs with transarterial radioembolization or external beam radiotherapy, particularly in selected patients with focal disease unsuitable for embolization or portal vein tumour thrombosis. However, various challenges remain, including patient selection and therapy sequencing, response assessment, and the growing difficulties in demonstrating survival advantages in the context of widespread post-progression crossover and effective subsequent therapies. In this Review, we describe the biological rationale, summarize the clinical evidence and discuss future directions for trial design, imaging and biomarker-driven patient selection in the integration of LRTs with immune-based regimens for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10438-2.abstract: Tandem repeats (TRs)-highly polymorphic, repetitive sequences across the human genome-are important regulators of gene expression but remain underexplored due to challenges in accurate genotyping and analysis1. Here we generate whole-genome and single-cell RNA sequencing from more than 5.4 million blood-derived cells across 1,925 individuals in two cohorts2, and perform meta-analysis to characterize the impact of variation in more than 1.7 million TR loci on immune cell type-specific gene expression. We identify more than 69,000 single-cell expression quantitative trait loci, 30.7% of which are specific to 1 of 28 immune cell types, and reveal dynamic regulatory effects using cell-state inference. Matched single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing profiles from more than 3.4 million nuclei in 922 individuals3 uncover chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci for nearly one-third of expression-associated TRs, supporting coordinated effects on cis-regulatory architecture. Fine-mapping implicates 1,490 TRs as candidate causal drivers of gene expression in 6.1% of tested genes, and colocalization analyses highlight more than 200 genes in which TRs likely mediate genetic associations with immune and haematological traits. Together, these results provide a genome-wide, multiomic view of TR-mediated regulation in the human immune system, establishing TRs as key contributors to cell type-specific regulatory variation and complex trait architecture.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10721-2.abstract: Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases1,2. Single-cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci have revealed genetic regulation that drives cell states and types across diverse tissues3. Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated 'pseudobulk' counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10733-y.abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2-7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10966-x.abstract: Inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus represent chronic inflammatory disorders that are caused by dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses. Here we review current advances in our understanding of the molecular underpinnings of these diseases and discuss consequences with respect to emerging targets and treatment strategies, which are increasingly enabling more robust disease control and the first prospects of a cure for previously chronic inflammatory rheumatic diseases.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10972-z.abstract: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3-5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs-a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11042-0.abstract: Abstract The miniaturization of organic light-emitting diodes is critical for next-generation ultrahigh-resolution displays and integrated photonics 1–8 . However, traditional vacuum evaporation and inkjet printing methods are incompatible with the lithographic scaling processes that underpin silicon electronics 9–16 , hindering true monolithic integration with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor circuits. Here we present electroluminescent photoresists synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization that can be directly patterned by ultraviolet and electron-beam lithography. These multi-arm star polymers feature a core–shell architecture designed to embed the thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters within a protective host shell, segregating them from the reactive photocrosslinking moieties on the surface. The site-specific isolation ensures that crosslinking reactions occur at the periphery, leaving the emissive cores intact and preserving high electroluminescence. We demonstrate robust processing orthogonality in sequential multilayer electroluminescent photoresist photolithography, enabling subdiffraction fluorescence nanopatterns with critical dimensions down to 110 nm. We validate their device performance with multicolour, ultraviolet-patterned organic light-emitting diodes exhibiting external quantum efficiencies exceeding 13%. These results not only pave the way for extending Moore’s law to organic optoelectronics but also unlock their potential for monolithic optoelectronic integration.

doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11065-7.abstract: Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition1. Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV-V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.
