doi:10.1213/ane.0000000000008378.abstract: Regional anesthesia provides significant perioperative benefits, including improved pain control and reduced opioid consumption. Clinical trial evidence underpins anesthetic practice, yet inadequate demographic representation and reporting may limit the ability to likely evaluate findings and perpetuate inequities. This systematic review assessed the reporting of race, ethnicity, and sex in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of regional anesthesia for total joint arthroplasty (TJA). The Aggregate Analysis of Clinical Trials (AACT) database was searched for US-based interventional RCTs of regional anesthesia for TJA published from 2015 to 2025. Trials were required to be registered and published in English. Exclusion criteria included conference abstracts, duplicate publications, and non-peer-reviewed reports. Data on trial characteristics, sample size, interventions, and participant demographics were compared from published articles and ClinicalTrials.gov. The primary outcome was reporting of participant sex, race, and ethnicity in publications and registry entries. Secondary outcomes included demographic distributions across racial and ethnic groups and associations between reporting and study characteristics (funding source, year of publication, center type, US region, sample size) using Fisher's exact test. Twenty-nine RCTs were included in the final analysis, representing 2914 participants. Of 29 journal articles, 28 studies (96.6%) reported sex, 14 (48.3%) reported race, and five (17.2%) reported ethnicity in the published journal articles. Among studies reporting race, 1068 (78.5%) participants identified as White, 253 (18.6%) as Black, 30 (2.2%) as other, 6 (0.4%) as Asian or Pacific Islander, and one (0.07%) as Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander. Conversely, the data from ClinicalTrials.gov reveals that of the same 29 studies, 22 (75.9%) reported sex, 12 (41.4%) reported race, and seven (24.1%) reported ethnicity. Trial characteristics did not show statistically significant associations when comparing studies that did versus did not report race, ethnicity, or sex. In this review of demographic reporting of US-based regional anesthesia RCTs for TJA, sex was consistently reported, whereas race and ethnicity were infrequently captured. The lack of difference in reporting practices across various trial characteristics points toward a broader issue within the field of regional anesthesia for TJA. Notable inconsistencies in demographic reporting on ClinicalTrials.gov were also observed. The absence of standardized demographic reporting underscores the need for journals to mandate consistent reporting practices in clinical research. Efforts to recruit more diverse study populations are essential to enhance the applicability of trial results and to address ongoing inequities in access to care and patient outcomes following TJA.

doi:10.1213/ane.0000000000008380.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication, particularly in older adults undergoing major surgery. Pharmacologic prevention remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether perioperative ketamine or esketamine reduces POD incidence and to explore optimal administration strategies. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to January 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing perioperative ketamine or esketamine with placebo or standard care. The primary outcome was POD incidence (risk ratio [RR]). Subgroup, meta‑regression, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed. Sensitivity analyses addressed active comparators and unit‑of‑analysis issues. Twenty-five RCTs (3344 patients) were included (ketamine: 9; esketamine: 16). Both agents reduced POD risk versus control (ketamine: RR 0.69, 95% CI, 0.49-0.98, P = .04; esketamine: RR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.36-0.95, P = .03). Benefit was more evident with high-dose regimens (single bolus: ketamine >0.5 mg/kg or esketamine >0.25 mg/kg; cumulative dose: ketamine >1.0 mg/kg or esketamine >0.5 mg/kg), bolus-plus-infusion, and in major surgery. The effect was observed when POD was assessed 2 to 7 days postoperatively, but not within 24 hours. TSA indicated that current evidence remains inconclusive due to insufficient information size. Dizziness risk increased (RR 1.45, 95% CI, 1.14-1.84, P = .002), while postoperative depressive symptoms decreased (RR 0.78, 95% CI, 0.63-0.96, P = .02; based on 2 studies, 493 patients). Perioperative ketamine and esketamine show a potential signal for POD reduction, particularly with optimized dosing in high‑risk patients. However, the evidence is currently inconclusive, and increased dizziness risk precludes routine recommendation. Large, multicenter RCTs are urgently needed.

doi:10.1213/ane.0000000000008390.abstract: During sevoflurane-induced anesthesia, electroencephalography analysis demonstrates alpha oscillations shifting from the occipital to the frontal regions, with further characteristic changes during maintenance and emergence. We aimed to exploratorily investigate whether alterations in alpha anteriorization and functional network efficiency are associated with postoperative delirium. This prospective, exploratory observational study enrolled 100 patients from a single tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into nondelirium (n = 81) and delirium (n = 19) groups based on delirium assessments. After excluding 17 patients due to artifacts on electroencephalography, 19-channel electroencephalography data were collected from 83 elderly patients under sevoflurane-induced anesthesia. Artifact-free epochs were extracted during the induction, maintenance, emergence, and postanesthesia care unit phases. Spectral, topographical, and network analyses were conducted. Postoperative delirium was assessed using confusion assessment method for intensive care unit and a chart review. Significant group differences emerged just before the loss of responsiveness, with the nondelirium group exhibiting robust alpha power amplification across all brain regions (median [interquartile range {IQR}] in dB; frontal: 4.24 [1.86-6.57] vs -0.88 [-1.59-3.38], P = .007; parietal: 3.71 [0.51-5.55] vs -0.95 [-2.33-1.11], P = .046; occipital: 2.81 [0.49-5.71] vs -0.04 [-2.06-1.27], P = .048), whereas the delirium group showed minimal changes. During the maintenance phase, spectral analysis revealed higher alpha power in the nondelirium group across all 19 channels (frontal: 5.42 [2.90-8.16] vs 2.89 [-0.03-5.09], P = .007; 18 of 19 channels significant by false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected permutation test). Network analysis demonstrated longer averaged characteristic path lengths in the delirium group (mean ± standard deviation [SD], 4.49 ± 0.62 vs 3.57 ± 0.16, P = .026, FDR-corrected), consistently in the frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, suggesting reduced network efficiency. Delirium was associated with early disruption of alpha anteriorization during induction and globally reduced functional network efficiency during maintenance. Perioperative electroencephalogram (EEG) transition features may serve as early markers of delirium susceptibility.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20378-w.abstract: Adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) for stage IIB/IIC melanoma was approved in December 2021 based on recurrence-free survival benefit without mature overall survival data. Given uncertainty regarding the risk-benefit balance in this population, we evaluated real-world utilization of adjuvant ICI in the first year following FDA approval and compared uptake with historical patterns observed in stage III melanoma. The National Cancer Database (NCDB) and Mayo Clinic Cancer Registry were queried for patients with stage IIB/IIC melanoma diagnosed in 2019-2020 (pre-approval) and 2022 (post-approval). Utilization was compared with historical patterns for stage III melanoma surrounding its December 2017 FDA approval. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with receipt of adjuvant ICI. Among 7039 patients with stage IIB/IIC melanoma in NCDB, adjuvant ICI use increased from 5% pre-approval to 32% post-approval (P < .0001), with higher utilization in stage IIC (40%) than IIB (27%). Younger age was the only consistent patient-level factor associated with treatment. Within our tertiary care system, 21% of eligible patients received adjuvant ICI post-approval. By comparison, stage III utilization at NCDB sites increased from 27 to 58% in the first year following its FDA approval. Adjuvant ICI use for stage IIB/IIC melanoma increased following FDA approval; however, most eligible patients did not receive therapy, and overall utilization remained lower than historical patterns observed for stage III disease, suggesting selective adoption driven by risk-benefit considerations.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20419-4.abstract: Delayed diagnosis and treatment worsen survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Despite many potential causes, the influence of social determinants of health (SDoH) is understudied. We evaluated whether SDoH impact delays in diagnosis and treatment among patients who underwent resection for PDAC. Adults resected at a high-volume center were included (January 2016-November 2024). SDoH included insurance status, census-level income and education, rural-urban residence, and Area Deprivation Index. Primary endpoints were time from first imaging to histological diagnosis and time from first imaging to treatment initiation. Delay thresholds were derived using receiver operating characteristic analysis against overall survival. Uni- and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with delays, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates, stratified by outpatient (OUP) versus emergency room (ER) presentation. Among 317 patients, the median age was 67 years, and 42.3% were female; 50.1% presented through ER. The median imaging-to-diagnosis interval was 11 days (interquartile [IQR] 3-27 days), and the median imaging-to-treatment interval was 40 days (IQR 27-59 days). In the OUP cohort, Medicare insurance was associated with delayed diagnosis compared with private insurance (OR 3.34 [95% CI 1.09-11.70]), whereas higher income was associated with up to 84% lower odds of delayed treatment. In the ER cohort, higher education was associated with reduced odds of delayed diagnosis (OR 0.27 [95% CI 0.07-0.88]) and delayed treatment (OR 0.33 [95% CI 0.11-0.91]). Post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) hospitalization predicted delays in the ER setting, whereas alarm symptoms reduced delays in both settings. SDoH are associated with diagnostic and treatment delays in resected PDAC. Targeted interventions may accelerate care and improve equity in outcomes.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20450-5.abstract: Use of pegulicianine fluorescence-guided surgery (pFGS) for intraoperative residual tumor assessment in breast cancer lumpectomy surgery removed additional tumor and reduced second surgeries. This study assessed breast satisfaction among patients with and without additional margin excision and preference for optimizing cosmesis versus avoiding a second surgery. Two clinical trials randomized stages 0 to 3 breast cancer patients to pFGS or standard lumpectomy. For pFGS, additional cavity margin specimens were taken at sites of pegulicianine fluorescence after standard lumpectomy. Surveys of BREAST-Q satisfaction were administered in trials 1 and 2, and surveys of cancer worry and patient preference information (PPI) were administered in trial 2. Satisfaction surveys were completed 6 to 12 months postoperatively by 14 % of the trial 1 and 67 % of the trial 2 patients. The mean postoperative breast satisfaction score was 75.8 (n = 99; range, 15-100) for the pegulicianine-assisted arm patients versus 79.0 (n = 19; range, 35-100) for the control subjects (p = 0.53). The mean breast satisfaction score was 73.6 (n = 52; range, 33-100) among the patients with additional pFGS-assisted cavity margins taken versus 78.5 (n = 66; range, 15-100) (p = 0.17) among those with no additional tissue taken. Overall, 70.6 % of the respondents strongly preferred or preferred avoiding a second surgery, 19.6 % had no preference, and only 9.8 % preferred to optimize cosmetic outcomes. No patient strongly preferred to optimize cosmetic outcomes CONCLUSIONS: No decrease in breast satisfaction was observed among the breast cancer lumpectomy patients undergoing pFGS intraoperative margin assessment despite additional tissue removal. Most of the patients valued avoiding a second surgery over maximizing cosmetic outcome.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20452-3.abstract: Lower socioeconomic status conveys a known survival disadvantage for patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). The potential role of the treating center volume in mitigating this disparity has not been described to date. Non-metastatic EAC patients were identified (NCDB 2012-2021). High- and low-risk zip code groups were derived from income and education quartiles. Center volume was delineated as "low" or "high," with an annual threshold of ≥ 10 esophagectomies. Standard chi-square modeling, multivariable Cox hazard regression models, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were used where appropriate. Of 7462 EAC patients, 38.2% (n = 2849) resided in high-risk zip code areas, and 87.1% were treated at low-volume centers. Clinical (p = 0.230) and pathologic (p = 0.992) staging distribution did not differ across zip codes. High-volume centers saw a slightly increased proportion of advanced disease (p = 0.001). Patients at high-volume centers experienced better survival (5-year overall survival [5yOS], 44.97%) than their low-volume counterparts (5yOS, 40.62%) (p < 0.001). Patients residing in high-risk zip code areas demonstrated worse 5yOS than their low-risk counterparts (38.20% vs 43.74%; p < 0.001). Evaluation of low-volume centers showed that the high-risk zip code group had shorter survival than their low-risk counterparts (36.80% vs 43.21%; p < 0.001). Interestingly, in high-volume centers, survival across zip code groups was notably comparable (45.69% vs 46.20%; p = 0.80). Center expertise may offer an avenue for mitigating sociodemographic survival disparities in esophageal cancer. As discussions regarding centralized oncologic care continue, particular attention should be paid to the impact of high-volume center referral on the treatment of patients with social risk factors.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20523-5.abstract: Abstract Background The current study aimed to assess oncologic safety with 24-month groin recurrence rates after the exclusive use of indocyanine green (ICG) for sentinel node (SLN) detection in early-stage, node-negative vulvar cancer. Methods This retrospective cohort study descriptively assessed consecutive patients with early (T1/2 < 4 cm) squamous vulvar cancer who underwent exclusive ICG-based inguinal sentinel node-mapping without radioactive tracer or blue dye. Results Data of 49 patients encompassing 94 groins at risk were available for analysis. The SLN detection rate was 90.4% (85/94) per groin. In nine (9.6%) groins, ICG failed to identify the SLN. These patients subsequently underwent lateralized systematic lymphadenectomy. Among patients with unifocal disease and a negative SLN (63 groins at risk in 33 patients), the 24-month groin recurrence rate was 1.6% (one unilateral recurrence) per groin. Conclusion Exclusive ICG-guided SLN-mapping demonstrated a low groin recurrence rate in early-stage node-negative vulvar cancer. The study results are within the range previously reported by the GROINSS-V study after a combined radioactive tracer and blue dye approach. These findings suggest that exclusive ICG-guided SLN-mapping is feasible and may provide oncologic outcomes comparable with those reported for conventional SLN-mapping in carefully selected patients with early-stage vulvar cancer treated at a tertiary care center.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20614-3.abstract: Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a challenging clinical problem requiring teams to balance complex oncologic disease, limited treatment options, and patient prognosis and values as they approach end of life. Presently, there is limited high-quality evidence to guide decision-making for MBO patients. A multidisciplinary modified Delphi process was undertaken to create guidance and support clinical decision-making in the medical and surgical care of this patient population. Multidisciplinary experts from all specialties regularly caring for MBO in Canada and the United States were invited for participation, including Acute Care Surgery, Surgical Oncology, Gynecologic Oncology, Gastroenterology, Radiology, Medical Oncology, and Palliative Care. Statements were evaluated through two rounds of surveys and a consensus meeting, with an a priori threshold of 80% agreement for approval. Forty-nine final evidence-informed statements were included following expert consensus review pertaining to Patient Assessment, Medical Management, Surgical Management, and Palliative Management, in addition to a unifying definition of MBO. Consensus statements address aspects of complex MBO care, including but not limited to, optimal preoperative evaluation and multidisciplinary review; timing and use of steroids, motility, and antisecretory agents; contraindications to surgery; key facets of consent and perioperative decision making; framework for the nuanced use of gastrostomies and IV fluids in the end-of-life setting. This Modified Delphi consensus provides multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the care of patients with this challenging problem. These expert approved statements provide much-needed clinical guidance to support best care balanced with patient values and avoidance of undue harm.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20615-2.abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative identification of high-grade dysplasia (HGD) or malignancy in intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) remains challenging using conventional guideline-based imaging criteria. Quantitative computed tomography (CT)-based features may detect subtle structural changes preceding overt radiologic findings. This study aimed to evaluate whether the pancreatic index (PI) and additional three-dimensional CT-derived quantitative features improve prediction of HGD or malignancy in IPMNs. Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients who underwent surgical resection for pathologically confirmed IPMNs between January 2001 and August 2024 and had available preoperative pancreas-protocol CT. Three-dimensional quantitative parameters were analyzed. Results Among 333 patients, 204 had low-grade dysplasia (LGD), 56 had HGD, and 73 had malignancy. PI decreased with increasing histologic grade (75.6 ± 10.2% in LGD, 74.5 ± 12.0% in HGD, 70.5 ± 12.6% in malignancy; p = 0.003). Pancreatic Hounsfield unit standard deviation (HU-SD) was significantly higher in HGD and malignancy than in LGD (25.6 ± 5.9, 29.0 ± 8.7, and 29.6 ± 6.2, respectively; p < 0.001). A combined model integrating guideline-based criteria with PI, CI, cystic HU-SD, pancreatic HU-SD, and pancreatic duct volume demonstrated better discrimination than the guideline-only model (area under the curve 0.800 vs. 0.760; p = 0.007). Conclusions Quantitative CT-derived imaging features provide incremental value for predicting HGD and malignancy when integrated with conventional guideline-based criteria. These noninvasive imaging biomarkers may enhance risk stratification and provide additional information to support clinical decision-making when integrated with conventional criteria. Further external validation is required to establish their clinical utility in routine practice.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20632-1.abstract: In the PRADO trial, a multicenter phase II study, patients with macroscopic stage III melanoma received neoadjuvant ipilimumab and nivolumab followed by resection of the marked index lymph node (ILN). Patients without a major pathological response (MPR) underwent therapeutic lymph node dissection (TLND), although some required TLND for other indications. We investigated whether baseline clinicopathological and preoperative response parameters identify patients benefiting from immediate TLND rather than ILN resection followed by potential secondary TLND. Data were collected from PRADO case report forms. Group differences were assessed using Fisher's exact, chi-square, or Mann-Whitney U tests. Logistic regression identified predictors of TLND, with a subgroup analysis restricted to pathology-positive TLND. Model performance was assessed using (cross-validated) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Ninety-nine patients were included; 36 underwent TLND: 20 (56%) with pathological nonresponse, eight (22%) with partial response, and eight (22%) for other indications (nodal recurrence after MPR, n = 3; extranodal extension, n = 1; suspicious nodes on imaging, n = 2; or infeasible ILN resection due to immune-related adverse events, n = 2). Age < 40 years (odds ratio 7.91, 95% confidence interval 1.35-46.30; P = 0.022) and radiographic increase in tumor size (odds ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.24; P < 0.001) were associated with TLND. Age younger than 40 years and unfavorable radiological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy were associated with TLND, suggesting these parameters may identify patients at risk of residual nodal disease and subsequent need for TLND.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20639-8.abstract: Primary breast angiosarcoma (PBA) is rare, and limited data exist because studies often combine primary and secondary angiosarcoma patients. For patients with PBA who received care at a comprehensive cancer center from 1991 to 2025 and underwent surgical resection, this retrospective study collected and analyzed clinicopathologic features, treatment patterns, and survival data. Among 176 patients, 138 met the inclusion criteria. The median age was 40 years (interquartile range [IQR], 32-49 years). Most of the tumors were high grade with a median size of 6.5 cm. Most of the patients underwent mastectomy (88%). Among the 50 patients (36%) who underwent axillary surgery, only 6 patients had nodal metastases. Multimodal treatment was performed for 121 patients (88%), including chemotherapy/surgery (n = 46, 38%), radiation therapy (RT)/surgery ( = 15, 12%), and chemotherapy/RT/surgery (n = 60, 50%). The median follow-up time was 3.7 years. The median overall survival (OS) was 6 years (IQR, 3.5-8.7 years), and the 5-year OS was 58%. Recurrence was experienced by 62% of the patients, with a median recurrence-free survival (RFS) of 3 years (IQR, 1.4-7.7 years). Most of the recurrences were distant (79%), with 14% of the patients experiencing local recurrence only. Tumor size larger than 5 cm and high-grade histology were independently associated with lower OS. When stratified by treatment modality, there was no statistical difference in OS (p = 0.475). Primary breast angiosarcoma arises in women with a median age of 40 years, and large, high-grade tumors are associated with worse survival outcomes. Distant recurrence is common, whereas nodal metastases and local failure are not. Most of the patients in this study received multimodal therapy without a clear impact of modality on OS. However, further collaborative studies may be required to assess the impact of modality on disease outcomes.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20657-6.abstract: Positive margins after breast-conserving surgery (BCS) require additional surgery, a negative patient experience that also adds costs to care. Pilot trials indicate the Breast Cancer LocatorTM (BCL), a novel supine magnetic resonance imaging-based guidance system, helps surgeons resect cancers with a low positive margin rate (PMR). Our objective was to evaluate BCL noninferiority and superiority compared with wire localization (WL) in reducing the PMR with BCS. Patients with nonpalpable, magnetic resonance imaging-visualized invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ undergoing BCS were prospectively randomized to either BCL or WL. In total, 418 randomized patients underwent surgery. The PMR was 14.4% (30/209) in the BCL group and 21.1% (44/209) in the WL group, a relative decrease of 32%. In primary analysis, the treatment difference was -7.1% (95.4% confidence interval [CI] -14.3 to 0.1). Noninferiority was demonstrated (p = 0.011). The one-sided p-value for superiority (p = 0.025) slightly exceeded the prespecified significance level of 0.023. In prespecified analysis stratified by final tumor type, the PMR was significantly lower in the BCL group (p = 0.019). Fewer BCL patients underwent re-excision: 12.9% versus 19.6%, a relative decrease of 34%. The PMR for all tumor types was lower in the BCL group, with a > 60% relative reduction in PMR in patients with ductal carcinoma in situ (20.6% vs. 53.3% [95% CI -52.1 to -9.1]) and invasive lobular carcinoma (9.1% vs. 25.6% [95% CI -32.9 to -0.2]). Adverse event rates were similar. BCL was noninferior to WL and superior in analysis stratified by final tumor type. Clinically meaningful relative reductions in PMR and re-excision rates were observed.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20684-3.abstract: Main duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (MD-IPMN) carries a substantial risk of malignant transformation and often requires surgical resection.1,2 Preservation of the remnant pancreas remains an important goal, particularly in elderly patients.3,4 Therefore, determining the optimal extent of resection requires a careful balance between oncological safety and preservation of pancreatic function.5,6 The utility of intraoperative pancreatoscopy during robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) for this purpose has not been well established.7 METHODS: We present two elderly patients with MD-IPMN who underwent RPD combined with intraoperative pancreatoscopy. After pancreatic transection, a Spyglass was introduced through a robotic port #1 and advanced into the remnant pancreatic duct under robotic guidance. The main pancreatic duct and branch ducts were systematically inspected for findings suspicious for high-grade dysplasia or skip lesions.8 Frozen-section analysis of the pancreatic margin was performed in both cases. The patients were in their 70s with pancreatic head IPMN and pancreatic duct dilation. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy demonstrated no suspicious lesions within the remnant pancreas. Frozen-section analysis confirmed the absence of carcinoma or high-grade dysplasia at the pancreatic margin. Based on these findings, no additional pancreatic resection was required, and the remnant pancreas was preserved in both patients. Final pathology revealed mixed-type IPMN with high-grade dysplasia and no invasive carcinoma in both cases. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy can be safely integrated into RPD and serves as an adjunct to preoperative imaging, potentially facilitating targeted biopsy. This approach may support preservation of the remnant pancreas in elderly patients with MD-IPMN.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20685-2.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have limited efficacy in estrogen receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER+/HER2-) breast cancer, and the mechanisms underlying immune resistance remain unclear. The androgen receptor gene (AR), expressed in a substantial proportion of ER-positive tumors, has been implicated in tumor biology; however, its role in the tumor immune microenvironment and immunotherapy response is not well understood. We investigated the association between AR expression, transcriptome-derived immune cell-associated signatures, and response to ICIs in 4046 patients with breast cancer across five cohorts with bulk transcriptomic data and two cohorts with single-cell transcriptomic data. High AR expression was consistently associated with reduced transcriptome-derived tumor-infiltrating leukocyte scores across multiple ER+/HER2- cohorts. Specifically, signatures associated with cluster of differentiation (CD)-8+ T-cell subsets, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages were significantly reduced in AR-high tumors, indicating a transcriptionally immune-suppressed tumor microenvironment. In the I-SPY2 cohort, AR-high tumors demonstrated significantly lower pathological complete response rates after neoadjuvant ICI therapy. Furthermore, AR expression showed a predictive performance for ICI response that was superior to that with programmed cell death protein-1 and programmed cell death ligand-1 (area under the curve 0.82 vs. 0.73 and 0.60, respectively). Interestingly, single-cell analysis revealed that AR expression across multiple cell types, including epithelial, endothelial, and myeloid, was associated with reduced ICI responsiveness. Additionally, AR inhibition using enzalutamide was associated with increased signatures associated with CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages. These findings suggest that AR expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and reduced response to ICIs in ER+/HER2- breast cancer.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20687-0.abstract: Abstract Background Early delayed gastric conduit emptying (DGCE) and pneumonia are among the most common complications following oesophagectomy. These issues can be challenging to address during minimally invasive surgery with pyloroplasty or pyloromyotomy. This study evaluated the impact of prophylactic endoscopic pyloric balloon dilatation (PBD) on early postoperative outcomes. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing oesophagectomy with gastric conduit reconstruction for cancer at two Australian tertiary centres (2017–2025) were retrospectively analysed. From 2023, intraoperative endoscopic-assisted PBD using a 20 mm balloon inflated for two minutes across the pylorus was adopted as standard practice. Primary endpoints were early DGCE and hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) within 30 days; secondary endpoints included nasogastric tube (NGT) output and duration, and hospital length-of-stay. Associations were examined using multivariable logistic regression and inverse-probability-weighted regression adjustment (IPWRA). Results Of 187 patients, 40 (21.4%) received PBD. Compared with controls, PBD was associated with reduced DGCE (15% vs. 40.1%; odds ratio [OR] 0.26, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.11–0.65) and HAP (20% vs. 40.8%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.17–0.80). Pyloric balloon dilatation independently predicted lower DGCE (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.12–0.91) and HAP (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.05–0.67), with absolute risk reductions of 27.4% and 30.8% respectively on IPWRA analysis. Pyloric balloon dilatation was also associated with lower postoperative NGT outputs, earlier NGT removal (median 6 [interquartile range (IQR) 4-11] vs. 4 [IQR 3–7] days; p = 0.032), and shorter hospital length of stay (median 13 [IQR 9–22] vs. 9 [IQR 8–16] days; p = 0.007). Conclusions Prophylactic PBD was associated with lower early DGCE and pneumonia. This enabled earlier nasogastric tube removal and shorter hospital stay, supporting its integration into contemporary practice.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20690-5.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with an increasing burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-associated HCC in Western populations. In treating HCC, recurrence after curative-intent therapy remains common, creating a compelling rationale for perioperative systemic therapy. This Landmark Series review examines the pivotal studies that have shaped the surgical and perioperative management of HCC, tracing the evolution from principles of resectability to contemporary adjuvant and neoadjuvant immune-based strategies. The development of perioperative therapy has been defined by both landmark negative trials and emerging evidence of efficacy. The STORM trial demonstrated that sorafenib's activity in advanced HCC did not translate into benefit after resection or ablation. The IMbrave050 trial subsequently demonstrated an early recurrence-free survival advantage with adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab that was not sustained with longer follow-up evaluation, whereas the KEYNOTE-937 trial failed to demonstrate benefit with adjuvant pembrolizumab. In contrast, early-phase neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor-based studies have demonstrated feasibility and meaningful pathologic responses, and the CARES-009 trial provided the first randomized phase III evidence of improved event-free survival with a perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-antiangiogenic strategy. Perioperative management of HCC is evolving toward an integrated, multidisciplinary treatment paradigm. Although no broadly applicable adjuvant systemic therapy has been established, emerging perioperative strategies provide proof of concept that systemic therapy may improve outcomes for selected patients. Future progress will depend on biomarker-driven patient selection, molecular residual disease assessment, standardized pathologic response criteria, and clinical trials identifying which patients require perioperative therapy and when treatment should be delivered.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20700-6.abstract: Cancer patients undergoing surgery are at significantly increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Although extended thromboprophylaxis is recommended, the optimal anticoagulant type and duration remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of different extended thromboprophylaxis in this population. A Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed to evaluate various thromboprophylaxis strategies for patients undergoing cancer-related surgery. We conducted both three-node and five-node network analyses to evaluate extended-duration versus standard-duration thromboprophylaxis strategies. Outcomes included venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. Net clinical benefit and risk-benefit assessments were additionally performed to determine the overall impact of prolonged anticoagulant therapy. Treatment effects were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs). A total of 14 randomized controlled trials involving 4,331 participants were included. Compared with placebo, extended-duration prophylaxis with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) (RR 0.12, 95% CrI 0.05-0.27) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) (RR 0.17, 95% CrI 0.05-0.55) significantly reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism without a corresponding increase in major bleeding. In net clinical benefit analyses, both prolonged DOAC therapy (RR 0.27, 95% CrI 0.14-0.49) and LMWH (RR 0.36, 95% CrI 0.17-0.76) demonstrated favorable overall outcomes. Risk-benefit evaluation suggested that prolonged DOACs provided a more advantageous balance than LMWH, with an NNH/NNT ratio of 4.17. Extended thromboprophylaxis is effective and safe for cancer patients undergoing surgery. Besides, DOACs appears to be the optimal anticoagulant for extended thromboprophylaxis, providing the greatest net clinical benefit.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20702-4.abstract: Cancer surgical research is essential to discover newer treatment options, enhance survival, improve quality of care, and more importantly, impede the rising global cancer burden. The inability to conduct cancer surgical research can have detrimental health and economic effects at the individual and societal levels. It is well known that there are several barriers to conducting cancer surgical research, and these barriers are exacerbated in low-resource settings. The second Lancet Oncology Commission on Global Cancer Surgery Action on research helps to address these barriers and outline strategies that promote cancer surgical research on the global stage. This study used the principles of Implementation Science taken from the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to help develop the content and increase the likelihood of success in implementing the recommendations in this Action. The Annals of Surgical Oncology Series on the second Lancet Oncology Commission on Global Cancer Surgery hopes to enhance the visibility of the eight critical Actions within this important Commission to the primary stakeholders, the surgeons. The authors hope this Action on research will help to address these barriers and implement resource-stratified solutions to build individual, institutional, and system-wide capacity for cancer surgical research. These efforts should lead to the development of a robust cancer surgical research infrastructure that will eventually translate to improved patient and population outcomes.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20710-4.abstract: Our objective was to investigate the prognostic utility of combined carbohydrate antigen (CA) 19-9 and Duke pancreatic monoclonal antigen type 2 (DUPAN-2) levels in patients undergoing curative-intent surgery for initially unresectable locally advanced (URLA) pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Data from patients who underwent curative-intent surgery for URLA PDAC from June 2010 to December 2024 were investigated. Eligible patients were grouped into normal/normal (N/N), normal/high (N/H), high/normal (H/N), and high/high (H/H) groups according to CA19-9 and DUPAN-2 levels. Grouping was performed before and after preoperative induction chemotherapy, and survival was compared among the groups. In total, 39 patients were included. Before preoperative chemotherapy, the N/N, N/H, H/N, and H/H groups accounted for 10.3%, 20.5%, 30.8%, and 38.5%, respectively; the H/H group was the largest. After chemotherapy, the four groups accounted for 48.7%, 15.4%, 25.6%, and 10.3%, respectively; the N/N group was the largest. Pre-chemotherapy 5-year overall survival rates were 75.0%, 31.3%, 0%, and 44.9%, respectively (p = 0.427). Among the post-chemotherapy groups, the corresponding rates were 44.3%, 16.7%, 44.4%, and 0%, respectively (p < 0.001); the H/H group had significantly lower survival than the other groups. Multivariate analysis identified the post-chemotherapy H/H group as an independent predictor of poor survival (p = 0.004). Patient grouping using the two markers after preoperative chemotherapy was associated with overall survival and may be useful for prognostic stratification. In patients being considered for curative-intent surgery, the post-chemotherapy H/H group may warrant careful attention.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20711-3.abstract: Neoadjuvant therapy can improve the survival outcomes of patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer (BRPC). However, standard neoadjuvant regimens remain lacking. This study evaluated the clinical feasibility of tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant setting for BRPC. In this prospective study, patients with BRPC preoperatively received three cycles of tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, and continued postoperatively. The primary endpoints were R0 resection rate and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Exploratory objectives were resistance to this regimen. Of 30 enrolled patients, 80.0% (24/30) completed neoadjuvant therapy and underwent surgical resection. R0 resection was achieved in 80.0% (24/30) of the patients and in 100.00% (24/24) of those resected. The 12-month OS and RFS rates were 87.5% (95% CI 64.3-95.8%) and 82.8% (95% CI 60-95.8%), respectively, with median RFS of 28 months (95% CI 16.9-39.1). Most TRAEs were grade I-II, with no serious events. Quantitative proteomics combined with machine learning identified NT5DC2, FAM3D, CXCL5, and TMT1B as candidate biomarkers of resistance to this neoadjuvant regimen. In paired pre- and postoperative tissues from treatment-sensitive patients, CD8+ T-cell infiltration tended to increase and CD163+ M2-like macrophages were significantly upregulated after surgery. Neoadjuvant tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel is promising for improving the resection rate in BRPC, with a favorable safety profile. NT5DC2, FAM3D, CXCL5, and TMT1B may serve as candidate biomarkers of preoperative drug resistance, and tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) analysis further reveals immune microenvironment remodeling in postoperative tumors from treatment-sensitive patients. These findings warrant validation in larger-scale studies. Trial Registration Chinese Clinical Trial registry (ChiCTR2200063680).

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20713-1.abstract: Metaplastic breast carcinoma (MpBC) is a rare and aggressive subtype of breast cancer, often characterized by triple-negative (TN) receptor status and a limited response to standard chemotherapy. The optimal treatment strategy remains undefined. This study evaluates overall survival (OS) in patients with TN-MpBC treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) or neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy (NACIO) compared with upfront surgery using the National Cancer Database. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using the National Cancer Database to identify patients diagnosed with stage I-III TN-MpBC between 2010 and 2022 and treated with NAC, NACIO, or upfront surgery. Primary endpoints included OS, pathologic complete response (pCR), and breast conservation rates. Continuous variables were analyzed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and categorical variables were assessed with the chi-squared or Fisher's exact test. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Breast conservation and pCR were analyzed using logistic regression, and OS was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model. Of 4953 patients, 3429 (69.2%) underwent upfront surgery, 1232 (24.9%) received NAC, and 292 (5.8%) received NACIO. No significant difference in OS was observed between NACIO and surgery-first approaches (hazard ratio [HR] 0.80; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-1.27; p = 0.3), but NAC was associated with a 37% increased risk of mortality compared with upfront surgery (HR 1.37; 95% CI 1.21-1.56; p < 0.001). NACIO was associated with a 62% higher likelihood of achieving pCR than was NAC (odds ratio [OR] 1.62; 95% CI 1.11-2.38; p = 0.013). The rate of breast conservation was not significantly different between NACIO and upfront surgery (OR 0.8; 95% CI 0.61-1.05; p = 0.11), but patients receiving NAC were 27% less likely to undergo breast-conserving surgery than were those undergoing upfront surgery (OR 0.73; 95% CI 0.63-0.84; p < 0.001). Stage significantly modified the association between treatment strategy and breast conservation (pooled Wald test, p = 0.022). In patients with TN-MpBC, NACIO demonstrated survival outcomes comparable to those with upfront surgery and improved pCR rates compared with NAC. These findings suggest that integrating immunotherapy into neoadjuvant treatment may offer clinical benefit, warranting further prospective investigation. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the baseline stage differences between the treatment groups and the potential for residual confounding inherent to retrospective database studies.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20718-w.abstract: Prefoldin subunit 2 (PFDN2), a component of the prefoldin complex, has been implicated in tumor progression and in cytoskeleton-related progression; however, its clinical relevance and biological role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study investigated the clinicopathological relevance and functional role of PFDN2 in HCC. Protein expression of prefoldin subunits (PFDN1-6) was examined in 265 HCC specimens using tissue microarrays. Associations with clinicopathological features and survival outcomes were analyzed. Functional roles of PFDN2 were assessed using Huh7 cells overexpressing PFDN2 (PFDN2-OE) and HLF cells with PFDN2 knockdown (PFDN2-KD). Migration, invasion, and proliferation assays were conducted, along with western blot analyses of Rac1-associated signaling and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress markers. Elevated PFDN2 expression was significantly associated with poor tumor differentiation and vascular invasion. Patients with high PFDN2 expression had worse overall and recurrence-free survival (p = 0.0257 and p = 0.0255, respectively). In vitro, PFDN2-OE enhanced migratory capacity and lamellipodia formation, accompanied by upregulation of Rac1, phosphorylated Rac1, Tiam1, and ARHGAP1. PFDN2-KD suppressed proliferation and increased ER stress markers, including PERK, phosphorylated PERK, and CHOP. PFDN2 overexpression is associated with aggressive tumor features and poor prognosis in HCC. PFDN2 promotes migratory activity through Rac1-associated signaling and may support cellular proliferation. These findings suggest that PFDN2 may serve as a molecular indicator of aggressive tumor behavior and potentially contribute to postoperative risk stratification.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20719-9.abstract: Time to surgery (TTS) for breast cancer has been increasing for decades, with delays associated with worse survival. A 2022 Commission on Cancer (CoC) quality measure requires upfront surgery within 60 days after diagnosis (BCSdx). The long-term effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on TTS and compliance with BCSdx are unknown. Using the National Cancer Database, the study identified 520,967 women with a diagnosis of clinical stages I to III invasive breast cancer from 2014 to 2023 who underwent upfront surgery. Time to surgery was defined as days from diagnosis to definitive surgery. Diagnosis year was modeled continuously and categorically (pre-pandemic 2014-2019, pandemic onset 2020, post-pandemic onset 2021-2023). Linear and logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with TTS and odds of not having surgery in ≤ 60 days. Between 2014 and 2023, the mean TTS increased from 37 to 50 days (+ 13 days). Compared with 2014-2019, the 2021-2023 period was associated with + 7.51 mean days (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.35-7.67 days) and 1.90 times (95% CI, 1.87-1.94 times) increased odds of not meeting BCSdx in the multivariable analysis. Longer TTS also was associated with immediate reconstruction (β = + 8.27 days), uninsured status (β = + 7.99 days), and diagnosis at another facility (β = + 6.55 days). The proportion of patients with a TTS of ≤ 60 days declined from 88% to 74%. The strongest predictors of noncompliance were uninsured status (odds ratio [OR], 2.10), diagnosis at another facility (OR, 1.81), immediate reconstruction (OR, 1.81), black race (OR, 1.72), and Hispanic ethnicity (OR, 1.70). The increase in TTS for breast cancer accelerated after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, with a concomitant decrease in BCSdx compliance. Strategies to improve care coordination, particularly for at-risk populations, are needed to address this quality measure.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20724-y.abstract: Reduced-port surgery has been developed to minimize abdominal wall trauma while maintaining the benefits of minimally invasive surgery. However, reduced-port robotic rectal surgery remains technically challenging due to interference of external arms. The modular design of the Hugo RAS system (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) provides greater flexibility in arm positioning to minimize external arm interference without compromising instrument maneuverability1-4. In abdominoperineal resection (APR), the incision for a permanent colostomy is inevitable. We report the first case of completely robot-assisted APR performed using the Hugo RAS system through a planned stoma site. Three robotic trocars were inserted through the planned left lower-quadrant stoma site, and one arm through the right lower quadrant. We call this approach SIPORS, Single-Incision Plus One Robot-assisted Surgery. The procedure is presented in the accompanying video. As the first case, a 50-year-old woman with rectal cancer underwent APR after systemic chemotherapy. The console time was 167 min. The procedure was completed without significant robotic arm interference. The postoperative course was uneventful except for transient cystitis. The circumferential and distal resection margins were 3 and 35 mm, respectively. The mesorectal specimen was complete, 25 lymph nodes were harvested, and the pathological stage was pT3N2bM1. SIPORS using the Hugo RAS at a planned stoma site was technically feasible and achieved an oncologically acceptable resection in this patient. It may offer improved cosmesis, reduced postoperative pain, fewer wound complications, and a lower risk of trocar-site incisional hernia. Further experience is needed to confirm its reproducibility and clinical benefits.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20727-9.abstract: Abstract Background The acute inpatient symptom state following oesophagectomy is multidimensional and heterogeneous. However, the structure, between-patient heterogeneity, and network features of symptoms remain incompletely characterised. Method We analysed 1047 postoperative patients with oesophageal cancer from four hospitals in Anhui Province, China, in the “Be Resilient to Oesophageal Cancer” program. We applied principal component analysis to summarise symptom dimensions and latent profile analysis to derive patient groups of symptom burden. Symptom networks were estimated and centrality computed to identify candidate targets. We then performed in silico node-perturbation simulations to estimate potential system-level effects of alleviating versus aggravating individual symptoms. Results Four symptom dimensions emerged from the principal component analysis: somatic discomfort and fatigue, psychological distress, social functioning impairment, and gastrointestinal/appetite-related symptoms. A low-burden group (80.2%) and a high-burden group (19.8%) were identified. The overall network’s most central symptom was “reduced social interaction” ( r = 2.52). Within groups, “worry” was most central in the low-burden group ( r = 2.08), whereas “incision pain” was most central in the high-burden group (r=2.56). Computer simulations revealed that, within alleviating interventions, somatic symptoms accounted for the highest proportion across all symptom types (incision pain: −20.68% to −9.17%). Conversely, within aggravating interventions, psychosocial symptoms constituted the largest share in both the overall symptom network and the low-burden group (helplessness: 24.13% to 30.27%), whereas somatic symptoms dominated the high-burden group (incision pain: 9.17%). Conclusion A multimethod pipeline identified reduced social interaction, worry, and incision pain as profile-specific, structurally prominent symptoms within the postoperative day 3 symptom networks. These findings highlight distinct psychosocial and somatic features across symptom-burden profiles and provide hypotheses for subsequent longitudinal and interventional studies.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20728-8.abstract: Staging laparoscopy (SL) is a minimally invasive approach for detecting occult metastases in patients with pancreatic cancer (PC) without signs of metastasis on imaging. This study aimed to identify the predictive factors for imaging-negative occult metastases. This prospective study enrolled 199 patients with histologically confirmed PC from three institutions between August 2021 and April 2023. All patients were scheduled for a treatment plan that included SL. The overall metastasis rate as detected using SL was 25.1%, which varied from 20.6% in patients with resectable PC (R-PC) to 33.8% in those with borderline resectable or locally advanced unresectable PC (BR/URLA-PC). In 152 patients who did not receive neoadjuvant therapy, BR/URLA status (odds ratio 3.261; 95% confidence interval 1.185-9.483, p = 0.022) and pancreatic body/tail lesions (odds ratio 2.653; 95% confidence interval 1.037-7.214, p = 0.042) were independent risk factors for occult metastatic lesions (M1). Among the 107 patients with R-PC, M1 disease was significantly associated with pancreatic body/tail lesions, tumor size, and elevated levels of tumor markers. In particular, elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels were consistent across all patients with M1 pancreatic head cancer. In contrast, no statistical differences were observed for any of these factors in the 45 patients with BR/URLA-PC. Our findings support the importance of SL in patients with BR/UR PC. For R-PC, patients with pancreatic head lesions and normal tumor marker values may represent a very low-risk subgroup where selective omission of SL can be considered in resource-constrained settings.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20729-7.abstract: Data on robot-assisted minimally invasive esophagectomy (RAMIE) after neoadjuvant therapy, particularly after neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy, remain scarce. This study compares the perioperative outcomes of RAMIE versus conventional minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) in patients with resectable esophageal cancer after neoadjuvant therapy. We conducted a dual-center, retrospective study of consecutive patients with esophageal cancer who underwent MIE after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy or neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy between 2020 and 2025. Propensity score matching was applied based on preoperative variables. Perioperative outcomes were analyzed. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 137 patients were allocated to each group. The RAMIE group demonstrated a higher rate of left recurrent laryngeal nerve lymph node dissection (67.9% vs. 53.3%, p = 0.02) and yielded more lymph nodes in this station after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (mean 1.6 vs. 1.0, p = 0.02). However, RAMIE was associated with a higher overall incidence of postoperative complications (38.0% vs. 24.8%, p = 0.03). No significant differences were observed in operation time, pathological complete response rate, severe complications, length of stay, 30-day readmission, or 90-day mortality. In expert hands, RAMIE achieves perioperative safety comparable to that with MIE after neoadjuvant therapy and offers a superior ability to dissect critical lymph node stations. This technical advantage establishes RAMIE as a viable and promising surgical option, warranting further prospective investigation in randomized trials.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20731-z.abstract: Cryoablation is emerging as a potential treatment option for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC). The aim of this study was to retrospectively evaluate the safety and efficacy of cryoablation in patients with LAPC. The study has been prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ID: ChiCTR2300068376). Adult patients with LAPC were stratified based on the treatment modality (cryoablation versus systemic therapy). The cryoablation was performed using a single cryoprobe under ultrasound guidance. The Kaplan-Meier method was utilized to evaluate and compare overall survival (OS) among the groups. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was employed to identify independent predictors of overall survival. Of 186 enrolled patients with LAPC between August 2022 and December 2024, 142 were in the cryoablation group and 44 in the systemic therapy alone group. The median OS was 17.8 months with systemic therapy alone and 18.7 months with cryoablation alone. Combined cryoablation and systemic therapy yielded a median OS of 22.1 months. Among patients receiving cryoablation combined with chemotherapy median OS was 19.8 months, and for combination systemic therapy group (chemotherapy + immunotherapy ± targeted therapy), it was 25.4 months. Multivariate analysis identified age, tumor location, treatment type, and jaundice as independent OS predictors. Additionally, nearly all patients experienced marked pain relief after cryoablation treatment. When combined with systemic therapy, cryoablation has a more significant survival advantage than systemic therapy alone. However, due to the heterogeneity of the cohort and potential immortal time bias, these survival outcomes should be interpreted with caution. Additionally, cryoablation offers effective benefits for relieving cancer pain and preserving functional quality of life in patients with LAPC.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20734-w.abstract: Ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI) during liver transplantation is associated with recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Machine perfusion (MP) is associated with a decreased risk of IRI complications. Our study evaluated the role of MP in post-transplant oncologic outcomes in patients with HCC. Adults with HCC transplanted between 2015-2025 from the United Network for Organ Sharing database were divided into MP and no-MP groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) was also performed. Post-transplant HCC recurrence (competing risk) and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Subgroup analysis was performed in populations within and beyond the Milan criteria. A total of 19,466 patients were included in this study. MP was used in 1,392 (7.2%). The MP group had shorter waitlist times, older donors, and more frequent DCDs (p=0.001). After PSM, 512 patients were included in each group (336 patients within Milan criteria in each). In the population beyond Milan after PSM (n=352), MP use was associated with a reduced risk of 1-year and 3-year HCC recurrence (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.09, p=0.02; aHR 0.27, p=0.02). MP use was not associated with the 1-year or 3-year OS (aHR 1.34, p=0.64; aHR 1.32, p=0.54). MP may potentially reduce the risk of HCC recurrence in recipients beyond Milan criteria, without significant difference in OS. However, as MP utilization increases, further validation into the role of MP and oncologic outcomes in larger cohort studies are required.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20735-9.abstract: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor (NET) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs (SBNET) and pancreatic NETs (PNETs). A retrospective single-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging. The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 (63.3%) SBNET patients (158 somatostatin receptor [SSTR] positron emission tomography [PET] and 90 Octreoscan) and 113 (54.3%) PNET patients (47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan). There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2.5% yearly increase (p < 0.01) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study (p = 0.82). At presentation, 82.3% (204/248) of the SBNET patients and 54.9% (62/113) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases. Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra-operative planning, and further management.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20736-8.abstract: Reliable biomarkers for predicting tumor aggressiveness and pathological upstaging in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remain limited. DR-70, a biomarker reflecting circulating fibrin and fibrin degradation products, has been associated with tumor progression in several malignancies. This study aimed to investigate the association between preoperative serum DR-70 levels and pathological stage and nuclear grade in patients with localized RCC. This prospective single-center study included 69 patients who underwent partial or radical nephrectomy for localized RCC. Tumors were staged according to the TNM classification and graded using the World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology system. Preoperative serum DR-70 levels were measured, and their associations with clinical stage, pathological stage, and nuclear grade were evaluated. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of pathological upstaging (≥ pT3). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to assess the predictive performance of DR-70. The median serum DR-70 level was 0.84 U/mL. DR-70 levels were significantly higher in high-grade tumors than in low-grade tumors (1.32 vs. 0.78 U/mL, p = 0.001). No significant association was observed between DR-70 levels and clinical stage (p = 0.53), whereas a significant association was found with pathological stage (p = 0.023). Multivariate analysis identified serum DR-70 as an independent predictor of pathological upstaging (≥ pT3) (odds ratio 1.40; 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.81; p = 0.008). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated good predictive performance for high-grade disease (area under the curve 0.823) and pathological upstaging (area under the curve 0.774), with an optimal cutoff value of 1.02 U/mL. Serum DR-70 was associated with tumor aggressiveness and independently predicted pathological upstaging in patients with localized RCC. These findings suggest that DR-70 may serve as a complementary biomarker for preoperative risk stratification and may help identify patients at increased risk of aggressive pathological features. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20764-4.abstract: Laparoscopic extended right posterior sectionectomy (eRPS), including the dorsal segment of the right anterior section (RAS), is a technically demanding but parenchyma-preserving alternative to right hepatectomy. Its success depends on accurate identification of the anatomically variable intersegmental plane. This study describes a tailored Glissonean approach according to the presence or absence of the anterior fissure vein (AFV). Between December 2020 and July 2023, six consecutive patients underwent laparoscopic eRPS including the dorsal RAS. Preoperative three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction was used to evaluate the right anterior Glissonean pedicle (RAG) branching pattern and presence of a definite AFV. When an AFV was identified, an AFV-guided transfissural approach was used; when absent, an intrahepatic Glissonean approach using the RAG as an intraparenchymal landmark was performed. Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence confirmed the ischemic boundary after target pedicle ligation. Median operative duration was 260 min and median blood loss was 175 mL, with no transfusions. A definite AFV was identified in five of six patients (83.3%). Median tumor size was 31 mm (range 15-52 mm), and all cases achieved R0 resection. Median hospital stay was 6.5 days (range 5-21 days). One patient (16.7%) experienced postoperative ileus, with no perioperative mortality. A tailored Glissonean approach guided by preoperative 3D reconstruction and complemented by ICG fluorescence provides a practical framework for laparoscopic eRPS. Careful case selection remains essential.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20765-3.abstract: Conventional survival analyses cannot fully account for recurrence as an intermediate event that dynamically influences subsequent mortality. Multistate models (MSMs) enable explicit modeling of transitions between clinically relevant disease states; however, their application among patients undergoing resection for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remains limited. An international multi-institutional database was queried to identify patients undergoing curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLM between 1998 and 2023. A four-state MSM was constructed comprising alive and recurrence-free, alive with recurrence, colorectal cancer (CRC)-related death, and non-CRC-related death. Transition probabilities and transition-specific prognostic factors were evaluated RESULTS: Among 3002 patients, 1624 (54.1%) developed recurrence and 911 (56.1%) died, predominantly from CRC-related causes (92.8%). The probability of recurrence decreased substantially the longer patients remained recurrence-free after surgery, whereas recurrence markedly worsened subsequent prognosis. High tumor burden score was independently associated with transition to recurrence (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06 per unit; 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.08; p < 0.001) but not post-recurrence mortality, suggesting that the adverse prognostic impact of tumor burden was mediated primarily through recurrence. Adjuvant chemotherapy reduced recurrence (HR 0.76; p = 0.005) and CRC-related death from the recurrence-free state (HR 0.39; p = 0.002). MSMs provide a dynamic framework to characterize disease evolution after CRLM resection and represent recurrence as a clinically meaningful time-dependent intermediate state rather than a simple binary endpoint. Recurrence was the dominant determinant of long-term prognosis, supporting the role of MSMs for individualized prognostication and surveillance after hepatectomy for CRLM.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20767-1.abstract: Innovation in surgical oncology is developing rapidly, and new therapies and technologies have expanded across academic centers, integrated networks, and community sites, at times outpacing the evidence, expertise, and necessary infrastructure. Although innovation is essential to our field's progress, patient safety and demonstrated efficacy must remain paramount. Adopting specialized or understudied approaches without appropriate guardrails risks patient harm and generates low-quality, confusing evidence that impedes progress for future patients with cancer. To provide structured, practical guidance on this challenge to our field, the Society of Surgical Oncology Quality Committee recommends application of the IDEAL framework for surgical innovation, which organizes the life cycle of new procedures, programs, and technologies into five stages: idea (stage 1), development (stage 2a), exploration (stage 2b), assessment (stage 3), and long-term study (stage 4). Using expert consensus, we illustrate this IDEAL-informed approach with four examples that represent the breadth of the current implementation landscape in surgical oncology: hepatic artery infusion pump chemotherapy, robotic nipple-sparing mastectomy, histotripsy, and artificial intelligence. These technologies are used as concrete illustrations of principle, not as the primary subject of this statement. The central tenant is this: before any program or technology is broadly taken to the bedside, there must be evidence to support its efficacy. The recommendations described in this report have been endorsed by the Society of Surgical Oncology.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20769-z.abstract: Tobacco smoking is prevalent among patients with rectal cancer, yet its effect on pathologic response to total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) remains unknown. This study evaluated the association between smoking status and pathologic response to TNT in locally advanced rectal cancer, using the neoadjuvant rectal (NAR) score and pathologic complete response (pCR) rate. This retrospective cohort study used the National Cancer Database to identify adults diagnosed in 2023 with clinical stage Ⅱ-Ⅲ rectal adenocarcinoma who received TNT followed by proctectomy. Smoking status at diagnosis was categorized as never, current, or former. Primary outcomes were favorable NAR score (< 8) and pCR (ypT0N0). Among 1767 patients, 49.7% were never smokers, 30.5% former, and 19.8% current smokers. Rates of favorable NAR score and pCR were highest among never smokers (33.4 and 21.7%), intermediate among former smokers (28.8 and 19.9%), and lowest among current smokers (25.5 and 16.3%). On multivariable analysis, current smoking was associated with lower odds of favorable NAR score than was never smoking (odds ratio 0.59; 95% confidence interval 0.40-0.86). A similar trend was seen for pCR, though this did not reach statistical significance (odds ratio 0.58; 95% confidence interval 0.34-1.00). Former smoking was not significantly different from never smoking in terms of a favorable NAR score or pCR. Current smoking status was independently associated with lower rates of response to TNT in locally advanced rectal cancer, whereas former smoking was not when compared with never smoking. These findings identify active tobacco exposure as a potential modifiable risk factor.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20770-6.abstract: Breast cancer patients from neighboring Hawaiian Islands face challenges including limited access to specialists and geographic isolation. Surgical delays longer than 8 weeks from diagnosis can negatively impact survival. Time from diagnosis to surgery (TTS) and predictors of delay are unknown for this population. Retrospective chart review was performed on breast cancer patients from neighboring Hawaiian Islands who underwent upfront surgery on O'ahu categorized as TTS of 8 weeks or longer. Demographic and clinical characteristics were evaluated. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical analyses. Binary logistic regression adjusted for confounding variables. The study reviewed 221 breast cancer patients (2014-2024) from neighboring Hawaiian Islands. The mean TTS was 9.4 weeks. In the univariate analysis, TTS longer than 8 weeks was associated with post-pandemic diagnosis versus during and before the pandemic (41.8 vs. 16.3 vs. 418%), preoperative diagnostic testing compared with no testing (79.6 vs. 20.4%), plastic surgery consultation compared with no consultation (51.0 vs. 49.0%,), and mastectomy compared with breast-conserving surgery (61.2 vs. 37.8%) (all p < 0.005). Multivariate analysis showed post-pandemic diagnosis (odds ratio [OR], 2.84; 95% CI, 1.15-7.00; p = 0.023), time from biopsy to consultation (OR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.13-1.56; p < 0.001), and preoperative diagnostic testing (OR, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.27-8.16; p = 0.014) as significant predictors of TTS longer than 8 weeks. Nearly half of neighboring Hawaiian Islands breast cancer patients experienced delay in surgery. Streamlining preoperative management could meaningfully shorten the time from biopsy to surgery and improve access to care and outcomes for this population.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20771-5.abstract: Cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) offers survival benefit for select patients with peritoneal surface malignancies (PSMs), yet the ethical dimensions of patient selection, informed consent, and multidisciplinary care remain underexplored. In a field still evolving, where patients with comparable profiles may exhibit vastly different prognoses, a structured ethical framework can serve as a compass for surgical decision-making. A narrative review of the literature examined the ethical considerations surrounding CRS/HIPEC for PSM. Topics include patient selection, the biological spectrum from indolent to aggressive disease, technical feasibility of complete cytoreduction, shared decision-making, surgical morbidity, palliative care integration, and special populations. The strength of evidence supporting CRS/HIPEC varies substantially by tumor biology, from near-curative outcomes in low-grade appendiceal neoplasms to marginal benefit in aggressive histologies such as sarcomatoid mesothelioma and signet ring cell carcinoma. When complete cytoreduction cannot be achieved, the procedure is unlikely to confer meaningful survival benefit and may cause significant harm. Traditional informed consent often omits the elements of informed decision-making; structured frameworks such as Best Case/Worst Case and REMAP (Reframe, Expect emotion, Map values, Align, Propose a plan) can bridge this gap. Decision regret data suggest that inadequate preoperative expectation setting contributes to patient dissatisfaction independent of surgical outcomes. Early palliative care and multidisciplinary collaboration improve prognostic understanding and alignment of treatment with patient goals. The ethical principles presented here are not rigid boundaries but flexible guides to help surgeons navigate clinical uncertainty. Although they focus on the surgical decision, they extend to every member of the multidisciplinary team caring for patients with PSM.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20772-4.abstract: To investigate the performance of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for diagnosing tumor thrombus (TT) and predicting response to pembrolizumab and axitinib in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with TT. We reviewed RCC patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT, mpMRI, and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. Diagnostic performance for detecting TT was analyzed, with TT confirmed by experienced pathologists. We further analyzed clear cell RCC (ccRCC) patients with TT who received pembrolizumab and axitinib and evaluated imaging features for predicting therapeutic efficacy by using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). Model calibration was assessed with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. A total of 166 RCC patients were initially included, of whom 56 had TT. 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT showed higher overall diagnostic performance for TT than contrast-enhanced CT and mpMRI, with incremental detection primarily observed for Mayo level 0-I TT. The sensitivity and specificity of PET/CT in diagnosing TT were 0.96 (95% CI 0.88-0.99) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.92-0.99), respectively. Then, 35 ccRCC patients with TT underwent an average of 5 cycles of pembrolizumab and axitinib, followed by surgery. Following neoadjuvant therapy, 21 patients exhibited a partial response, while 14 showed nonresponse. TT SUVmax demonstrated significant predictive value for response to neoadjuvant therapy, with an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-0.92; bootstrap-corrected, 0.79). The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated adequate calibration (P > 0.05). 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT may provide incremental value for detecting low-level TT and shows potential for predicting response to pembrolizumab plus axitinib in RCC. However, the clinical significance of detecting early TT remains uncertain.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20774-2.abstract: The optimal extent of lymph node examination in older adults undergoing curative-intent gastric adenocarcinoma treatment remains uncertain, as concerns about postoperative complications and potentially decreased benefit in overall survival may lead surgeons toward more limited dissections. Patients with stage I-III gastric adenocarcinoma who underwent gastrectomy between 2010 and 2022 were identified using the National Cancer Database. Patients were stratified by age ( 75th percentile length of stay) were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses were performed in patients aged ≥ 80 and ≥ 85 years. Among the 47,342 patients identified, 11,235 were aged ≥ 75 years. Examination of ≥ 35 lymph nodes compared with < 16 nodes was associated with improved survival in patients aged < 55 years (hazard ratio [HR] 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-0.87), 55-64 years (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.57-0.77), 65-74 years (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.58-0.76), and ≥ 75 years (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.61-0.91). This was persistent among patients who received preoperative chemotherapy and patients aged ≥ 80 years. Greater nodal yield was not associated with higher odds of adverse modified textbook short-term outcomes in any age group. Greater nodal yield was associated with improved survival and equivalent or improved short-term outcomes across all age groups, even in older patients. These findings suggest age alone should not justify limiting lymphadenectomy in resectable gastric adenocarcinoma.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20775-1.abstract: Bone and soft tissue sarcomas are heterogeneous cancers. We developed a large language model (LLM)-based extraction workflow to extract six variables from surgical pathology reports of patients with musculoskeletal sarcoma: tumor diagnosis, greatest dimension, closest margin, tumor grade, necrosis, and viability. We hypothesized that the pipeline could achieve clinically acceptable accuracy and serve as a scalable solution to augment or replace manual chart abstraction in sarcoma registry development. We retrospectively collected 1106 surgical pathology notes of patients who underwent surgical resection of bone or soft tissue sarcoma at three sites of a single institution. Notes were split into a training set (n = 353) and a testing set (n = 753). Prompt engineering and fine-tuning were used to query the open-source LLMs Llama3-70B-Instruct and Gemma4-31B-Instruct. Accuracy, F1 score, and specificity were calculated to evaluate the performance of extracted points. On the testing set, both models achieved accuracy of at least 0.85 on extracting all data points and specificity of at least 0.84 on predicting "unknown" when data were not available in the note. The Gemma model achieved higher sensitivity on detecting positive margins than the Llama model: 0.92 versus 0.78. Both LLMs took less than 1 second on average to extract each data point from each pathology note. Registry development for heterogeneous cancers such as sarcoma is limited by the labor-intensive nature of manual data abstraction, and our pipelines achieved promising results. These findings support the feasibility of LLM-based workflows as scalable and accurate alternatives to manual data abstraction for sarcoma clinical registries.
