doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20781-3.abstract: Responses to chemotherapeutic agents vary substantially among patients with bladder cancer. The lack of preclinical models that accurately predict the clinical efficacy of intravesical chemotherapy remains a major barrier to precision oncology. In this prospective multicenter study (NCT06662071), 63 patients with bladder cancer were enrolled at four medical centers. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) were established using specimens obtained by transurethral resection of bladder tumor. A total of 35 PDOs underwent high-throughput screening with a panel of eight clinically relevant chemotherapeutic agents. To identify the optimal classification strategy, we evaluated six distinct approaches by combining two statistical methods (the Jenks natural breaks method and the tertile method) with three sensitivity indicators (viability, nAUC, and IC50) and assessed the concordance between drug sensitivity profiles and real-world clinical follow-up data. We successfully established 41 PDOs. Comparative analysis indicated that post-digestion cell viability and total cell count may influence the success of PDO establishment. The PDOs showed high morphological and molecular concordance with the primary tumors. Among the six candidate strategies, IC50-Jenks showed the highest numerical concordance with clinical outcomes, with accuracy of 88.2% (95% CI, 63.6-98.5%) and specificity of 93.3% (95% CI, 68.1-99.8%). Representative case studies confirmed the utility of PDOs in identifying therapeutic futility and supporting the feasibility of bladder-sparing strategies. This multicenter feasibility study suggests that bladder cancer PDOs may support exploratory assessment of chemotherapy sensitivity. The proposed classification approach requires validation in larger, prospectively designed, clinically homogeneous cohorts before it can inform routine treatment decisions.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20792-0.abstract: Our objective was to investigate whether cryptorchidism independently influenced cancer-specific survival (CSS) and overall survival in patients with testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs). We conducted a cohort study using the Surveillance Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database (2000-2022; 21 registries). Patients with TGCTs who underwent orchiectomy were identified and classified by primary site code as having descended (C62.1) or undescended (C62.0) testis. The final analytical cohort comprised 10,353 patients (10,103 descended, 250 undescended). Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression adjusting for age, histology, stage, tumor size, race/ethnicity, and chemotherapy receipt. PSM (1:4 nearest neighbor) was performed as a sensitivity analysis to account for baseline differences between groups. Seminoma was significantly more prevalent in the undescended group (65.2% vs 51.4%; p < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in CSS between descended and undescended groups (log-rank p = 0.876). On multivariable Cox regression, cryptorchidism was not an independent predictor of CSS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.14; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.50-2.57; p = 0.762). Independent predictors of worse CSS included distant stage (HR 21.89; p < 0.001), nonseminoma histology (HR 3.11; p < 0.001), regional stage (HR 3.27; p < 0.001), older age (HR 1.04; p < 0.001), and Hispanic (HR 1.96; p < 0.001) and non-Hispanic Black race/ethnicity (HR 2.91; p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses by histology and stage consistently showed no survival difference. In the PSM cohort (249 vs 988), cryptorchidism remained non-significant (HR 1.55, 95% CI 0.60-3.95; p = 0.365; log-rank p = 0.62). Cryptorchidism was not independently associated with CSS or overall survival in patients with TGCTs. Prognosis and management should remain guided by established tumor-related prognostic and risk-stratification factors.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20794-y.abstract: Sentinel lymph node biopsies (SLNBs) carry risk. Therefore, refinement of sentinel lymph node (SLN) identification protocols may improve patient safety. Currently, the 10 % Geiger count threshold is standard for SLN identification, yet the utility of more restrictive thresholds remains unexplored. This study explored whether a 30 % threshold could maintain diagnostic reliability while reducing the number of nodes removed. A single-institution, retrospective review of all malignant melanoma patients who underwent SLNB with technetium-99m sulfur colloid (99mTc) lymphatic mapping with or without methylene blue dye was performed. Only patients with at least two SLNs, preoperative clinical staging, and reported final pathology were considered for analysis. Individual SLN Geiger counts were calculated as fractions of the highest count value (percent hottest node [PHN]) found in the associated LN basin. Positive and negative predictive values were calculated and compared for the cohort using the gold standard 10 % and experimental 30 % Geiger count thresholds. Pathologic stage was determined for patients who had pathologically positive SLNs that remained unidentified by the 30 % count threshold. The study included 1,001 patients with 1,098 involved LN basins. Compared with the traditional 10 % threshold, the 30% threshold was associated with a higher positive predictive value and a comparable negative predictive value across all LN basins sampled and upon stratification by tumor preoperative T stage. The optimal Geiger count threshold was calculated to be 52.3 % for this cohort. In this exploratory retrospective review, a 30 % Geiger count threshold appeared to identify SLNs without compromising disease detection. These results suggest that higher thresholds may suffice for accurate staging and merit prospective evaluation.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20810-1.abstract: Breast surgery and reconstruction rates in the USA continue to rise, with over 90% of new breast cancer diagnoses occurring in peri- or postmenopausal women. Despite the relevance of menopause to wound healing, postoperative outcomes in this population remain understudied. Estrogen hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may aid wound healing and menopausal symptoms, but carries prothrombotic risk. We investigate postsurgical outcomes after breast surgery and reconstruction among postmenopausal patients on HRTs compared to those without HRT use. Using the TriNetX database, we compared patients with and without HRT use within 1 year preceding breast reconstruction. Mastectomy and reconstruction procedures were identified using CPT codes. HRT use was identified using ICD-10 and RxNorm codes. Cohorts were propensity-matched for demographics and comorbidities. Risk differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for outcomes within 90 days postoperatively. Analyses were performed within TriNetX, with significance set at P < 0.05. Two cohorts were generated, with 3750 HRT+ and 75503 HRT- patients. After propensity matching, two cohorts of 3750 patients each were created. After propensity adjustment, there was no significant association between HRT use and postoperative mortality, VTE, or wound healing complications, which were comparably low across all surgery types. Among patients undergoing autologous reconstruction, 1-year revision rates were higher in the HRT+ cohort. Systemic hormone replacement therapy was not associated with an increased complications after breast reconstruction, including mortality, thrombosis, infection, and wound dehiscence. Further prospective studies across surgical populations are needed to validate these findings.

doi:10.20892/j.issn.2095-3941.2026.0488.abstract: The aims of the study were to elucidate the regulatory role of rhomboid family protein 2 (RHBDF2) in breast cancer chemoresistance and the underlying molecular mechanisms to provide a theoretical basis and research direction to facilitate the development of potential therapeutic interventions. Chemoresistance and apoptosis assays, and mouse tumor-bearing models were used to evaluate the correlation between RHBDF2 expression and breast cancer chemoresistance. Doxorubicin accumulation, rhodamine efflux, immunohistochemical staining, Western blot, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to validate the regulatory relationships in protein expression and function for RHBDF2, MDR1 (ABCB1), and SEC62 (a critical component of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane insertion machinery). Immunofluorescence staining and immunoprecipitation assays were employed to determine the molecular mechanisms underlying RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis-mediated regulation of breast cancer chemoresistance. The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis constitutes the core regulatory pathway in breast cancer chemoresistance. When RHBDF2 is highly expressed, it binds to heat shock cognate protein 70 (HSC70), a central chaperone-mediated autophagy receptor, thereby blocking the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62, maintaining SEC62 protein levels, and promoting membrane integration of MDR1 to enhance drug resistance. Under downregulated RHBDF2 expression, the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62 increases, leading to impaired MDR1 function and substantially reduced cellular drug resistance. The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis is the core signaling pathway that governs chemoresistance in breast cancer. Targeted interventions against key molecules or related signaling nodes in this axis can provide a theoretical basis for developing novel therapeutic strategies to reverse chemoresistance, with great clinical translational value.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1740218.abstract: Lorlatinib is a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that has been shown to have high efficacy in the first line setting for treatment of advanced ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, some adverse events have been described that require proper follow-up and management to obtain the maximum benefit from treatment and minimize risk to the patient. These include dyslipidemia and weight gain, conditions that in Latin America have a high prevalence in the general population, which coupled with limitations in timely access to specialized care, could influence both manifestation and management. The objective of this consensus is to provide recommendations tailored to our real-world setting that will optimize the monitoring and early management of toxicities in patients treated with lorlatinib in Latin America.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1740407.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma carries a poor prognosis making its management challenging. Histotripsy is a non-invasive, non-ionizing, and non-thermal therapy that mechanically disrupts tumors through acoustic cavitation. We present the case of a 59-year-old man with locally advanced, multifocal, stage II intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who achieved a complete pathologic response in the explanted liver after treatment with histotripsy and systemic drug therapy consisting of gemcitabine, cisplatin, durvalumab, and trastuzumab deruxtecan. This case highlights the potential role of noninvasive histotripsy as a bridging therapy to transplantation in selected patients with cholangiocarcinoma.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1754407.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits significant morphological heterogeneity that has traditionally been attributed to etiological, environmental, and biological factors. Recent evidence suggests, however, that genetic background may influence tumor characteristics and behavior in HCC. To investigate associations between established HCC genetic risk factors and first-order radiomic features. We evaluated a retrospective cohort of 210 patients with HCC who underwent contrast-enhanced MRI and genetic profiling for three established HCC risk variants (PNPLA3 rs738409-G, TM6SF2 rs58542926-T, and MAU2 rs58489806-T). We screened first-order radiomic features in the full cohort and then focused the primary analysis on 77 treatment-naive patients whose tumor morphology had not been modified by therapy. Patients were stratified into at-risk (≥1 risk allele, n=52) and wild-type (no risk alleles, n=25) groups. Eighteen first-order radiomic features were screened using the Mann-Whitney U test and AUC analysis. The leading feature, kurtosis, was then subjected to univariate and multivariate analysis for clinical and imaging features to identify any confounding effect. In addition, a 10-fold cross-validated cutpoint stability, sensitivity analysis, and Cox/Kaplan-Meier survival analysis were also conducted. Among 18 features, kurtosis best distinguished at-risk from wild-type genotypes in treatment-naive patients (AUC = 0.67, p=0.014), with wild-type tumors showing more uniform, sharply peaked intensity patterns. Tumor volume correlated modestly with kurtosis (Spearman's ρ=0.45, p<0.0001), but volume alone did not discriminate genotype (Mann-Whitney U, p=0.3994). The genotype-kurtosis association remained significant after adjusting for volume and shape (ANCOVA, p=0.029) and strengthened after adjusting for nine clinical/demographic covariates (p=0.003), indicating kurtosis reflects biological information beyond tumor size. The empirical cutpoint was stable across 10-fold cross-validation (mean=3.35, SD = 0.05), and results were unchanged in sensitivity analysis. Kurtosis was not associated with overall survival (Cox HR = 1.19, p=0.13). No genotype-related discrimination was observed in the pooled full cohort, consistent with treatment-related alteration of tumor texture. In a cohort of 210 genetically profiled patients with HCC, genotype-related radiomic features were not apparent when treated and untreated tumors were analyzed together. However, restricting the analysis to the treatment-naive subgroup (n=77) revealed tumor kurtosis as a reproducible, biologically plausible first-order imaging correlate of established HCC genetic risk status.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1758462.abstract: The introduction of volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) has enabled dosimetric improvements during prostate bed (PB) radiotherapy; however, the planning target volume (PTV) margins remain substantially greater than for prostate radiotherapy. New approaches are required to further optimise rectal dose and minimise target and organ motion. ProSpare®, a self-inserted rectal obturator designed to facilitate daily image guidance, may enhance radiotherapy accuracy and reduce treatment-related morbidity. Patients scheduled to receive adjuvant or salvage PB radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy were randomised to either standard-of-care (SOC) PB-IMRT using centre-standard PTV margins and verification protocol (SOC) or PB-IMRT with daily ProSpare®-guided radiotherapy using a reduced 5-mm posterior margin. Dose and fractionation schedules were selected by each centre according to protocol recommendations. The primary endpoint is patient-reported EPIC bowel function and bother at 2 years. Secondary endpoints include acute Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) and CTCAE toxicity, patient-reported outcomes, device tolerability, and anorectal dosimetry. We report the results from the prespecified analysis of these secondary endpoints. Between 2017 and 2023, 162 patients were recruited; 158 began radiotherapy and were evaluable at 18 weeks. Acute toxicity data were available for 146 patients (SOC 76/81, ProSpare 70/77). Compared with SOC, ProSpare® was associated with lower 18-week RTOG ≥grade 1 gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) toxicity (39% vs. 31% and 37% vs. 29%, respectively). The incidence of worst CTCAE grade 2 GI and GU toxicity was <6%. Of 51 responders, 50 found ProSpare® tolerable and would recommend its use. Use of ProSpare® resulted in consistently lower ano-rectal dose-volume parameters. ProSpare®-guided prostate bed radiotherapy (PBRT) resulted in lower acute RTOG bowel toxicity at all time points. Patient-reported tolerability was very favourable. Use of ProSpare® improved rectal and anal canal dosimetry. ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT02978014.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1768933.abstract: Malnutrition, altered body composition, and sarcopenia are common among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with poor treatment tolerance and adverse clinical outcomes. PhA, derived from BIA, reflects cellular membrane integrity and body cell mass and has been increasingly investigated as a potential marker of nutritional status and prognosis in oncology. However, the clinical relevance of PhA in patients with CRC has not yet been systematically synthesized. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for observational studies published between January 2000 and October 2025 that assessed PhA in adult patients with CRC. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the AXIS tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, outcome definitions, and PhA cut-off values, a narrative synthesis was conducted. A total of 10 studies involving 1,439 patients were included. Lower PhA values were consistently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Four studies reported significantly shorter overall or progression-free survival among patients with low PhA. Four studies demonstrated associations between low PhA and unfavorable short-term outcomes, including postoperative complications, prolonged hospital stay, cancer-related complications, and early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Several studies also reported positive associations between PhA and indicators of nutritional status, body composition, muscle mass, muscle strength, and hydration balance. One longitudinal study showed that postoperative increases in PhA were accompanied by improvements in body composition parameters and reduced early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Current evidence indicates that BIA-derived phase angle is associated with nutritional status, body composition, treatment tolerance, and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer. However, heterogeneity in measurement protocols and cut-off values limits direct clinical application. Standardized assessment methods and prospective studies are needed to establish CRC-specific reference values and to determine whether interventions that improve PhA can translate into improved clinical outcomes.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1773440.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that oral microbiota dysbiosis and periodontal pathogens contribute to the initiation and progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the potential role of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in P. gingivalis-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment formation during OSCC progression. Genes associated with P. gingivalis and TIGIT were obtained from GeneCards and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases. Candidate hub genes were identified through bioinformatic analyses. An SCC7 syngeneic orthotopic transplantation mouse model was established, and SCC7 cells were injected together with Porphyromonas gingivalis. Tumor growth was assessed by measuring tumor volume and weight. Expression levels of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT were evaluated by immunohistochemistry and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Flow cytometry was performed to analyze tumor-infiltrating immune-cell populations. The TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 was used to investigate the involvement of TLR4-associated signaling. Bioinformatic analysis identified TLR4 as a biologically relevant candidate hub gene potentially linking P. gingivalis-associated signaling and TIGIT-related immune regulation. Exposure to P. gingivalis significantly promoted tumor growth and increased the expression of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT in tumor tissues. Flow cytometric analysis revealed immune microenvironment remodeling characterized by increased proportions of CD4+ T cells, TIGIT-positive Tregs, and IL-10-positive cells, accompanied by reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and decreased frequencies of Ki67+CD8+ and CD44+CD8+ T cells. Treatment with the TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 partially reversed these tumor-promoting, immunological, and molecular changes. Our findings suggest that exposure to P. gingivalis may promote OSCC progression by contributing to immune microenvironment remodeling. Increased expression of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT, together with the effects of TLR4 inhibition, supports the potential involvement of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in this process. However, the precise molecular mechanisms require further validation using genetic and functional approaches.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1780678.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression (CIM) is the most common adverse reaction of tumor chemotherapy and may lead to treatment delay, dose reduction, life-threatening infection, and poor prognosis. Current predictive methods remain suboptimal, with insufficient interpretability and limited clinical application. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for early CIM risk prediction using routine laboratory data. A total of 1,000 cancer patients from Northeast Yunnan Central Hospital between January 2024 and January 2025 were enrolled and divided into a case group (n=500, with myelosuppression) and a control group (n=500, without myelosuppression).All observed samples were randomly split into a training set (70%) and a validation set (30%). The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) was used to select optimal variables for model construction. The predictive performance of 15 different ML models was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1-score, Youden's index, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), decision curve analysis (DCA), and residual boxplots. The best-performing model was selected for SHAP-based interpretability analysis and internally validated using a confusion matrix, clinical impact curve, and calibration curve.Additionally, 488 patients treated at Northeast Yunnan Provincial Central Hospital between June 2025 and November 2025 were selected as an independent external validation cohort for external validation. After screening, 15 clinical indicators were used for ML model development. All models demonstrated excellent discrimination. The LightGBM model showed the best overall performance (AUC: 0.999 [0.998-1.000]; sensitivity: 0.986; specificity: 0.989; accuracy: 0.987; PPV: 0.989; NPV: 0.986; F1-score: 0.987; Youden's index: 0.974). According to the LightGBM model, CIM risk increased when the following feature thresholds were met: white blood cell count 10%, red blood cell count <4×1012/L, mean platelet volume <8 fL, and plateletcrit <0.1%.In the independent external validation (n=488), the LightGBM model remained stable and reliable, with an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI: 0.920-0.959), sensitivity of 0.818, specificity of 0.888, accuracy of 85.2%, and favorable calibration and clinical net benefit. The LightGBM prediction model developed in this study can enable early identification of high-risk patients, providing a reference for healthcare providers to implement early interventions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1794020.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in cancer care over the years. It shows promise in areas like pain management, psychological support, surgical training, and rehabilitation. Even though more studies are being done, there has not been a thorough analysis of the research trends in this field. This study looks at how VR interventions in cancer research have evolved over the past two decades, identifies research hotspots, and explores future directions. We collected publications related to VR in cancer research from the Web of Science Core Collection and Pubmed, covering the period from 2005 to 2025. Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace software, we performed bibliometric and visual analyses. These included examining publication trends, contributions by countries and institutions, author collaboration networks, journal impact, keyword co-occurrence, and citation bursts. A total of 1,259 publications from 110 countries were included. The number of publications fluctuated over time but generally increased, reaching its highest point in 2024 with 184 articles. The United States and China were the most active countries. Jordan had the highest average number of citations per paper. Among institutions, McGill University published the most papers, followed by the University of Toronto. The most productive journal was Surgical Endoscopy and Other Interventional Techniques, whilst Cancers and Supportive Care in Cancer showed the fastest growth. Main research themes included pain management, anxiety reduction, breast cancer, and surgical training. Emerging trends involve the combination of augmented reality (AR), digital health, and artificial intelligence (AI) with VR. This study shows that VR research in cancer care is expanding worldwide, with most contributions coming from North America and Europe. Pain management remains the most common application. New technologies such as AR, AI, and telemedicine are becoming more integrated into VR interventions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1796519.abstract: Atypical spindle cell lipomatous tumor (ASCLT) is a rare benign adipocytic neoplasm, and primary involvement of the retroperitoneum is exceedingly uncommon. Because its imaging features overlap with those of other fat-containing tumors, particularly atypical lipomatous tumor/well-differentiated liposarcoma (ALT/WDL), preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. We report a case of primary retroperitoneal ASCLT in a 58-year-old woman whose lesion was incidentally detected during a routine physical examination. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a small, well-defined fat-containing mass located between the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery, with fat-related signal attenuation on fat-suppressed sequences, no obvious diffusion restriction, and mild reticular enhancement after contrast administration. Complete surgical excision was performed, and postoperative histopathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of ASCLT, with no MDM2 amplification. Compared with previously reported retroperitoneal ASCLT cases, the present case provides detailed CT and multiparametric MRI findings for a small, incidentally detected lesion adjacent to major abdominal vessels. Recognition of this imaging pattern may help include ASCLT in the preoperative differential diagnosis and support appropriate surgical planning, while definitive diagnosis still requires pathological and molecular confirmation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1800218.abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer incidence and mortality among women worldwide, with ongoing challenges in early detection, accurate diagnosis, prognosis estimation, and treatment-response assessment. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has rapidly advanced breast cancer research by enabling analysis of high-dimensional imaging, pathological, genomic, and clinical data. However, the rapid expansion of this literature has resulted in substantial fragmentation across clinical tasks, data modalities, algorithmic paradigms, and software ecosystems. This systematic review presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of AI-driven breast cancer research published recently. Using a multi-database, Scopus and Web of Science, as primary data sources, a systematic bibliometric framework integrating performance analysis, science mapping, and thematic evolution was employed. The analysis is guided by explicit research questions examining: (i) the evolution of AI applications across diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment-response prediction; (ii) the adoption of explainable AI and hyperparameter optimization practices; (iii) the datasets, software frameworks, and algorithms shaping the field; (iv) the role of mammography as a core modality; and (v) emerging research hotspots, including transformer-based architectures. Unlike prior bibliometric studies focused mainly on citation metrics, this work adopts a task-aware, methodologycentric perspective, offering actionable insights to support reproducible, interpretable, and clinically integrated AI systems for breast cancer care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1801070.abstract: Breast cancer mortality in Chile has shown divergent trends over recent decades, with declining age-adjusted rates alongside increasing crude mortality driven by population aging. In 2005, Chile incorporated breast cancer into the Explicit Health Guarantees Regime (AUGE/GES), ensuring universal access, timeliness, quality standards, and financial protection across the continuum of care. Whether this policy produced an independent, detectable impact on population-level breast cancer mortality remains uncertain. We conducted an interrupted time series (ITS) analysis of female breast cancer mortality in Chile from 1990 to 2024. Annual death counts were obtained from national vital statistics and modeled using negative binomial regression with population offsets. Age-standardized mortality rates were calculated using the 2017 Chilean population as the reference. ITS models estimated changes in level and slope associated with two intervention points: the consolidation of the National Breast Cancer Program in 1995 and the implementation of AUGE/GES in 2005. Analyses were performed for the total female population and by age group. While the absolute number of deaths and crude mortality rates increased over time, age-standardized breast cancer mortality declined steadily throughout the study period. A significant change in trend was observed after 1995, consistent with the early programmatic organization of breast cancer services. In contrast, no additional statistically significant change in level or slope was detected after 2005 at the population level or among women aged ≥40/≥50 years. Age-stratified analyses revealed a more pronounced post-2005 decline among women aged 65-69 and ≥80 years, suggesting age- and cohort-specific effects. Breast cancer mortality risk in Chile has declined primarily due to long-term secular trends and early programmatic strengthening, while population aging has driven increasing crude mortality. The AUGE/GES reform has consolidated access and financial protection, with heterogeneous benefits in older cohorts, but without generating a detectable additional inflection in national mortality trends. Further mortality reductions will require integrated, equity-oriented strategies emphasizing organized screening, timely diagnosis, and high-quality treatment across the life course.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1804620.abstract: This comprehensive review explores advancements in the treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC), emphasizing the transformative impact of targeted therapies and immunotherapies. Given TNBC's aggressive nature and limited therapeutic options, this review provides an in-depth analysis of emerging strategies that aim to enhance patient outcomes. Within targeted therapies, we discuss molecular subtypes and evaluate the efficacy of PARP inhibitors, EGFR inhibitors, and PI3K inhibitors, integrating insights from clinical trials. The immunotherapy landscape is examined through immune checkpoint inhibitors, Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and novel vaccine-based approaches. Combination strategies are assessed, focusing on clinical efficacy, safety, and resistance mechanisms. Additionally, we highlight emerging therapeutic innovations, including bispecific antibodies, advanced drug delivery systems, and personalized medicine approaches. Beyond treatment modalities, the review addresses key challenges such as therapy resistance, biomarker-driven treatment selection, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence in TNBC management. Future directions emphasize ongoing clinical trials and evolving therapeutic paradigms aimed at improving survival and quality of life for TNBC patients. As the field progresses, a multidisciplinary approach integrating precision oncology, innovative therapeutics, and patient-centered care will be critical. In conclusion, this review encapsulates current breakthroughs and envisions a future where targeted and immune-based interventions redefine TNBC treatment, offering new hope for patients and clinicians alike.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1811232.abstract: To establish baseline growth rates of lung nodules in untreated head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma(ACC) patients and analyze associated clinical and molecular factors influencing these rates. CT was used to calculate the diameter of 74 pulmonary metastatic nodules in 37 patients under natural state. The diameter growth rate of lung metastatic nodules was fitted with a linear regression equation, and the differences in the progression rate of lung metastasis among patients were compared. Additionally, clinical features such as location, pathological subtypes, and staging were also collected to compare their correlation with the growth rate of lung metastatic nodules. Subsequently, single-cell sequencing data from three lung metastatic nodules of differing diameters within the same case were analyzed. We defined three different states based on the progression of lung metastases: rapid progression was defined as a monthly diameter increase of more than 1 mm in 16.2% (6/37) of the patients; slow progression was defined as a monthly diameter increase between 0.3-1 mm in 56.8% (21/37) of the patients; and stable state was defined as a monthly diameter increase of less than 0.3 mm in 27.0% (10/37) of the patients. In addition, factors such as low expression of TP63, a higher pathological grade (Grade III), and a nodule diameter greater than 10mm at initial diagnosis of lung metastasis were identified as significant predictors for a faster diameter growth rate (P<0.05). Subsequently, through single-cell sequencing analysis, it was found that rapidly progressing nodules exhibited upregulation of signals related to hypoxia, vascular genesis, and a weakening of immune response-related signals. The findings of this study suggest that baseline characteristics based on the growth rate of pulmonary metastatic nodules may be used to help stratify the progression rate of lung metastasis. In particular, based on our observations, for patients with pulmonary metastatic lesions presenting with a nodule diameter > 10 mm, pathological grade III, and low TP63 expression at initial diagnosis, clinicians might consider adopting closer follow-up monitoring or potentially initiating intervention measures earlier. Additionally, for rapidly growing pulmonary metastatic nodules, it may be worth considering targeted therapy against hypoxic/anti-angiogenic pathways or combination with immunotherapy aimed at restoring or enhancing local immune responses.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1811434.abstract: To evaluate the predictive value of a nomogram incorporating ultrasound and clinical features for cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with thyroid cancer. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients pathologically diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) between April 2024 and January 2025. Radiomics features were extracted from two-dimensional thyroid ultrasound images, and feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five classifiers were compared, and logistic regression was selected to construct the radiomics model. A clinical-radiomics model integrating the radiomics score and clinical predictors, together with a standalone clinical model, was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated in a held-out internal validation set. Sex, Radscore, age, and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were identified as independent predictors of CLNM in patients with PTC. Based on these variables, radiomics, clinical, and clinical radiomics models were constructed; the models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.735, 0.792, and 0.867, respectively, in the validation set. DeLong's test and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the clinical radiomics model outperformed the radiomics model in the validation set, offering a higher net clinical benefit. A nomogram integrating ultrasound imaging and clinical data effectively predicts the risk of CLNM in patients with PTC and may assist clinicians in developing individualized treatment strategies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1813354.abstract: Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially fatal complication after radical surgery for gynecologic malignancies, yet population-specific risk tools remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 500 consecutive patients who underwent radical surgery for cervical, endometrial, or ovarian cancer (January 2022-January 2025). The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n=351, 70%) and a validation set (n=149, 30%) at a 7:3 ratio. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression, and 10 machine-learning algorithms were trained and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated, and the optimal model was interpreted using SHAP. DVT occurred in 116 patients (23.2%). Five variables were independently associated with DVT: age, Caprini score, lymphocyte count, preoperative D-dimer, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR).Across candidate models, CatBoost achieved the optimal overall performance on the validation set, yielding an AUC of 0.816 (95% CI: 0.738-0.881), with sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI: 0.700-1.000) and specificity of 0.730 (95% CI: 0.515-0.876), and SHAP analysis ranked the predictors by mean absolute SHAP value in the following order: lymphocyte count, Caprini score, age, preoperative D-dimer, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). An interpretable CatBoost-based model enables individualized postoperative DVT risk stratification after gynecologic cancer surgery and may support targeted, evidence-based thromboprophylaxis and perioperative nursing management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1814886.abstract: Hypochloremia is associated with poor prognosis in various malignant tumors. However, longitudinal trajectories of serum chloride in cancer patients and their relationship with mortality remain unexplored. This study aimed to delineate dynamic serum chloride trajectory patterns and analyze their association with mortality in patients with malignancies. This retrospective cohort study included 4,115 patients with malignant tumors from the MIMIC-IV database who had serial serum chloride measurements within the first 5 days of ICU admission, plus an additional 518 patients from Zibo Municipal Hospital for external validation. We applied group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) to stratify patients into three distinct serum chloride trajectory classes. The primary outcomes were 28-day and 365-day all-cause mortality, which were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to verify the robustness of the study findings. Three distinct serum chloride trajectory patterns were identified in both the MIMIC-IV primary cohort and the external validation cohort: Class 1 (initial hyperchloremia resolving to normal levels), Class 2 (persistent normochloremia), and Class 3 (progressive hyperchloremia). In the fully adjusted Cox regression model (Model 3), Class 3 was an independent predictor of 28-day (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.26-1.92) and 365-day all-cause mortality (HR = 1.38, 95%CI: 1.19-1.60) in the MIMIC-IV cohort. This prognostic value was validated in the external validation cohort, where Class 3 was also associated with a significantly increased 28-day mortality risk (HR = 1.90, 95%CI: 1.08-3.33). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that Class 3 patients had significantly lower survival rates at both 28-day and 365-day follow-ups. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses further verified the robustness of the association between progressive hyperchloremia and adverse mortality outcomes. Progressive hyperchloremia trajectory independently predicts early and late mortality in cancer patients, and may offer a dynamic, low-cost biomarker for risk stratification.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1819986.abstract: Accurate early diagnosis of Clinically Significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is crucial for improving patient survival rates. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable, confidence-based deep learning model for csPCa classification using biparametric MRI (bpMRI). A retrospective analysis was conducted on bpMRI data from 410 patients. A classification model was constructed using the visual geometry group 16-layer (VGG-16) network, incorporating gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for visual interpretability, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) for uncertainty estimation, and a rejection mechanism. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC). Across all predictions, the confidence-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 79.3% before rejection. At a confidence threshold of 0.8, 80.8% of predictions were retained, among which the selective accuracy was 94.6%, with 99 false-positive and 2 false-negative predictions. Besides, the model's accuracy outperformed that of a senior radiologist (94.6% vs 90.8%). Qualitative Grad-CAM visualization demonstrated that the classifier frequently assigned high activation to MRI regions considered suspicious for csPCa; however, quantitative spatial agreement with lesion annotations was not assessed. This confidence-based model identifies csPCa lesions and provides reliable confidence scores without pixel-level annotations. By rejecting uncertain predictions, it enhances the transparency and safety of clinical decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1832969.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification of cystic renal lesions (CRLs) remains a clinical challenge, primarily due to morphological overlap which often leads to the overtreatment of indolent cysts. To address this, we developed and validated an integrated deep learning framework that combines interactive segmentation with tri-phase CT feature integration to refine malignancy prediction. This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 434 patients with CRLs from four institutions, partitioned into training (n=195), validation (n=100), and external test (n=139) cohorts. The reference standard was histopathological diagnosis or ≥4 years of radiological stability. For volumetric segmentation, we implemented an interactive 'human-in-the-loop' Swin UNETR model. To integrate complementary information across the three CT phases, we then deployed a Tri-Phase-Channel (TPC) Perceiver architecture to integrate features extracted by parallel SEResNet50 backbones from unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic CT phases. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against the single-phase SEResNet50 models and the Bosniak classification version 2019 using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). In the external test cohort, the interactive segmentation model yielded a Dice score of 0.890. For malignancy prediction, the TPC-Perceiver attained an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI: 0.911-1.000), significantly outperforming the Bosniak classification version 2019 (AUC 0.884; p =0.016). At the fixed probability threshold of 0.5, the model achieved a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 96.7%, compared with 100.0% and 76.9%, respectively, for the clinical standard. Furthermore, decision curve analysis indicated that the deep learning framework conferred greater net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. The integrated framework showed favorable performance for cystic renal lesion risk stratification. Exploratory pairwise AUC comparisons favored the TPC Perceiver over the single-phase models and the clinical Bosniak v2019 assessment, while its AUC was comparable to that of the previous SETD model. The sensitivity-specificity profile observed at the fixed threshold suggests potential value in reducing false-positive risk stratification. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required before clinical implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1835503.abstract: Treatment intensification with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) combined with docetaxel, an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, or selected triplet regimens is recommended for eligible patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC). Despite increasing adoption, implementation remains variable in routine clinical practice. To characterize temporal trends in first-line systemic treatment for mCSPC and identify factors associated with receipt of guideline-concordant treatment intensification using exploratory explainable machine learning. National treatment patterns were evaluated using the Pfizer Oncology Quality Care Insight Tool derived from IQVIA Anonymized Patient Longitudinal Data, and institutional patterns were evaluated within Avera Health. The exploratory cohort included 42 patients with documented mCSPC treated between 2018 and 2023. Guideline-concordant treatment intensification was defined as ADT combined with docetaxel or a novel hormonal therapy within 90 days of ADT initiation. Potential outcome-derived variables were excluded before modeling. Six predictive approaches were evaluated using repeated nested stratified cross-validation, with 5-fold outer cross-validation repeated 20 times and 5-fold inner cross-validation repeated three times. Recursive feature elimination was performed within outer training folds, and class imbalance was addressed using SMOTE within resampling. Thirty-two (32) of forty-two (42) patients (76.2%) received guideline-concordant treatment intensification. Treatment-pattern analysis showed increasing use of first-line novel hormonal therapy and declining ADT monotherapy over time. Under repeated nested validation, discrimination was modest and variable across models. The Decision Tree achieved the highest patient-level AUC (0.675; 95% CI, 0.421-0.929), whereas Random Forest achieved an AUC of 0.650 (95% CI, 0.383-0.917), accuracy of 85.7%, precision of 88.2%, recall of 93.8%, and F1 score of 0.909. Feature-selection stability identified insurance coverage for novel hormonal therapy as the most consistently selected predictor, followed by positive core proportion and smoking history. These three variables were retained in the final explanatory Random Forest model, and global SHAP and Random Forest importance analysis showed broadly concordant rankings. Treatment intensification for mCSPC increased substantially in routine practice. Repeated nested validation produced more conservative and variable performance estimates than the original single-split analysis, underscoring the exploratory nature of this small cohort. Healthcare access and selected clinical factors warrant further evaluation in larger, multicenter datasets.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1837994.abstract: The malignant transformation of endometriosis has garnered widespread attention; however, most cases of malignant transformation occur in ovarian endometriomas, while extraovarian malignant transformation is rare. We present an uncommon instance of extraovarian endometrioid adenocarcinoma originating from the uterosacral ligament(USL) in a 41-year-old female, which emerged from deep infiltrating endometriosis of the uterosacral ligament 4 years after a previous clinical diagnosis of adenomyosis. A 41-year-old woman, presenting with progressively worsening secondary dysmenorrhea for 4 years and dyspareunia for over 1 year, underwent "laparoscopic total hysterectomy, left adnexectomy, right salpingectomy, right ovarian endometrioma cystectomy, bilateral uterosacral ligament DIE lesion resection, anterior rectal resection, rectal DIE lesion resection with end-to-end anastomosis, left ureteral DIE lesion excision, and pelvic adhesiolysis." Postoperative pathology revealed a well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the uterosacral ligament (FIGO grade 1), arising from malignant transformation of pelvic endometriosis. Subsequently, a completion surgery was performed, consisting of "transabdominal right oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy, omentectomy, biopsy of an ileal surface lesion, resection of a right pelvic wall peritoneal lesion, and pelvic adhesiolysis." Postoperative pathological examination revealed a metastatic carcinoma in the right obturator lymph node. The final diagnosis was stage IV according to the FIGO 2009 staging system (FIGO stage IV) pelvic endometriosis-associated malignancy with direct invasion of the rectal wall by the USL adenocarcinoma. The patient underwent six cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with paclitaxel and carboplatin given every three weeks. Over five years after finishing treatment, there are no signs of recurrence. This paper describes an unusual case where deep infiltrating endometriosis of the uterosacral ligament led to malignant transformation. During long-term treatment and surgery for endometriosis, the potential for malignant transformation and the malignant characteristics of endometriosis should be fully considered. Prompt and thorough surgical intervention is crucial.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1840185.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model by integrating radiomic features from B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (DCE-US) parametric imaging, as well as clinical and conventional ultrasound features, for preoperative prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) complicated with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). A total of 191 patients with pathologically confirmed HT-complicated PTC were retrospectively enrolled between December 2023 and July 2025. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=133) and a validation set (n=58) at a 7:3 ratio using a random number generator. Radiomic features were extracted from BMUS images and DCE-US peak enhancement parametric maps. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and interclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process including the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors of CLNM were identified using multivariate logistic regression incorporating clinical and ultrasound features. Three predictive models were constructed: a clinical-ultrasound model, a radiomics model, and a combined multi-modal model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis. TG-Ab, TR-Ab, extrathyroidal extension, filling defects, BMUS Rad-score, and DCE-US Rad-score were independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the training and validation sets, the combined model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.936 and 0.916, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.825, 0.876) and the clinical-ultrasound model (AUC = 0.760, 0.800; DeLong test, P < 0.05). Calibration curves showed good model fitting. DCA confirmed that the combined model provided greater clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI verified that the combined model significantly improved CLNM prediction performance. SHAP analysis revealed that DCE-US Rad-score was the most important predictor for CLNM. A multi-modal predictive model combining dual-modality ultrasound radiomic scores (BMUS and DCE-US) with clinical and ultrasound features can effectively and robustly predict CLNM in patients with HT-complicated PTC and performs better than single-modal models. This model provides an objective reference for the formulation of individualized surgical strategies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1842525.abstract: To characterise age-related gradients in colorectal lesion severity and prespecified high-risk endoscopic features in a lesion-confirmed screening colonoscopy cohort and to evaluate an investigator-defined red-flag composite as an exploratory marker of advanced pathology. Helicobacter pylori was assessed as a secondary exposure. This retrospective cohort included 291 participants with histologically confirmed lesions in four age groups (36-45, 46-55, 56-65 and 66-72 years). Logistic regression evaluated predictors of advanced neoplasia (high-grade dysplasia [HGD] or adenocarcinoma); adenocarcinoma-only and age × H. pylori interaction analyses were exploratory because events were sparse. With advancing age, body mass index, H. pylori positivity, adenoma, sessile serrated lesions, HGD, adenocarcinoma and high-risk endoscopic features increased, whereas hyperplastic polyps decreased (all P < 0.05). Age (per 10 years), male sex, H. pylori positivity, lesion size ≥10 mm, proximal location and JNET 2B/3 pattern were independently associated with advanced neoplasia. Red-flag positivity (≥2 of four features) increased from 5.2% to 32.7% and enriched for adenocarcinoma, although positive predictive values were imprecise and non-monotonic. Colorectal lesion severity and high-risk endoscopic features showed an age-related gradient. The red-flag composite is an exploratory descriptive construct, not a validated predictive score. H. pylori findings, especially interaction analyses, are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1847737.abstract: Background Zoledronic acid is used to prevent skeletal complications in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases. Real world data on its use in resource-limited setting, particularly in sub-saharan Africa, remain scarce. Aim To describe clinical outcomes, skeletal-related events, safety and quality of life in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases treated with zoledronic acid in Côte d’Ivoire. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single center cohort study including 144 patients with mCRPC and bone metastases treated with zoledronic acid at Treichville university Hospital between January 2019 and December 2021. The primary endpoint was skeletal event-free survival (SEFS) defined as the time from the first zoledronic acid administration to the first on-treatment skeletal related event (SRE). Patients without an SRE were censored at their last available follow-up. Results The median age was 67 years (range: 42–91), and 133 patients (92.4%) were older than 50 years. Before zoledronic acid initiation, 59 patients (41.0%) had experienced at least one skeletal-related event. After treatment initiation, 30 patients (20.8%) experienced at least one new on-treatment SRE, whereas 114 (79.2%) did not. Among patients who experienced an SRE, the median time to the first event was 9 months (range 5-11). Median SEFS was not reached and the estimated 12-month SEFS was 79.2%. The most frequently documented adverse events were bone pain (18.8%), constipation (18.1%) and nausea (9.7%). FACT-G data at both baseline and 12-month were available for 129 patients (89.6%) and mean scores across all four FACT-G domains, as well as the total FACT-G score, were numerically lower at 12 months than at baseline. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort of patients with mCRPC and bone metastases, 20.8% experienced a new SRE after zoledronic acid initiation, while median SEFS was not reached. FACT-G scores decreased during follow-up. These findings provide real-world data on zoledronic acid use in a resource-limited setting.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1848924.abstract: The optimal timing and fractionation of perioperative stereotactic radiotherapy for resected brain metastases remain uncertain. We evaluated the comparative evidence for preoperative and postoperative stereotactic treatment and the validity of indirect comparisons. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov for comparative studies published or posted through 12 August 2026. Primary outcomes were local control or failure, leptomeningeal disease (LMD), and radiation necrosis (RN). Compatibility for quantitative synthesis was assessed by treatment definition, analysis unit, outcome definition, effect measure, and estimation method. Compatible patient-level hazard ratios (HRs) for local failure were combined in an exploratory fixed-effect network model. Incompatible evidence and patient-level and lesion-level estimates were synthesized separately. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were also assessed. Sixteen comparative studies were included, comprising six randomized trials and ten non-randomized studies. Three studies provided compatible patient-level HRs and formed a four-treatment local-failure network. Postoperative single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) reduced local failure compared with observation in one randomized trial (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.24-0.88). Estimates for preoperative versus postoperative single-fraction SRS (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 0.38-6.49) and postoperative single-fraction SRS versus three- to five-fraction treatment (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.09-7.32) were imprecise. All indirect comparisons had wide confidence intervals that included 1. Each direct comparison was informed by one study, and the network contained no closed loop. Some indirect estimates were sensitive to the evidence selected for the single-fraction versus fractionated-treatment comparison. Evidence for LMD and RN did not form compatible connected networks and was synthesized descriptively. Certainty was moderate for postoperative single-fraction SRS versus observation and very low for the remaining local-failure comparisons. Randomized evidence supports postoperative single-fraction SRS over observation for reducing local failure. However, current evidence does not establish a reliable hierarchy among preoperative SRS, postoperative single-fraction SRS, and postoperative fractionated treatment. Evidence for LMD and RN remains insufficient for network comparison. Treatment decisions should account for individual clinical characteristics until adequately powered prospective comparisons become available. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261341468.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1849274.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and lethal malignancies, whose prognostic prediction is particularly challenging. Histopathological biomarkers are critical for cancer prognosis assessment. Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have made it possible to automate the classification and detection of information from whole-slide pathology images using deep learning. This study aims to utilize AI deep learning to analyze histopathological slides of HCC patients for prognostic stratification, thereby assisting in the development of clinical treatment plans. The Otsu thresholding method was employed to automatically segment whole-slide images (WSIs) from two HCC datasets, The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and HCC slides from Ansteel General Hospital. The pathological features of WSIs, extracted by the pretrained CONCH model were utilized as model inputs. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and additional metrics. Then Attention Heatmap Visualization was employed to analyze interpretability. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov curve was utilized to stratify patients into distinct risk groups. Survival analysis was performed to evaluate differences in overall survival between distinct risk groups. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were used to identify key clinical indicators and pathological features as significant predictors. The riskRegression package generated calibration curves comparing predicted versus observed survival outcomes. Calibration curves were quantify the deviation between model-predicted probabilities and actual observed outcomes. A prognostic prediction model was developed using the CLAM self-attention framework based on TCGA dataset, whose generalization capability was verified by histologically stained slide data from a proprietary dataset. The results showed that the model could achieve better migration. Mortality rates demonstrated a progressive increase across ascending risk groups. The risk stratification system possesses potential clinical utility for guiding treatment selection. Forest plots generated demonstrated that the risk stratification system functions as an independent prognostic predictor for HCC. Calibration curve analysis confirmed the predictive accuracy of the model, and this finding from Decision Curve Analysis underscores its superior utility in guiding clinical decision-making. This study developed a prognostic prediction model, whose risk stratification could be an independent prognostic predictor for HCC and a guide for therapeutic decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1850604.abstract: Pancreatic cancer is a highly lethal malignancy for which mortality remains close to incidence. We combined complementary global estimates and longitudinal cancer-registry data to characterize its current burden, recent incidence trends, and demographic implications to 2040. GLOBOCAN 2020 was used for cross-sectional estimates of pancreatic cancer incidence and mortality in 185 countries and territories. Continuous annual incidence trends from 2000 to 2017 were estimated from selected non-overlapping CI5plus registry populations with complete coverage over the study period. Age-standardized rates were calculated using the Segi-Doll world standard population. Log-linear models and continuous segmented regression selected by the Bayesian information criterion were used to estimate annual percentage changes (APCs). IARC Cancer Tomorrow fixed-risk demographic projections were used to estimate incident cases through 2040; annual risk-change scenarios of -0.5% and +0.5% were examined as sensitivity analyses. In 2020, an estimated 495,773 pancreatic cancer cases and 466,003 deaths occurred worldwide; the ASIR and ASMR were 4.86 and 4.53 per 100,000, respectively, and the mortality-to-incidence ratio was 0.94. Northern America and Europe had the highest regional ASIRs (8.04 and 7.77), whereas Asia contributed the largest number of cases (233,701). In pooled selected CI5plus populations, incidence increased during 2000-2006 (APC 1.43%, 95% CI 1.27-1.59) and 2006-2017 (APC 1.02%, 95% CI 0.94-1.10). The relative increase was greatest among adults younger than 50 years (APC 1.61%, 95% CI 1.37-1.85), although their absolute rate remained low. Under the fixed-risk demographic scenario, global incident cases were projected to reach 843,772 in 2040, a 70.2% increase from 2020. Pancreatic cancer imposes a substantial and geographically unequal burden, with mortality remaining close to incidence. Combining GLOBOCAN with CI5plus distinguishes contemporary global burden from observed registry-based trends and supports risk-based surveillance, registry strengthening, and health-system capacity planning.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1851636.abstract: To develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model that integrates extracellular volume fraction (ECV) derived from contrast-enhanced CT with clinical and imaging features for preoperative prediction of World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). A retrospective cohort of 263 patients with pathologically confirmed ccRCC from two institutions was analyzed. Patients from Hospital A (n=184) were randomly divided into training (n=128) and internal validation (n=56) cohorts, while patients from Hospital B (n=79) served as an independent external validation cohort. CT-derived ECV, arterial enhancement fraction (AEF), and conventional imaging features were extracted. Six machine learning models (Logistic Regression [LR], eXtreme Gradient Boosting [XGBoost], Gaussian Naive Bayes [GNB], Support Vector Machine [SVM], K-Nearest Neighbors [KNN], Light Gradient Boosting Machine [LightGBM]) were constructed, and the best-performing model was identified based on bootstrap resampling. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Tumor size (low-grade: 4.99 ± 1.98 cm; high-grade: 6.20 ± 2.72 cm, P = 0.002), ECV (low-grade: 0.46 ± 0.09; high-grade: 0.57 ± 0.12, P<0.001), and AEF (low-grade: 1.37 ± 0.24; high-grade: 1.56 ± 0.25, P<0.001) were significantly higher in high-grade ccRCC, while hematocrit (HCT, low-grade: 0.41 ± 0.05; high-grade: 0.38 ± 0.06, P<0.001) was lower. The optimal LR model achieved robust performance: training cohort AUC = 0.995 (95% CI: 0.990-0.999), internal validation AUC = 0.903 (95% CI: 0.818-0.988), external test AUC = 0.857 (95% CI: 0.756-0.958). SHAP analysis showed ECV, tumor diameter, and AEF were the top 3 predictors. An interpretable ML model incorporating CT-derived ECV and imaging features effectively predicts preoperative WHO/ISUP grade of ccRCC, providing a noninvasive tool for individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1853848.abstract: Pancreatitis in patients with hematologic malignancies, particularly lymphoma, is a challenging complication with heterogeneous etiologies. Large studies with systematic etiological classification and prognostic models are lacking. This retrospective multicenter study (2020-2025) included patients with hematologic malignancies who developed acute pancreatitis. Etiologies were adjudicated using predefined criteria. A nomogram-based prediction model was developed with internal bootstrap validation. Among 1,705 patients, 31 (1.82%) developed pancreatitis: 19 lymphoma (61.3%), 9 leukemia (29.0%), and 3 plasma cell disorders (9.7%). In the lymphoma cohort (median age 59 years, 57.9% male), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (47.4%) and peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) (21.1%) were most common. Etiology distribution: treatment-related (36.8%), direct pancreatic infiltration (31.6%), conventional (15.8%), multifactorial (10.5%), and infection-related (5.3%). Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided tissue acquisition had 83.3% diagnostic sensitivity for direct infiltration; positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET-CT) showed a "tetrad sign" in 5/6 cases. Severe pancreatitis occurred in 21.1% of lymphoma-associated pancreatitis. The nomogram (incorporating time to pancreatitis ≤30 days, recent L-asparaginase (LAsp)/immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) exposure, and absence of pancreatic mass) discriminated treatment-related from non-treatment-related etiologies with AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.71-0.96). PTCL subtype (HR 3.12, 95% CI 1.28-7.61, p=0.012), multifactorial etiology (HR 2.56, 95% CI 1.02-6.42, p=0.045), and age ≥65 years (HR 2.01, 95% CI 0.95-4.25, p=0.07) predicted 1-year mortality (C-index 0.79). Lymphoma-associated pancreatitis is rare (1.8% of hematologic malignancies). Treatment-related causes slightly outnumber direct infiltration. EUS-guided tissue acquisition and PET-CT are valuable for differential diagnosis. The nomogram may assist etiological classification and risk stratification, but prospective validation is required.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1856673.abstract: Hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-low (HER2-low) metastatic breast cancer (MBC) constitutes the predominant subtype of advanced breast cancer, with most patients eventually developing resistance to endocrine therapy (ET) and cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i). This case report describes a 64-year-old woman with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-low MBC involving lung, pleural, and lymph node metastases who achieved a remarkable and sustained radiographic complete response (rCR) to palbociclib plus fulvestrant, followed by letrozole after fulvestrant injection intolerance. The patient exhibited near-complete regression of metastatic lesions within 18 months and maintained remission for over 6 years, far exceeding the typical median progression-free survival observed in clinical trials. The prolonged remission observed underscores the existence of biologically distinct tumor subsets with exceptional sensitivity to CDK4/6 inhibition, warranting investigation into underlying molecular mechanisms.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1859581.abstract: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) midline carcinoma (NMC) is an extremely rare, highly aggressive, and poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm that predominantly arises from the midline epithelial structures of the head and neck. It is driven by genetic rearrangements of the NUTM1 gene, with the most common aberration being a translocation that forms a fusion gene with BRD4 on chromosome 19p13.1. The diagnosis of NMC is challenging due to its non-specific clinical and histological features, and it typically requires a combination of immunohistochemical detection of NUT protein and molecular assays to confirm NUTM1 gene rearrangement. The prognosis of NMC is dismal, with a median overall survival of less than one year. To date, no standard treatment regimen has been established, and only individualized therapeutic strategies have been reported in the literature. Herein, we present a case of a 40-year-old female patient with NMC of the left nasal cavity who presented with nasal mass, nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, mild epistaxis, and hyposmia. The patient was diagnosed with NMC based on pathological and immunohistochemical findings, and was staged as T2N0M0. She received multidisciplinary treatment including neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radical surgery, adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) maintenance therapy. Up to the latest follow-up in February 2026, the patient had achieved complete remission with no evidence of tumor recurrence. We conclude that comprehensive and intensive first-line multidisciplinary therapy is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in patients with NMC, a disease with inherently high risks of recurrence and progression and a poor natural prognosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1859604.abstract: Middle-aged and older adults (MAOs; defined as individuals aged ≥40 years) account for the global cancer burden, contributing to 70-80% of cases. Characterizing cancer profiles in this demographic is essential for developing targeted prevention and treatment strategies to mitigate global impacts. Using Global Burden of Diseases (GBD) 2021 data, we analyzed incidence, prevalence, mortality and Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) for 31 cancers among MAOs (aged≥40) across 204 countries/21 regions(1990-2021). Trends were quantified via Joinpoint regression, and autoregressive integrated moving-average (ARIMA) models projected the burden through 2035. Risk attribution utilized population attributable fractions across Socio-demographic Index (SDI) quintiles. An order-independent Shapley decomposition attributed projected cancer incidence changes during 2021-2035 to population growth, aging, and age-specific incidence rate shifts. In 2021, MAOs accounted for 48,804,114 incident cases and 9,434,210 deaths. Females exhibited a 1.14-fold higher age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) than males, yet males had a higher age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR). Projections suggested a continued rise in cancer burden through 2035. Peak incidence occurred in ages 60-69 and the highest mortality in ages 70-79. Breast cancer was the main cancer in females; tracheal/bronchus/lung cancer in males. Tracheal/bronchus/lung cancer dominated mortality across all groups except middle-aged women (breast cancer). High-SDI regions bore the greatest burden, characterized by tracheal/bronchus/lung and colorectal cancers, while low-SDI regions shifted toward breast, cervical and stomach cancer. Risk factor analysis from 2010-2021 revealed rising metabolic risks, with high body mass index (BMI) and fasting plasma glucose-attributable DALYs increasing by 12.39% and 11.36% respectively, especially in high-SDI regions. Conversely, while most behavioral risks declined, smoking remained the leading risk factor, contributing over 60% to lung cancer DALYs. In low-SDI regions, behavioral drivers such as unsafe sex (accounting for >90% of cervical cancer risk) and air pollution remained the dominant persistent risks. This study, the first focusing on MAOs' global cancer burden, reveals heterogeneous patterns by age, gender, and SDI. Lung cancer was the leading cause of death (smoking as main risk). Metabolic risks rose in high-SDI regions, behavioral risks in low-SDI regions. In conclusion, MAOs' cancer burden will rise through 2035; region-specific precision strategies are essential.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1861461.abstract: Recurrence remains common after initial transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). This study aimed to identify routinely available clinicopathological, treatment-related, and inflammatory factors associated with recurrence and to characterize recurrence-free survival (RFS). This retrospective cohort included patients with pathologically confirmed Ta, T1, or primary carcinoma in situ (CIS) who underwent initial TURBT between January 2017 and December 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used as the primary analysis to evaluate factors associated with documented recurrence during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed as a complementary analysis incorporating recurrence timing and censoring. Kaplan-Meier analysis, sensitivity analyses, restricted cubic spline analysis, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and bootstrap-corrected model evaluation were also performed. Among 605 patients, 237 (39.2%) experienced recurrence during a median follow-up of 34.0 months. Multiple tumors were associated with higher recurrence odds and hazard (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.27-2.78; adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.62; 95% CI, 1.25-2.10). Higher recurrence odds and hazards were also associated with increasing tumor diameter, T1 or primary CIS, high-grade pathology, concomitant CIS, and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Maintenance intravesical therapy was inversely associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.34-0.72; adjusted HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.47-0.81). Estimated RFS rates were 81.5%, 63.8%, and 54.1% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The bootstrap-corrected area under the curve was 0.769 for the logistic model, and the bootstrap-corrected Harrell's C-index was 0.739 for the Cox model. Recurrence after initial TURBT was associated with greater tumor burden, adverse pathological characteristics, concomitant CIS, and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Maintenance intravesical therapy showed an inverse observational association with recurrence. These routinely available factors may support postoperative risk stratification and risk-adapted surveillance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1863699.abstract: Clozapine is the gold standard for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). It requires strict monitoring of full blood count (FBC), due to the risk of neutropenia and agranulocytosis. AB is a woman in her mid-40s with TRS, diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. She was commenced on a chemotherapy regimen of docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab. Four days after the initial infusion, AB developed neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count of 0.2 × 109/L. In accordance with local protocols and discussion with the Clozapine Patient Monitoring Service (CPMS), clozapine was immediately discontinued. Two weeks after clozapine cessation, AB displayed catatonic symptoms characterised by mutism, posturing, and automatic obedience, scoring 27 on the Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale (BFCRS). A positive lorazepam challenge confirmed the diagnosis of clozapine-withdrawal catatonia. Despite regular high-dose benzodiazepines and treatment with antipsychotics, AB's presentation continued to deteriorate, characterised by prominent delusions and hallucinations, impeding oncological treatment. AB was seen extensively by liaison psychiatry and treated with high-dose typical and atypical antipsychotics; however, she failed to respond adequately to treatment. Given AB's extensive previous history of management on clozapine without previous haematological disturbance and ongoing decline in mental state, coupled with the timeline of symptoms 4 days after the administration of chemotherapy agents associated with neutropenia, namely, carboplatin, the decision was taken to reinstate clozapine. Following titration of clozapine and transfer to a specialist psychiatric unit, AB's symptoms resolved rapidly, allowing for the successful completion of chemotherapy. Carboplatin was omitted in subsequent cycles, with no further episodes of neutropenia. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of neutropenia in psychiatric patients on clozapine, who are also undergoing treatment for comorbid medical conditions. The presence of neutropenia in clozapine patients may lead to diagnostic overshadowing and delay the diagnosis of the underlying cause of neutropenia, resulting in delays to treatment as well as unnecessary cessation of clozapine and risk of relapse. Furthermore, this case highlights the risk of catatonia associated with the withdrawal of clozapine and the importance of its rapid identification and management. Clinicians should consider differing aetiologies of neutropenia in clozapine patients, especially those undergoing chemotherapy. Furthermore, clinicians should be skilled in recognising catatonia and initiating prompt treatment.
