doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1864354.abstract: Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is an uncommon mesenchymal spindle cell neoplasm (incidence ~1.4 per million). Although most SFT occur in the thoracic cavity, they can also arise in the retroperitoneum, pelvis, head, and neck. While the majority exhibit benign behavior, approximately 5% are associated with paraneoplastic syndromes, most notably Doege-Potter syndrome (DPS). DPS is characterized by non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) resulting from tumor hypersecretion of high-molecular-weight insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2), which saturates insulin and IGF receptors causing refractory, life-threatening hypoglycemia. Due to nonspecific presentation and low incidence, DPS secondary to pelvic SFT is frequently misdiagnosed, underscoring the need for heightened clinical awareness. A 56-year-old man presented to the neurology department with acute loss of consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence. He had a 3-year history of hypertension but no diabetes mellitus. Initial laboratory tests showed a blood glucose of 4.76 mmol/L; however, during hospitalization, he developed recurrent severe hypoglycemia, with a nadir glucose of 1.6 mmol/L. Further biochemical evaluation during fasting hypoglycemia revealed undetectable insulin (<0.2 mIU/L) and low C-peptide (0.14 ng/mL). Contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT demonstrated a 17.8 cm heterogeneously enhancing pelvic mass causing bladder compression and left ureteral displacement. The patient declined preoperative biopsy. Preoperative euglycemia was maintained with continuous intravenous dextrose infusion, and open en bloc surgical resection was performed. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry (positive for STAT6, CD34, and CD99; Ki-67 8%) confirmed an atypical solitary fibrous tumor. Postoperatively, hypoglycemic symptoms resolved completely, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 6 without further hypoglycemic episodes. Pelvic SFT with DPS frequently presents with recurrent hypoglycemia or altered consciousness rather than local compressive symptoms. Early recognition of non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) and prompt cross-sectional imaging are essential for accurate diagnosis. Complete surgical resection is definitive and results in full resolution of hypoglycemia. Given the unpredictable biological behavior of SFT, long-term follow-up is essential. Heightened clinical awareness may improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1865004.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurs frequently after resection. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) mediates tumor angiogenesis, but its post-operative behavior is poorly described. We compared serum VEGF and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) trajectories over the first post-operative year. In this single-center prospective pilot study, 21 patients undergoing curative resection were assessed and 19 analyzed (8 recurrence, 11 non-recurrence). Both markers were measured before surgery and at 3, 6 and 12 months. Trajectories were compared using mixed-effects models with a group × time interaction (time categorical) and a random intercept; VEGF was modeled on the native scale, AFP on the log10 scale. All analyses are exploratory. Eight of 19 patients (42.1%) recurred, at a median of 177.5 days. VEGF trajectories differed between groups (interaction p = 0.041). In the recurrence group, estimated mean VEGF fell from 188.4 to 82.5 pg/mL by 3 months, rose to 103.9 at 6 months and fell to 67.9 at 12 months. Reductions from baseline were significant in the recurrence group only (all p ≤ 0.003). The 6-month rise was not itself significant (+21.2 pg/mL; p = 0.552). Observed VEGF never differed between groups; AFP was higher in the recurrence group at 12 months (15.61 versus 2.04 IU/mL; p = 0.016). Serum VEGF declines markedly after resection, most steeply in patients who recur, and the groups follow different trajectories. The transient six-month rise coincided with the median time to recurrence but was not significant. Given the small, stage-imbalanced cohort, these findings are hypothesis-generating.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1868586.abstract: Oncogenic KRAS mutations drive 25-30% of western lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cases, however the mechanisms that restrain tumor progression remain poorly defined. N-Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (N-WASP) regulates actin cytoskeleton dynamics and epithelial architecture, but its role in KRAS-driven lung tumorigenesis is unclear. We generated a conditional N-WASP knockout in KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma mice (N-WASPLKO/KRASG12D) using Sftpc-CreERT2, and assessed N-WASP knockdown A549 cells (A549KD) in 3D culture for tumor burden, ERK signaling, transcriptomic changes, and E-cadherin expression. Conditional deletion of N-WASP in type II alveolar cells (N-WASPLKO) markedly increased tumor number and size in KRASG12D mice. The tumors isolated from these mice retained strong pro-surfactant protein C expression, confirming alveolar epithelial origin and predominantly adopted a solid growth pattern, indicative of disrupted epithelial organization. Mechanistically, N-WASP loss enhanced KRAS-driven ERK1/2 activation in lung tissue, consistent with increased mitogenic signaling. In A549 cells, N-WASP deficiency disrupted cytoskeletal architecture, promoted proliferation, and impaired cell-cell adhesion, recapitulating in vivo tumor phenotypes. A kinase inhibitor screen identified Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity as a driver of this hyperproliferative phenotype, with ROCK inhibition normalizing proliferation in N-WASP-deficient cells, linking elevated Rho/ROCK signaling to the increased ERK1/2 activation observed upon N-WASP loss. Transcriptomic profiling of N-WASP-deficient lungs revealed coordinated upregulation of genes regulating proliferation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and tumor-promoting pathways, alongside downregulation of epithelial differentiation and adhesion programs. These results establish N-WASP as a critical suppressor of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma, linking cytoskeletal integrity to oncogenic signaling and transcriptional regulation. Our findings highlight the interplay between actin dynamics, epithelial architecture, and KRAS signaling, suggesting that targeting N-WASP dependent pathways could modulate lung cancer aggressiveness and offer novel therapeutic opportunities.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1870939.abstract: Advances in pediatric oncology treatment have had a positive impact on the childhood cancer survival rates across the world. Despite this, children who are receiving treatment can experience treatment related physical impairments such as fatigue, muscle weakness, less mobility, and various day to day functional limitations, and this can quietly harm their quality of life. In this context, the need for physical rehabilitation increases as it supports physical functioning and generally supports well-being throughout the duration of treatment. Despite the increase in evidence showing that rehabilitation matters in pediatric oncology, the use of physiotherapy services stays uneven, especially in low- and middle-income countries, including India. Parents, who act as the main caregivers as key healthcare decision makers, strongly shape whether and how their child can take part in rehabilitation. However, the evidence on how Indian parents experience and make sense of physiotherapy rehabilitation during their child's cancer journey is limited. Therefore, this study is designed to explore and understand the lived experiences and meaning-making of Indian parents regarding physiotherapy rehabilitation during their child's cancer treatment. A phenomenological qualitative design will be employed in this study to investigate the lived experiences of Indian parents of children with cancer who are receiving physiotherapy rehabilitation. The participants who have a child aged 8-17years diagnosed with cancer and exposed to physiotherapy will be parents or primary caregiver of children will be recruited from a pediatric oncology center at a tertiary care hospital by using a purposive sampling method. Data will be collected from 8-17years old child's parents or primary caregiver of children diagnosed with cancer and exposed to physiotherapy until data and thematic saturation is achieved. Data collection will be carried out through semi-structured in-depth interviews in English or Kannada using an interview schedule. The interview schedule will be validated by experts using the Content Validity Index and the Delphi technique. The interviews will be audio recorded, transcribed and translated in the language used for the interview and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's approach of reflexive thematic analysis. Trustworthiness, credibility, confirmability, dependability, and transferability will be achieved through bracketing, reflexivity, independent coding, and audit trail. This phenomenological study will offer valuable insights into the meaning of physiotherapy rehabilitation to Indian parents in the context of pediatric oncology and how it is experienced. An understanding of parental beliefs, expectations, emotions and barriers to physiotherapy rehabilitation will potentially help guide culturally appropriate, family-centered rehabilitation interventions and facilitate the integration of physiotherapy into pediatric oncology care pathways in low- and middle-income settings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1874176.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a malignant tumor characterized by high recurrence and metastasis rates, as well as a poor prognosis. Cuproptosis is a form of programmed cell death driven by abnormal copper-ion metabolism. Existing studies have shown that its occurrence is closely regulated and associated with the progression of HCC. However, it is still unclear how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) control the process in HCC. The purpose of this work is to clarify how the lncRNA AP003469.2 influences cuproptosis and promotes the development of HCC. This study utilized RNA sequencing data from the TCGA-LIHC dataset to screen for cuproptosis-related lncRNAs exhibiting significant expression differences. Following the initial screening, the expression of lncRNA AP003469.2 was validated using qRT-PCR. Subsequent in vitro and in vivo studies confirmed AP003469.2's biological role in HCC. To understand the fundamental mechanisms, we determined the subcellular localization of the proteins using nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). The regulatory relationships between miR-4732-3p and LIPT1 and between AP003469.2 and miR-4732-3p were then verified using dual-luciferase reporter assays. In addition, we utilized Western blotting, copper assays, CCK-8, and immunohistochemistry to evaluate related proteins and markers indicative of cuproptosis. A poor prognosis was observed to be positively correlated with elevated expression of AP003469.2 in HCC. In both in vivo and in vitro experimental methods, AP003469.2 stimulated important malignant characteristics in HCC cells, including invasion, migration, and proliferation. Furthermore, by controlling LIPT1 expression and modulating copper homeostasis and important proteins, including FDX1, SLC31A1, and HSP70, AP003469.2 acts as a molecular sponge for miR-4732-3p, attenuating cuproptosis. Our research demonstrated that the AP003469.2/miR-4732-3p/LIPT1 axis could suppress cuproptosis to promote HCC progression. Therefore, AP003469.2 may serve as a target for HCC treatment or diagnosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1874176.title: LncRNA AP003469.2 promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression by regulating cuproptosis via the miR-4732-3p/LIPT1 axis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1874405.abstract: Availability of clinical trials for prostate cancer in the US varies greatly by region. County-level analyses are vital to characterize healthcare access, disease burden, and population-level disparities. Utilizing the ClinicalTrials.gov trial database, we collated all interventional prostate cancer trials between June 1, 2019, and June 1, 2025. We compiled data on county characteristics along with Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) designations derived from the CDC, NCI, and the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry data. A zero-inflated negative binomial regression model was used to evaluate trial availability. Trial characteristics were summarized using descriptive analysis. We found 884 eligible trials. Among 3,145 counties, only 631 had at least one clinical trial over the study period. Most trials (51%) included patients with metastatic disease. Sixteen percent of trials investigated curative treatments, while 65% examined palliative interventions. The majority of studies (52.5%) had funding from pharmaceutical companies. There was no significant relationship between trial availability and incidence or mortality rates. Among counties with at least one trial, those with a low SVI had twice as many trials per household when compared to those with high SVI (IRR 2.05, 95% CI 1.54 - 2.74, p<0.001). Counties with no trials were more rural (72.3% vs 22.0%) and had fewer specialist physicians (17.1% vs 69.1%). Prostate cancer trials are disproportionately concentrated in the US, with lower representation in vulnerable areas. Expanding trial access to underserved areas is a crucial step in promoting equitable access to care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1876642.abstract: This study aimed to relieve radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) by assessing the use of prophylactic pirfenidone. Subjects were lung cancer patients with prior ICI treatment who received thoracic radiotherapy. Patients with lung cancer were enrolled in this phase II single-arm study. All candidates had a history of prior ICI exposure (≥2 cycles; interval ≤6 months) scheduled for thoracic radiotherapy (≥50 Gy). Patients received oral pirfenidone (1800 mg/day) from one week pre-radiotherapy to four weeks post-completion. The primary endpoint was the 6-month incidence of ≥grade 2 RILI, compared to a 40% historical control (p0=0.40; p1=0.22; α=0.10; power=80%). Secondary endpoints included pulmonary function (DLCO%, FVC%) and safety. A total of 39 patients were enrolled in this trial. At the 6-month follow-up, the incidence of grade 2 or higher RILI was 23.1% (9/39; 95% CI: 11.1%-39.3%). This rate was statistically significantly lower than the 40% incidence from the historical control cohort (p=0.0205). Grade 3 RILI occurred in 7.7% (3/39); no grade 4-5 events occurred. Mean DLCO% declined by 7.6 ± 5.4% at 3 months and 6.5 ± 5.8% at 6 months. The pirfenidone completion rate was 84.6% (median relative dose intensity: 89.3%). Common adverse events were fatigue (43.6%), nausea (41.0%), and appetite loss (33.3%), mostly grade 1-2. Preventive use of pirfenidone was associated with a lower observed incidence and severity of RILI than the predefined historical control in ICI-pretreated lung cancer patients receiving thoracic radiotherapy. Additionally, the intervention showed a potential protective trend for pulmonary diffusion function. These findings require further validation in a phase III trial.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1876656.abstract: Oxaliplatin-induced hypersensitivity reactions (HSRs) can interrupt clinically indicated treatment for gastrointestinal malignancies. We evaluated the early implementation of a multidisciplinary oxaliplatin desensitization pathway at Vinmec Times City International Hospital. We conducted a retrospective case series of patients who underwent oxaliplatin desensitization between 2022 and 2025 following an index HSR. Clinical characteristics, skin testing results, desensitization procedures, breakthrough reactions (BTRs), and subsequent oxaliplatin treatment completion were reviewed. Ten patients underwent desensitization after index HSRs occurring at a median of six oxaliplatin cycles (range, 2-11); six index reactions were Brown grade 2. Skin prick testing was negative in all patients, whereas intradermal testing was positive in six, negative in three, and equivocal in one. Three patients initially underwent a three-bag desensitization procedure and seven a four-bag procedure. Eight BTRs occurred in six patients, none requiring epinephrine. Seven patients completed all additional oxaliplatin cycles planned by their oncology team, receiving a median of four additional cycles. Three patients discontinued oxaliplatin after BTRs: two because of recurrent reactions despite procedure modification and one because the patient declined further treatment after a single BTR in the metastatic setting. Multidisciplinary oxaliplatin desensitization enabled most patients in this early case series to continue and complete planned oxaliplatin treatment, although BTRs were common. Given the small, retrospective cohort, these findings are descriptive and require further study to establish comparative safety or efficacy, superiority of a specific desensitization procedure, or predictors of treatment completion.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1878061.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain major diagnostic challenges because classification often depends on modality-specific evidence that is stored in separate public datasets. This study evaluates a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework using two independent and unpaired data sources: colorectal histopathological image patches and structured HCC clinical-biochemical records. The study is therefore positioned as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets. The CNN branch extracts spatial and glandular texture features from curated CRC image patches, whereas the LSTM branch treats fixed-order clinical attributes as a structured feature sequence to learn inter-feature dependencies in the HCC records. Under internal public-dataset testing with bootstrap uncertainty estimation, the full CNN + LSTM + MLP framework achieved an accuracy of 0.978 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), Macro-F1 of 0.977 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), and Macro OVR AUC of 0.997 (95% CI, 0.996-0.998). Ablation and baseline comparisons showed lower performance for CNN only (accuracy 0.938), LSTM only (0.875), clinical encoder only (0.890), CNN + LSTM (0.966), CNN + clinical MLP (0.958), late fusion (0.952), EfficientNet-B0-style fusion (0.970), ViT-tiny-style fusion (0.960), XGBoost (0.910), random forest (0.900), and logistic regression (0.875). The full model also exceeded the EfficientNet-B0-style baseline in Macro AUC by 0.003 (95% CI, 0.002-0.004; paired bootstrap P = 0.007; McNemar exact P = 0.011). Grad-CAM and SHAP analyses are used to interpret branch-specific decisions, while the findings remain limited to internal public-dataset validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1878424.abstract: Although multiple instruments exist to assess frailty, it remains unclear whether the association between frailty and clinical outcomes in older colorectal cancer (CRC) patients varies by the assessment tool used. Accordingly, the aim of this study was to compare the feasibility and clinical utility of four common frailty scales in this patient population. We conducted a 3-year prospective cohort study involving geriatric patients (≥65 years) with CRC. Preoperative frailty was assessed using four established scales: the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), the Frailty Phenotype (FP), the Geriatric-8 (G-8) scale, and the 32-item Frailty Index (FI). The differences in the perioperative outcomes and postoperative one-year all-cause mortality rate were compared across the four scoring systems. A total of 1,096 patients were included in the primary analysis. The effective response rates and median completion times for the four frailty scales were as follows: CFS (91.1%; 6 min), FP (65.7%; 10 min), G-8 (71.6%; 8 min), and 32-item FI (58.3%; 18 min). The final analysis included 615 patients who completed all assessments. Frailty prevalence was estimated at 27.0% (CFS), 23.6% (FP), 33.0% (G-8), and 36.9% (FI). The four frailty scales demonstrated good predictive efficacy for postoperative clinically relevant complications, postoperative recovery, 30-day readmission, and one-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that the G-8 scale (OR = 2.412, 95%CI: 1.300-4.474, P = 0.008) and 32-item FI (OR = 3.035, 95%CI: 1.359-6.779, P = 0.017) served as independent risk factors for postoperative clinically relevant complications. Only the 32-item FI emerged as an independent predictor of 1-year all-cause mortality (HR = 2.777, 95%CI: 1.247-6.218, P = 0.020). In conclusion, all four frailty scales demonstrated robust discriminatory capacity for clinical outcomes in older CRC patients. Although the 32-item FI exhibited a stronger independent correlation with adverse outcomes following multivariate adjustment, its clinical utility must be weighed against a longer administration time. This study provides crucial evidence to guide the selection of an appropriate frailty assessment tool based on specific clinical contexts.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1883338.abstract: Although bladder cancer mortality has modestly declined in the United States, co-occurring substance use disorders (SUDs) may contribute to adverse outcomes and widening health disparities among affected individuals. This study evaluated temporal trends in mortality involving both bladder cancer and SUDs in the United States between 1999 and 2023. Mortality data related to patients aged ≥25 were obtained from the CDC WONDER Database. Deaths involving bladder cancer were identified using ICD-10 code C67 in combination with ICD-10 codes F10-F19 for substance use disorders listed among multiple causes of death. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated and Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Between 1999 and 2023, 63,258 deaths involving both bladder cancer and SUDs were identified. Overall, the AAMR increased significantly at an annual average percentage change (AAPC) of 13.38% (95% CI: 10.69-16.14). Males had a substantially higher mortality burden than females (50,299 vs 12,959). White individuals and adults aged ≥85 were accounted for the largest mortality burden. Mortality rates were consistently higher in nonmetropolitan populations and increased across all U.S. census regions. Mortality involving bladder cancer and coexisting SUDs increased over time and mirrored broader national substance-related mortality trends. These findings support integrated oncology- and addiction-focused care approaches, as well as public health strategies aimed at improving access to cancer care, addiction treatment, and rural health services.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1884458.abstract: To describe the management of recurrent lumbar schwannomas located within the intertransverse space and psoas compartment using a single-incision hybrid approach that combines open surgery with Arthroscopic-Assisted Uniportal Spinal Surgery (AUSS). A 78-year-old woman presented with a 1-month history of low back pain and left-sided radiculopathy. Seventeen years earlier, she had undergone lumbar schwannoma removal. MRI revealed multiple recurrent tumors along the left L4 nerve root, including lesions in the paraspinal and deep intertransverse-psoas compartments. A hybrid surgical strategy was employed: superficial tumors were resected via an open approach, and deeper lesions were removed endoscopically using AUSS through the same incision. All tumors were successfully excised en bloc. AUSS provided high-definition visualization that facilitated circumferential dissection of a tumor densely adherent to the L4 nerve root. The patient experienced rapid relief of symptoms postoperatively, with complete resolution of radicular pain. Follow-up CT/MRI confirmed full tumor resection and adequate neural decompression. Histopathology confirmed multiple schwannomas. A combined open-AUSS approach through a single incision offers a feasible and safe option for treating recurrent lumbar schwannomas extending across multiple anatomical compartments. This hybrid strategy minimizes tissue disruption and may represent an effective alternative for managing complex recurrent paraspinal tumors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885291.abstract: Prostate cancer is one of the most commonly diagnosed cancers in men worldwide. Radiation therapy is a widely used treatment for prostate cancer, but it carries the risk of adverse effects on adjacent organs such as the rectum. Therefore, to provide additional protection for the rectum during prostate radiation, perirectal spacers are inserted into Denonvilliers’ space, the thin fascial layer located behind the prostate gland and in front of the anterior rectal wall. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based hydrogels and recently FDA-approved stabilized hyaluronic acid (sHA) spacers have been designed to create a biodegradable space between the prostate and rectum, with each having its own unique characteristics and both having the potential to infiltrate the rectum. We present two clinical cases of rectal infiltration associated with either the insertion of a PEG-based hydrogel or an sHA spacer. Due to the distinct characteristics of the two spacer types, rectal infiltration was managed with either a conservative or definitive approach. With the PEG-based hydrogel, we implemented conservative management with antibiotics and close monitoring. In sharp contrast, for the sHA spacer, we proactively reversed the infiltration with hyaluronidase (Hyal) prior to starting radiation. These cases illustrate the clinical utility of these management approaches and contribute to the growing body of evidence on the management of potential complications associated with perirectal spacers, potentially supporting the use of newer spacer technologies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885302.abstract: The optimal local treatment strategy for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC) following neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) remains controversial. This study aimed to compare the survival outcomes and recurrence patterns of radical surgery and definitive radiotherapy (RT) following NICT in patients with LA-ESCC. Patients with LA-ESCC who underwent NICT (2019-2023) were enrolled and categorized into surgery or RT groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) and Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). The differences in recurrence patterns between the two groups were compared. A total of 278 patients were included, comprising 218 (78.4%) and 60 (21.6%) patients in the surgery and RT groups, respectively. After PSM, the surgery group (n=117) maintained a significant OS benefit over the RT group (n=60) (3-year OS rates: 72.1% vs. 59.5%; P = 0.028), whereas the PFS rates were comparable between the two groups (3-year PFS rates: 59.4% vs. 46.9%; P = 0.12). For patients with upper esophageal cancer, RT showed a trend toward improved survival (3-year PFS rates: 76.9% vs. 55.5%, P = 0.34; 3-year OS rates: 74.0% vs. 61.8%, P = 0.50). Among the responders after NICT (near-cCR/cPR), PFS and OS were similar between the surgery and RT groups (3-year PFS rates: 68.9% vs. 66.9%, P = 0.64; 3-year OS rates: 80.2% vs. 70.7%, P = 0.20). Regional lymph node recurrence predominated in the surgery group (50.0%), whereas locoregional esophageal recurrence was most frequent in the RT group (37.0%). The treatment-related mortality rates were 0.8% (1/117) in the surgery group and 1.7% (1/60) in the RT group, indicating the overall safety of the treatments. Radical surgery remains the standard treatment for LA-ESCC after NICT. Definitive RT may be an organ-preserving option in selected patients, especially those with upper esophageal cancer or a favorable response to NICT.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885312.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monitoring. A key focus is on integrating AI with multi-omics data, including proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to support precision oncology and personalized treatments. We address important validation challenges, like model interpretability, data quality, and regulatory issues that must be solved before AI can be widely used in clinics. By summarizing current evidence and targeting research gaps, this review offers a clear view of how AI is enhancing the discovery, personalization, and validation of anticancer treatments.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885498.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate whether voxel-level IVIM-based habitat analysis supports exploratory pretreatment stratification of Ki-67 proliferation status in cervical cancer. Between January 2019 and June 2025, medical records of 149 patients with histopathologically confirmed cervical cancer were initially screened. Before image-quality assessment, 49 were excluded because IVIM MRI had been performed after chemoradiotherapy (n = 5), cervical biopsy sampling (n = 21), or lesion excision (n = 10), or because no pathological Ki-67 immunohistochemistry result was available (n = 13). Of the remaining 100 patients, 17 were excluded because of severe image artefacts (n = 11) or lesions too small for reliable ROI delineation (n = 6), leaving 83 patients for analysis. Patients were stratified into high Ki-67 (Ki-67 >70%, n = 38) and low/equal Ki-67 (Ki-67 ≤70%, n = 45) groups. Solid-tumour regions were analysed with patient-level K-means clustering using normalised D, f, and ADC features; D* was excluded from clustering because of voxel-level fitting instability. Habitat labels were harmonised according to quantitative parameter profiles and treated as image-defined phenotypes. Habitat-derived features, conventional ROI parameters, and logistic models were evaluated for Ki-67 stratification. Hab1 ADC was lower in the high- than in the low/equal-Ki-67 group (median [Q1-Q3], 0.947 [0.862-1.161] vs. 1.257 [1.113-1.455] × 10-3 mm2/s; P < 0.001; BH q = 2.04×10-6), whereas Hab3 volume proportion was higher (0.396 [0.341-0.488] vs. 0.279 [0.190-0.390]; P = 0.002; BH q = 0.006). Hab1 ADC outperformed conventional ROI ADC for identifying high Ki-67 status [AUC, 0.826 (95% CI, 0.726-0.909) vs. 0.563 (95% CI, 0.429-0.695); paired DeLong P < 0.001]. The combined Hab1 ADC and Hab3 volume proportion model showed the numerically highest discrimination (apparent AUC, 0.877; 95% CI, 0.794-0.938), but this numerical improvement over Hab1 ADC alone was not statistically significant (paired DeLong P = 0.056). Fixed-feature leave-one-out validation of the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.771-0.923) and a Brier score of 0.157 (95% CI, 0.112-0.204). IVIM-based habitat analysis showed exploratory potential for non-invasive Ki-67 stratification by isolating a low-diffusivity imaging compartment otherwise obscured by conventional whole-tumour averaging. The combined habitat model should be interpreted as a research-stage imaging biomarker, not a clinical decision tool, and requires prospective external validation before clinical translation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885499.abstract: Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are characterized by a low mutational burden and limited recurrent driver mutations, suggesting that other mechanisms contribute to tumor development. One of the most frequent genomic alterations in SI-NETs is loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 18 (chr18del), which defines a major molecular subtype. However, the epigenetic consequences of this event remain poorly understood. In this study, we used long-read whole-genome sequencing to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in twelve primary tumors. Native methylation detection and copy-number profiling enabled stratification of tumors according to chromosome 18 status and direct comparison of epigenetic states between chr18del and non-chr18del (diploid) tumors. Chr18del tumors displayed widespread hypomethylation relative to diploid tumors, while chromosome 18 showed spatially structured regional methylation differences, including localized regions of increased methylation. Cross-platform validation using an independent Illumina EPIC methylation cohort confirmed the direction and distribution of many methylation events. Integration with the corresponding transcriptomic dataset revealed that a subset of methylation changes was associated with differential gene expression consistent with established promoter- and gene-body methylation models. Functional categorization of these methylation states revealed regulatory patterns linked to neuronal signaling, intracellular signaling cascades, and interactions with the extracellular matrix. Together, these findings support an association between chromosome 18 status and widespread methylation differences that extend beyond the affected chromosome and are linked to transcriptional programs relevant to neuroendocrine tumor biology.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885566.abstract: Mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is uncommon in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP-NETs), yet it represents a critical biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) eligibility. Treatment-associated reduction or loss of MMR protein expression, often without corresponding MSI-H, has been reported in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but comparable changes have not been described in neuroendocrine tumours. Persistent discordance between immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based MMR protein assessment and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an emerging and clinically challenging phenomenon. We report a 55-year-old woman initially diagnosed with rectal NET Grade 1 on endoscopic biopsy; the tumour was upgraded to NET Grade 2 (Ki-67 approximately 20%) on the surgical resectionk specimen. Hepatic metastases were confirmed four months after resection. The first liver biopsy (January 16, 2026) demonstrated partial MMR protein loss by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2+, MSH6-, PMS2-), while concurrent NGS showed microsatellite stability (MSS) and a tumour mutational burden (TMB) of <1 mut/Mb. The patient received two cycles of surufatinib 250 mg orally once daily combined with intravenous carboplatin (500 mg, day 1) and etoposide (160 mg, days 1-3). Restaging CT demonstrated disease progression. A repeat liver biopsy (March 17, 2026) revealed complete loss of all four MMR proteins by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2-, MSH6-, PMS2-), while NGS again confirmed MSS and TMB <1 mut/Mb. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of apparent progressive complete MMR protein loss in the context of sequential platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal NET Grade 2, with persistent IHC-NGS discordance throughout. These findings raise an important question regarding how IHC-defined dMMR should be interpreted in the absence of NGS-confirmed MSI-H, and highlight the complexity of immunotherapy eligibility decisions in rare tumour types. Prospective data are needed to guide clinical practice.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1888445.abstract: Mixed-grade glioma surgical cohorts exhibit highly variable low-grade glioma (LGG) proportions across studies. This meta-analysis quantifies pooled LGG proportions to provide cohort-level epidemiological benchmarks for researchers, with applications in clinical trial design, health economics, and institutional benchmarking. A single-arm meta-analysis of 191 cohort studies (25,847 patients) with Grade II numerators and denominators from Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, and Scopus (PRISMA 2020) used Freeman-Tukey random-effects synthesis with Cochrane risk-of-bias assessments; subgroup analyses examined study design, geography, era, molecular specificity, and interventions; sensitivity analyses tested robustness. The pooled LGG proportion was 57% (95% CI: 52%-61%; I²=99%; n=191). Mixed LGG/high-grade gliomas (HGG) cohorts showed 41% (32%-50%; 45 studies, 6,847 patients) versus 82% (77%-88%) in pure WHO Grade II cohorts (25 studies). Surgery-only cohorts demonstrated 46% (33%-59%) versus 86% (74%-98%) with targeted therapies, and 93% (90%-96%) in randomized controlled trials. Sensitivity analyses confirmed stability (50%-62%). In mixed-grade glioma cohorts, an LGG proportion approaching 60% may serve as a cohort-level epidemiological reference for understanding the historical grade composition of mixed surgical series. This meta-analysis primary value lies in applications such as clinical trial design, health economics and epidemiological modeling, and institutional benchmarking. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261323907.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1888804.abstract: Colon cancer is a leading global malignancy influenced by genetic, environmental, and microbial factors. This study integrates ecological theories, including Hubbell's neutral theory, augmented by Ning et al.'s (2019, PNAS) stochasticity analysis framework, and classic niche theory, to assess the contributions of stochastic colonization and deterministic niche selection in shaping microbiome assembly and dynamics in colon cancer tissues. Specialist species were identified using Levins' niche breadth analysis. By reanalyzing the datasets from Nejman et al., including 22 normal adjacent tissue (NT) and 22 primary tumor (PT) samples, we find: (i) deterministic niche selection appears to dominate community assembly and diversity maintenance in both NT and PT microbiomes, as demonstrated by the normalized stochasticity ratio (NSR: 0.267 for NT, 0.287 for PT; both below 0.5; Wilcoxon PT>NT, p=0.027). Only 18.2% NT and 27.3% PT samples fit the neutral model, confirming stochastic drift plays a limited role and niche selection predominates in structuring tissue microbiomes. (ii) Through niche breadth analysis, we identified 106 specialist species, of which 14 are known CRC-associated taxa, including Fusobacterium nucleatum, Escherichia coli, Enterococcus faecalis, and Peptostreptococcus anaerobius. These species have established roles in inflammation, genotoxicity, immune modulation, and chemoresistance. (iii) These findings suggest that deterministic niche-based selection, rather than stochastic colonization, appears to govern microbial community assembly in colon cancer tissues. (iv) We postulate that the tumor microenvironment imposes biochemical filters-including hypoxia, lactate accumulation, and altered pH-that select for specialist species capable of adapting to these conditions. (v) While the sample size is modest and validation in independent cohorts is needed, our study demonstrates an integrative framework for understanding colon cancer microbiome dynamics. We propose testable hypotheses for future research: (i) specialist species abundance may correlate with tumor stage or patient survival; (2) depletion of specialists may alter tumor progression in preclinical models; and (3) hybrid neutral-niche models may better fit larger longitudinal datasets. By integrating ecological theory with microbiome research, this study offers insights into the forces driving microbial community assembly in tumor tissues and highlights potential targets for microbiome-based diagnostics and therapeutics.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1889495.abstract: Evidence on prostate cancer (PCa) knowledge and PSA-related testing behavior in Palestine remains limited. We assessed general awareness, factual knowledge, willingness to undergo PSA testing if offered, reported prior PSA testing/prostate examination, and factors associated with prior testing. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey from 19 November to 21 December 2025 among adult men aged 18 years or older recruited from Palestinian communities. The full cohort comprised 1,047 consenting participants. The exported dataset contained two incompatible response formats for the 12 factual knowledge items; composite knowledge analyses were therefore limited to 568 respondents with complete, unambiguous single Yes/No responses. Knowledge was scored from 0 to 12 using the study answer key. Willingness and prior testing were analyzed as binary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression assessed factors associated with prior testing. Mean age was 28.7 ± 12.4 years and 78.6% were aged 18-39 years. Overall, 80.0% had heard of PCa, 26.1% had heard of PSA testing, 31.2% were willing to undergo PSA testing if offered, and 5.6% reported prior PSA testing and/or prostate examination. Among the 568 scorable knowledge respondents, mean knowledge was 7.07 ± 1.84 of 12 and 89.1% had limited knowledge (<80% correct); KR-20 was 0.235. Adequate knowledge was associated with lower willingness (12.9% vs 32.8%; p=0.002) but not prior testing (3.2% vs 6.1%; p=0.526). In the full cohort, older age (aOR 1.08 per year; 95% CI 1.05-1.10), healthcare background (aOR 2.10; 95% CI 1.17-3.77), and first-degree family history (aOR 2.22; 95% CI 1.01-4.86) were independently associated with prior testing. Among never-tested participants, the leading reported barriers were low perceived personal risk (55.3%) and lack of physician/healthcare-provider recommendation (43.1%); multiple responses were allowed. In this predominantly young online sample, general awareness exceeded detailed factual knowledge, while willingness and reported prior testing were low. The divergence between knowledge and behavior should be interpreted cautiously because knowledge analyses used a restricted subset and the shortened scale had low internal consistency. Findings support culturally appropriate, risk-adapted clinician-patient communication and further validation of locally adapted measurement tools.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1890109.abstract: Lymph node (LN) involvement is a critical determinant of staging and prognosis in Wilms tumor (WT). However, conventional binary nodal staging (positive vs. negative) is often compromised by significant variability in surgical lymph node sampling. The lymph node ratio (LNR), which integrates metastatic burden and sampling adequacy, has emerged as a potential prognostic alternative. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether LNR serves as an independent predictor of survival outcomes in children with WT. A systematic query of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov was executed, covering the period from their earliest records through May 10, 2026. Retrospective cohort studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) or risk ratios (RRs) for survival outcomes based on LNR in children with WT were included. Overall survival (OS) was the primary outcome; 5-year, 10-year, and 20-year OS were secondary outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by LNR cutoff (≥0.40 vs. <0.40). Six retrospective cohort studies involving 4,190 patients met the inclusion criteria. High LNR was significantly associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.67-2.64). This prognostic significance persisted across secondary outcomes, including 5-year OS (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.11-1.17), 10-year OS (RR = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.15-1.23), and 20-year OS (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.10-1.19). Subgroup analysis revealed no significant interaction based on the LNR cutoff (P = 0.74). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness and stability of the pooled findings. Higher LNR appears to be associated with poorer overall survival in children with WT and may serve as a useful prognostic indicator. By accounting for both nodal disease burden and surgical effort, LNR may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional nodal status. While LNR represents a valuable adjunct for individualized treatment decisions, prospective studies are required to establish standardized clinical cut-offs and integrate LNR into formal risk-adapted protocols. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261396220.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1891182.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. Pachymic acid (PA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from Poria cocos, exhibits antitumor activity, but its effects on CRC and the involvement of PTPN1 remain unclear. This study investigated whether PTPN1 downregulation contributes to PA-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in HCT-116 CRC cells. Cell proliferation and migration were evaluated using viability, DNA synthesis, colony formation, wound healing, and transwell assays. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis-related proteins, and the subcellular distribution of cytochrome c and Bax were examined. PTPN1 expression and overexpression rescue experiments were used to assess its functional involvement. PA inhibited cell proliferation and migration, increased ROS levels, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. These changes were accompanied by increased Bax, Bim, and cleaved caspase-3 expression, decreased Bcl-2 expression, and cytochrome c release from mitochondria into the cytoplasm. PA also downregulated PTPN1 expression. PTPN1 overexpression attenuated the effects of PA on proliferation, migration, ROS accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential, and apoptosis-related protein expression. It also attenuated cytochrome c redistribution. These findings support a contribution of PTPN1 downregulation to PA-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in HCT-116 cells. Validation in additional CRC models, normal colonic epithelial cells, and in vivo systems is needed to establish the generalizability and therapeutic relevance of these findings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893041.abstract: To compare the therapeutic outcomes of neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery (NACT-IDS) and primary debulking surgery (PDS) in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (AEOC) and to evaluate factors associated with prognosis. This retrospective study included 97 patients with AEOC treated between April 2015 and July 2020. According to treatment strategy, 36 patients underwent PDS and 61 underwent NACT-IDS. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and perioperative outcomes were compared between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate survival outcomes. Additional adjusted models were used to account for baseline imbalance. Because CA-125 normalization occurred after treatment initiation, it was defined as a serum CA-125 concentration of ≤35 U/mL and analyzed as a time-dependent covariate. Significant baseline differences were observed between the groups in age, BMI, baseline CA-125 level, and FIGO stage (all P<0.05). During a median follow-up of 43 months [95% CI (39.87, 50.32)], 53 of 97 patients (54.64%) died. Median OS was 41 months in the PDS group and 43 months in the NACT-IDS group, and median PFS was 20 months in both groups. No significant differences were found in unadjusted OS or PFS between the groups (OS: log-rank P = 0.484; PFS: log-rank P = 0.410). After adjustment for age, BMI, log-transformed baseline CA-125 level, and FIGO stage, treatment strategy was not associated with OS [adjusted HR = 0.88, 95% CI (0.49, 1.58), P = 0.667] or PFS [adjusted HR = 1.07, 95% CI (0.64, 1.79), P = 0.798]. Patients who achieved complete cytoreduction (R0) had longer median OS than those with incomplete cytoreduction (R1+R2) [43 vs. 38 months, P = 0.025] and longer median PFS [22 vs. 18 months, P = 0.040]. After adjustment, NACT-IDS remained associated with shorter operation time, lower intraoperative blood loss, earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy, and a lower likelihood of drainage-tube placement, whereas its association with postoperative complications was no longer statistically significant. Residual disease was associated with higher mortality [adjusted HR = 2.61, 95% CI 1.10-6.18, P = 0.029]. CA-125 normalization was associated with lower hazards of death [time-dependent adjusted HR = 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.99, P = 0.047] and progression or death [time-dependent adjusted HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.42-0.95, P = 0.026]. In this exploratory single-center retrospective non-randomized cohort, NACT-IDS was associated with shorter operation time, lower intraoperative blood loss, earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy, and less frequent drainage-tube placement than PDS, but not with a significantly lower adjusted postoperative complication rate or with OS or PFS. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent survival efficacy or causal treatment benefit. Residual disease was associated with poorer survival, whereas documented CA-125 normalization showed a favorable time-dependent prognostic association.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893803.abstract: Malignant ascites is a common, severe complication of advanced solid tumors, driven by multifactorial pathogenesis, including impaired lymphatic drainage, vascular endothelial growth factor-induced vascular hyperpermeability, pro-permeability inflammatory cytokines, and profound peritoneal immunosuppression. Clinically, it correlates with poor prognosis, reduced overall survival, and substantial quality-of-life deterioration. Current treatment remains predominantly palliative: repeated large-volume paracentesis offers transient symptom relief, fails to prevent reaccumulation, and carries procedural risks. Emerging evidence indicates malignant ascites is not merely passive fluid accumulation but an active, immunosuppressive niche shaped by bidirectional crosstalk among tumor cells, stromal components, diverse immune subsets (e.g., regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, dysfunctional CD8+ T cells), and soluble mediators. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in immunomodulatory treatment for malignant ascites, with an emphasis on strategies targeting the ascitic immune microenvironment. Intraperitoneal administration of immune checkpoint inhibitors has shown acceptable safety and preliminary activity in early-phase single-arm trials, although confirmatory data from larger controlled studies are lacking. In randomized trials, the T-cell engager catumaxomab prolonged puncture-free survival, while the bispecific antibody M701 has shown similar benefits in a phase II randomized controlled study; these findings support further investigation of localized T-cell redirection. Preclinical and early-phase clinical studies suggest that intraperitoneal oncolytic viruses can induce immunogenic tumor cell death and T-cell activation, with single-cell analyses indicating remodeling of the ascitic immune microenvironment. Future directions include integrating ascites immune phenotyping, patient-derived organoids for drug sensitivity testing, and machine learning-based decision support to guide personalized immunotherapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893907.abstract: Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) accounts for approximately 85% of all CRC cases and exhibits limited responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), representing a major challenge in current cancer immunotherapy. At the tumor-cell intrinsic level, low tumor mutational burden (TMB), impaired neoantigen generation, aberrant activation of oncogenic pathways such as WNT/β-catenin signaling, and defects in interferon-γ signaling contribute to impaired immune recognition and immune escape. Within the TME, the accumulation of immunosuppressive populations, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), together with extracellular matrix remodeling and chemokine dysregulation, establishes an immune-excluded microenvironment that restricts effective antitumor immune responses. Furthermore, metabolic alterations, including enhanced glycolysis, lactate accumulation, and amino acid metabolic reprogramming, impair immune cell function and promote immunosuppression. Epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone remodeling, and non-coding RNA regulation, further contribute to the silencing of immune-related genes and reinforcement of immune evasion. In addition, recent advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented insights into the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization of MSS CRC immune ecosystems. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the molecular and cellular mechanisms driving immune resistance in MSS CRC and discusses future therapeutic opportunities for transforming immunologically "cold" MSS tumors into responsive immune microenvironments.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893983.abstract: Accurate noninvasive estimation of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may support multidisciplinary discussions, but multimodal MRI-ultrasound evidence remains limited. We developed and externally validated a clinicopathological deep learning radiomics nomogram and explored its potential auxiliary value in a strictly hypothetical post-hoc surgical-planning scenario. With institutional review-board approval and waived consent, this retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study included 436 biopsy-proven TNBC patients who underwent NAT and surgery: Center 1 training cohort (n = 268) and internal validation cohort (n = 86), plus historical cases from cooperating Centers 2-3 for external validation (n = 82). pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Pretreatment dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and B-mode ultrasound were analyzed. Intratumoral and 5-mm peritumoral ring radiomics features were extracted and selected by LASSO. DenseNet-121 extracted modality-specific deep features, fused using multi-head self-attention. Age, tumor size, Ki-67, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), cT/N stage, and histological grade were integrated with imaging scores in a logistic-regression nomogram. Parameters and thresholds were locked after Center 1 development and applied once to external data. No model output was used clinically. Feature standardization and ComBat harmonization parameters were strictly locked to the training cohort before application to validation data. pCR occurred in 182/436 patients (41.7%). The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.917 (95% CI, 0.881-0.947) in training, 0.883 (0.814-0.937) in internal validation, and 0.856 (0.773-0.921) in external validation, exceeding clinical (external AUC, 0.721), radiomics (0.786), and deep learning (0.819) models. External sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy at the locked threshold were 0.765, 0.813, and 0.793, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (slope, 0.93; intercept, -0.06; Brier score, 0.16). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit for thresholds of 0.20-0.70. Multi-threshold analysis revealed that a high-specificity threshold (0.65) yielded a positive predictive value of 0.85, potentially identifying a subset of patients with very high confidence of achieving pCR. Compared with the clinical model, external reclassification improved (continuous net reclassification improvement [NRI], 0.34; integrated discrimination improvement [IDI], 0.11; P = 0.003 and P = 0.008, respectively). Among the few multicenter TNBC studies combining MRI, ultrasound, intratumoral/peritumoral radiomics, and attention-based deep learning, this nomogram showed good retrospective accuracy for pCR prediction after NAT. The model is presented as an aid for pCR prediction and preoperative stratification rather than as direct support for surgical decision-making. Prospective validation and clinical-impact studies are required before implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1894239.abstract: Colorectal adenomas (CRAs) are the primary precancerous lesions in the development of colorectal cancer; establishing a simple, cost-effective and non-invasive tool for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy is of great significance for risk stratification. To investigate the association between peripheral blood metabolic and inflammatory markers and the risk of colorectal adenomas, and to develop a personalised risk prediction model for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy. This study was a single-centre retrospective case-control study conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong Second Medical University. The study included 2,437 patients with colorectal polyps who underwent endoscopic resection between January 2020 and December 2025. Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors and peripheral blood biochemical markers, with a particular focus on the triglyceride-to-glucose (TyG) ratio and markers of systemic inflammation. Patients with colorectal adenomas confirmed by histopathology. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The study included 2,437 participants (mean age 58.57 years; 1,323 men [54.29%]), patients in the adenoma group (n=1,584) were significantly older and had a higher proportion of men compared with the control group (n=853). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that male sex (OR, 1.621; 95% CI, 1.269-2.074), age ≥56.5 years (OR, 1.868; 95% CI, 1.515-2.205) and a TyG index ≥8.562 (OR, 1.271; 95% CI, 1.015-1.590) were independent risk factors for the development of colorectal adenomas. The AUC of this predictive model was 0.631 and 0.607 in the training and validation sets, respectively, indicates moderate discriminatory power. The model is well calibrated; analysis of the decision curve shows that, across a range of threshold probabilities, the model yields a positive net benefit compared with strategies involving either universal treatment or universal non-treatment. The findings suggest that male gender, advanced age and an elevated TyG index are independently associated with the risk of colorectal adenomas. The non-invasive nomogram developed in this study provides a simple risk stratification tool to aid in distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1894543.abstract: In oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), body mass index (BMI) is an available but imperfect marker of nutritional reserve. Evidence on pretreatment BMI in surgery-based European OSCC cohorts remains limited, especially regarding perioperative outcomes. This study evaluated associations of pretreatment BMI with overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and perioperative outcomes after curative-intent R0 resection. This retrospective single-center cohort included adult patients with previously untreated primary OSCC, available pretreatment BMI, and curative-intent R0 surgery between 2014 and 2023. BMI was assessed continuously and by World Health Organization (WHO) categories. OS and RFS were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, pathological T category, nodal status, microvascular free-flap reconstruction, and diabetes mellitus. Perioperative outcomes included red blood cell (RBC) transfusion, RBC units transfused, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay. A total of 274 patients with available pretreatment BMI were included; 116 deaths occurred. Five-year OS ranged from 31.4% in patients classified as underweight to 82.0% in patients with obesity. Higher BMI was associated with lower mortality (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.013), and obesity was associated with improved OS compared with normal weight (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.96; p = 0.037). BMI was not significantly associated with RFS after adjustment (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.00; p = 0.080). Higher BMI was associated with fewer perioperative RBC transfusions (any transfusion: OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98; p = 0.012; number of units: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.95; p = 0.001). BMI was not independently associated with PEG placement or hospital length of stay; ICU findings depended on BMI modeling. Higher pretreatment BMI was associated with better OS and lower perioperative RBC transfusion requirements, whereas associations with RFS and most other perioperative outcomes were not significant after adjustment. Given the retrospective design and limitations of BMI as a body-composition marker, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Pretreatment BMI may help identify low-BMI patients warranting early supportive-care assessment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895612.abstract: Current clinical diagnostic models lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity for Hepatoblastoma (HB) individualized prediction. This study aimed to identify robust hub genes for HB diagnosis and molecular subtyping by integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets and machine learning algorithms. Four merged GEO hepatoblastoma datasets (GSE131329, GSE132037, GSE104766, GSE133039) were analyzed by differential expression and WGCNA to identify HB-related genes. Further use three algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest) to identify central genes. In addition, consensus clustering was used for molecular typing, and four deconvolution algorithms (TIMER, MCPcounter, xCell, quanTIseq) were used to characterize the tumor microenvironment. The biological function of SDS in hepatoblastoma was elucidated through in vitro experiments (CCK-8 detection, colony formation assay, Transwell assay), as well as in vivo using a xenograft mouse model. A total of 268 differentially expressed genes (77 up, 191 down) were identified. WGCNA revealed the blue module as most correlated with HB (correlation coefficient 0.66). Three machine learning algorithms jointly selected four hub genes (CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, TTC36). Consensus clustering based on these four genes stratified HB into two subtypes (Clust1, Clust2). Clust1 exhibited enhanced immune infiltration and activation of complement, IFN-α, and IL6-JAK-STAT3 pathways. Low SDS expression associated with cell cycle pathways, whereas high SDS expression associated with immune-related pathways. Functionally, SDS overexpression significantly suppressed HB cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis in vitro, and markedly reduced tumor growth in vivo. Integrated machine learning identified CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, and TTC36 as robust diagnostic genes for hepatoblastoma. SDS, in particular, exerts a tumor-suppressive role and is closely linked to the immune microenvironment, making it a promising diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HB.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895799.abstract: Fecal incontinence (FI) is prevalent in critically ill oncology patients, frequently compounded by chemotherapy-induced diarrhea (CID) and severe thrombocytopenia. Conventional indwelling balloon catheters (IBCs), the standard approach to FI management in the ICU, generate intraluminal radial pressures that frequently exceed mucosal capillary perfusion thresholds and are formally contraindicated by manufacturers in patients with platelet counts below 50 x 109/L. This retrospective analysis and structured narrative literature review evaluates the safety, fecal containment efficacy, and nursing workload impact of a novel pressure-free automated stool management (ASM) system in high-risk oncology ICU patients. A retrospective analysis was conducted at a major academic comprehensive cancer center in the United States during 2025. Outcome data from 190 unique adult oncology ICU patients, including two structured evaluation cohorts of 20 patients each, followed by broader institutional implementation (n=150), were compiled from standardized nursing quality improvement product evaluation forms completed throughout each patient's device-use period. A prospectively designated thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47; platelet counts <50 x 109/L at device deployment) was analyzed separately. A structured narrative literature review was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, and CINAHL (final search: February 2026). Across 190 unique device placements, zero device-related adverse events were observed (adverse event rate 0%; 95% CI upper bound 1.6%, rule of three). In the thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47), zero device-related adverse events were observed (95% CI upper bound 6.4%). No device-related mucosal bleeding, perforation, ulceration, necrosis, or device malfunction requiring intervention was documented. The device achieved 100% successful fecal diversion, with no major leakage event (defined as stool output requiring linen replacement) recorded. The per-assessment leakage rate was 1.7% (11 positive assessments out of 646 total), all representing minor peripheral moisture requiring only topical hygiene management with no linen change. Daily nursing time with ASM was 6.8 minutes per patient per day; contextual comparison with published estimates of 120 minutes per patient per day (IBC protocol) and 174 minutes per patient per day (absorbent pad management) from Vargo et al. yields estimated differences of 94% and 96%, respectively, subject to methodological differences between datasets. Retrospective chart review identified no chemotherapy delays or ICU length of stay prolongation attributable to device-related complications. This early institutional experience with a novel pressure-free ASM across 190 unique oncology ICU placements, including 47 in patients with severe thrombocytopenia, was not associated with any observed device-related adverse event. These findings represent hypothesis-generating preliminary data and do not establish superiority over conventional devices. The clinical need for safe fecal management alternatives in thrombocytopenic oncology patients is substantive; these data provide rationale for appropriately powered prospective comparative trials.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895987.abstract: The clinical utility of postoperative radioiodine (131I) ablation remains unclear for patients with initially diagnosed non-distant metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) with harboring TERT promoter(TERT-p) mutations, it is unknown whether 131I therapy reduces the risk of persistent or recurrent disease. This study investigated clinicopathological features, 2-year dynamic therapeutic responses and progression-free survival (PFS) in this specific patient cohort. A single-center retrospective cohort study enrolled 113 eligible patients, allocated to the 131I ablation group (n=62) and non-131I group (n=51). Two-year dynamic risk stratification assessed treatment response. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models were used for survival analysis. The predominant TERT-p variant was C228T (89.4%), and most patients carried concurrent BRAFV600E mutations. Only initial surgical approach remained an independent intergroup variable. Within 2 years, 46.0% achieved acceptable responses, associated with sex and primary surgery (p=0.036,p < 0.001). High baseline ATA risk was strongly correlated with structural residual lesions and unfavorable therapeutic response (p < 0.001).No significant between-group differences in response were observed across all ATA risk subgroups. The median follow-up was 4.6 years; 3- and 5-year PFS rates were 67.5% and 39.1%. Age ≥55 years, N1b stage and high baseline ATA risk were independent adverse predictors of PFS. Both 2-year therapeutic response and PFS at the end of follow-up exhibited no statistical differences between the 131I group and non-131I group. In this retrospective observational cohort, postoperative 131I ablation was not associated with improved PFS among patients with non-distant metastatic TERT-p-mutant PTC. Advanced age, N1b lymphatic metastasis and high baseline ATA risk independently predict poor outcomes. Biologically, TERT-p mutations induce tumor dedifferentiation and impaired iodine uptake, diminishing 131I efficacy. Clinically, routine 131I yields no survival benefit for this high-risk molecular subgroup, guiding individualized surveillance and avoiding redundant 131I exposure.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896549.abstract: This review summarizes the definition, diagnosis and prevalence of anxiety and depression symptoms and disorders in people with cancer, followed by an overview of integrative therapies that are guideline-recommended for managing these conditions. Recommended therapies include mindfulness-based interventions, yoga, relaxation, music, reflexology, Taichi/Qigong, acupuncture, lavender aromatherapy and hypnosis. This is followed by a summary of emerging therapies that show preliminary evidence of efficacy, but are not yet included in guideline recommendations, including other forms of aromatherapy, light therapy, biofield therapies, psychedelic-assisted therapy and nature-based interventions. The paper concludes with a summary of common methodological issues and suggestions for future research directions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896620.abstract: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma (HAC) is a rare, malignant, extrahepatic tumor with hepatocellular differentiation. HAC is often associated with elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) concentrations, which makes it difficult to distinguish from primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It is a difficult diagnosis based on histopathology, as the immunohistochemistry (IHC) profile often overlaps with hepatocellular carcinoma. HAC can arise from multiple organs, including the stomach, esophagus, colon, pancreas, duodenum, and peritoneum, with the stomach being the most common site. The treatment of HAC is not well defined, as randomized trial data is not available. The overall prognosis of metastatic HAC with standard combination chemotherapy is extremely poor. Here, we present a case of metastatic duodenal HAC that achieved a sustained complete response to chemotherapy-free dual immune checkpoint blockade, which, to our knowledge, represents the first published report of a sustained complete response to chemotherapy-free dual immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic duodenal HAC and suggests a potential approach that warrants further clinical investigation. We acknowledge that a degree of diagnostic uncertainty remains, as HAC and HCC can exhibit essentially identical morphologic and immunophenotypic features, making the distinction largely clinical.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896620.title: Case Report: Metastatic duodenal hepatoid adenocarcinoma: a rare pathology with exceptional response to dual immune checkpoint blockade.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896625.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) changes for treatment response in colorectal cancer(CRC) patients receiving CAPOX chemotherapy, providing a reliable indicator for clinical efficacy monitoring. Clinical data of CRC patients who first received the CAPOX regimen at the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 1, 2016 and January 31, 2026 were retrospectively collected. Parameters included operation date, chemotherapy administration dates, disease progression (PD) time, preoperative CEA, baseline CEA before chemotherapy, CEA before each cycle, and CEA within three months post-chemotherapy. Disease-free survival (DFS) was calculated. Patients were divided into Group 1: CEA is in the normal range (all values are ≤ 5ng/ml); Group 2: Decreasing or normalization type (not Group 1, and the last valid value ≤ 5ng/ml, or a decrease of ≥20% compared to the individual's previous peak); Group 3: Persistent or new-onset abnormal type (the rest, that is, the last value > 5 and the decrease from the peak value < 20%). Survival curves were plotted using the Kaplan-Meier method, and multivariate Cox regression was used to assess correlations between CEA changes, treatment efficacy, and DFS. Median DFS (mDFS) was 55.668 months (95% CI: 51.511-58.826) in Group 1 (n=84); 42.271 months (95% CI: 35.438-49.104) in Group 2 (n=47) and 19.980 months (95% CI: 11.198-28.762) in Group 3 (n=11). Dynamic changes in serum CEA have good predictive value for the efficacy of CAPOX chemotherapy in CRC. This predictive value is primarily significant in TNM Stage III patients and serve as an independent prognostic factor. Patients with decreased or persistently normal CEA levels have a better prognosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896692.abstract: The triplet combination of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), and a programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor has emerged as a highly promising strategy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy and safety of this triple-therapy compared with the dual-therapy of a TKI plus a PD-1 inhibitor. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials or comparative cohort studies that assessed HAIC plus a TKI and a PD-1 inhibitor (H-T-P) versus a TKI plus a PD-1 inhibitor (T-P) for uHCC. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and disease control rate (DCR). The secondary endpoint was treatment-related adverse events (AEs). A random-effects model was employed to pool data, calculating hazard ratios (HRs) or relative risks (RRs) with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A total of 12 studies involving 2,386 patients with uHCC were included. Compared with T-P dual therapy, the H-T-P triple therapy was associated with significantly improved OS (HR, 0.51; 95%CI, 0.47-0.56; P < 0.001) and PFS (HR, 0.59; 95%CI, 0.51-0.68; P < 0.001). Furthermore, the H-T-P group demonstrated a significantly higher ORR (RR, 1.97; 95%CI, 1.73-2.24; P < 0.001) and DCR (RR, 1.19; 95%CI, 1.11-1.28; P < 0.001). Regarding safety, while no significant difference was observed in the overall incidence of all-grade AEs (P = 0.238), the incidence of grade ≥3 AEs was significantly higher in the triple-therapy arm (RR, 1.29; 95%CI, 1.13-1.48; P = 0.004), consisting primarily of manageable hepatotoxicity and hematologic toxicities. Our findings indicate that for patients with uHCC, the H-T-P triple-therapy regimen is superior to dual therapy in terms of survival benefits and tumor response. The associated increase in severe toxicity is considered predictable and clinically manageable. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251113276.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1897872.abstract: Core-binding factor acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML) is defined by one of two founding fusions, but cooperating lesions may differ between fusion subtypes. We characterized the broader diagnostic co-mutational architecture of pediatric CBF-AML and examined its relationship with post-induction measurable residual disease (MRD) and outcome. This retrospective analysis included 170 children with diagnostic whole-exome sequencing (WES) data (2019-2023), a subset of a reported 289-patient cohort. Candidate leukemia-associated variants were curated conservatively because matched normal samples were unavailable. Variant frequencies were compared between RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and CBFB::MYH11 AML with false-discovery-rate control. Associations with MRD were tested using Fisher's exact test. Primary feature-specific Cox models for event-free survival (EFS) were adjusted only for fusion subtype and induction regimen; sensitivity analyses additionally addressed age and presenting WBC count, MRD, and transplantation. In a limited selection audit, fusion-subtype and FLT3-ITD distributions were similar between WES-included and non-included patients, whereas clinical-source KIT positivity was more frequent in the WES subset. The analytic cohort included 138 RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and 32 CBFB::MYH11 cases; 137 received FLAG-IDA, and 33 received DAE induction. At least one curated candidate variant was present in 135 patients (79.4%), and 69 (40.6%) had alterations in two or more genes. Tyrosine-kinase signaling alterations occurred in 115 patients (67.6%). RAS-pathway alterations were enriched in CBFB::MYH11 AML (53.1% vs. 19.6%; P < 0.001, q=0.002), driven principally by NRAS (50.0% vs. 15.2%; P < 0.001, q < 0.001). Chromatin-modifier alterations were numerically enriched in RUNX1::RUNX1T1 AML (24.6% vs. 6.2%; P = 0.028) but did not remain significant after multiplicity correction (q=0.114). After false-discovery-rate correction, no tested genomic feature was associated with MFC-MRD or molecular MRD positivity after the second induction. With a median follow-up of 33.2 months, 3-year EFS and overall survival were 84.2% and 89.8%, respectively. No baseline genomic feature showed a significant association with EFS in either the primary or expanded baseline-covariate models. Among WES-profiled patients, pediatric CBF-AML showed fusion-specific co-mutational architecture, especially RAS-pathway enrichment in CBFB::MYH11 AML. In this WES-defined cohort, baseline genomic features were not established as response or outcome predictors. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; they do not support treatment-specific causal inference.
