doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1897905.abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) is an adverse pathological feature in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and an indication for adjuvant radiotherapy but is conventionally reported as a binary variable. The prognostic relevance of its quantitative morphological features remains incompletely defined. In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 101 consecutive patients with pathologically node-negative OSCC treated by curative-intent resection (January 2023 - March 2024) were analysed. Six block-level morphological PNI parameters were assessed on digitised H&E whole-slide images by two pathologists: largest involved nerve diameter (P1), maximum nerves involved (P2), pattern of invasion (P3; intratumoural, extratumoural or both), maximum circumferential extent (P4), nerves with mitotic figures (P5), and minimum distance from the tumour front to the nearest uninvolved nerve (P6). Interobserver reproducibility was evaluated for all five PNI parameters. Cutpoints were derived by maximally selected rank statistics. Univariate and bivariable Cox regression, bootstrap stability, and a composite 0-6 score were evaluated against disease-free survival (DFS) and locoregional control (LRC). PNI was identified in 34 of 100 evaluable patients; binary comparison showed a non-significant trend toward inferior DFS (p = 0.104) and no LRC difference (p = 0.490). Among 30 of the 34 PNI-positive patients with complete morphological data (11 DFS events; median follow-up 20.7 months), nerve diameter >429 µm was the strongest predictor of DFS (HR 3.96, 95% CI 1.18-13.02, p = 0.026), and the most consistently selected variable in LASSO bootstrap resampling (64.8%). Large nerve calibre (P1), an extratumoral component (P3) and intraneural mitoses (P5) co-occurred as an aggressive triad (pairwise φ 0.52-0.61). The composite 0-6 score was associated with DFS (HR 1.34 per point, 95% CI 1.01-1.77, p = 0.044) and stratified patients into low-risk (0-2) and high-risk (3-6) groups for DFS (p = 0.003) and LRC (p = 0.045). PNI in node-negative OSCC is biologically significant and prognostically influential even within this favourable-prognosis (pN0, R0) subgroup; quantitative morphological characterisation, particularly of invaded nerve diameter, adds prognostic information beyond binary reporting. A composite morphological score may identify PNI-positive patients for future prospective evaluation of risk-adapted adjuvant strategies; external multicentre validation is required before clinical application.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1898263.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that aberrant HHLA2 expression is closely implicated not only in tumorigenesis, disease progression, and metastatic spread, but also in the intricate modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment. Nevertheless, the biological functions of HHLA2 and the molecular mechanisms underlying its action in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remain unexplored. HHLA2 expression was systematically assessed in LSCC tumor specimens and matched adjacent tissues using multiplex immunofluorescence (mIHC). The functional consequences of HHLA2 silencing in LSCC cells were evaluated through a series of in vitro assays, including CCK-8-based proliferation analysis, wound-healing (scratch) assays, and invasion assays. Transcriptomic sequencing integrated with public database mining was subsequently performed to identify key target genes potentially governed by HHLA2 in regulating LSCC biological behavior. Furthermore, Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) pathway analyses were conducted to delineate the signaling networks and molecular pathways through which HHLA2 might exert its regulatory effects in LSCC. HHLA2 expression was significantly elevated in LSCC tumor tissues, and associated with poor prognosis in patients. Functional experiments revealed that suppression of HHLA2 leads to marked inhibition of LSCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, underscoring its essential role in sustaining malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, we identified potassium channel tetrameric domain 12 (KCTD12) as a pivotal target of HHLA2 in mediating these oncogenic processes. Importantly, forced overexpression of KCTD12 effectively counterbalanced the inhibitory effects induced by HHLA2 depletion, thereby restoring proliferative, migratory, and invasive potential to LSCC cells. Furthermore, pathway enrichment analyses indicated that the TNF-NF-κB signalling pathway might serve as a key conduit through which HHLA2 orchestrated both tumor cell functions and immune regulatory mechanisms. The HHLA2-KCTD12 axis may regulate the phenotype of LSCC cells and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment through the TNF-NF-κB signaling pathway. HHLA2 enhanced the proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities of LSCC cells and might contribute to immune microenvironment remodeling via modulation of TNF-NF-κB signaling through the HHLA2-KCTD12 axis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1898480.abstract: Conversion therapy may create an opportunity for liver resection in selected patients with initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but reported conversion rates use heterogeneous denominators and endpoints. We estimated actual completed hepatectomy using a verified all-treated denominator. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library/CENTRAL, Wanfang Data, and CNKI were searched through April 10, 2026. Eligible cohorts included initially or baseline unresectable HCC, an all-treated denominator, and completed liver resection events. Two authors independently assessed eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias. Random-effects logit proportion meta-analysis, Hartung-Knapp sensitivity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out analyses, treatment-strategy subgroups, publication-year meta-regression, and small-study-effect diagnostics were undertaken. PROSPERO: CRD420261360108. Thirty-seven reports represented 36 unique studies; 34 studies involving 5,137 patients and 1,042 completed hepatectomies entered the quantitative synthesis. The crude aggregate resection rate was 20.3% (1,042/5,137), whereas the random-effects modeled pooled rate was 25.40% (95% CI, 20.74%-30.69%; I2=91.5%; tau2=0.5132). The Hartung-Knapp 95% CI was 20.12%-31.51%, and the prediction interval was 7.16%-60.04%. Leave-one-out estimates ranged from 24.52% to 26.64%. Treatment-strategy differences were not statistically significant (Qm=5.17, df=2, P = 0.075). Publication-year meta-regression did not show a clear linear association (OR per decade 1.19, 95% CI 0.77-1.83; P = 0.440), and Egger's test did not indicate significant funnel asymmetry (P = 0.381). Approximately one-quarter of patients initiating conversion therapy underwent actual hepatectomy, but the crude and modeled estimates differ because substantial heterogeneity changes random-effects study weighting. The pooled estimate is a cross-study, cross-era benchmark for multidisciplinary decision-making rather than a universal patient-level probability or a treatment-specific efficacy estimate. www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261360108.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1898567.abstract: Recurrent and metastatic non-anaplastic thyroid cancer has traditionally been considered relatively radioresistant. We evaluated whether anatomic site or histology risk group better predicts local control (LC) following stereotactic radiation therapy (SBRT/SRS). We retrospectively reviewed 32 patients with 66 treated lesions (42 skeletal, 24 non-skeletal) treated between 2012 and 2025. Histology was dichotomized into low-risk (papillary, follicular, medullary, Hürthle cell; n=61) and high-risk (poorly differentiated and squamous cell carcinoma; n=5). BED10 was calculated using α/β = 10 Gy. LC was defined per RECIST 1.1. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests were used. Intra-patient correlation was addressed via generalized estimating equations (GEE) and Cox shared frailty models. A multivariable GEE model included histology risk, site, BED10, PTV volume, prior surgery, and age. Median follow-up was 15.0 months. Six local failures occurred (crude LC 90.9%); 1- and 2-year LC were 96.5% and 87.1%. Histology risk was the dominant determinant: low-risk histology achieved 95.1% crude LC versus 40.0% for high-risk (log-rank p=0.002). In multivariable GEE analysis, low-risk histology was independently associated with LC (OR 158.0, 95% CI 1.72-14,479.7; p=0.028), whereas skeletal site was not (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.02-51.8; p=0.974). BED10 was not associated with LC after adjustment (p=0.752). Skeletal and non-skeletal LC were similar after histology stratification (95.0% vs 95.2% among low-risk). Treatment was well tolerated; no Grade ≥3 radiation toxicity, myelopathy, or fractures occurred. In stereotactic radiation for metastatic non-anaplastic thyroid cancer, histology risk grouping-not anatomic site or dose escalation-is the dominant predictor of local control. These findings support histology-based risk stratification for SRT patient selection.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1898779.abstract: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and prognostic influencing factors of carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) in patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC). The clinical data of 39 patients with LS-SCLC who received CIRT from June 2020 to August 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Survival outcomes and adverse reactions were evaluated, and Cox regression was used to analyze prognostic factors. All patients completed the treatment. The 3-month objective response rate (ORR) was 64.10%. The 1- and 2-year local control rates were both 91.2%. The 1- and 2-year overall survival (OS) rates were 91.65% and 62.45%, with a median OS of 44 months. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 72.00% and 47.77%, with a median PFS of 24 months. Serum levels of NSE, CYFRA21-1, SCC and CEA decreased significantly after treatment. Acute treatment-related adverse reactions were mainly grade I-II and could be relieved after symptomatic treatment. Stratified Cox regression indicated that KPS score was an independent protective factor for OS. Univariate analysis suggested that the magnitude of post-treatment reduction in SCC and CYFRA21-1 was potentially associated with survival outcomes. CIRT achieves favorable local tumor control with low acute radiotherapy-related toxicity, and can serve as an alternative therapeutic option for LS-SCLC. This is a single-center, small-sample retrospective study, and the conclusions regarding efficacy and prognosis need to be further verified in larger-sample cohorts.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1899114.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has demonstrated substantial clinical efficacy across HER2-expressing malignancies. However, interstitial lung disease (ILD) represents a clinically relevant and potentially serious adverse event associated with its use, requiring early recognition, exclusion of alternative etiologies and coordinated multidisciplinary management. Delayed identification may increase the risk of severe pulmonary toxicity and premature discontinuation of an otherwise highly effective therapy. In this manuscript, we aim to provide practical guidance on the early detection and management of T-DXd-related ILD. A structured multidisciplinary discussion involving oncologists, pneumologists, and radiologists was conducted to evaluate the epidemiology, risk factors, diagnostic pathways, and management strategies for ILD in patients treated with T-DXd. Evidence from the published literature was reviewed to inform and support the panel's recommendations. ILD may arise in up to 15% of patients receiving T-DXd. While most events occur during the first year of treatment, continued vigilance is warranted throughout therapy. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) is essential for early detection, and prompt treatment interruption combined with timely corticosteroid therapy is critical to prevent progression. The panel emphasized the importance of standardized imaging protocols, structured radiologic reporting, early multidisciplinary involvement, and patient education to facilitate prompt recognition and management. Proactive surveillance strategies, including baseline and interval HRCT, multidisciplinary collaboration and patient-centered monitoring, are essential to minimize ILD-related morbidity while preserving access to T-DXd therapy. The implementation of standardized clinical pathways and the development of biomarker-driven approaches may further improve personalized ILD risk management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1900262.abstract: Background BI-RADS category 4 breast lesions are suspicious and generally undergo tissue diagnosis, but malignancy risk remains heterogeneous across BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C. We developed and internally validated an interpretable mammography-based model for risk stratification within this diagnostic category. Methods This single-center retrospective diagnostic prediction study included 441 patients, each contributing one index BI-RADS 4 mammographic lesion. Outcomes were verified histopathologically in 397 lesions and by longitudinal imaging stability in 44. Three primary models and a sensitivity model excluding BI-RADS were evaluated. Internal validation used 1,000 paired patient-level bootstrap resamples in which imputation, encoding, standardization, penalty selection, LASSO selection, and coefficient estimation were repeated. Results Of 441 lesions, 165 were malignant. Malignancy rates were 15.7% (34/216), 46.4% (70/151), and 82.4% (61/74) in BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C, respectively. The final model retained BI-RADS 4B, BI-RADS 4C, architectural distortion, circularity-deficit irregularity score, contour serration score, and normalized GLCM contrast. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.770 (95% CI, 0.729-0.815) for BI-RADS only, 0.774 (0.733-0.814) for clinical plus BI-RADS, and 0.841 (0.809-0.877) for the full mammography-based model. Clinical variables did not improve validated performance. The full model improved corrected AUC versus BI-RADS only by 0.072 (0.028-0.108) and versus clinical plus BI-RADS by 0.067 (0.029-0.103). Its corrected calibration intercept was 0.002 (-0.209 to 0.208) and slope was 1.445 (1.140-1.753). Within-category AUCs were 0.785, 0.721, and 0.758 for BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C; the pathology-only corrected AUC was 0.835 (0.799-0.871). Conclusion Structured and quantitative mammographic features improved internally validated discrimination and within-category risk stratification beyond BI-RADS subcategory alone. Because predicted risks were under-dispersed and validation was limited to one center, the model should be used only as a research-stage risk-stratification and prioritization tool, not to replace biopsy. External validation and recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1900370.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound molecular and metabolic heterogeneity associated with distinct phenotypic states. However, the contribution of transcription factor (TF)-driven regulatory programs to metabolic subtype stratification remains poorly understood. This study aims to determine whether TF-based classification can identify prognostically relevant glycolytic and lipogenic PDAC subtypes. Bulk transcriptomic data from multiple PDAC cohorts and single-cell RNA sequencing data were integrated to characterize TF-associated metabolic heterogeneity. Metabolic signatures and TFs were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) and AddModule Score (AMS). Differential expression, enrichment analysis, integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis, and deep neural network-based metabolic flux modeling were performed to investigate metabolic programs and functional differences between TF-defined subtypes. Additionally, RNA interference, RT-qPCR, lipid droplets staining, lactate assay, and transwell assays were used to evaluate the roles of TP63 in metabolic regulation. Glycolytic and lipogenic TF-defined metabolic subtypes were identified across multiple independent PDAC cohorts. These subtypes exhibited distinct metabolic programs, differentiation states, and prognostic outcomes. The glycolytic TF-defined subtype was associated with worse prognosis and differentiation, whereas the lipogenic TF-defined subtype exhibited more favorable clinical features. Integration of public bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses, together with deep neural network-based metabolic flux modeling, revealed consistent metabolic heterogeneity at both cellular and functional levels. Notably, TP63 was identified as a potential regulator of glycolytic-lipogenic metabolic reprogramming in PDAC. TF-based classification delineates glycolytic and lipogenic subtypes in PDAC, underscoring the critical role of TF-regulated metabolic programs in patient stratification. These findings highlight the prognostic significance of glycolytic and lipogenic metabolic heterogeneity and support the development of metabolism-targeted therapeutic strategies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1900671.abstract: Serum free light chain (sFLC) testing is central to the diagnosis and monitoring of plasma cell disorders, but assay availability and implementation can vary by laboratory setting. We evaluated a domestic latex-enhanced immunoturbidimetric Kehua serum sFLC assay against Freelite and N Latex systems. Residual serum samples from 133 adults with suspected or established monoclonal gammopathies were measured in parallel by Kehua and Freelite; 122 were also tested by N Latex. Precision was assessed with low- and high-level serum controls. Method agreement was evaluated using correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, Bland-Altman analysis, qualitative concordance and comparator-defined ROC analysis. Kehua within-run CVs were <5% for κ and λ controls. Agreement with Freelite was excellent for FLC-κ, FLC-λ and κ/λ ratio (Pearson r = 0.988-1.000; CCC = 0.983-0.999), with Passing-Bablok slopes close to unity. Agreement with N Latex was also strong (r = 0.991-0.998), although κ/λ ratio showed proportional bias. Total qualitative concordance was 89.47-93.23% versus Freelite and 83.61-91.80% versus N Latex, with Cohen's κ of 0.67-0.85. Comparator-defined ROC AUCs were 0.994-0.999 for elevated FLC-κ or FLC-λ and 0.796-0.869 for κ/λ ratio abnormality. The Kehua serum assay demonstrated acceptable precision and good clinical agreement with two imported methods. It may serve as a domestic option for routine serum sFLC quantification, provided method-specific intervals are maintained and the same platform is used for serial monitoring.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1901172.abstract: Ovarian cancer typically spreads via peritoneal seeding, hematogenous, or lymphatic routes. Bile duct metastasis is extremely rare, and peribiliary metastasis manifesting as diffuse Glissonian sheath infiltration without a detectable mass lesion, to our knowledge, has not been well documented. A 42-year-old woman with stage IVB high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, previously treated with cytoreductive surgery and multiple lines of chemotherapy, presented with fatigue, anorexia, and mild jaundice. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) revealed bile duct wall thickening, peribiliary edema (Glissonian sheath edema), and diffuse inflammatory changes without a discrete mass. Autoimmune and infectious workups were negative. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with biopsy showed micropapillary clusters of atypical cells. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CK7, CK19, PAX-8, P16, and mutant-type p53; CEA focally positive; ER negative; Ki-67 high. This confirmed metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma of ovarian origin involving the common bile duct wall. Imaging (MRI/MRCP) suggested diffuse peribiliary involvement compatible with Glissonian sheath infiltration, although the small biopsy did not directly sample the intrahepatic sheath itself. We hypothesize that the radiological changes reflect peribiliary lymphatic spread, but this remains an inference based on imaging-pathology correlation rather than a histologically proven mechanism. Effective biliary drainage could not be achieved because the patient was unable to tolerate the nasobiliary drain. She was discharged against medical advice and died shortly thereafter, according to family report. In cancer patients with unexplained cholestasis, peribiliary metastasis should be considered even when no mass is seen on cross-sectional imaging. ERCP with biopsy and immunohistochemistry are essential for diagnosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1901768.abstract: Tonsillar metastasis from hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is extremely rare. We report an 84-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B who presented with a right-lobe HCC and portal vein tumor thrombosis. Three months after diagnosis, intrahepatic metastases were treated with transarterial chemoembolization and lenvatinib. Twenty-three months later, he developed blood-tinged sputum; imaging and laryngoscopy revealed a left tonsillar mass with concurrent pulmonary and hepatic progression. Tonsillectomy yielded an undifferentiated carcinoma lesion. Compared with the primary tumor, the tonsillar metastasis lost hepatocyte specific antigen (Hep Par-1) and Arginase-1 expression, showed a markedly elevated Ki-67 index (80%), but retained Glypican-3 and heat shock protein 70 (HSP70). A diagnosis of metastatic HCC was favored based on integration of clinical history, laboratory findings, and pathological immunohistochemistry. In HCC patients, any unusual head and neck lesion warrants suspicion of metastasis; a multi-marker panel is critical for diagnosis, as loss of Arginase-1 does not rule out HCC.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1901931.abstract: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) is a rare yet highly aggressive malignancy with severely limited treatment options. The efficacy of immunotherapy for ES-SCLC remain limited, with only 14% of patients deriving additional benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), underscoring significant heterogeneity in patient response. This study aimed to develop a model for the accurate prediction of prognosis and therapeutic response to optimize treatment strategies. 99 and 25 ES-SCLC patients were enrolled as training and independent internal validation cohorts. Baseline CT images, clinical data, and laboratory markers were collected. Prognostic factors were screened via Cox regression. A mediastinal window CT-based deep learning model (MWDL) was developed and combined with Progastrin-releasing peptide (log(ProGRP + 1)) and bone metastasis to establish the novel MWGB-Cox model. ProGRP and bone metastasis were independent prognostic factors with area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.705 and 0.666 respectively for predicting 1-year OS. Among the pure deep learning models, the MWDL model achieved better performance with a mean AUC of 0.813 than the deep learning model based on lung window CT images (LWDL, AUC 0.756). Whereas the multimodal MWGB-Cox model not only achieved the highest AUC (0.902) for 1-year OS prediction, but also effectively overcame the limitation of insufficient sensitivity. The predictive performance of the MWGB-Cox model was further validated in the independent internal validation cohort. This novel, simple, and cost-effective multimodal MWGB-Cox model integrating CT-based deep learning, log(ProGRP + 1), and bone metastasis could robustly predict 1-year OS of ES-SCLC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy, providing a reliable tool for clinical decision-making. By integrating CT-based deep learning, log(ProGRP + 1) levels, and bone metastasis, the novel multimodal model achieved the highest predictive AUC (0.902) with improved sensitivity, serving as a simple, cost-effective tool for clinical decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1902158.abstract: The strategy for opportunistic endoscopic screening driven by family history of gastric cancer needs to be optimized in a tailored manner through further risk stratification. A hospital-based cross-sectional study included health check-up controls and gastric cancer patients at West China Hospital, Sichuan University. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, family history of malignancies, and serology were analyzed for associations with gastric cancer risk. Associations between family history of gastric cancer and incident gastric cancer risk were assessed, and a rapid cost-effectiveness analysis was performed. In total, 58,218 observations were analyzed, including 619 gastric cancer patients. Family history of gastric cancer was an independent risk factor for gastric cancer (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 5.59, 95% CI 3.81-8.20) and was associated with an increased risk of upper digestive tract benign comorbidities (aOR = 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.71). For persons with a family history of gastric cancer who were older than 40 years (odds ratio [OR] = 2.36, 95% CI 1.29-4.32), endoscopic screening could be mildly recommended in general practice. Endoscopic screening should be moderately recommended for those with a family history of gastric cancer if they were older than 60 years (OR = 8.90, 95% CI 3.84-20.61) and strongly recommended if they also had upper digestive tract benign comorbidities (OR = 16.78, 95% CI 7.03-40.06), seropositivity for carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and/or carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) (OR = 20.77, 95% CI 9.15-47.14), or anemia (OR = 80.11, 95% CI 33.07-194.05). A rapid cost-effectiveness analysis indicated that moderate-to-strong recommendations were preferred, but based on willingness-to-pay considerations, mild-to-strong recommendations had a considerable detection rate for gastric cancer. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent findings for decision-making. Family history of gastric cancer is an independent risk factor for gastric cancer. Optimized risk stratification based on family history can improve the cost-effectiveness of detecting gastric cancer. The mechanism by which a family history of gastric cancer increases gastric cancer risk and a more tailored family history-driven endoscopic screening strategy require further investigation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1903085.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent extracranial solid malignant tumor in infants and children. Approximately half of children with high-risk NB exhibit primary resistance to first-line therapy or experience disease relapse within two years post-treatment, leading to dismal overall survival. PANoptosis is an inflammatory programmed cell death modality integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis; nevertheless, the functional relevance of PANoptosis-related genes (PRGs) in NB remains largely undefined. This study aimed to explore PRGs associated with NB prognosis and their link to the tumor immune microenvironment, so as to identify novel therapeutic targets for NB. mRNA expression profiles from three public NB datasets (GSE49711-NB, TARGET-NB and E-MTAB-8248-NB) were used to investigate the prognostic roles of 19 previously reported PRGs. Independent Cox regression screening was performed in each cohort to identify cohort-specific prognostic PRGs, followed by Venn intersection analysis to identify conserved prognostic genes. PARP1 expression was validated in tumor tissues from 127 clinical NB patients. The GIS score based on PARP1 expression and clinical metadata were combined to assess its prognostic value. In vitro functional assays were performed to explore the anti-tumor effects and mechanisms of the PARP1 inhibitor AZD5305. Venn intersection analysis identified PARP1 as the only shared gene with consistent prognostic significance across heterogeneous NB patient populations. In vitro experiments revealed that AZD5305 markedly suppressed NB cell proliferation, migration and invasion, triggered cell apoptosis, and arrested cell cycle progression at the G0/G1 phase. This study adopts a multi-cohort parallel screening strategy to mine conserved therapeutic targets for NB. Our data indicate that PARP1 inhibition via AZD5305 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for NB treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1903512.abstract: Patients with cancer with deleterious DPYD variants are at significantly increased risk for severe toxicity with standard fluoropyrimidine doses. Prior to recent guidelines recommending it, the uptake of pre-treatment DPYD testing in the United States has been low. We aimed to explore oncologists' perceptions and barriers to DPYD testing adoption on a national level. Survey invitations were sent to U.S. oncologists listed in the American Medical Association (AMA) Masterfile in April and May 2025. The surveys assessed physician knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of DPYD testing in clinics caring for patients with cancer in the United States. Descriptive statistics were used to evaluate survey responses. Of 5,525 physicians invited to participate, 47 oncologists completed the survey (response rate: 0.85%). The majority (85%) indicated that DPYD testing could help them manage patients; however, only 34% reported routinely performing DPYD testing. Most physicians (77%) agreed that adequate resources were available to order DPYD testing. When directly asked, 36% indicated that limited laboratory access was a barrier. In open-ended responses, respondents identified insurance reimbursement concerns (21%) and prolonged turnaround time (19%) as additional barriers. Forty-three percent reported needing assistance interpreting results and applying them to drug selection and dosing. Webinars (25.5%) and self-paced online modules (21%) were the most preferred educational modalities. Most respondents indicated that DPYD testing could help manage patients, yet concerns persist. While regulatory guidance is evolving, these preliminary findings from a small sample highlight the need for future research to characterize implementation barriers and inform policy development. Our findings highlight gaps in implementation that can inform targeted strategies to improve the integration of DPYD testing into oncology practice, with the potential to enhance patient safety and reduce fluoropyrimidine-related toxicity.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1904498.abstract: To investigate tumor vascular habitat parameters based on dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion-weighted imaging (DSC-PWI) for differentiating glioblastoma (GBM) from solitary brain metastasis (SBM). In this single-center retrospective study, imaging data from 141 patients with pathologically or clinically confirmed malignant brain tumors (74 GBM, 67 SBM) were analyzed. The hemodynamic tissue signature (HTS) method was used to segment the lesions and construct four tumor vascular habitats: high angiogenic tumor (HAT), low angiogenic tumor (LAT), potentially infiltrated peripheral edema (IPE), and vasogenic peripheral edema (VPE). Pearson correlation analysis was used to quantify the correlations among habitat hemodynamic parameters. Habitat characteristic parameters were calculated, and ROC were plotted to evaluate the diagnostic performance. A nomogram model was constructed using logistic regression. GBM exhibited significantly higher median relative cerebral blood volume (rCBVmedian) and median relative cerebral blood flow (rCBFmedian) than SBM across all four habitat regions (all p < 0.001). In terms of volumetric parameters, the ratio of IPE volume to peritumoral volume (V (IPE)/V (P)) was significantly higher in the GBM group (p < 0.001). Among individual habitat parameters, LAT rCBFmedian showed the best diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.786 (95% CI: 0.709-0.850). In the GBM group, the perfusion parameters of the IPE and VPE were significantly positively correlated with those of the HAT, whereas no such correlation was found in the SBM group. A nomogram incorporating lesion location, enhancement pattern, and LAT-rCBFmedian yielded an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.79-0.92) for distinguishing GBM from SBM, with good calibration. Tumor vascular habitat parameters based on DSC-PWI demonstrate significant differences between newly diagnosed GBM and SBM, and the nomogram shows certain value in differentiating between the two tumor types.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1904801.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype with poor prognosis, especially in postmenopausal women who are routinely treated with anthracycline/taxane-based chemotherapy. However, wide inter-individual variation in disease-free survival (DFS) underscores an urgent need for reliable predictive markers and practical prognostic tools. We aimed to develop and validate a real-world nomogram that integrates clinically accessible predictive markers for individualised DFS prediction in this specific population. In this two-centre real-world study, we enrolled 479 postmenopausal TNBC patients who received initial adjuvant anthracycline/taxane-based chemotherapy (sequential or concurrent). Patients were randomly assigned 7:3 to a training cohort (n=335) and a validation cohort (n=144). We used univariate and multivariate Cox regression with stepwise bidirectional selection to identify independent predictors, which were then incorporated into a nomogram. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, and calibration plots. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two cohorts (all P>0.05). Multivariate Cox analysis identified four independent predictors: postoperative pathological T stage (T2+T3 vs T1: hazard ratio [HR]=2.607, 95% CI 1.347-5.047, P = 0.004); N stage (N2 vs N0: HR = 4.077, 2.049-8.112, P 20% (vs ≤20%: HR = 2.060, 1.082-3.919, P = 0.028). The nomogram achieved excellent discrimination: training cohort C-index=0.899; validation cohort C-index=0.861. Time-dependent AUCs for 1-, 3-, and 5-year DFS were 0.915, 0.945, and 0.959 in the training cohort, and 0.895, 0.943, and 0.900 in the validation cohort, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes. We developed and validated a real-world nomogram integrating four readily available predictive markers-T stage, N stage, sTIL, and Ki67-that accurately predicts 1-, 3-, and 5-year DFS in postmenopausal TNBC patients receiving standard anthracycline/taxane chemotherapy. This practical tool supports personalised risk stratification and clinical decision-making, directly addressing the need for predictive markers in advancing breast cancer chemotherapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1905004.abstract: Brain metastases (BM) from prostate cancer (PCa) are rare, typically occurring in a small subset of patients with advanced disease or tumors with neuroendocrine differentiation. Diagnosis can be particularly challenging when prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels remain low or undetectable. We describe four patients with prostate adenocarcinoma who developed brain metastases despite low or modestly elevated PSA levels relative to disease burden(<0.01 to 6.5 ng/ml). All patients underwent surgical resection followed by focal stereotactic radiosurgery and androgen deprivation therapy, with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors used in selected cases. Molecular profiling was available for three patients and demonstrated heterogeneous genomic findings, including PTEN alteration (Case 1), CDK4 amplification (Case 2), and an ATM mutation (Case 3), while testing was unavailable in Case 4. No pathogenic TP53 or RB1 alterations were identified in the profiled tumors. Two patients achieved durable biochemical and radiographic complete remission, one remained in remission before dying of an unrelated cause, and one developed biochemical recurrence without radiographic progression. These findings highlight the biological heterogeneity of central nervous system involvement in prostate cancer and emphasize that brain metastases should be considered even in patients with low PSA levels. Further studies are needed to better define the molecular determinants and biomarkers associated with this uncommon presentation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1905052.abstract: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) combined with lenvatinib and tislelizumab has shown potential activity in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but early treatment failure (ETF) remains common. We developed an exploratory model to estimate ETF, defined as radiologically confirmed progressive disease (PD) or all-cause death within 6 months after treatment initiation. This single-center retrospective study included advanced HCC patients treated with the triple regimen from June 2021 to June 2024. Baseline clinical, imaging, and hematological variables were analyzed. LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection. Restricted cubic splines assessed linearity, and λ.1se was examined as a sensitivity analysis. A multivariable logistic regression model was presented as a nomogram. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were evaluated, with 1000-resample bootstrap internal validation repeating the modeling pipeline. Among 118 patients, 33 (27.9%) experienced ETF; 28 had radiologically confirmed PD and 5 died without prior documented PD. At λ.min, LASSO selected maximum tumor diameter, Vp4 portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT), baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), ALBI score, and log10-transformed alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Under λ.1se, four predictors were retained, with SII excluded. The final model had an apparent ROC-AUC of 0.903 and an optimism-corrected ROC-AUC of 0.866. Calibration showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA suggested net benefit over an exploratory threshold range of approximately 0.10-0.50, which should not be interpreted as a validated treatment-switching threshold. The nomogram showed promising internal discrimination for estimating 6-month ETF risk in advanced HCC patients receiving SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab. Given the modest sample size and single-center design, the model remains exploratory and hypothesis-generating. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation or use for treatment selection.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1905649.abstract: Lenvatinib, a multi-kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR 1–3 and FGFR 1–4, is a first-line therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). While palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia and generalized erythematous rashes are recognized side effects, lenvatinib-induced lichenoid drug reactions (LDRs) remain infrequently reported and pose significant diagnostic challenges when presenting as viral exanthematous mimics. This case describes an 82-year-old female with metastatic HCC who developed a generalized, pruritic, and vesicular rash mimicking disseminated herpes zoster shortly after initiating lenvatinib. Despite prior shingles vaccination, empiric intravenous acyclovir was initiated. A skin biopsy revealed a lichenoid dermatitis with Civatte bodies and significant eosinophilia, confirming an LDR. The eruption resolved following systemic corticosteroid therapy, indicating a likely reaction to recent lenvatinib exposure. This case highlights the importance of histopathological verification and chronological drug reconciliation in differentiating drug-induced dermatotoxicity from viral exanthems in fragile oncology populations.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1906141.abstract: This study assessed MAGEA4 expression in recurrent bladder cancer, examined its relationships with molecular and immune subtypes, and evaluated its association with treatment response and prognosis. This single-center exploratory cohort study enrolled 20 patients. RNA sequencing was performed on recurrent tumor tissue samples. The EU molecular subtypes were determined. Immune subtypes were classified, and PD-L1 and HER2 status were assessed. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed. Patients were divided into MAGEA4-high and MAGEA4-low groups using the cohort median expression level. Differences in the composition of molecular/immune subtypes were compared. Within-cohort ROC analysis was used to assess discrimination of clinical benefit, and PFS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods. The top 20 genes with the most prominent between-subtype expression differences were identified. Genes upregulated in the Luminal papillary subtype were enriched in terms related to cell-cell junctions and epithelial structure maintenance. Downregulated genes were enriched in pathways associated with immune activation and inflammatory infiltration. Enrichment signals involved the PI3K-Akt, MAPK, neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, and JAK-STAT pathways. Significant differences in PD-L1 status, TMIT subtypes, and EU subtypes were observed between MAGEA4-high and MAGEA4-low groups, and the six MAGEA4-immune/molecular association tests remained below q<0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. MAGEA4 expression also differed according to PD-L1 status, TMIT subtype, and binary EU subtype grouping. Within-cohort ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0.798, 0.800, and 0.750 in the overall, immunotherapy, and combination-therapy cohorts, respectively; the bootstrap optimism-corrected overall AUC was 0.793. High MAGEA4 expression was associated with shorter PFS. MAGEA4 expression was associated with PD-L1 status, TMIT immune subtypes, and EU molecular subtypes, showed within-cohort discrimination of clinical benefit, and was associated with poorer PFS. These findings support further evaluation of MAGEA4 as a candidate molecular stratification marker in independent cohorts.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1906231.abstract: To develop and validate a nomogram that integrates ultrasound features of the primary tumor and axillary lymph nodes with lymphovascular invasion (LVI) for early postoperative risk stratification of high axillary nodal burden (HNB; ≥3 positive nodes) in patients with node-positive invasive breast cancer. A total of 175 consecutive patients with node-positive invasive breast cancer who underwent surgery between July 2023, and October 2025 were retrospectively included in the development cohort, and an additional 86 patients treated during the same period comprised of the internal validation cohort. Two senior radiologists independently reviewed preoperative ultrasound images and clinicopathological data, including LVI assessed in postoperative surgical specimens. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors and construct the nomogram. The proportions of patients with posterior echo attenuation, microcalcification, claw sign, angular margin sign, spiculation sign (significant long spicules/short spicules), suspicious axillary lymph node status, and lymphovascular invasion were all higher in the high-load group than in the low-load group (all P < 0.05). Multivariate regression analysis showed that the absence of the marginal angular margin sign (OR = 0.190, 95% CI: 0.084 - 0.432, P < 0.001) and the normal axillary lymph node status (OR = 0.208, 95% CI: 0.089 - 0.456, P < 0.001) were independent protective factors for HNB, whereas lymphovascular invasion (presence) (OR = 2.707, 95% CI: 1.363 - 5.377, P = 0.004) was an independent risk factor. ROC analysis showed that the combined detection of marginal angular margin sign, lymph node status, and lymphovascular invasion had a higher AUC value for predicting HNB than individual detections (Z = 4.176, 3.781, and 3.672, respectively; P < 0.05). The nomogram incorporating the angular margin sign, axillary lymph node ultrasound status, and LVI provides effective early postoperative risk stratification for HNB in patients with node-positive invasive breast cancer and may facilitate timely adjuvant treatment decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1906245.abstract: Conversion strategy is the optimal treatment for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). However, a severe lack of future liver remnant (FLR) may result in early withdrawal. In this small sample retrospective study, we investigated FLR changes after conversion therapies. Notably, patients with ipsilateral Vp3 portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) showed a significant FLR increase after treatment and provided an advantage for carrying out radical surgery. 53 uHCC patients with Vp0 to Vp3 tumor thrombus were enrolled and divided into two groups (Vp0-2 and Vp3) based on the initial PVTT status. All patients received anti-PD-L1 and anti-VEGF therapy combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) every three weeks. The FLR was measured at baseline and after 3-4 cycles. The odds ratio (OR) between Vp3 and FLR changes was calculated. Among the 53 patients, 28 achieved complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) after conversion treatment. FLR did not change in Vp0-2 group, regardless of the response. While a significant FLR increase was observed in Vp3 group, especially in patients with CR and PR. 10 cases of successfully converted Vp3 patients showed an average FLR enlargement of 18.5%. According to our study, Vp3 patients demonstrated greater FLR enlargement after conversion therapy combined with HAIC, probably due to the thrombus' restriction on blood flow to the tumor side liver. This observation may help to increase both the surgeons' and the uHCC patients' confidence in continuing treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1906629.abstract: Cisplatin has been a standard chemotherapeutic agent for advanced non-small cell lung cancer for decades. Conventionally administered intravenously, it undergoes systemic distribution, exposing both tumour and healthy tissues to the drug. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection of cisplatin is emerging as a potential intratumoural drug delivery (ITDD) strategy. However, rigorous preclinical research is needed before ITDD can be more widely adopted. We used our experimentally induced ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) model, generated by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) infection, to evaluate transthoracic and transbronchial ITDD techniques. We compared systemic platinum exposure following intravenous cisplatin delivery with that following intratumoural cisplatin administration. Both non-recovery and recovery studies were conducted in a total of eight sheep. ITDD techniques were successfully developed and performed in three tumour bearing sheep during non-recovery procedures. To provide a reference for systemic platinum exposure, intravenous cisplatin was administered to three JSRV-infected sheep that did not develop OPA. Intravenous administration produced a rapid plasma platinum peak followed by a rapid decline. ITDD resulted in preferential platinum deposition within targeted lung tumours while producing substantially lower systemic platinum exposure compared with intravenous administration. Intratumoural cisplatin delivery was also evaluated in a recovery procedure using a single sheep, comparing single-site and fractionated administration over a 28-day period, with tumour biopsies confirming lesion presence before treatment. Following ITDD, tumour volumes were observed to decrease over the study period. The recovery experiments demonstrated the feasibility of repeated tumour biopsies, intratumoural injections, longitudinal CT monitoring and recovery anaesthesia using the OPA model. To our knowledge, this is the first report of direct intratumoural cisplatin administration into ovine lung tumours. This study also provides proof-of-concept that this clinically relevant large animal lung cancer model can serve as a translational platform for evaluating intratumoural therapeutic delivery strategies relevant to human lung cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1906977.abstract: Prion proteins (PrP) are primarily known for their role in neurodegenerative conditions like Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, where the misfolded, pathogenic isoform PrPSc propagates by using the normal cellular prion protein, PrPc, as a template, leading to aggregation and neuronal death. PrPc is a widely expressed glycoprotein that, beyond its role in prion disease, has emerged in specific contexts as a modulator of several hallmark cancer processes, including proliferation, apoptosis resistance, cellular signaling, adhesion, survival, and motility. This paper explores current evidence on how PrPc, and its misprocessed isoform pro-PrP, contribute to tumor progression across multiple cancer types, using colorectal cancer (CRC) as a unifying disease model to integrate mechanisms that are otherwise dispersed across the literature. This review will examine PrPc's role in sustaining proliferative signaling, resisting apoptosis, promoting migration and metastasis through its interaction with filamin A (FLNa), and contributing to therapy resistance. The goal is to consider the extent to which these mechanisms converge specifically in CRC, and what this means for PrPc's potential as a diagnostic and therapeutic target.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1907524.abstract: We present a 79-year-old male patient with MSI-H/TMB-H (91.5 mutations/Mb) metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who progressed following abiraterone and enzalutamide treatment. When toripalimab was started, his serum PSA was 102 ng/mL. We maintained androgen-deprivation therapy with leuprorelin and stopped enzalutamide. Toripalimab 240 mg was given intravenously every 21 days. His PSA dropped below 0.09 ng/mL after three treatment cycles. We retrospectively applied RECIST version 1.1 criteria and selected the locally invasive prostate-soft-tissue mass as our only measurable non-nodal target lesion. Its maximal diameter shrank from 119 mm at baseline to 43 mm after six cycles (63.9% reduction), and further to 31 mm after 25 cycles (73.9% reduction), satisfying criteria for partial response. Pelvic lymph nodes could only be classified as non-target disease because short-axis diameters were unavailable in imaging reports, though these nodes resolved on imaging after six cycles. Bone lesions were not included in RECIST response evaluation and were interpreted separately on serial bone scans. At cycle 31 (roughly 21 months after toripalimab commencement), PSA stayed undetectable without clinical or radiological signs of progression; the biochemical response persisted for about 19 months starting from cycle 3. As of manuscript revision, the patient remains on toripalimab plus leuprorelin with routine follow-up. No treatment-related adverse events were identified using CTCAE version 5.0. We also conducted a targeted narrative review of mCRPC cases treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors other than pembrolizumab. This single-case observation highlights the value of genomic profiling for mCRPC patients with relevant biomarkers. Readers should interpret these findings as hypothesis-generating and not proof of universal toripalimab activity.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1907591.abstract: The practice of artificial intelligence has recently expanded several social spheres, with the pharmaceutical domain leading the way. Given that AI can facilitate rational drug design, it is plausible to envision its involvement in developing pharmaceutical products from the laboratory to the patient's bedside. AI recognizes hit and lead compounds, followed by validation of therapeutic targets and optimization of molecular design. Artificial intelligence significantly impacts drug discovery and development processes, including target identification, molecule design, drug-drug interactions, drug repurposing, optimization of clinical trials, drug toxicity prediction, drug formulation, and delivery. AI-assisted approaches are progressively being employed for identification and prioritization of targets, biomarker discovery and virtual screening as well as prediction for the interaction of protein and ligand and their molecular properties followed by ADMET screening, molecular design and repurposing to be suited for clinical trial optimization. The significance of automation will be boosted by adopting the most recent artificial intelligence-based technologies, reducing the time it takes for drugs to be available in the market with improved quality, production process safety, and resource utilization. The application of artificial intelligence may not only aid in rapid decision-making but can also enhance the process of incorporating the newly discovered drug into the optimum dosage form, which leads to faster manufacturing of higher-quality drugs and ensures consistency among batches. The potential of artificial intelligence in drug discovery and development, has been explored in this review, encircling several stages from identification of target to its clinical applications, followed by drug development approaches encompassing the future of artificial intelligence in the pharmaceutical sector, along with crosstalk on the tools and tactics used to enforce artificial intelligence, current difficulties, and respective solutions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1907942.abstract: To investigate utility of a novel ratio, lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR), for improved prognostic stratification in RCC. We conducted a retrospective machine learning-based analysis in a multicenter RCC cohort who underwent surgery (Radical or Partial Nephrectomy). Cut-off for "low" or "high" LCR was delineated by receiver operating characteristics/area under curve (ROC/AUC). Multivariable Analysis was conducted for predictors of all-cause mortality (ACM) and cancer-specific mortality (CSM). LCR, along with UCLA Integrated Staging System (UISS) factors, were included into MVA model to evaluate CSM. Employing Classification and Regression Tree (CART), we developed a decision tree based on hazard ratios (HR). The predictive performance was calculated using ROC/AUC. We analyzed 2071 patients [low LCR n=598/high LCR n=1473; cut-off=237.87 (AUC = 0.80)], median follow-up 60 months). Low LCR is an independent risk factor for ACM (HR = 2.75, p 2.0 (high-risk)]. AUC of 0.91 was revealed for the modified UISS model (AUC = 0.85 in the classic UISS model). Our findings are limited by retrospective design. This study provides evidence supporting the prognostic significance of LCR in RCC. While low LCR was associated with poorer survival outcomes, incorporating LCR into the UISS model enhanced prognostic stratification in RCC patients. Further investigation is requisite to validate our findings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1908021.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) has highly heterogeneous postoperative survival. Although contemporary prognostic assessment ideally requires molecular, functional, and surgical-detail variables, these data are often unavailable in population-based and multicenter real-world datasets. Adults with histologically recorded GBM and tumor-directed surgery (resection or biopsy) in SEER formed the derivation cohort. A multivariable Cox model estimated 6-, 12-, and 18-month overall survival and was externally evaluated in CGGA and an independent institutional cohort without refitting. Because extent of resection, biopsy details, performance status, MGMT promoter methylation, IDH status, and treatment-regimen details were unavailable or non-harmonizable, the model was explicitly intended for registry-based survival stratification when contemporary core prognostic variables are absent. The study included 3, 842 patients in the SEER derivation cohort, 512 in the CGGA validation cohort, and 96 in the institutional validation cohort. Age, marital status, year of diagnosis, tumor location, tumor size, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy were retained in the final model. The model showed acceptable discrimination and calibration in the derivation cohort and reproducible risk stratification in both validation cohorts. In the independent non-public institutional validation cohort, the 6-, 12-, and 18-month AUCs were 0.748, 0.721, and 0.694, respectively, with a Harrell's C-index of 0.708, supporting reproducible risk stratification in a real-world clinical patient cohort. This multicohort study developed a registry-compatible survival stratification model for surgically managed glioblastoma for GBM using routinely available variables. The model may support survival estimation under data-constrained conditions, but should not be interpreted as a comprehensive neuro-oncology prognostic system or treatment decision-support tool.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1908104.abstract: In colorectal cancer, the AJCC T category is defined by the depth of bowel wall invasion rather than by the absolute size of the primary tumor. The clinical value of tumor size in assessing tumor aggressiveness, metastatic risk, and prognosis remains insufficiently investigated. To evaluate the clinical value of tumor size in assessing potential metastatic risk and prognostic stratification in colorectal cancer. We retrospectively included 10,513 patients with colorectal cancer who underwent surgical treatment at FUSCC between 2008 and 2020. We integrated tumor size with clinicopathological characteristics to assess metastatic risk using machine-learning models and SHAP-based interpretation. By modeling tumor size as both a categorical and continuous variable, we further investigated its prognostic relevance using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression incorporating restricted cubic splines. Additionally, an independent cohort of 6,739 patients from Changhai Hospital was used for external validation. Machine-learning identified lymph node metastasis as the primary predictive endpoint, with the CatBoost model achieving the highest AUROC of 0.800. SHAP analysis showed that smaller tumor diameter contributed positively to predicted metastatic risk. Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis further demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between tumor diameter and OS, with mortality risk increasing as tumor diameter decreased within the approximately 0-3 cm range. Among younger male patients with locally advanced disease, tumors ≤3 cm were associated with significantly worse OS and DFS than tumors >5 cm (both P < 0.001). External validation yielded similar findings. Smaller tumor size may paradoxically indicate higher lymph node metastatic risk and poorer prognosis in a subset of patients with colorectal cancer, particularly younger male patients with locally advanced disease. Tumor size may therefore serve as a complementary factor for postoperative risk stratification beyond conventional TNM staging.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1908104.title: New insights into tumor size in colorectal cancer: smaller size, higher risk?

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1908617.abstract: Advanced recurrent gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after prolonged tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) exposure requires integration of surgical oncology, molecular reassessment, and continuous systemic therapy. We report a 72-year-old man with a 21-year history of gastric GIST who underwent initial resection in 2005, resection of recurrent disease in 2009, and long-term imatinib therapy. After years of apparent disease stability, he independently reduced imatinib and had a prolonged surveillance gap before recurrence was detected in 2024. Following tumor rupture and short-interval progression on sunitinib and regorafenib, he received ripretinib. In January 2026, clinically necessary maximal cytoreductive surgery was performed for bulky recurrent peritoneal disease with bleeding, anemia, abdominal-wall involvement, high risk of re-rupture, and invasion or close involvement of the right colon. Pathology confirmed recurrent high-risk spindle-cell GIST. Postoperative next-generation sequencing identified a founding KIT exon 11 deletion and a secondary KIT exon 17 p.Asn822Tyr activation-loop mutation; ripretinib was resumed after recovery of oral intake. Three-month CT showed recurrent peritoneal tumors, while a right hepatic subcapsular low-enhancement nodule was favored to represent post-ablation change. This case illustrates that surgery in resistant recurrent GIST may be necessary for local complication control and tissue acquisition, but even after maximal macroscopic cytoreduction, durable management depends on continuous genotype-informed systemic therapy and close surveillance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1909040.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as potential treatment options for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) resistance. We evaluated their efficacy and safety in this setting. PubMed, Embase,and the Cochrane Library were searched for prospective clinical studies. Overlapping reports were assessed before endpoint-specific synthesis. Comparable proportional outcomes from non-randomized studies were pooled using random-effects models, whereas randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were summarized separately. Eight eligible clinical study reports were included. Four non-randomized reports contributed five independent underlying trial datasets; however, the ORR and DCR meta-analysis each included four non-overlapping analytical estimates because one pooled Dato-DXd estimate represented two underlying trial datasets that were not entered separately. The pooled ORR was 39.2%(95% CI,31.1%-48.0%),and the pooled DCR was 78.9%(95% CI,72.3%-84.2%).Three comparable non-overlapping datasets contributed to the grade ≥3 TEAE analysis, yielding a pooled incidence of 65.2%(95% CI,50.2%-77.7%),whereas four analytical datasets contributed to the ILD analysis, with a pooled reported incidence of 6.0%(95% CI,4.1%-8.5%).Two RCTs provided comparative evidence supporting sac-TMT, particularly for ORR and PFS. ADCs showed antitumor activity after EGFR-TKI resistance, but efficacy and toxicity varied across platforms. Additional randomized trials and biomarker-informed studies are needed to define the optimal use of individual ADCs. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261288638, identifier CRD420261288638.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1909193.abstract: High-grade gliomas remain among the most aggressive tumors in neuro-oncology. Although prognosis is strongly influenced by tumor biology, survival in low- and middle-income countries is also shaped by health-system factors, including delayed diagnosis, limited surgical infrastructure, incomplete adjuvant therapy, and restricted molecular diagnostics. The implementation of the 2021 World Health Organization Classification of Central Nervous System Tumors has further exposed diagnostic inequities, as integrated histomolecular classification depends on molecular tools that are not uniformly available in resource-limited settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize contemporary evidence on survival outcomes, surgical access, extent of resection, adjuvant treatment delivery, and molecular diagnostic gaps among patients with high-grade gliomas treated in low- and middle-income countries. A systematic search was conducted following PRISMA 2020 recommendations. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, Global Index Medicus, LILACS, African Index Medicus, IndMED, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2016 and May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with histologically or molecularly confirmed WHO grade 3 or grade 4 gliomas treated in low- or middle-income countries and reporting survival, surgical-access, adjuvant-treatment, or molecular-diagnostic outcomes. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO as CRD420261398058. A total of 30 independent studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Twenty-four studies contributed overall survival data, 18 reported surgical-access outcomes, 21 evaluated adjuvant-treatment delivery, and 12 examined molecular-diagnostic availability. Most included investigations were retrospective institutional cohorts, although registry-based studies, randomized clinical trials, and molecular implementation studies were also identified. Survival outcomes varied substantially across healthcare settings and were consistently influenced by delayed diagnosis, limited access to maximal safe resection, incomplete radiotherapy, restricted temozolomide availability, treatment abandonment, and insufficient molecular characterization. Survival in high-grade gliomas in low- and middle-income countries is not determined by tumor biology alone. It is shaped by sequential "survival gates": timely diagnosis, access to maximal safe resection, completion of radiotherapy and temozolomide-based chemotherapy, molecular classification, and longitudinal follow-up. Future strategies should move beyond simple guideline translation and focus on scalable neuro-oncology pathways that improve surgical capacity, adjuvant-treatment continuity, and access to essential molecular diagnostics. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261398058, identifier CRD420261398058.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1909193.title: High-grade gliomas where resources define survival: a systematic review and meta-analysis of outcomes, surgical access, and molecular diagnostic gaps in low- and middle-income countries.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1909979.abstract: The optimal integration of surgery and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) following modern neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains controversial. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have substantially improved outcomes in both resectable and unresectable disease, prospective randomized data directly comparing surgery and definitive CRT after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy are lacking. InDuRanS is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial conducted in Germany. Patients with (borderline) resectable stage IIB-IIIA/B (N2) NSCLC receive three cycles of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy with durvalumab plus platinum-paclitaxel. Patients with persistent resectability are randomized 1:1 to surgery or definitive CRT. Both treatment arms receive consolidation durvalumab for up to 12 months. The primary endpoint is 2-year event-free survival in 158 randomized patients. Key secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety and tolerability, health-related quality of life, and an extensive exploratory translational research program. InDuRanS is the first randomized trial to directly compare surgery versus definitive CRT within a contemporary multimodal treatment sequence incorporating both neoadjuvant and consolidation immunotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B NSCLC. Its results are expected to help define optimal local treatment strategies in an evolving therapeutic landscape. InDuRanS is currently active and open to enrollment as of April 2025, with primary completion anticipated in 2028 (NCT06810609).

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1910070.abstract: Imaging-guided interventional radiotherapy (IG-IRT) is the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer but remains time-consuming and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to improve efficiency and reproducibility. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2010 and 2026 investigating AI-based imaging applications in cervical IRT. Eligible studies included original research evaluating segmentation (targets and organ at risk), planning, reconstruction, image registration and applicator selection. Fifty-two studies were included. Deep learning-based segmentation showed variable performance across anatomical structures and studies, with Dice coefficients approaching or exceeding 0.90 for some organs at risk and target volumes in the best-performing models. Individual studies reported shorter processing times, reduced contouring variability, accurate applicator reconstruction, and potential support for applicator selection. However, the substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity precluded direct comparisons among AI approaches. The available studies suggest that AI may support the automation of selected workflow steps and assist treatment-related decision-making in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy. While several applications have achieved high technical performance, most remain at the proof-of-concept stage, and robust external validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed before routine clinical adoption.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1910817.abstract: This study aimed to compare the effects of various first-line systemic therapies on health-related quality of life (HR-QoL) in patients with unresectable advanced gastric cancer (GC), and to comprehensively integrate survival benefits and HR-QoL outcomes associated with different treatments. A systematic literature search was conducted in the MEDLINE, CENTRAL and Scopus databases for studies published from database inception to December 2025. Manual retrieval of reference lists and abstracts from major oncology conferences held between 2016 and 2025 was performed as supplementary screening. Eligible studies were phase III randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared immune checkpoint inhibitors or targeted agents with platinum-based chemotherapy as first-line regimens for advanced GC and reported data on HR-QoL deterioration. Time to deterioration (TTD) of HR-QoL domains was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-STO22 and EQ-5D questionnaires. The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was applied to rank all included treatments based on HR-QoL indicators. We further performed an exploratory composite analysis integrating overall-survival and HR-QoL outcomes via the minimum distance criterion. In total, 10 RCTs enrolling over 8000 patients and covering six HR-QoL domains met the inclusion criteria. SUCRA analyses indicated that trastuzumab and tislelizumab had the lowest probability of the deterioration of global health status, physical function, nausea/vomiting, appetite loss and pain. When HR-QoL was combined with overall survival (OS) via an exploratory minimum distance criterion composite analysis, trastuzumab and tislelizumab showed favorable comprehensive performance across most evaluated domains. This composite metric remains exploratory without established uncertainty estimates and should not serve as primary evidence for clinical decision-making. This network meta-analysis suggests that trastuzumab (for HER2-positive disease) and tislelizumab (for largely biomarker-unselected populations) deliver the balance between HR-QoL preservation and OS benefit within their respective biomarker-eligible patient subgroups among systemic treatment options for unresectable advanced GC. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261422326.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1910929.abstract: We report the management of a 36-year-old man presenting with rapidly progressive and highly symptomatic cutaneous metastases (CMs) from metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). He was referred to palliative radiotherapy because of painful and pruritic skin lesions. His history included two synchronous colorectal adenocarcinomas. Comprehensive next-generation sequencing identified the rectosigmoid tumor as the metastatic source and revealed a pathogenic germline BRCA1 mutation, supporting a precision systemic strategy (olaparib plus pembrolizumab). CMs were the patient's dominant source of morbidity and progressively involved new skin sites; the patient therefore, received three sequential courses of helical tomotherapy (Radixact®), each delivering 30 Gy in 10 fractions to extended superficial volumes exceeding 50 cm. Each course treated adjacent fields with limited high-dose overlap. Deformable co-registration with the prior plans and cumulative-dose review confirmed that the high-dose overlap was limited, distinguishing this approach from re-irradiation. A posterior skin strip was consistently spared to preserve lymphatic drainage and reduce the risk of compartment toxicity. All three courses produced a very good partial response (VGPR) at six weeks, with toxicity limited to grade 1 dermatitis (no grade ≥2). Crucially, repeated irradiation maintained durable symptom control, avoided escalation of opioid analgesia for approximately six months, and allowed continuation of the same systemic regimen for nine months until lung progression. This case illustrates that iterative skin-directed radiotherapy can deliver safe, repeatable, high-quality palliation in extensive CMs.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1911550.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA regulatory networks, and established an AML prognostic model to evaluate the tumor immune microenvironment. Combining survival analysis, clinical correlation, immune infiltration assessment and m6A modification analysis, SLC15A3 was preliminarily screened as a candidate prognostic gene for AML. Subsequent weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning (ML) and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses further identified SLC15A3 as a promising prognostic biomarker for AML. Finally, RT-qPCR and Western blotting assays verified its aberrant expression in AML cells. Consistent with bioinformatic prediction,SLC15A3 serves as a shared candidate biomarker for AML and COVID-19,although its mechanistic role linking AML and SARS-CoV-2-related inflammation requires further functional validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1912108.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) continues to present therapeutic challenges because of pathway redundancy and treatment resistance, underscoring the need for multi-target and systems-level strategies. Baicalein (BA), a flavonoid metabolite from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, shows antitumor potential, yet integrative and immune-related evaluations of BA in LUAD remain limited. We integrated network analyses with TCGA-LUAD transcriptomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), network topology, GO/KEGG enrichment, bulk RNA-seq-based immune-infiltration estimation (CIBERSORT), molecular docking, and clinical association analysis (GEPIA2/HPA). Cell viability was assessed in A549 cells​ using the CCK-8 assay, and AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression were further examined experimentally by western blot analysis. A total of 117 candidate BA-LUAD overlapping targets were identified, and six candidate hub genes (EGFR, AKT1, TP53, BCL2, HIF1A, and ESR1) were prioritized. Enrichment analyses suggested that the candidate network was associated with oncogenic signaling and stress-response programs, particularly PI3K-AKT/MAPK signaling, ROS-related processes, apoptosis, and p53 signaling. CCK-8 assays showed that BA reduced A549 cell viability in vitro, with IC50 values of 54.93 μM at 24 h and 22.83 μM at 48 h. Among the prioritized candidates, AKT1 and BCL2 were selected for focused experimental assessment in A549 cells. BA treatment reduced AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression in A549 cells, whereas total AKT1 remained largely unchanged. HIF1A expression showed broad associations with computationally estimated immune-cell fractions and poorer overall survival. These findings prioritize a BA-associated candidate network in LUAD involving kinase signaling, apoptosis-related regulation, oxidative-stress responses, and immune-microenvironment associations. The CCK-8 results support an inhibitory effect of BA on A549 cell viability in vitro, and the observed changes in AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression provide focused experimental support for selected components of the candidate network; further in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate biological relevance and translational potential.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1913036.abstract: Frailty is associated with poor short-term surgical outcomes, but whether the Fried frailty phenotype is associated with long-term mortality after curative colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, independently of age and tumor stage, is uncertain. We examined this association using restricted mean survival time (RMST), which does not require proportional hazards. This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 304 patients aged ≥60 years who underwent curative CRC surgery at three centers in China in 2018-2019. The preoperative Fried phenotype was analyzed as robust (n=131), pre-frail (n=57), or frail (n=116); binary (robust versus non-robust) and ordinal codings were secondary. The primary outcome was 5-year all-cause mortality. Because proportional hazards were violated (Schoenfeld test P = 0.011), the RMST difference at 60 months was the primary effect measure, adjusted by pseudo-observation regression for age, sex, and TNM stage, the minimal adjustment set from a directed acyclic graph. Stage-specific and time-varying-effect analyses were also performed. Over a median follow-up of 60 months, 27 patients (8.9%) died. Five-year survival was 96.2%, 84.2%, and 88.8% in robust, pre-frail, and frail patients (log-rank P = 0.015). Unadjusted RMST differences versus robust patients were -2.38 months (95% CI -4.45 to -0.78) for pre-frail and -2.73 months (-4.58 to -1.09) for frail patients. After adjustment for age, sex, and TNM stage they were -1.48 months (-3.42 to 0.45; P = 0.13) and -0.81 months (-2.56 to 0.93; P = 0.36); for non-robust versus robust patients, -1.16 months (-2.50 to 0.19; P = 0.092). Estimates were in the same direction within every stage but imprecise. The hazard ratio for non-robust patients appeared higher in the first 36 months than later, but period-specific estimates were unstable and did not differ significantly (P = 0.15). The Fried frailty phenotype identified older patients with lower 5-year survival after curative CRC surgery. After adjustment for age and tumor stage the association was attenuated and imprecise, so an independent effect could not be established with 27 deaths. The apparent early concentration of excess mortality in non-robust patients is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger cohorts with treatment and cause-of-death data.
