doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1913564.abstract: Survival differences by age are well recognized in adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LBL), but their timing, competing-mortality structure, and behavior across recent diagnosis periods remain less clear. This retrospective SEER cohort included adults diagnosed during 2010-2023, excluding Burkitt leukemia/lymphoma. We estimated overall survival (OS), 3-year restricted mean survival time (RMST), and cumulative incidence of ALL/LBL-attributable and other/unknown-cause death. Cox, Fine-Gray, spline, and exploratory time-split models assessed age associations. Among 9,491 patients, 4,618 died: 3,828 deaths were attributed to ALL/LBL and 790 to other or unknown causes. Three-year RMST was 1.89, 2.10, and 2.14 years in 2010-2014, 2015-2019, and 2020-2023, respectively; the recent-period difference was 0.044 years (95% CI -0.016 to 0.104; P = 0.150). Median follow-up in 2020-2023 was 22 months. Compared with age 18-39 years, the adjusted overall-mortality HR for age >=75 years was 6.258 (95% CI 5.627-6.960). Because proportional hazards were violated, this HR should be read as a summary association. The exploratory HR was 8.201 (95% CI 7.224-9.311) during the first year and 3.496 (95% CI 2.885-4.236) thereafter. At 3 years, cumulative incidence in patients aged >=75 years was 70.4% for ALL/LBL-attributable death by registry attribution and 12.8% for other/unknown-cause death. The spline test supported departure from linearity (P<0.001); the age-by-period interaction was not significant (P = 0.182), whereas an exploratory age-by-subtype interaction was nominally significant (P = 0.024, unadjusted for multiplicity). Older age was associated with higher mortality, especially in the first year after diagnosis. ALL/LBL-attributable death predominated by registry attribution even in the oldest group. The 3-year comparison did not establish a survival difference between 2015-2019 and 2020-2023; limited follow-up and residual case-mix differences preclude concluding that progress has stopped.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1913732.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely due to invasion, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Dysregulated cholesterol metabolism is increasingly recognised as a driver of gastric cancer progression, but how intracellular cholesterol trafficking contributes to malignant junctional remodelling remains poorly understood. MLN64/STARD3 is a cholesterol-binding lipid transfer protein associated with cancer progression, yet its functional role in gastric cancer cell architecture and aggressiveness has not been fully defined. In this study, we investigated whether MLN64 is associated with cholesterol-dependent tight junction organisation and malignant behaviour in gastric cancer cells. Stable MLN64 knockdown in AGS and HGC-27 cells reduced membrane-associated free cholesterol, as shown by an approximately 50% decrease in the Filipin III membrane/cytoplasm fluorescence ratio in both cell lines. MLN64 depletion was also associated with reduced ZO-1 protein abundance, disrupted junctional ZO-1 localisation, and impaired tight junction integrity, including reduced transepithelial resistance, altered impedance, and increased paracellular permeability. Functionally, MLN64 depletion attenuated gastric cancer cell proliferation and invasive capacity, supporting an association between this cholesterol-trafficking axis, junctional organisation, and aggressive cellular phenotypes. To explore the pharmacological tractability of this pathway, in silico screening of an FDA-approved drug library identified Digoxin and Targretin as candidate compounds predicted to interact with the MLN64 START domain. Digoxin showed a favourable predicted binding energy of -13.73 kcal/mol. Functional validation showed that these agents phenocopied several effects of MLN64 depletion, including altered cholesterol distribution, reduced junctional ZO-1 organisation, impaired adhesion/migration dynamics, and reduced barrier function. Together, these findings identify MLN64 as a regulator associated with cholesterol-dependent tight junction remodelling in gastric cancer cells. Digoxin and Targretin provide preliminary evidence that this pathway may be pharmacologically tractable; however, direct target-engagement and rescue studies will be required to establish causality and determine whether their effects are mediated through direct interaction with MLN64. The MLN64- cholesterol axis may represent a potential vulnerability in gastric cancer membrane organisation and progression.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1913768.abstract: Drug resistance continues to pose a significant challenge, accounting for a large proportion of relapses and playing a major role in cervical cancer-related mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence has indicated that the aberrant expression of non-coding RNAs, especially circular RNAs (circRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and microRNAs (miRNAs) is responsible for drug resistance, which poses a significant challenge to the success of chemotherapy. Addressing drug resistance is crucial for improving patient outcomes and reducing the burden of cervical cancer on healthcare systems. In this review, we summarize the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which circRNAs, miRNAs and lncRNAs mediate drug resistance to common drugs used in the treatment of cervical cancer. This work underscores non-coding RNAs as a promising therapeutic target, offering a potential avenue for overcoming chemoresistance in cervical cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1913824.abstract: Modified FOLFIRINOX (mFFX) and gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (GnP) are both recommended as standard first-line regimens for unresectable pancreatic cancer (PC). However, direct head-to-head comparative evidence remains scarce, and prior studies have largely failed to distinguish mFFX from standard FOLFIRINOX (sFFX). We systematically compared mFFX with GnP to evaluate their efficacy and toxicities. We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing mFFX with GnP as first-line therapy for unresectable PC published between January 2013 and May 2026. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed using hazard ratios (HRs). Objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were evaluated using risk ratios (RRs). Events of toxicities were assessed using odds ratios (ORs). Five studies (three RCTs and two retrospective studies) involving 1204 patients (578 in the mFFX arm and 626 in the GnP arm) were included. Compared with GnP, mFFX was associated with a shorter OS (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.09-1.45; P = 0.002) and PFS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.04-1.40; P = 0.01), along with a borderline lower DCR (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81-1.00; P = 0.05; I2 = 62%), which was consistent across RCTs (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.94; I2 = 0%) but not observed in retrospective studies (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.71-1.29; I2 = 87%), and ORR did not differ significantly between the two regimens. As for toxicity profiles, mFFX showed an elevated incidence of grade ≥3 diarrhea (OR 5.63) and anorexia (OR 4.44). By contrast, grade ≥3 neutropenia (OR 0.66) and white blood cell decrease (OR 0.49) occurred more frequently under GnP. GnP was associated with more favorable OS and PFS than mFFX, a borderline DCR advantage, and distinct toxicity profiles. Given the modest effect size and the limitations of this study, clinical decision-making should integrate patient age, performance status, and anticipated second-line therapy. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251175959.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1914051.abstract: Kinesiophobia and frailty are common concerns during postoperative recovery in older adults, but their longitudinal relationship after radical prostatectomy (RP) remains unclear. This study examined changes in kinesiophobia and frailty and their reciprocal prospective associations during the first 3 months after RP. A prospective longitudinal study included 380 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing RP. Kinesiophobia and frailty were assessed at 24-48 hours, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively using the TSK-17 and TFI. Cross-lagged panel models were estimated using robust maximum likelihood with full information maximum likelihood for missing data and adjustment for prespecified covariates. Complete-case analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Kinesiophobia and frailty both decreased significantly over the 3-month follow-up (both P < 0.001). T1 frailty was prospectively associated with T2 kinesiophobia (β = 0.210, 95% CI 0.121-0.300, P < 0.001), whereas T1 kinesiophobia was not associated with T2 frailty (β = 0.068, 95% CI -0.034-0.170, P = 0.193). From T2 to T3, significant prospective associations were observed in both directions: kinesiophobia with subsequent frailty (β = 0.278, 95% CI 0.181-0.374, P < 0.001) and frailty with subsequent kinesiophobia (β = 0.154, 95% CI 0.069-0.239, P < 0.001). Kinesiophobia and frailty were dynamically related during early recovery after RP, with their prospective associations varying across postoperative stages. These findings highlight the importance of considering both constructs over time and may help inform stage-specific monitoring during postoperative recovery.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1914278.abstract: Ultrasound-based risk models provide a valuable tool to support non-expert clinicians in evaluating adnexal masses, potentially reducing unnecessary surgeries for benign conditions. However, their implementation in clinical practice across China remains suboptimal, and direct comparisons of their diagnostic accuracy within this specific population are still needed. To evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of three ultrasonography-based risk models-the International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) Simple Rules (with expert adjudication for inconclusive cases), the IOTA Assessment of Different Neoplasias in the Adnexa (ADNEX) model, and the Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS)-for distinguishing benign from malignant adnexal lesions in a Chinese cohort. This retrospective diagnostic study was conducted at a single Chinese academic medical center and included consecutive patients aged 18 to 89 years with adnexal masses that were managed surgically between January 2023 and December 2024. Each adnexal lesion was systematically evaluated using the IOTA Simple Rules, ADNEX model, and O-RADS classification. The diagnostic performance of these models was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and likelihood ratios, using surgical pathology as the reference standard. A secondary analysis evaluated the models' performance stratified by menopausal status. An additional analysis was to evaluate the supplementary value of tumor markers for the O-RADS model. A total of 459 female patients with a 15.5% malignant tumor prevalence were included. Mean age was 43.0 (15.2) years overall, with 40.7 (14.4) in benign and 55.3 (13.3) in malignant cases. Overall, 121 (26.4%) patients were postmenopausal. The AUCs for discriminative performance of the ADNEX and O-RADS models were 0.95 (95%CI, 0.93-0.97) and 0.96 (95%CI, 0.94-0.97), respectively. After converting the ADNEX continuous individualized risk into the discrete ordinal categories of O-RADS, the ADNEX performance was reduced to an AUC of 0.92 (95%CI, 0.90-0.95). The AUC of the Simple Rules was 0.95 (95%CI, 0.93-0.97) and yielded a sensitivity of 95.8% (95%CI, 88.1%-99.1%), specificity of 94.3% (95%CI, 91.5%-96.4%). For a binary comparison of all models (benign vs malignant), a uniform 10% risk threshold (O-RADS score of 4-5) was used. The sensitivity and NPV of all models were above 91% and 98%, respectively. The O-RADS model exhibited the highest sensitivity (97.2%; 95%CI, 90.2%-99.7%), whereas the Simple Rules model demonstrated superior specificity 94.3% (95%CI, 91.5%-96.4%) and the highest PPV (75.6%; 95%CI, 65.4%-84.0%). The sensitivities were higher for menopausal groups, while the specificities were higher for premenopausal patients for the ADNEX and O-RADS model. The addition of tumor markers did not improve the diagnostic sensitivity or specificity of the O-RADS model. In this diagnostic study of a Chinese cohort, the Simple Rules, ADNEX, and O-RADS models demonstrated effective performance in distinguishing benign from malignant adnexal lesions, consistent with previous reports from European and American populations. The use of such risk-stratification models can enhance the accuracy and reproducibility of adnexal mass assessment, particularly for non-specialist clinicians, and may support clinical decision-making and potentially reduce​ avoidable surgical interventions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1914617.abstract: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is characterized by high recurrence rates, highlighting the need for effective, non-invasive diagnostic and risk stratification tools. Although urinary biomarkers are increasingly used worldwide, molecular data specific to Chinese NMIBC populations remain limited. This study explores the potential utility of TERT promoter and FGFR3 hotspot mutations detected in urinary tumor DNA (utDNA) in a prospective Chinese cohort. We prospectively enrolled 106 newly diagnosed NMIBC patients between February 2023 and August 2023 at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (ChiCTR2300076543). First-morning urine samples were collected prior to TURBT. A PCR-based UI-Seek assay was employed to detect hotspot mutations in the promoter region (M1: c.-146 C>T, C250T; M2: c.-124 C>T, C228T) and FGFR3 gene (M1: c.742 C>T, p.R248C; M2: c.746 C>G, p.S249C). The overall mutation rates for TERT promoter and FGFR3 were 49.06% and 15.09%, respectively, with a combined sensitivity of 55.66%. Compared with published study cohorts from Western countries and Japan, Chinese NMIBC patients showed differences in molecular mutation profiles. Notably, the TERT-M2 mutation was associated with tumor aggressiveness, with significant correlations observed for T1 stage (P = 0.011), high-grade tumors (P = 0.011), and high/very high EAU risk categories (P 24 months, n = 40) groups. T1 stage, high tumor grade, high/very high-risk stratification, and TERT mutations (especially the TERT-M2 subtype) were significantly associated with early recurrence (P 0.05). This study characterizes the mutational landscape of urinary tumor DNA (utDNA) in Chinese patients with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). Our findings suggest that utDNA-based detection of TERT promoter mutations, particularly the M2 subtype, and FGFR3 mutations may provide complementary molecular information for recurrence risk assessment. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings and evaluate the clinical potential of utDNA as a non-invasive molecular tool in NMIBC management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1914773.abstract: Oral cancer remains a major global health challenge, with delayed diagnosis contributing to poor prognosis and reduced survival. Dental students play an important role in early detection; however, deficiencies in preparedness and diagnostic confidence have been reported. This study assessed oral cancer knowledge, oral potentially malignant disorder (OPMD) awareness, and diagnostic confidence among Saudi dental students. A quantitative cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 354 dental students and interns from governmental and private dental schools in Saudi Arabia. The questionnaire assessed oral cancer knowledge, OPMD knowledge, and self-reported diagnostic confidence related to screening and biopsy procedures. Participants were classified as meeting or not meeting a study-defined minimum operational threshold of ≥60% of the maximum possible score in each domain; this cutoff was not interpreted as a definition of "good" performance or clinical competence. Associations between participant characteristics and study outcomes were examined using chi-square tests and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses. Overall, 81.9% of participants met the oral cancer knowledge threshold, 55.4% met the OPMD knowledge threshold, and 24.0% met the diagnostic confidence threshold. Most participants correctly identified major oral cancer risk factors, including tobacco smoking (97.2%), alcohol consumption (92.7%), and human papillomavirus infection (86.7%). However, clinically oriented response patterns highlighted areas for educational attention. 20.1% selected the prespecified specialist-referral response for management of a persistent suspicious lesion, while 35.6% recognized factors associated with increased malignant transformation risk in leukoplakia. Intern status remained independently associated with meeting the oral cancer knowledge and diagnostic confidence thresholds in multivariable analyses. The diagnostic-confidence outcome reflected self-perceived preparedness rather than observed screening, referral, or procedural competence. A high proportion of Saudi dental students met the study-defined oral cancer knowledge threshold; however, self-reported diagnostic confidence and preparedness for early detection remained considerably lower. Strengthening competency-based oral cancer education and clinical training may improve early detection preparedness and referral practices among future dental practitioners. Because the domains assessed different constructs and had different effective cutoffs, their threshold proportions should not be compared directly; the diagnostic-confidence findings represent perceived preparedness only.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1915361.abstract: Abscess-like presentations are common in surgical practice, but malignant soft-tissue and lymphoid disorders can occasionally imitate infection and delay definitive treatment. Anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (ALCL) is a CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that may involve skin, lymph nodes, or soft tissue and can show extensive necrosis, inflammatory change, and systemic symptoms. A 17-year-old female student presented with a 3-week history of progressive painful erythema and swelling of the left axilla after ineffective intravenous antibiotic treatment elsewhere. On admission, the lesion was large, indurated, tender, and clinically suspicious for a soft-tissue infection with possible abscess formation. Incision and drainage yielded only scant purulent fluid but abundant friable nodular tissue, and cultures were negative. Persistent fever, local progression, lymphadenopathy, and poor response to antimicrobial therapy prompted multidisciplinary reassessment. Histopathology of the solid tissue demonstrated large pleomorphic lymphoid cells, and immunohistochemistry showed strong CD30 and ALK expression, establishing ALK-positive ALCL. The patient was transferred to hematology and received initial cytoreductive therapy with brentuximab vedotin and short-course zeprumetostat, after which the local tumor burden decreased and delayed wound closure was performed. She subsequently received five cycles of brentuximab vedotin plus CHP and chidamide maintenance after complete remission. A presumed abscess that yields little pus but contains solid friable tissue should not be managed as infection alone. In refractory, culture-negative, or biologically discordant soft-tissue lesions, early biopsy of the cavity wall and solid components may help reduce diagnostic delay and redirect care toward malignancy-specific treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1915652.abstract: TROP2 is expressed in many epithelial tumors including breast and lung cancers. It is a clinically validated ADC target based on approvals of sacituzumab govitecan for triple-negative breast cancer and datopotamab deruxtecan for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. An alternative cytotoxic approach was previously tested with PF-06664178/RN927C, an anti-TROP2 ADC with an auristatin payload, which entered clinical studies but could not be dosed efficaciously due to dose-limiting toxicities including skin rash, mucosal inflammation, and neutropenia. TroptimAb-SL-MMAE was engineered using an optimized anti-TROP2 sacituzumab antibody sequence (TroptimAb) to address issues related to hydrophobicity, non-specific uptake, and ADC developability. Sacituzumab was re-humanized and modified to enhance FcRn-mediated salvage which extended systemic half-life and potentially improving tumor distribution. Its affinity was avidity-tuned to preferentially bind cells with higher TROP2 expression to reduce on-target/off-tumor toxicity. An engineered cysteine in the Fc domain enabled generation of a homogeneous DAR2 ADC and shielded the linker-payload to reduce hydrophobicity and improve biophysical properties. Linker conjugation chemistry was also optimized to improve stability versus earlier cysteine-conjugated ADCs. We describe the preclinical profile of TroptimAb-SL-MMAE including its design, mechanism of action, anti-tumor activity, and pharmacokinetics.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1915658.abstract: Anti-CD38-based quadruplets such as daratumumab-bortezomib-lenalidomide-dexamethasone (D-VRd) or daratumumab-bortezomib-thalidomide-dexamethasone (D-VTd), where lenalidomide is not reimbursed, are the internationally recommended first-line treatment for transplant-eligible myeloma. There is ongoing debate about whether anti-CD38 exposure impairs stem cell collection. Most studies compare daratumumab-containing with non-daratumumab induction whilst keeping the mobilisation strategy constant. None have compared two mobilisation agents against each other in both daratumumab-exposed and daratumumab-naïve patients. We reviewed 66 patients (22 received Ara-C, 44 received CY) who were mobilised at a single centre in Poland between 2018 and 2024. No patients received plerixafor. Patients who were mobilised with Ara-C collected more CD34+ cells than those who received CY, with a median of 12.6 (IQR 9.1-15.9) versus 7.7 (4.9-12.1) ×10⁶/kg (p=0.005), with comparable apheresis sessions. Previous D-VTd treatment did not reduce the overall yield (p=0.43). The benefit of Ara-C persisted in the D-VTd subgroup, despite heavy confounding between induction and mobilisation choice. This is the first direct comparison of Ara-C and CY in the daratumumab era. Ara-C-based mobilisation was associated with higher CD34+ yields than CY in a plerixafor-free setting. The apparent advantage in D-VTd-treated patients is exploratory and requires prospective confirmation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1915743.abstract: To explore perceived barriers and facilitating factors related to symptom-related help-seeking among men with genitourinary malignancies and inform the development of symptom-management support. Men with genitourinary malignancies were recruited through purposive sampling at a tertiary hospital. Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Fifteen men were interviewed, and two themes with five subthemes were identified. Barrier factors comprised limited symptom knowledge, psychosocial concerns, and difficulties accessing information and symptom-management support. Facilitating factors comprised social and family support and perceived benefits of seeking professional help. The findings suggest potential priorities for symptom-management support, including symptom education, family and social support, and accessible professional advice. Their relevance should be considered in relation to the cancer types, age distribution, and care setting represented in this study.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1916194.abstract: To compare pathological complete response (pCR) across different neoadjuvant treatment strategies in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and to identify clinicopathological factors associated with pCR. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 247 consecutive patients with locally advanced ESCC who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2024 and June 2025 were included. Patients were categorized into four treatment groups: chemotherapy alone (CT, n = 50), chemoradiotherapy (CRT, n = 38), chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (CT+IO, n = 142), and chemoradiotherapy plus immunotherapy (CRT+IO, n = 17). Pathological complete response was defined as ypT0N0. Clinicopathological characteristics were compared using χ² or Fisher's exact tests. Factors associated with pCR were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Overall, 63 patients (25.5%) achieved pCR. The pCR rate was lower in the CT group than in the CT+IO group (6.0% vs. 26.8%). After adjustment for potential confounders, chemotherapy alone remained associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO (OR = 0.174, 95% CI, 0.046-0.658, P = 0.010). No significant differences were observed between CT+IO and either CRT or CRT+IO. Receipt of more than two neoadjuvant treatment cycles was associated with higher odds of pCR (OR = 2.764, 95% CI, 1.372-5.565, P = 0.004). Compared with cT3 disease, cT2 disease was associated with higher odds of pCR (OR = 3.049, 95% CI, 1.356-6.857, P = 0.007). Neoadjuvant treatment regimen, the number of neoadjuvant treatment cycles, and pretreatment clinical T stage were associated with pathological complete response in locally advanced ESCC. Chemotherapy alone was associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO, whereas receipt of more than two treatment cycles was associated with higher odds of pCR. These findings provide real-world evidence regarding factors associated with pathological response.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1916194.title: Comparative effectiveness of neoadjuvant treatment strategies and predictors of pathological complete response in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a real-world retrospective cohort study.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1916260.abstract: Glioblastoma remains one of the most treatment-resistant cancers, and temozolomide (TMZ) resistance is a central barrier to durable clinical response. Inhibition of exportin-1 (XPO1) by selinexor has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome resistance in solid tumors; however, its ability to sensitize TMZ-resistant GBM cells and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We evaluated selinexor and TMZ, alone and in combination, in three GBM cell lines with distinct TMZ sensitivity profiles (LN18, resistant; U87MG, moderate; LN229, sensitive), assessing viability, apoptosis, cell cycle distribution, MMR/survival gene expression, apoptotic protein levels, and long-term colony-forming capacity. Selinexor potently sensitized GBM cells to TMZ across all three lines, with the most clinically meaningful effects observed in the TMZ-resistant background. The combination produced synergistic growth inhibition and robust apoptotic induction that neither agent achieved independently, driven by convergent suppression of MCL1 and BIRC6, partial restoration of mismatch repair gene expression, and CHK1-mediated checkpoint activation. Combination treatment induced nuclear p53 accumulation, markedly reduced BCL-2, and increased PARP cleavage, and durably suppressed long-term proliferative capacity. These findings position selinexor as a mechanistically rational TMZ sensitizer in resistant GBM and support further preclinical and translational investigation of this combination strategy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1916260.title: Selinexor enhances temozolomide efficacy in glioblastoma through modulation of multiple resistance-associated mechanisms.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1917039.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are closely associated with the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the clinical value of CTC detection in patients receiving systemic therapy for advanced HCC remains to be fully elucidated. A total of 125 patients with advanced HCC who underwent systemic therapy were enrolled in this study. Five milliliters of peripheral blood were collected at five time points: before treatment initiation, and 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after treatment. CTCs were isolated and captured using the Isolation by Size of Epithelial Tumor Cells (ISET) method. Tumor response to systemic treatment was evaluated according to the modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST). We further analyzed the correlation between dynamic changes in peripheral blood CTC levels and tumor response to systemic therapy. The overall objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were 39.2% (49/125) and 82.4% (103/125), respectively. Dynamic monitoring of CTCs revealed that CTC levels remained persistently high and gradually increased in patients with progressive disease (PD). In patients with complete response (CR) or partial response (PR), CTC levels decreased progressively during treatment and stayed at low levels thereafter. For patients with stable disease (SD), CTC counts began to decline 3 months after treatment but remained higher than those in patients with CR or PR. Baseline CTC levels were negatively correlated with treatment efficacy: patients with higher baseline CTC counts exhibited poorer tumor responses. Patients with baseline CTC counts < 15, CTC counts < 13 at 1 month post-treatment, and CTC counts < 10 at 3 months post-treatment were more likely to achieve an objective tumor response and obtained better therapeutic outcomes. Additionally, these patients had significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) compared with those who exceeded the above cut-off values. Peripheral blood CTC counts are correlated with tumor treatment response in patients with advanced HCC. Serial CTC detection serves as a valuable tool for evaluating the efficacy of systemic therapy in advanced HCC.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1917039.title: Correlation between circulating tumor cell levels and tumor response in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma undergoing immunotherapy and molecular targeted therapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1917420.abstract: To analyze the correlation between inflammation, nutrition and metabolic indicators and the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to construct and validate a nomogram for predicting PTC risk among patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgery, to assist clinicians in making more individualized clinical decisions. Retrospective population-based cohort study. A retrospective study was conducted on the clinical medical records of patients with thyroid masses who underwent surgical treatment at Hebei General Hospital from 2020 to 2024. Independent risk factors for the onset of PTC were screened through Logistic regression analysis. A risk prediction model for the onset of PTC based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators was constructed using R4.3.3 software and externally validated. A total of 1727 patients who underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid nodules were enrolled, among whom 1167 patients (67.6%) were pathologically-confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and 560 patients (32.4%) had benign thyroid nodules after surgery. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated combined Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) (OR = 1.887, 95%CI: 1.174-3.031, P = 0.009), combined metabolic syndrome (MetS) (OR = 2.157, 95%CI: 1.449-3.211, P < 0.001), and elevated uric acid (UA) (OR = 1.640, 95%CI: 1.112-2.417, P = 0.013) were independent risk factors for PTC onset. Age ≥ 55 years (OR = 0.318, 95%CI: 0.238-0.424, P < 0.001), other marital status (OR = 0.067, 95%CI: 0.012-0.392, P = 0.003), and increased prognostic nutritional index (PNI) (OR = 0.934, 95%CI: 0.902-0.966, P < 0.001) were independent protective factors against PTC onset. Based on the above independent risk factors, a nomogram for PTC was constructed. The AUC of the ROC curve in the modeling group was 0.702, and that in the external validation group was 0.721, indicating that the nomogram has good predictive performance. The calibration curve and decision analysis curve also indicate that the nomogram has good predictive performance and clinical application efficacy. Combined HT, combined MetS, and elevated UA are independent risk factors for PTC onset, whereas age ≥ 55 years, other marital status, and PNI level represent independent protective factors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1917420.title: Construction and validation of a nomogram based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators for predicting the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1917474.abstract: To identify latent psychological resilience profiles in older patients after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) and examine their association with physical resilience. A total of 300 patients with prostate cancer were recruited from a Class III Grade A hospital in Sichuan Province between December 2025 and May 2026. Assessments were conducted on postoperative day 3 using the general information questionnaire, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and Physical Resilience Instrument for Older Adults. Latent profile analysis was performed using the total score on the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Generalized linear regression was used to analyze the relationship between psychological and physical resilience across categories among elderly patients after RARP. Three latent psychological resilience profiles were identified among older patients after RARP. Physical resilience scores differed among people with different psychological resilience. The results of generalized regression analysis showed that patients in different psychological resilience profiles of RARP patients were related to their physical resilience (P < 0.05). Older patients after RARP showed heterogeneous psychological resilience profiles, and profile membership was associated with physical resilience. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine the temporal direction and clinical utility of these profiles.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1917548.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy of the male genitourinary system with high metastatic potential and poor clinical outcomes, for which effective biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain limited. This study employed a multi-omics approach, integrating transcriptome profiles, age-related gene screening, and machine learning techniques, to analyze four GEO datasets, in order to identify key diagnostic biomarkers for prostate cancer (PCa). Differentially expressed aging-related genes were identified, with enrichment analyses revealing significant involvement in PCa. Using machine learning algorithms, a robust diagnostic model centered on GSTP1 was developed, demonstrating high predictive performance. GSTP1 depletion drove multiple oncogenic phenotypes, including enhanced proliferation, migration, invasion, and the inhibition of cellular aging and DNA damage, suggesting that GSTP1 may promote cellular senescence while restraining malignant progression. Furthermore, its expression correlated with distinct immunocyte profiles, highlighting a role in shaping the PCa immune landscape. Our findings confirm that GSTP1 functions as an aging-associated stress response gene, offering new perspectives on prostate cancer pathogenesis and showing promise for advancing therapeutic strategies that target both aging and immune associations. This study provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging aging biomarkers in precision oncology and highlights GSTP1 as a promising candidate for clinical translation in PCa management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1918231.abstract: CDK4/6 inhibitors have reshaped treatment for hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, but resistance frequently emerges and may interact with metastatic phenotypic evolution. We developed an integrated resistance-discordance framework and explored its clinical interpretability in invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) with gastric metastasis. Public MSK-INK4 (cBioPortal study ID: breast_ink4_msk_2021) and MBCproject (brca_mbcproject_wagle_2017) cohorts were curated for HR+/HER2-negative disease. A five-module CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance score (0-5) was constructed from predefined mutation and copy-number events. In MBCproject RNA-seq samples, single-sample gene-set enrichment analysis quantified proliferation and estrogen-response activity. Discordance burden was defined as z(proliferation score) minus z(ER score), using primary tumors as the reference. Three institutional IDC gastric-metastasis cases were projected onto the framework for interpretability but not inferential testing. Seventy HR+/HER2-negative MBCproject samples and 1116 deduplicated MSK-INK4 metastatic samples were analyzed. MBCproject metastases had higher resistance scores than primary tumors (P = 0.001), whereas metastatic scores were similar between MBCproject and MSK-INK4 (P = 0.202). Metastases showed higher proliferation activity (P = 0.014) and a trend toward lower ER activity (P = 0.071). The high-resistance/high-discordance quadrant was enriched for PI3K-axis events (OR = 16.52; P = 0.034), chromatin-remodeling loss-of-function events (OR = 12.47; P = 0.001), and cell-cycle/RB-axis events (OR = 9.03; P = 0.001). Among the three IDC gastric-metastasis cases, two available gastric NGS profiles mapped to predefined resistance modules, and the case with increased gastric Ki-67 showed the strongest IHC-adapted discordance and projected toward the high-resistance/high-discordance phenotype. Coupling resistance-associated genomic events with metastatic phenotype discordance may provide a clinically interpretable lens for HR+/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and for rare IDC gastric-metastasis presentations.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1918612.abstract: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney (MEST) is a rare renal neoplasm with biphasic differentiation comprising epithelial and stromal components. It typically appears as a mixed cystic-solid mass on imaging, and the prognosis is favorable in the vast majority of cases. We report a case of MEST with a prominent fat component on imaging: a 54-year-old woman was admitted with a 1-month history of left flank distension and pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed a mixed cystic-solid mass at the lower pole of the left kidney, with a prominent low-attenuation fat-density area surrounding the mass. Preoperatively, the lesion was considered an unusual angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts (AMLEC). Because the lesion was small, located at the lower pole, and relatively well circumscribed, the patient underwent laparoscopic left partial nephrectomy. Postoperative histopathologic examination confirmed that the left renal mass was benign; however, immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated positivity for EMA and PCK in the epithelial component and for PR and ER in the stromal component, supporting a diagnosis of MEST. The adipose tissue submitted separately with the tumor was located around the tumor and could not be definitively confirmed as an intratumoral component. This case demonstrates that MEST may also exhibit prominent adipose tissue on imaging and illustrates the diagnostic pitfall in which fat-related imaging findings cause MEST to mimic AMLEC, making the early distinction between MEST and cystic change in fat-containing renal tumors challenging.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1918905.abstract: Carotid body tumors (CBTs) are rare and highly vascular paragangliomas arising at the carotid bifurcation. Surgical resection remains the standard treatment for CBTs. However, the conventional transcervical approach inevitably leaves a visible cervical scar, which may negatively affect quality of life in patients with cosmetic concerns. A 27-year-old woman presented with a progressively enlarging right neck mass over a 6-month period. Ultrasonography demonstrated a hypervascular lesion surrounding the carotid arteries, and fine-needle aspiration was avoided because of the vascular nature of the tumor. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 4-cm enhancing mass at the carotid bifurcation, highly suggestive of a CBT. Because the patient expressed concern regarding a visible cervical scar, a retroauricular approach was selected after thorough discussion of its potential risks and benefits. The operation was performed by a head and neck surgeon with intraoperative assistance from a vascular surgeon. Complete tumor resection was successfully achieved despite the need for repair of two small arterial defects encountered during tumor mobilization. The operative time was 300 minutes, and the estimated blood loss was 900 mL. The postoperative course was uneventful, and no major complications or tumor recurrence were observed during 12 months of follow-up. The patient reported satisfaction with the cosmetic outcome, although no objective cosmetic assessment was performed. In carefully selected patients with Shamblin type I or II CBT, the retroauricular approach may represent a feasible hidden-scar alternative to the conventional transcervical approach.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1918936.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention in recent years because of its critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and imposes a substantial mortality burden. This study aimed to systematically analyze the global research landscape, hotspots, and developmental trends of ferroptosis in CRC research from 2017 to 2025. English-language publications related to ferroptosis and CRC published between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases. A total of 1, 354 original articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package in R were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses to evaluate annual publication trends, country/region and institutional collaboration networks, author contributions, journal distribution, co-cited references, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. The number of publications in this field increased rapidly after 2020 and peaked in 2025. China ranked first in both publication output and total citations, followed by the United States, and China-United States collaboration constituted the core of the international collaboration network. Central South University was the most productive institution, while journals such as Frontiers in Oncology and Frontiers in Immunology served as major publication platforms. Research hotspots were mainly concentrated on chemotherapy resistance, the tumor immune microenvironment, PANoptosis, prognostic models, non-coding RNAs, gut microbiota, and the regulation of ferroptosis by traditional Chinese medicine and natural products. Ferroptosis has become a rapidly evolving frontier in CRC research. The research focus is gradually shifting from fundamental molecular mechanisms toward translational medical directions, including chemosensitization, combination immunotherapy, reversal of drug resistance, and precise prognostic evaluation. This study provides a systematic reference for understanding the global knowledge structure and future research directions in the field of ferroptosis and CRC.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1919105.abstract: Cervical cancer is one of the most common malignancies of the female reproductive system worldwide, and its development is closely associated with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV). γδ T cells, as key effector cells bridging innate and adaptive immunity, exert unique and complex regulatory functions in tumor immune surveillance. However, the distribution patterns, functional polarization states, and antitumor mechanisms of distinct γδ T-cell subsets within the cervical cancer microenvironment have not yet been systematically elucidated, and the impact of HPV infection on the functional remodeling of γδ T-cell subsets remains controversial. This review summarizes the distribution characteristics and functional polarization states of the major γδ T-cell subsets, including Vδ1, Vδ2, and Vδ3 T cells, in the cervical cancer microenvironment. We further discuss the molecular mechanisms through which these subsets participate in immune surveillance via T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling, NKG2D-mediated recognition, Fas/FasL signaling, and cytokine secretion, and examine the regulatory effects of HPV infection on γδ T-cell subset remodeling. In addition, recent preclinical advances in γδ T-cell subset-based adoptive immunotherapy and combination strategies involving immune checkpoint blockade in cervical cancer are reviewed. Overall, this review aims to provide a theoretical basis and new perspectives for optimizing immunotherapeutic targets and developing individualized treatment strategies for cervical cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1919412.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics resolves tissue organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), whereas most clinically annotated cohorts remain bulk transcriptomic datasets. We evaluated six literature-informed curated composite programs across bulk, single-cell and spatial datasets without assuming a discrete ecosystem taxonomy. The programs comprised Macrophage-rich, T cell-inflamed, Antigen-presentation, Stromal/fibrotic, Immune-cold/exclusion and Proliferative/cycling, with 22 memberships per program (132 memberships, 121 unique genes and 11 shared memberships). In 498 GSE31312 tumors, principal components 1 and 2 (PC1 and PC2) explained 48.6% and 20.8% of score variance. No candidate discrete taxonomy demonstrated sufficient stability for retention; k=2 met silhouette and size criteria but failed both bootstrap-stability thresholds. Historical 15-edge concordance was high for GSE10846 (rho=0.936) and GSE181063 (rho=0.982), whereas the most restrictive GSE10846 edge-exclusion sensitivity, removing both shared-gene and proliferation-associated edges, reduced rho to 0.690. Single-cell analysis of 14,368 DLBCL cells from four patients and eight samples provided descriptive lineage context. In Visium V2 areas, the antigen-presentation series was treated as AP-residual (HLA-unmeasured) because only 13/22 program genes were measurable and all nine HLA genes in the defined program were unavailable. Matched-random-gene-set support was broad but not universal (24/30 DLBCL, 18/24 context/background, 42/54 overall; 25/32 primary-plus-exploratory), whereas both depth-adjusted residual endpoints were supported in 30/30 DLBCL area-program combinations. These findings support continuous program-level interpretation while retaining explicit provenance, stability, assay, method and sampling limitations.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1920042.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common neurological complication of cancer treatment that worsens function and quality of life. Topical herbal medicines are increasingly used as localized interventions for neuropathic symptoms; however, their clinical efficacy remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of topical herbal formulations for CIPN in cancer populations. We systematically searched Scopus, MEDLINE (Ovid), CINAHL, and Cochrane CENTRAL for randomized controlled trials assessing the use of topical herbal formulations in adults with CIPN. Outcomes included validated measures of CIPN pain, overall severity, sensory function, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool implemented in RevMan 5.3, and all procedures were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Five trials involving 201 participants were included, with an overall moderate risk of bias due to limited blinding and underpowered sample sizes. In breast cancer patients, henna vs. standard care significantly improved the overall severity of oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy, as measured by the CIPN Assessment Tool (p < 0.001), with significant reductions in sensory and functional subdomain scores. In a mixed-cancer population, Costus sp. oil vs. placebo significantly reduced neuropathic pain intensity, as measured by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) (p = 0.001), and improved Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy/Gynecologic Oncology Group - Neurotoxicity (FACT/GOG-Ntx) scores (p = 0.028). Trials evaluating ajwain cream, Citrullus colocynthis oil, and a multi-compound essential oil formulation did not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in CIPN severity, pain, or quality of life compared with placebo. None of the included studies incorporated quantitative sensory or functional testing. All interventions were well tolerated, with only mild localized skin reactions reported. Despite modest benefits from certain herbal treatments in reducing CIPN pain and sensory symptoms, current evidence is limited by small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, and the lack of objective outcome measures. Rigorous, adequately powered RCTs with objective CIPN measurements are needed.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1920051.abstract: To evaluate whether a protocolized intraoperative temperature-management strategy based on time-segmented warning thresholds and tiered, feedback-guided warming interventions reduces hypothermia and improves early postoperative recovery in patients undergoing radical esophagectomy. This single-center retrospective comparative cohort study included 116 adults who underwent elective radical esophagectomy at The affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University between August 2024 and January 2026 and were managed with either a time-segmented, feedback-guided tiered warming protocol (n = 58) or conventional warming (n = 58). Core temperature was monitored continuously with a lower esophageal probe until the start of esophageal mobilization and with a nasopharyngeal probe thereafter, and was recorded every 15 min. All warming adjustments were implemented manually by the clinical team according to predefined thresholds. The primary endpoint was intraoperative hypothermia, defined as a core temperature below 36 °C at any time from incision to skin closure. Secondary endpoints included severe hypothermia, nadir temperature, hypothermia burden, postoperative shivering, time to extubation, post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) recovery time, coagulation indices, 30-day complications, length of stay, and hospital cost. Intraoperative hypothermia occurred in 53 of 58 control patients (91.4%) and 5 of 58 intervention patients (8.6%) (risk ratio 0.09, 95% CI 0.04-0.22; P < 0.001). Severe hypothermia below 35.5 °C developed in 27 control patients (46.6%) and in none of the intervention patients. Median nadir core temperature was 35.55 °C in the control group and 36.27 °C in the intervention group (P < 0.001). Compared with conventional warming, the protocol reduced postoperative shivering (5.2% vs 51.7%), shortened time to extubation by 8.9 min, lowered the rate of any postoperative complication (34.5% vs 62.1%; P = 0.005), shortened hospital stay (12.2 vs 13.5 days; P = 0.010), and reduced mean in-hospital cost by 8,911 CNY (P < 0.001). The treatment effect was materially unchanged in adjusted analyses using Firth penalized logistic regression (adjusted odds ratio 0.004, 95% CI 0.000-0.024) and modified Poisson regression (adjusted risk ratio 0.10, 95% CI 0.04-0.23). In adults undergoing radical esophagectomy, a time-segmented, feedback-guided tiered warming protocol substantially reduced intraoperative hypothermia and was associated with faster early recovery, fewer postoperative complications, shorter hospitalization, and lower cost. Because the intervention was a multicomponent warming bundle, the contributions of its individual components cannot be separated, and the associations with complications, hospital stay, and cost should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. The protocol uses standard perioperative equipment and can be implemented without specialized hardware.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1920798.abstract: Background Evidence on the prognostic associations of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and BRCA1-associated protein 1 (BAP1) in pleural mesothelioma (PM) remains inconsistent, and joint data from Latin American cohorts are limited. We evaluated these biomarkers in a Colombian cohort. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included adults with histologically confirmed PM treated at the Instituto Nacional de Cancerología, Bogotá, from January 2011 through December 2023. PD-L1 was quantified using tumor proportion score (TPS), with ≥1% as the primary threshold; BAP1 was classified as retained or lost by nuclear immunoreactivity. Overall survival (OS) was measured from pathologic diagnosis to death. Event-free survival (EFS) was measured from diagnosis to first documented progression or death; patients without an event were censored at last contact. Kaplan–Meier methods and separate multivariable Cox models were used. Results Sixty-seven patients were included; 60/67 (89.6%) had locally advanced or metastatic disease. PD-L1 TPS ≥1% was present in 26/67 (38.8%), and BAP1 loss in 47/61 evaluable tumors (77.0%). All 67 patients died. Median OS was 9.20 months (95% CI, 6.11–14.13), and median EFS was 6.51 months (95% CI, 5.49–9.13). PD-L1 TPS ≥1% was not clearly associated with OS (adjusted HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.57–1.86) or EFS (adjusted HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 0.62–2.00). BAP1 loss also showed no clear adjusted association with OS (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 0.78–3.16) or EFS (HR, 1.65; 95% CI, 0.82–3.33). Conclusions Neither PD-L1 TPS ≥1% nor BAP1 loss showed a clear adjusted association with survival. These jointly measured estimates extend the evidence from an underrepresented Latin American population but require external validation; the exploratory ≥5% and ≥10% analyses were based on only 14 and 7 patients, respectively.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1921935.abstract: Primary pericardial mesothelioma (PPM) is an exceedingly rare, highly invasive cardiac neoplasm with insidious onset and non-specific clinical symptoms. Due to the lack of typical early manifestations and effective routine diagnostic methods, PPM is often misdiagnosed and missed, resulting in delayed treatment and poor prognosis. A 42-year-old male presented with 6 months of recurrent chest tightness and pain, worsening over 2 months, and two prior admissions for unexplained pericardial effusion. On admission, he had tachycardia, distant heart sounds, bilateral lower extremity edema, and a 3×2 cm hard, fixed left supraclavicular lymph node. Imaging confirmed pericardial effusion with abnormal pericardial lesions. Ultrasound-guided pericardiocentesis yielded only a small amount of red jelly-like material, with cytology suggesting epithelioid neoplastic cells. Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic malignant mesothelioma. Nivolumab immunotherapy showed no improvement. Pericardial tumor resection revealed diffuse, fish-flesh-like tumor invading the myocardium and great vessels. Final pathology confirmed epithelioid-type PPM. Patients with recurrent unexplained pericardial effusion and atypical sonographic features, such as flocculent echoes and irregular pericardial thickening, should raise suspicion for PPM. Early recognition of these signs and timely pathological confirmation are critical to avoid diagnostic delays and may improve outcomes.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1922633.abstract: At present, the prognostic value of serum uric acid (SUA) in Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) remains controversial, and relevant clinical evidence lacks systematic and comprehensive verification. This the first-ever meta-analysis comprehensively synthesized evidence across various regimens to systematically evaluate the association between serum uric acid (SUA) levels and survival outcomes in NPC patients. This meta-analysis was strictly performed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Eligible clinical studies focusing on the prognostic role of SUA in NPC were systematically retrieved from domestic and international electronic databases. All retrieved literatures were screened strictly based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The methodological quality of enrolled studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Literature screening, data extraction, and quality evaluation were independently conducted by two investigators, and any discrepancies were resolved by consensus or consultation with a third senior researcher. Key prognostic data including hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for Overall Survival (OS), Progression-Free Survival(PFS), and Distant Metastasis-Free Survival (DMFS) were extracted and pooled for quantitative analysis to evaluate the prognostic significance of SUA in NPC. The pooled results demonstrated that elevated SUA was significantly correlated with OS in NPC patients, with a combined HR of 0.245 (95% CI: 0.092-0.398). In contrast, no statistically significant associations were observed between SUA levels and PFS or DMFS. The pooled HR for PFS was 0.557 (95% CI: 0.070-1.044), and the pooled HR for DMFS was 0.715 (95% CI: 0.023-1.407). The 95% CI of both PFS and DMFS crossed the invalid value of 1, indicating no significant statistical difference. SUA level is an independent prognostic factor for OS in patients with NPC, and higher levels of uric acid may improve the overall survival of patients. No significant correlation was identified between SUA levels and PFS or DMFS in NPC patients. SUA may serve as a novel, convenient, and non-invasive biomarker for prognostic evaluation of NPC, may provide a reference for prognostic risk stratification and individualized management. Further large-sample, high-quality prospective cohort studies are warranted to validate the present findings. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261483250, identifier CRD420261483250.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1922758.abstract: Esophageal carcinoma with ductal differentiation (ECDD) is a rare esophageal cancer (EC), characterized by distinctive morphological features, including bilayered duct-like structures and a biphenotypic immunophenotype. Multiple myeloma (MM) is a plasma cell neoplasm. The synchronous occurrence of these two entities is exceedingly rare. We report an 80-year-old male who presented with fatigue, anemia, and hypoalbuminemia. Endoscopic examination revealed a high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia of the esophagus. Following endoscopic submucosal dissection, pathological examination confirmed ECDD. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated that the inner layer cells of the duct-like structures were positive for CK7 and CAM5.2, while the outer layer cells were positive for p40 and p63. Concurrently, elevated serum globulin levels prompted further evaluation, leading to a diagnosis of MM. At 13 months postoperatively, no recurrence or metastasis of EC was observed, and the patient's MM remained stable. This case highlights that in elderly patients presenting with hematological abnormalities, the possibility of coexisting solid malignancy and plasma cell dyscrasia should be considered. ECDD has distinctive pathological features, and accurate recognition is critical to avoid misdiagnosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1923113.abstract: Current global data on epidemiology, treatment patterns, outcomes, and care pathways for patients with gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) are needed. A systematic review included publications from Embase and Medline (interventional: 2005-2025; observational: 2021-2025) and conference abstracts (2022-2024). Benign gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) studies, case reports, and case series were excluded. Treatment response rates and 95% CIs were calculated from aggregated data. Of 117 included studies, 66.7% (n=78) were cohort studies; 54.7% (n=64) were conducted in Asia. GTN incidence from GTD varied from 6.2% in the UK to 16.8% across Asian studies. Methotrexate and dactinomycin were the most common real-world first-line treatments in low-risk GTN. Second-line and high-risk patients' treatment included diverse multiagent regimens and immunotherapy. Across trials, first-line treatment response with dactinomycin (82.9%) was higher than methotrexate (70.5%); in observational studies, response was similar and inversely associated with GTN risk score. Nausea and other gastrointestinal events were more common with dactinomycin than methotrexate. Incidence of GTN varied by region and setting. Consensus supports methotrexate or dactinomycin as first-line therapy in low-risk GTN. Treatment options were more diverse in high-risk GTN and later-line regimens. Unmet needs to improve response rates and minimize toxicity persist.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1923603.abstract: MYH9 is upregulated in various malignancies, but its role in breast cancer chemoresistance remains unclear. We investigated whether MYH9 regulates doxorubicin (ADR) resistance via GRP78 stabilization and PERK pathway modulation. MYH9 expression was analyzed in breast cancer tissues and cell lines by immunohistochemistry and western blot. ADR-resistant MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines were established. MYH9 knockdown/overexpression and GRP78 overexpression were achieved by lentiviral transduction. Protein interactions, degradation assays, PERK signaling, apoptosis, and in vivo drug responses were evaluated. MYH9 was significantly upregulated in breast cancer tissues, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (95.2%), and further elevated in ADR-resistant cells. MYH9 overexpression enhanced ADR tolerance, while knockdown sensitized resistant cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, MYH9 directly bound GRP78 (but not CALR or GRP94), inhibiting ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation. MYH9 depletion reduced GRP78 levels and activated the PERK pathway (p-eIF2α, ATF4, CHOP), promoting apoptosis via Bax/Bad upregulation and Bcl-2 downregulation. ERS induction with thapsigargin enhanced ADR sensitivity, whereas 4-PBA attenuated it. GRP78 overexpression rescued ADR resistance, confirming GRP78 dependency. MYH9 confers ADR resistance in breast cancer by stabilizing GRP78 and suppressing PERK-driven apoptosis, identifying the MYH9/GRP78 axis as a potential therapeutic target for overcoming chemoresistance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1923622.abstract: Evidence on pneumonitis after thoracic radiotherapy following immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) exposure remains limited. We examined associations with voxel-wise EQD2 mean lung dose (MLDEQD2) and the ICI-radiotherapy interval. This single-center retrospective cohort included 98 patients in a 90-day competing-risk analysis of grade ≥2 radiation pneumonitis (CTCAE), comprising 26 pneumonitis events, 70 event-free observations, and two deaths before pneumonitis. Archived DICOM doses were converted voxel-wise using α/β = 3 Gy. Cumulative incidence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method, and Fine-Gray regression included continuous MLDEQD2 and treatment interval. Supplementary logistic analyses included 96 patients. The 90-day pneumonitis cumulative incidence was 26.5% (95% CI 17.7%-35.3%). The adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio (SHR) for MLDEQD2 was 1.339 per Gy (95% CI 1.113-1.612; P = 0.002). The interval SHR was 0.784 per 10 days (95% CI 0.639-0.963; P = 0.020). Physical MLD showed a consistent association (SHR 1.197 per Gy, 95% CI 1.036-1.382; P = 0.015). Higher MLDEQD2 and shorter treatment intervals were associated with grade ≥2 symptomatic pneumonitis in this treatment sequence. Clinical ascertainment and dose-reconstruction uncertainties limit interpretation. The absence of an ICI-naive comparator precludes conclusions about ICI-specific radiosensitization. Prospective validation is required before these associations can inform dose constraints or treatment scheduling.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1925326.abstract: Residual cancer burden (RCB) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) provides prognostic information, but its combination with immune microenvironment features for recurrence prediction remains underexplored. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 420 consecutive patients with breast cancer who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by definitive surgery between January 2015 and June 2024. Residual cancer burden (RCB) and post-neoadjuvant immune features, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), CD8, FOXP3, and the proportion of CD163-positive among CD68-positive macrophages, were assessed. Patients were stratified by calendar era and randomly partitioned within strata into a training cohort (n=294) and an internal hold-out validation cohort (n=126). A LASSO-penalized Cox workflow was used for predictor selection, followed by unpenalized Cox refitting. Model performance was evaluated using C-statistics, time-specific Brier scores, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and 5-year time-dependent decision curve analysis. During a median follow-up of 61 months, 126 first recurrence events were observed (88 training and 38 validation). The final combined model retained RCB category, triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), CD8 status, and CD163-positive macrophage proportion. The combined model achieved C-statistics of 0.79 (95% CI 0.75-0.83) in the training cohort and 0.75 (95% CI 0.69-0.81) in the internal validation cohort, with corresponding 5-year Brier scores of 0.142 and 0.158. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected C-statistic of 0.772 and calibration slope of 0.92. The combined model provided the greatest net benefit among the evaluated models over 5-year threshold probabilities of approximately 15%-45%. Integration of RCB with TNBC status and post-neoadjuvant CD8 and CD163-positive macrophage features may provide incremental prognostic information for recurrence after neoadjuvant therapy. The model showed acceptable internal discrimination and calibration, but external validation is required before clinical implementation or treatment-directed use.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1925747.abstract: Portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) is one of the most clinically consequential manifestations of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It reflects aggressive tumor biology, compromises portal venous inflow, and reduces the therapeutic window for locoregional intervention. Historically, macroscopic portal vein invasion generally placed patients within advanced-stage treatment pathways, in which systemic therapy constituted the standard treatment backbone and curative-intent approaches were applicable only to selected patients. This paradigm has now shifted. In recent years, the management of unresectable HCC has been reshaped by immune-based systemic therapy, more active tyrosine kinase inhibitor-based combinations, hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), selective transarterial therapies, thrombus-directed radiotherapy, and increasingly standardized multidisciplinary conversion strategies. Consequently, a subset of patients with liver-dominant HCC and PVTT can now be downstaged to radical resection or other definitive local treatment, particularly when liver function is preserved and therapy is initiated before irreversible hepatic decompensation develops. This review summarizes recent advances in the diagnosis and classification of PVTT, the biological and technical rationale for conversion therapy, and the evolving evidence for systemic therapy, HAIC, transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), radiotherapy, triple-modality treatment, salvage surgery, and postoperative management. It also highlights key limitations, including the predominance of retrospective East Asian cohorts, heterogeneity in PVTT classification and treatment protocols, uncertainty regarding the optimal timing of surgery, and the absence of validated biomarkers for selecting patients most likely to benefit from aggressive multimodality treatment. Overall, the available evidence supports integrating response-guided multidisciplinary strategies into established evidence-based treatment frameworks for carefully selected patients. Even so, conversion therapy for HCC with PVTT remains an evidence-evolving strategy that should be applied with careful patient selection, disciplined treatment sequencing, and substantial institutional expertise rather than adopted as a universal standard of care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1926379.abstract: To improve the diagnostic accuracy of benign versus malignant parotid tumors using non-contrast CT. We propose a clinician-in-the-loop hybrid framework that mitigates low soft-tissue contrast by fusing semi-automated 3D visual features with expert semantic descriptors. This multi-center retrospective study analyzed non-contrast CTs from 367 patients. We developed AttenNet, a semi-automated model. First, an nnU-Net module automates 3D tumor segmentation, eliminating manual bounding boxes. A 3D-ResNet backbone then extracts volumetric features, which are dynamically fused with radiologist-provided semantic labels via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention Fusion (MHAF) mechanism. This allows the network to query visual morphology based on expert priors. Diagnostic performance and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability were evaluated. The segmentation achieved a median Dice of 0.827. AttenNet (3D-ResNet) yielded an AUC of 0.908, significantly outperforming the image-only 3D-ResNet (AUC: 0.741) and expert-feature models (AUC: 0.821). External validation (n = 20) reached an AUC of 0.560-0.910.However, given the extremely small sample size, these results must be interpreted strictly as an exploratory proof-of-concept rather than definitive confirmation of generalizability. Grad-CAM confirmed that AttenNet highlights clinically essential geometric indicators-specifically tumor margins and internal heterogeneity-for differentiating malignancy, whereas single-modality baselines focused on background artifacts. This clinician-in-the-loop paradigm successfully integrates spatial imaging with expert reasoning. While multimodal fusion drove the primary performance gains, the MHAF mechanism provided enhanced spatial interpretability.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1927397.abstract: Whole-brain radiotherapy (WBRT) remains an important treatment for patients with diffuse brain metastases, but radiation-induced cognitive decline is a major concern. Hippocampal-avoidance WBRT (HA-WBRT) and memantine are recommended by international guidelines for eligible patients, yet the extent of their adoption across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region remains unclear. A cross-sectional, anonymous questionnaire was distributed to radiation oncologists practising across the MENA region between January and March 2025 by email and professional social media. Because distribution was open, no sampling frame or response denominator could be defined, so the sample is a convenience sample. The instrument assessed self-reported practice patterns, availability and reported utilisation of HA-WBRT and memantine, perceived barriers, and follow-up and cognitive-assessment practices. All proportions are reported at the respondent level. Categorical comparisons used the chi-squared or Fisher's exact test with exact p values and odds ratios; multivariable logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors by centre was performed as an exploratory analysis. Reporting follows STROBE and CHERRIES. In total, 124 radiation oncologists from 45 centres across 15 countries responded. HA-WBRT was reported as being routinely offered to eligible patients by 60 respondents (48.4%) and memantine by 34 (27.4%); 28 (22.6%) reported offering both routinely and 58 (46.8%) neither. When asked what proportion of their WBRT patients actually received both interventions, 70 (56.5%) answered never and only 4 (3.2%) more than 50%. Memantine was reported as available in the respondent's centre by 48 (38.7%), while 66 (53.2%) did not know whether it was approved for brain metastases. The most frequently endorsed barriers were concern about missing intracranial disease (72; 58.1%) for HA-WBRT and lack of experience with the drug (84; 67.7%) for memantine. Formal cognitive testing was infrequent: 90 respondents (72.6%) reported using no cognitive assessment tool. Among the radiation oncologists who responded, self-reported routine use of cognitive-preservation strategies during WBRT was limited, with reported utilisation lower than reported offering. These findings describe the practices reported by a convenience sample and should not be interpreted as establishing the prevalence of underuse across the MENA region.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1928806.abstract: Yttrium-90 microsphere selective internal radiation therapy (Y90-SIRT) is a common local interventional treatment for hepatocellular Carcinoma and liver metastases. With the increasing use, extrahepatic complications have been gradually recognized. We report a case of a 47-year-old patient with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who gradually developed distal esophageal ulcers and subsequent benign cicatricial stricture, clinically presumed to be radiation-induced, following Y90-SIRT treatment. Concurrent lenvatinib may impair mucosal repair function. This rare sequela emphasizes rigorous preoperative vascular evaluation, long-term monitoring and timely intervention, particularly for patients undergoing combined targeted treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1928835.abstract: Immune-mediated liver injury caused by checkpoint inhibitors (ILICI) differs from chemotherapy- or targeted drug-related hepatotoxicity in pathogenesis and management. Biomarkers to distinguish ILICI from other anticancer agent-induced liver injuries are lacking. We compared the clinicopathological features, treatments, and outcomes of ILICI versus other anticancer agent-related liver injuries to identify distinguishing biomarkers. We retrospectively included patients with liver injury during anticancer therapy at Fujian Cancer Hospital between June 2022 and November 2024. Cases were classified as ILICI or non-ILICI using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v5.0 and the Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method. Sixty-seven patients were enrolled, including 30 ILICI and 37 non-ILICI. ILICI was associated with more high-grade liver injury than non-ILICI (P = 0.001), with similar latency, recovery time, and prognosis. Corticosteroids were administered in 70% of ILICI vs. 5.4% of non-ILICI patients (P 30% in LSECs, lymphocytes, and KCs discriminated ILICI with an AUC of 0.811 (95%CI: 0.641-0.980). Sensitivity analyses and Firth penalized logistic regression confirmed that this finding remained robust after adjustment for confounders including pre-biopsy corticosteroid use and inactive HBV carrier status. ILICI was associated with more severe hepatic inflammatory necrosis and a greater need for immunosuppressive therapy than non-ILICI. The PD-L1 positivity rate >30% in LSECs, lymphocytes, and KCs may serve as a potential diagnostic biomarker for ILICI.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1929067.abstract: Previous studies have identified an association between a tumor microenvironment characterized by a predominance of T helper cell type 2 (Th2) system cells (Th2 cells, M2 macrophages, innate lymphoid cells type 2), regulatory T cells, and myeloid derived suppressor cells with poorer cancer prognosis. In contrast, a tumor microenvironment characterized by Th1 system cells (Th1 cells, M1 macrophages, natural killer cells, CD8+ cells, innate lymphoid cells type 1) is associated with a more favorable prognosis. T2-high asthma, a quintessential Th2-dominance-based disease, is associated epidemiologically with more than double the incidence of lung, breast, prostate, and colon cancers, suggesting a connection between the Th2 immune dominant patient macroenvironment and the Th2 immune dominant tumor microenvironment. Stress, air pollution, toxicants, sleep disruption, obesity, and many other influences from the exposome are known to drive the patient into Th2 dominance. Thus, the authors hypothesize that there is a through-line connecting the exposome, patient macroenvironment, and tumor microenvironment. With this context in mind, specific defects in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle produce oncometabolites that drive oncogenic development in tissues. However these same TCA cycle defects drive macrophages to the M1 phenotype, which activates the Th1 system. Th1 system cells are responsible for clearance of oncogenically transformed cells. This should represent a check against the oncogenic influence of the oncometabolites created by the TCA cycle breaks. The authors hypothesize that, in Th2 dominant patients, the TCA cycle breaks fail to shift macrophages to the M1 phenotype, the Th1 system fails to upregulate, and the normal check against oncogenic development fails to occur. If confirmed by subsequent studies, this model may help explain the more than doubled incidence of common cancers in asthma and potentially other Th2 atopic diseases. The authors discuss clinical implications and approaches for operationalizing existing knowledge of the exposome and its impact on patient immunology.
