doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1929709.abstract: Glioblastoma (GB) represents one of the most aggressive primary brain tumors characterized by poor prognosis, high relapse and resistance to conventional therapies. Salidroside, a naturally occurring glucoside derived from Rhodiola rosea, has been reported to exhibit pro-apoptotic and anti-proliferative properties across multiple cancer models; however, its mechanistic basis in glioma and its therapeutic potential remain incompletely characterized. Neuroglobin (Ngb) protein expression was analyzed in 101 glioma brain tissue specimens and 5 normal brain tissues by western blot and immunohistochemical staining. In silico analyses of oxidized and reduced state of Ngb with salidroside was performed along with pharmacokinetics and toxicity predictions to computationally evaluate possible binding interactions and drug-like properties. Further, to determine the underlying mechanisms, in vitro assays were performed in U87MG and LN229 human glioblastoma cells treated with salidroside. MTT assay, transwell assay, Annexin V/PI staining, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), CYP2E1 activity, intracellular NADPH levels, Fe2+/Fe3+ ratio and markers of oxidative stress including ROS assay and lipid peroxidation were also measured. The mechanism of Ngb aided apoptosis was investigated by protein expression of Ngb, caspase 3 and cytosolic cytochrome c in glioma cells. Ngb expression in glioma tissues samples significantly downregulated with increasing tumour grade as determined by immunoreactivity and western blot analysis. In-silico analyses predicted a possible interaction of salidroside with reduced state of Ngb, In vitro studies suggested significant reduction in cell viability, migration and invasion in both U87MG and LN229 cells on supplementation with salidroside. These effects were accompanied by increased CYP2E1 activity, altered intracellular NADPH levels indicating induction of oxidative stress. Mitochondrial dysfunction, manifested as reduced MMP, elevated lipid peroxidation and increased cytosolic cytochrome c release indicated activation of intrinsic apoptotic pathway. Computational analyses additionally predicted a preferential interaction with the reduced form of Ngb, providing a mechanistic hypothesis warranting experimental validation. Salidroside exerts multi-faceted anti-cancer effects in glioblastoma cells, potentially involving upregulation of Ngb levels in glioma cells, modulation of redox homeostasis, mitochondrial integrity and intrinsic apoptotic signaling.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1930072.abstract: To develop and externally validate a ridge logistic regression model containing only pre-procedural predictors to estimate the individual probability of requiring chest drainage after CT-guided percutaneous core-needle lung biopsy. This multicenter retrospective study included 2,492 patients. All 2,092 patients who underwent biopsy at Institution 1 from 2015 to 2025 were used for model development, and 400 patients treated at Institution 2 in 2025 formed the external-validation cohort. Nine variables available before needle entry were prespecified: age, sex, planned position, emphysema, lesion short-axis diameter, longitudinal lesion location, anatomical lobe, planned fissure traversal, and visceral-pleural adjacency. A ridge-penalized logistic model was fitted; the penalty was selected by stratified 10-fold cross-validation using the one-standard-error rule, and the complete modeling process was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The frozen model was applied directly to Institution 2 without refitting, recalibration, or threshold optimization. Development and external-validation sample sizes were formally assessed retrospectively using the Riley frameworks. Chest drainage was required in 127/2,092 patients (6.1%) at Institution 1 and 34/400 (8.5%) at Institution 2. At Institution 1, the apparent AUC was 0.786 (95% CI, 0.745-0.827) and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.766. For the frozen model at Institution 2, the AUC was 0.683 (95% CI, 0.579-0.779) and the Brier score was 0.0755 (95% CI, 0.0550-0.0982). The external calibration intercept was 0.41 (95% CI, 0.00-0.72), calibration slope was 1.13 (95% CI, 0.52-1.85), and observed-to-expected ratio was 1.44 (95% CI, 1.00-1.89), indicating systematic underprediction. The development sample was slightly smaller than required under conservative assumptions. Under the prespecified stringent precision targets, external validation would require approximately 17,397 patients and 1,479 events, whereas the available cohort contained 400 patients and 34 events. External validation should therefore be interpreted as independent but preliminary. The pre-procedural model showed moderate discrimination in an independent external institutional cohort but underestimated absolute risk. Prospective multicenter validation, with local recalibration where appropriate, is required before routine clinical use.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1930319.abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) is a major etiological factor in gastric carcinogenesis and has been associated with alterations in the tumor immune microenvironment. However, how H. pylori -related transcriptional features intersect with the broader molecular and immune heterogeneity of established gastric cancer remains incompletely characterized. Methods Single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE234129) were used for exploratory comparison according to H. pylori status and to define an initial candidate gene set. An eight-gene prognostic signature was subsequently developed in TCGA-STAD and evaluated in independent gastric cancer cohorts. Model-development optimism was assessed using 1, 000 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples. Immune features were evaluated using CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, TIDE, and immunophenoscore, while observed anti-PD-1 response was explored in the disease-matched PRJEB25780 cohort. RGS1 was further assessed in an independent immunohistochemical cohort. Results Exploratory single-cell analyses suggested differences in immune-cell composition, T-cell states, and antigen-presentation-related pathways according to H. pylori status. The eight-gene prognostic signature stratified overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort and two independent GEO cohorts. After full-pipeline bootstrap correction, model discrimination was modest (corrected C-index = 0.575). In TCGA-STAD, addition of the eight-gene score to a clinicopathological model improved prognostic discrimination. High-risk tumors were characterized by distinct stromal, genomic, and immune features, including higher stromal activity, lower tumor mutational burden, and differences in computational immune-response-related profiles. At the tissue level, RGS1 expression was associated with survival and selected immune-cell features. In the IHC cohort, high RGS1 expression remained independently associated with poorer overall survival (OS) after multivariable adjustment (HR = 2.36, 95% CI 1.36-4.10, p = 0.002) and was accompanied by lower CD8-positive and higher CD163-positive and FOXP3-positive cell densities. In the independent H. pylori -annotated GSE62254 cohort, the five non-ribosomal components showed nominal gene-set-level enrichment in H. pylori -positive tumors (CAMERA P = 0.044). Conclusions This study developed an eight-gene survival-associated prognostic signature and characterized its immune associations in gastric cancer. H. pylori -related findings were exploratory and did not establish H. pylori specificity of the final model. Further prospective validation is required given the modest optimism-corrected performance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1930401.abstract: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains a lethal stage of prostate cancer with poor prognosis. Clinical trials for mCRPC are growing rapidly worldwide. However, a comprehensive systematic analysis of the global research and development landscape in mCRPC remains lacking. This study queried the Trialtrove database for interventional trials in mCRPC registered between January 1, 2020 and March 27, 2026. After exclusion of unrelated trials and non-therapeutic studies, 474 trials were analyzed. The therapeutic landscape for mCRPC has evolved into a highly diversified and dynamic field, overwhelmingly dominated by early-phase investigations. Targeted therapy, particularly PARP inhibitors, remain the leading class, while radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT), centered on 177Lu-PSMA, has reached a mature stage of development. Immunotherapy is expanding beyond checkpoint blockade into bispecific T-cell engagers and cellular therapies, and endocrine therapy is being reshaped by PROTAC degraders. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are also gaining momentum, with B7 homolog 3 protein (B7-H3) as the most actively pursued targets. Combination regimens account for 39.2% of trials. mCRPC clinical research landscape has diversified remarkably, shifting from conventional chemotherapy and endocrine therapy toward mechanism-based, biomarker-guided, and combination-oriented strategies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932226.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors with endocrine therapy are standard of care for hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in metastatic and adjuvant settings. The ribociclib label lists dry eye and increased lacrimation among ocular reactions in under 10% of patients, and isolated vortex keratopathy, epithelial keratopathy, and palinopsia are described. To our knowledge, neither neurotrophic keratitis (NK) nor management of an ocular adverse event with amniotic membrane transplantation (AMT) has been reported with any CDK4/6 inhibitor. A 42-year-old premenopausal woman with stage IIB (cT2N1) HR-positive/HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma achieved a pathologic complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and bilateral mastectomy. Adjuvant abemaciclib was discontinued after one month for refractory gastrointestinal toxicity, without ocular complaints. Ribociclib 400 mg/day was initiated. After approximately four months she developed bilateral blurred vision; optometry identified bilateral inferior superficial punctate keratitis (SPK), and preservative-free lubrication was started. At the fifth-month visit, bilaterally reduced corneal sensitivity, a feature of early neurotrophic keratopathy, was documented, and prednisolone acetate 1% was begun. With symptoms failing to improve, ribociclib was held. At the six-month visit, with central SPK, tear-film instability, and further visual decline despite corticosteroid, amniotic membrane grafts with bandage contact lenses were placed sequentially in each eye, and topical cyclosporine 0.05% was started. Ribociclib was permanently discontinued. Right-eye vision normalized within five months; the left eye recovered over fifteen months. Anastrozole and all other concomitant medications were continued without recurrence. To our knowledge, this appears to be the first reported case of bilateral neurotrophic keratitis during CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and the first ribociclib-associated ocular adverse event refractory to standard topical therapy that improved after procedural intervention. A Naranjo score of 5 indicates a probable association, supported by a documented normal ocular baseline on the same concomitant medications, absence of ocular toxicity during brief prior abemaciclib exposure, and improvement after dechallenge with continued anastrozole. As a single, signal-generating case, causality cannot be established; additional reports and pharmacovigilance analyses are needed. As adjuvant use expands, clinicians should watch for corneal nerve toxicity beyond dry eye, ask routinely about visual symptoms, and refer early for eye care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932265.abstract: Tumour budding is an established prognostic marker in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but its reliability and prognostic performance in preoperative biopsy specimens remain uncertain. This study compared tumour budding assessment in matched biopsy and resection specimens and evaluated their respective prognostic value. We retrospectively analysed 256 patients with OSCC and matched preoperative biopsy and resection specimens. Tumour budding at the invasive front was assessed on hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections according to the International Tumour Budding Consensus Conference criteria and agreement between biopsy- and resection-based assessment was evaluated alongside associations with clinicopathological characteristics, disease-specific survival and occult nodal metastasis using logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Biopsy-derived tumour budding showed only weak correlation with resection findings and systematically underestimated high tumour budding, resulting in poor categorical agreement (κ = 0.11) and low sensitivity (9.8%) despite high specificity (98.9%). Nevertheless, both biopsy- and resection-based tumour budding were associated with disease-specific survival when mutually adjusted for each other. The C-index was numerically higher for resection-based than biopsy-based assessment (0.72 vs. 0.60), with only a modest increase when both measures were combined (C-index 0.74). Both biopsy- and resection-derived tumour budding were also associated with local recurrence and distant metastasis in mutually adjusted Cox models, although these secondary analyses remain exploratory. Interpretation is limited by the small biopsy high-budding group (n = 10) and the limited number of events for several secondary outcomes. For later lymph-node metastasis, only resection-derived tumour budding remained statistically significant after mutual adjustment, whereas the association with biopsy-derived tumour budding was borderline. Resection-derived tumour budding, but not biopsy-derived tumour budding, remained associated with occult nodal metastasis after mutual adjustment, while no statistically significant specimen-type interactions were detected for the evaluated clinicopathological characteristics, with several estimates remaining imprecise. Preoperative biopsy-derived tumour budding may provide clinically relevant prognostic information in OSCC despite systematically underestimating high tumour budding. Although resection-based assessment showed a numerically higher C-index, biopsy assessment may provide complementary preoperative prognostic information but should not be considered a surrogate for resection-based assessment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932336.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a major clinical challenge because of delayed diagnosis and the lack of validated non-invasive biomarkers for OSCC detection. Epigenetic alterations during oral carcinogenesis represent promising biomarker candidates. This study aimed to prioritize clinically relevant epigenetic biomarkers and validate EPHA5 using an integrated genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic approach. Genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic profiling were performed to identify epigenetically deregulated genes in OSCC. Candidate genes were prioritized by integrating DNA methylation, transcriptomic data and biological relevance. EPHA5 was subsequently selected for validation and evaluated by quantitative methylation-specific PCR (QMSP) and quantitative real-time PCR (QRT-PCR) in tissue, saliva and serum samples from independent cohorts comprising patients with OSCC, oral premalignant lesions (OPML) and healthy controls. Genome-wide analysis identified 661 upregulated and 577 downregulated genes together with 2,431 differentially methylated regions corresponding to 1,776 genes. Integrated analysis generated a panel of 51 candidate genes, from which EPHA5 was prioritized using integrated DNA methylation, gene expression, pathway enrichment and biological relevance. EPHA5 promoter hypermethylation was detected in 66.7% of OSCC tumors, whereas concurrent promoter hypermethylation and reduced expression were observed in 28.6% of tumors. Methylation was also detected in 54.5% of OPML lesions and in the saliva of 47.6% of OSCC patients but was rarely detected in healthy controls. Tumor EPHA5 methylation significantly discriminated OSCC from healthy controls (AUC = 0.780, p = 0.004; sensitivity, 71.4%; specificity, 75%). Salivary EPHA5 methylation also significantly discriminated OSCC from healthy controls (AUC = 0.717, p = 0.025; sensitivity, 52.4%; specificity, 87.5%), whereas serum methylation showed no significant diagnostic utility (AUC = 0.571, p = 0.462). Discrimination between OSCC and OPML was limited and did not reach statistical significance (tumor AUC = 0.662, p = 0.068; salivary AUC = 0.600, p = 0.264). Frequent tumor hypermethylation together with detectable salivary methylation supports further evaluation of EPHA5 as a candidate non-invasive epigenetic biomarker for OSCC. However, its moderate diagnostic performance, limited discrimination between OSCC and OPML, and lack of external validation indicate that larger prospective studies and evaluation within multimarker methylation panels are required before clinical implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932583.abstract: Multiple prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET tracers are used for patient selection in radioligand therapy (RLT). This study compared treatment response to RLT across different PSMA tracers. We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent Lu-177 PSMA-617 RLT with baseline imaging using either Ga-68 PSMA-11 or F-18 DCFPyL PET. PET parameters were measured, including SUVmean, SUVmax, and total tumor volume (TTV). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with PSA50 response, and Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with overall survival. Of 140 patients analyzed (Ga-68 PSMA-11: n=51; F-18 DCFPyL: n=89), SUVmax and SUVmean did not differ significantly between groups; however, TTV was significantly higher in the Ga-68 PSMA-11 group (p=0.038). In multivariable analysis adjusted for age, baseline PSA, PET tracer type, SUVmean, and log-transformed TTV, PET tracer type was not significantly associated with PSA50 response (OR, 1.318; 95% CI, 0.585-2.970; p=0.505), whereas higher SUVmean was associated with greater odds of PSA50 response (OR, 1.285; 95% CI, 1.126-1.466; p<0.001). Overall survival did not differ significantly between tracer groups (HR, 0.760; 95% CI, 0.507-1.138; p=0.183), with median overall survival of 8.4 and 12.6 months. In multivariable analysis, PET tracer type was not significantly associated with overall survival (HR, 0.736; 95% CI, 0.475-1.139; p=0.168), whereas higher SUVmean was associated with a lower risk of death (HR, 0.886; 95% CI, 0.825-0.950; p<0.001) and higher log-transformed TTV was associated with a higher risk of death (HR, 1.415; 95% CI, 1.194-1.678; p<0.001). PET tracer type was not significantly associated with PSA50 response or overall survival following RLT. Higher SUVmean was associated with greater odds of PSA50 response and a lower risk of death, whereas higher TTV was associated with overall survival.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932640.abstract: The Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) quantifies the inflammatory potential of diet. Evidence linking DII to prostate cancer remains limited and inconsistent. We evaluated the prospective association between DII and incident prostate cancer in a large population-based cohort. We included 30,972 men who were free of prostate cancer at baseline. The DII was derived from 27 dietary components assessed by the Oxford WebQ. Incident prostate cancer was identified from linked cancer-registry records (ICD-10 C61). Cox regression was the primary analysis, with age included in all adjusted models; logistic regression was secondary. Lag, additional-covariate, and age-stratified Cox models assessed sensitivity. Mediation and Mean Adequacy Ratio (MAR) analyses were exploratory. During a median follow-up of 13.8 years (IQR 13.5-14.2; 406,058 person-years), 1,546 participants developed incident prostate cancer. The unadjusted inverse association (HR per 1-unit DII increase 0.951, 95% CI 0.927-0.977) was attenuated after adjustment for age and other covariates (fully adjusted HR 0.986, 95% CI 0.956-1.018; P = 0.389; Q4 vs Q1 HR 0.928, 95% CI 0.788-1.093; P for trend = 0.426). The secondary logistic analysis was likewise null (OR per 1-unit increase 0.982, 95% CI 0.950-1.015; P = 0.275). Age-adjusted lag analyses and exploratory CRP/NLR mediation analyses did not materially alter this interpretation. DII was inversely correlated with the revised 18-nutrient MAR (Pearson r = -0.694; Spearman ρ = -0.756), but neither index was associated with prostate cancer in the age-adjusted joint model. An apparent inverse DII-prostate cancer association in unadjusted analyses was explained largely by age differences across DII categories. After adjustment for age and other covariates, neither logistic nor time-to-event analyses supported an independent association. These findings underscore the importance of rigorous age control in prostate cancer epidemiology and should not be interpreted causally.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932765.abstract: Missed treatment workdays can prolong overall treatment time and may reduce tumor control, yet routine audits often conflate weekends, statutory holidays, and departmentally accepted rest schedules with untreated institutional workdays. We quantified calendar-defined missed-workday gaps-inter-fraction intervals containing ≥1 untreated institutional workday after excluding routine rest days-among patients with first treatment between June 2021 and December 2025 who were linkable between the MOSAIQ radiotherapy information system and the institutional oncology database (1,319 patients; 1,342 episodes). A locked stratified sample of 100 algorithm-positive gaps underwent documentation-based chart review as unplanned relevant (UR) or planned/appropriate (PA). We analyzed linkage sensitivity, opportunity-adjusted site rates with patient-clustered confidence intervals (CIs), opportunity-offset Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE) including calendar year, and episode-clustered phase GEE. Under the documentation-based chart-review rule, 92 of 100 algorithm-positive gaps were labeled UR (17 department/equipment; 75 patient-factor) and 8 PA. Gaps occurred in 638/1,342 episodes (47.5%; patient-level 48.0%). Linked versus unlinked prevalence was 48.2% versus 51.7% (absolute difference -3.4 percentage points, 95% CI -11.2 to 4.4; P = 0.435). Among subgroups with ≥50 episodes, head and neck had the highest prevalence (75.3%) and breast the lowest (41.3%); opportunity-adjusted rates were 5.63 (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 4.76-6.52) versus 2.63 (2.36-2.92) per 100 opportunities. Opportunity-offset Poisson GEE with calendar year gave a head-and-neck versus breast incidence rate ratio (IRR) of 2.99 (95% CI 2.18-4.11). An exploratory phase GEE (29,763 intervals; 1,323 clusters) showed a late versus early odds ratio (OR) of 1.31 (95% CI 1.12-1.54; P = 0.0009; absolute rates 2.8% vs 3.6%); after site, year, and intent adjustment, the OR was 1.32 (95% CI 1.12-1.57). This operational audit of institutional workdays without recorded treatment-rather than clinically confirmed unplanned interruptions-shows frequent gaps after excluding routine rest. Most reviewed positives received patient-factor labels under a documentation rule. Calendar-aware auditing may support departmental monitoring; priority-based compensation remains a proposed application.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1932811.abstract: Systemic inflammation is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of long-term health outcomes. The Inflammatory Burden Index (IBI), derived from C-reactive protein, neutrophil count, and lymphocyte count, integrates multiple components of systemic inflammatory and immune status. However, evidence regarding its association with long-term mortality among individuals with and without a history of cancer remains limited. We investigated the associations of IBI with mortality outcomes using two population-based cohorts, the UK Biobank (UKB) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 1999-2010), and an independent clinical cohort of patients with gastric cancer. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations between IBI and mortality outcomes. Stratified analyses were performed by history of cancer and among participants with digestive tract cancers, and sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness. The UKB included 455,423 participants, of whom 54,813 had a history of cancer, and NHANES included 24,708 participants, of whom 2,159 had a history of cancer. Participants with a history of cancer were more frequently represented in the highest IBI quartile in both cohorts. Higher IBI was consistently associated with increased all-cause, cancer-specific, and CVD-specific mortality. In the UKB, among participants with a history of cancer, the highest versus lowest IBI quartile was associated with higher risks of all-cause (HR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.53-1.71), cancer-specific (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.45-1.64), and CVD-specific mortality (HR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.41-2.33). Consistent associations were observed in NHANES and remained robust in continuous and sensitivity analyses. Among participants with digestive tract cancers, higher IBI was associated with increased all-cause and cancer-specific mortality. In the independent gastric cancer cohort (n = 793), the highest IBI quartile was associated with poorer overall survival after multivariable adjustment (HR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.59-4.02). Higher IBI was consistently associated with increased all-cause, cancer-specific, and CVD-specific mortality across population-based cohorts, with additional evidence from participants with digestive tract cancers and an independent gastric cancer cohort. These findings support the potential prognostic relevance of IBI as a readily accessible marker of systemic inflammatory burden.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1933062.abstract: Gastric metastasis from breast carcinoma is uncommon and is most often associated with invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), although carcinoma of no special type (NST) and mixed tumors also occur. Metastatic deposits closely mimic diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma, and the distinction from a primary gastric tumor carries major therapeutic consequences. Estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status may differ between the primary tumor and its metastasis, with direct implications for systemic therapy. We report three women managed at a single Malaysian tertiary center. Case 1 (56 years old; metachronous interval of approximately 4 years) had an ER-positive, HER2 3+ (immunohistochemistry [IHC]) carcinoma of no special type that presented as a circumferential Siewert III gastroesophageal junction (GOJ) tumor with gastric satellites; the metastasis retained E-cadherin and was HER2 2+ with a non-amplified in situ hybridization (ISH) result, a discordance from the HER2 3+ primary. Case 2 (47 years old; synchronous) presented with a linitis plastica-like pattern and gastric outlet obstruction (GOO) from an ER-positive, HER2-negative carcinoma; the primary showed patchy E-cadherin and the metastasis showed focal E-cadherin, consistent with a mixed ductal-lobular phenotype; PR expression was lost between the primary (strong, >90%) and the metastasis (negative). Case 3 (91 years old; effectively synchronous, approximately 6-year course) had a lobular carcinoma with E-cadherin loss and a decline in PR expression (from focal weak positivity in the primary to negative in the metastasis), with a protracted course dominated by recurrent feeding-tube complications. In each case, the diagnosis rested on morphology, a breast-oriented IHC panel, and comparison with the known breast primary rather than on any single marker. This series illustrates that gastric and GOJ metastases from breast carcinoma are morphologically and endoscopically heterogeneous and are not confined to E-cadherin-negative ILC. E-cadherin reflects tumor phenotype and cell cohesion rather than the organ of origin, and it should not be used to distinguish a breast metastasis from a primary gastric carcinoma. Because clinically relevant ER, PR, and HER2 discordance may occur, these biomarkers should be reassessed in metastatic tissue, with results interpreted proportionately to the available evidence.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1933386.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has overtaken viral hepatitis as the fastest-growing cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in most high-income countries. What makes this epidemic clinically treacherous is a feature that distinguishes MASLD-related HCC from other aetiologies: roughly half of all cases arise in livers that have never progressed to cirrhosis, slipping through the net of conventional surveillance strategies. The molecular journey from fatty liver to malignancy unfolds through at least six interlocking programmes: lipotoxic rewiring of hepatocyte metabolism, including acquired lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) dysfunction, oncogenic glucose reprogramming through the p53-PUMA-mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) axis, and a preliminary MLKL-Mfn2 axis linking metabolic stress to mitochondrial dysfunction; a chronic shift in the hepatic immune milieu toward tumour-permissive tolerance; gut microbiota dysbiosis flooding portal circulation with pro-inflammatory metabolites; progressive collapse of autophagic flux with p62/SQSTM1 accumulation and lipolysosome formation; and pervasive epigenetic rewriting spanning DNA methylation, novel histone marks, and non-coding RNA networks. We also discuss emerging biomarkers and therapeutic strategies, closing with a brief note on Doublecortin-like kinase 1 (DCLK1) as a candidate marker at the intersection of cancer stem cell identity and immune microenvironment subversion.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1933438.abstract: To compare overall survival (OS) in patients with relapsed neuroblastoma treated with dinutuximab beta (DB) after relapse with that of two comparator populations: historical controls with no prior anti-disialoganglioside-2 exposure and patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy. The objectives were to evaluate the effectiveness of DB in the relapsed setting and to assess a potential legacy effect of prior first-line therapy. This unanchored indirect comparison used individual patient data from three cohorts: historical controls with no prior anti-GD2 therapy (N/N), patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy and did not receive subsequent DB (DB/N), and patients treated with DB after relapse without prior exposure (N/DB). Harmonized eligibility criteria were applied across cohorts, and follow-up was aligned using a common post-relapse index date. Adjusted comparisons were performed using propensity score reweighting. Overall survival was measured from the observed (N/DB) or imputed (N/N and DB/N) post-relapse index date and analyzed using weighted Kaplan-Meier methods and weighted Cox proportional hazards models, with hazard ratios (HR) reported. For the N/N and DB/N cohorts, the post-relapse index date was imputed using a quantile regression model estimating the interval from first relapse to initiation of DB, fitted to data from the N/DB cohort. A total of 329 patients were assessed, of whom 266 were included in the weighted analyses. Baseline imbalances in age at relapse, time from diagnosis, MYCN status, and International Neuroblastoma Staging System (INSS) stage were largely resolved after weighting. No evidence of a legacy effect of first-line DB exposure was observed, as OS did not differ significantly between patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy and historical controls (HR = 1.26, 95% CI 0.70-2.26; p=0.437). In contrast, DB administered after relapse was associated with significantly improved OS compared with both historical controls (HR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.81; p=0.003) and patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy (HR = 0.42, 95% CI 0.25-0.72; p=0.001). These findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. This adjusted indirect comparison demonstrated that DB administered after relapse was associated with significantly improved OS compared with both historical controls and patients who relapsed after prior first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy. No evidence of a legacy effect of first-line DB immunotherapy was identified. These findings support the clinical relevance of DB in the relapsed setting and indicate that prior first-line DB maintenance alone was not associated with a persistent post-relapse survival advantage. The study did not evaluate DB retreatment after prior first-line exposure.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1934075.abstract: Conflict-related displacement profoundly disrupts pediatric cancer care, yet clinical outcomes data for evacuated children treated at regional oncology centers remain scarce. We describe the clinical characteristics, diagnostic challenges, nutritional and psychosocial burden, and outcomes of children evacuated from Gaza and treated at King Hussein Cancer Center (KHCC), Jordan. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged ≤21 years evacuated from Gaza to KHCC between November 2023 and March 2026. Demographic and clinical characteristics, cancer type and stage, diagnostic concordance, nutritional and psychosocial status, and survival outcomes were assessed. Overall survival (OS) and event-free survival (EFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. A total of 169 patients were included; median age was 6.7 years (range, 0.01-21.3), and 62% were male. Median time from symptom onset to presentation was 3 months (range, 1-62). Among staged solid tumors, lymphomas, and brain tumors, 41.6% had distant disease at presentation. All patients with leukemia presented with systemic disease at diagnosis, and all patients with retinoblastoma presented with moderate-to-advanced intraocular disease (International Intraocular Retinoblastoma Classification Groups C-E), with 83% classified as high-risk (Groups D/E). Diagnostic discordance occurred in 19.5% of cases. Nutritional and psychosocial burden was substantial: 26.3% were underweight (44/167 assessed), 50.3% had vitamin D deficiency (75/149 assessed), and 41.4% reported clinically significant psychological distress. During a median follow-up of 8.0 months, 24 patients died (14.2%), including 2.4% who died within 30 days of presentation. One- and 2-year OS were 81.3% (95% CI, 72.1-87.7%) and 75.7% (95% CI, 64.6-83.7%), respectively; corresponding EFS estimates were 76.5% (95% CI, 67.0-83.6%) and 70.6% (95% CI, 59.4-79.3%). PICU-admitted patients had markedly lower 1-year OS (52.7% vs 86.8%; HR, 5.56; log-rank P<0.0001) and EFS (48.9% vs 81.8%; HR, 4.27; log-rank P<0.0001). Children evacuated from Gaza presented with advanced disease, diagnostic discordance, malnutrition, and substantial psychosocial burden, reflecting the clinical consequences of conflict-related disruption of healthcare. Despite these challenges, multidisciplinary care at a regional center of excellence achieves meaningful survival outcomes. These findings underscore the need for protected humanitarian evacuation pathways, integrated supportive care, and sustainable international funding for pediatric oncology services in conflict settings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1934294.abstract: To compare the safety outcomes of totally implantable venous access port (TIVAP) implantation through the internal jugular vein (IJV), subclavian vein (SCV), and axillary vein (AxV) in patients with breast cancer, and to explore a pre-removal thrombosis risk-stratification framework integrating D-dimer levels and vascular ultrasonography findings. Data from 475 breast cancer patients who underwent TIVAP implantation were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were classified according to implantation route: IJV (n = 161), SCV (n = 138), and AxV (n = 176). Baseline characteristics, procedure variables, postoperative complications, and Clavien-Dindo grades were analyzed. Among these patients, 234 underwent both pre-removal D-dimer testing and vascular ultrasonography, and 18 asymptomatic thrombotic events were identified. Firth penalized logistic regression was used to explore factors associated with thrombosis. ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminatory ability of D-dimer, and the optimal cutoff was determined using the Youden index. Patients were categorized into four scenarios according to D-dimer and ultrasonography findings. Baseline characteristics were comparable among the three groups. The complication rate was higher in the SCV group than in the IJV and AxV groups (16.67% vs. 7.45% vs. 5.68%, P = 0.002). Catheter fracture and pinch-off syndrome occurred exclusively in patients receiving SCV access. Firth penalized logistic regression showed that higher D-dimer levels and longer catheter dwell time were associated with asymptomatic catheter-related thrombosis. D-dimer showed moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.721). At the ROC-derived cutoff of 0.251 μg/mL, sensitivity was 77.78%, specificity was 76.85%, LR+ was 3.36, and LR- was 0.29. Integration of D-dimer and ultrasonography yielded four exploratory pre-removal profiles, including 166 double-negative, 4 D-dimer-negative/ultrasound-positive, 50 D-dimer-positive/ultrasound-negative, and 14 double-positive patients. Compared with the SCV approach, the AxV approach showed a lower observed complication rate in this retrospective cohort, whereas no statistically significant difference in overall complications was observed between the AxV and IJV groups. D-dimer alone was insufficient to exclude thrombosis. The combined D-dimer/ultrasonography framework should be regarded as exploratory and requires prospective validation before its potential clinical application can be considered.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1934498.abstract: This study aimed to explore the correlation between the ability of M2-type tumor-correlated macrophage-derived exosomes (EXOs) to trigger the aggressiveness of gastric cancer (GC) cells and the miR-132-3p expression. EXOs were isolated from the conditioned media of M0 and M2 macrophages and characterized by transmission electron microscopy and Western blotting. miR-132-3p expression was determined by qRT-PCR. HGC-27 cells were divided into the control, miR-132-3p mimic, miR-132-3p inhibitor, M0-EXO, and M2-EXO groups. Cell viability, proliferation, migration, and invasion were assessed using CCK-8, EdU, and Transwell assays. Intracellular GSH, SOD, MDA, and iron levels were measured using colorimetric assays. FTH1, LIFR, and GPX4 expressions were detected by Western blotting. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were performed to investigate miR-132-3p-mediated transcriptional changes and ferroptosis-related pathways in HGC-27 cells. miR-132-3p was significantly enriched in M2 macrophage-derived exosomes and was highly expressed in GC, with its expression associated with tumor stage, grade, and other clinicopathological features. M2-Exo treatment significantly increased miR-132-3p levels in HGC-27 cells. Both miR-132-3p overexpression and M2-Exo treatment enhanced the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HGC-27 cells, and were accompanied by reduced intracellular iron and MDA levels, increased GSH content and SOD activity, upregulated FTH1 and GPX4 expression, and decreased LIFR expression. In contrast, miR-132-3p inhibition produced largely opposite effects. RNA-seq identified 275 differentially expressed genes following miR-132-3p overexpression, including 216 upregulated and 59 downregulated genes. GO and KEGG analyses revealed significant alterations in biological processes and pathways related to oxygen transport, ATP synthesis, oxidative phosphorylation, thermogenesis, spliceosome function, and endoplasmic reticulum protein processing. Integration of the RNA-seq-derived DEGs with FerrDb identified 12 ferroptosis-related DEGs, including 11 upregulated genes and 1 downregulated gene. qRT-PCR validation showed expression patterns broadly consistent with the RNA-seq results. miR-132-3p expression in the EXOs of M2-type macrophages was significantly elevated, and the EXOs of M2-type macrophages significantly triggered the aggressiveness of GC cells and inhibited ferroptosis in GC cells, which may be resulting from the prevention of ferroptosis through the transport of miR-132-3p; nevertheless, the specific mechanism of action needs to be further elucidated.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1934583.abstract: Inflammatory markers have been reported to be associated with outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, whether early treatment-related changes in these markers provide additional prognostic information remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between dynamic changes in peripheral blood inflammatory markers during chemotherapy and survival outcomes in patients with NSCLC. We retrospectively analyzed 479 patients with NSCLC who received chemotherapy. Changes in lymphocyte, platelet, and neutrophil counts, as well as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were calculated as absolute differences (D-values) between baseline measurements obtained before the first chemotherapy session and post-chemotherapy measurements obtained within 7 days after the first session. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Additional Cox models were used to examine the association of PLR D-value with OS after accounting for baseline PLR and clinical covariates. A prognostic nomogram was constructed as an exploratory risk-estimation model. Greater changes in the evaluated hematological markers were associated with shorter OS in Kaplan-Meier analysis. In the primary multivariable Cox regression, high PLR D-value was associated with shorter OS (hazard ratio, 1.422; 95% confidence interval, 1.001-2.020; P = 0.049), together with sex, anemia status, and tumor extent. After adjustment for baseline PLR and clinical covariates, however, PLR D-value was no longer significantly associated with OS when analyzed either as a continuous variable (HR per 50-unit increase, 1.010; 95% CI, 0.947-1.078; P = 0.762) or using the original high/low classification (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.91-1.89; P = 0.145). The nomogram had an apparent C-index of 0.630 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.618 after 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Greater changes in PLR during chemotherapy were associated with shorter OS in the primary categorical analysis. However, this association was attenuated after baseline PLR and clinical factors were taken into account, indicating that the additional prognostic contribution of PLR D-value may be limited. The nomogram should be considered exploratory and requires external validation before clinical application.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1934901.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have significantly improved outcomes in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) but may induce immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including hypophysitis. Although endocrine irAEs usually present with nonspecific constitutional symptoms, atypical manifestations may delay diagnosis and expose patients to unnecessary invasive procedures. We report the case of a 76-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line nivolumab, ipilimumab, carboplatin, and pemetrexed who developed profound asthenia, altered mental status, bilious vomiting, and severe gastrointestinal dilation suggestive of acute mechanical bowel obstruction after two treatment cycles. Computed tomography demonstrated marked gastric and intestinal distension, and surgical management was initially considered. Endocrine evaluation subsequently revealed central hypothyroidism and secondary adrenal insufficiency, consistent with ICI-induced hypophysitis. Prompt initiation of physiological hormone replacement with intravenous hydrocortisone followed by thyroid hormone supplementation resulted in rapid neurological and systemic recovery, complete restoration of gastrointestinal motility, radiological resolution of bowel dilatation, and avoidance of surgery. Follow-up imaging also demonstrated a partial tumor response, which has remained durable for more than two years without additional anticancer treatment while the patient continues long-term endocrine replacement therapy. This case expands the clinical spectrum of ICI-induced hypophysitis by describing an unusual presentation as acute paralytic ileus mimicking mechanical bowel obstruction. It underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for endocrine irAEs in patients receiving ICIs who develop unexplained multisystem deterioration or apparent surgical abdomen. Early hormonal assessment and timely replacement therapy can be lifesaving, prevent unnecessary surgical interventions, and allow optimal multidisciplinary management without compromising oncologic outcomes.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1934901.title: Case Report: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced hypophysitis presenting as acute paralytic ileus mimicking mechanical bowel obstruction in a patient affected by advanced non-small cell lung cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1935087.abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies among women worldwide and is frequently curable when identified at an early stage. However, advanced and metastatic disease continue to account for a substantial proportion of breast cancer-related deaths, particularly among patients with aggressive subtypes such as inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a clinicopathologic entity that spans hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive, and triple-negative disease. Although advances in molecular profiling and systemic therapies have improved outcomes, substantial challenges persist in identifying patients at risk for recurrence, accurately assessing treatment response, and determining optimal therapeutic strategies. These challenges are driven by marked tumor heterogeneity and the dynamic interplay between malignant cells and their surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME). This review examines key barriers to the diagnosis and management of IBC, set against the broader landscape of advanced breast cancer. It discusses the clinical significance of late metastatic relapse, rapidly progressive disease, shortcomings of current prognostic frameworks, and the difficulties associated with monitoring metastatic involvement. Also highlighted are emerging approaches, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and other liquid biopsy technologies, that may enhance risk stratification, longitudinal surveillance, and detection of molecular resistance; these applications remain investigational, and established clinical approaches are distinguished from emerging strategies throughout. The TME is further explored as a critical determinant of tumor behavior, with emphasis on lymphoid and myeloid immune cells, stromal components, and immune checkpoint pathways that promote immune evasion and therapeutic resistance. Finally, this review surveys evolving treatment paradigms, including immunotherapeutic approaches, RNA-based diagnostics and therapeutics, most of which remain preclinical, and antibody-drug conjugates, which are expanding the therapeutic landscape for advanced disease. Together, these developments underscore the potential of integrating molecular, immunologic, and circulating biomarker data to enable more precise disease characterization and treatment selection, as essential for developing more effective, personalized strategies for patients with IBC and other advanced breast cancers.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1935144.abstract: Neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) is a rare, aggressive subtype with hormonal resistance and poor prognosis. Traditional serum biomarkers such as prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and neuron-specific enolase (NSE) are often present at low or normal levels, making it difficult to accurately reflect disease burden and progression, and thus renders them unsuitable for dynamically monitoring NEPC. We report a 64-year-old man with mixed neuroendocrine carcinoma and adenocarcinoma of the prostate, with bladder involvement. The adenocarcinoma component had a Gleason score of 5 + 4 = 9. Pretreatment 18 F‑FDG PET/CT showed uptake in prostatic and bladder lesions, while a sclerotic lesion at the sixth thoracic vertebra exhibited no FDG avidity. After chemotherapy, radiotherapy and long-term treatment with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in combination with bicalutamide, PSA levels became undetectable and NSE levels remained within the normal range with no significant change from baseline. However, follow‑up 68 Ga‑PSMA PET/MR revealed intense persistent uptake in the prostate and bladder and new avid lesions in the sixth thoracic vertebra and both scapulae. At the most recent follow-up, 68 Ga-PSMA PET/MR scan revealed decreased PSMA uptake in the prostate and bone lesions, as well as increased PSMA uptake in the bladder. A repeat bladder biopsy confirmed chronic inflammation rather than tumor progression. PSA and NSE levels remained largely unchanged during follow-up, while the clinical significance of the 68 Ga-PSMA PET findings required further assessment. This case demonstrates that the results of multi-tracer PET scans in patients with NEPC should be interpreted with caution and considered alongside the clinical course and biochemical markers. When necessary, a definitive diagnosis should be confirmed by histopathology.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1935311.abstract: Current preoperative assessment of meningioma brain invasion (BI) demands imaging analytical frameworks that optimize computational efficiency while capturing multidimensional tumor-pathology correlations. Building upon the inherent advantages of 2.5D MRI in synthesizing multiplanar biological data with manageable processing loads, this study innovatively integrates deep transfer learning (DTL), a technique bridging pretrained network knowledge with target domain adaptation, to systematically identify tumor-invasive biological signatures and develop an optimized predictive system using preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI). This retrospective study enrolled 674 patients with pathologically confirmed meningiomas, including 53 with BI and 621 without BI. The cohort was stratified into a training set and an independent test set. Tumor regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated on CE-T1WI, and radiomics and DTL features were extracted. Radiomics and DTL features were fused via early fusion, followed by feature selection. Within the training cohort, five-fold cross-validation was performed, with SMOTE applied exclusively to the training portion of each fold; validation folds and the independent test set retained their original class distributions. The effectiveness of the models was compared using the area under the ROC curve (AUC). In the training set, ComM achieved an AUC of 0.977, while in the test set, its AUC reached 0.935. ComM demonstrated the best performance (training set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCClinM > AUCDTLM; test set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCDTLM > AUCClinM), showing excellent preoperative predictive capability for meningioma BI. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model fit, and the calibration curve revealed that ComM was closest to the ideal curve. ClinM, RadM, DTLM, DTLRM, and ComM based on 2.5D CE-T1WI all exhibited good performance in predicting meningioma BI. The clinical-radiomics-DTL fusion model (ComM) demonstrated the highest efficacy, suggesting that DTL provides additional features correlated with meningioma BI that differ from radiomics features. This model shows potential clinical utility for preoperative prediction; however, further external validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1935484.abstract: Serplulimab, a first-line therapy for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), can cause checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP). The clinical features and outcomes of serplulimab-induced CIP in patients with Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) stage IV chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain unclear. An 80-year-old man with ES-SCLC and preexisting GOLD stage IV COPD received first-line serplulimab plus chemotherapy. After achieving an initial partial response, chemotherapy was discontinued due to reduced tolerance following bacterial pneumonia, and he was continued on serplulimab monotherapy. Three days after the first maintenance dose of serplulimab, he presented with acute severe chest tightness, dyspnea, and hypoxemia and was admitted to the hospital 4 days later. Chest CT revealed new bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Extensive workup for infection, acute exacerbation of COPD, and tumor progression was negative; the case was ultimately classified as grade 4 serplulimab-induced CIP. He was treated with high-dose methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, and empiric anti-infective therapy, with significant clinical improvement. Follow-up CT at 2 months post-discharge showed significant resolution of pulmonary infiltrates. Severe, life-threatening CIP can occur in elderly patients with ES-SCLC and preexisting GOLD stage IV COPD. In this patient, prompt recognition, intensive immunosuppression, and permanent programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor discontinuation contributed to a favorable outcome. Whether preexisting GOLD stage IV COPD confers an increased risk of severe CIP in this understudied population warrants further investigation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1935499.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, and most patients present with unresectable or metastatic disease. In recent years, approaches such as locoregional therapy, immunotherapy and targeted therapy have achieved significant breakthroughs in the transformation treatment of advanced iCCA. We report a case of successful conversion therapy using envafolimab plus olaparib combined with locoregional therapies in advanced iCCA. A 65-year-old male with obstructive jaundice was diagnosed with metastatic iCCA (cT3N1M1, Stage IV) harboring a 117 mm left hepatic lobe lesion, with enlarged lymph nodes, and pulmonary nodules suspicious for metastasis. Next-generation sequencing revealed MSI-H and TMB-H status, along with DDR gene alterations (CDK12 and HDAC2). He received multimodal treatment comprising TACE, HAIC, PD-L1 blockade (envafolimab), and exploratory PARP inhibition (olaparib). Over 20 months, the primary lesion shrank from 117 mm to 42 mm, with regression of lymph nodules and pulmonary nodules and normalization of CA19-9. He underwent R0 resection and pathological examination confirmed a pathological complete response (pCR/ypT0N0) in the resected specimens. At the last follow-up (October 15, 2025), the patient had achieved a progression-free survival of 36 months and a postoperative recurrence-free survival of 16 months. This case demonstrates that the TACE plus HAIC combined with PD-L1 blockade and exploratory PARP inhibition is a promising conversion therapy strategy. It provides preliminary evidence for PARP inhibitor therapy in DDR-altered cholangiocarcinoma, supporting further investigation in prospective trials.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1935795.abstract: Altered N-glycosylation plays a critical role in immune regulation, yet the spatial distribution of N-glycans within immune niches of immunologically "cold" tumors remain poorly defined. Here, we combine matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) with highly multiplexed immunohistochemistry using photocleavable mass tags. This integrated workflow enables spatial mapping of N-glycosylation and immune markers within lymphoid aggregates (LAs) in prostate and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tissues, two malignancies that respond poorly to immunotherapy. Given the role of N-glycosylation in immune regulation, spatially resolved N-glycan profiling may provide insight into molecular heterogeneity within lymphoid aggregates and their surrounding tumor microenvironment. To assess the relationship between N_glycosylation and immune markers, candidate LAs from tissue samples collected from patients with varying stages of prostate cancer, PCa (n=49) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC (n=26) were identified via histological stains prior to enzymatic release of N-glycans and MALDI-MSI. MALDI-IHC was used to target immune cell markers and extracellular matrix proteins. In tissues with LAs, three N-glycan structural classes were identified when detectable: oligo-mannose, fucosylated tetra-antennary, and bisecting N-acetylglucosamine in fucosylated bi,- tri- and tetra- antennary structures, with some N-glycans common to both tumor types. LAs showed predominantly central CD20 and CD44 signal surrounded by CD3 signal localized along the tumor periphery. Our analysis revealed unique N-glycan patterns within and surrounding LAs, with variable profiles in distant regions, highlighting heterogeneity in LA-associated N-glycan profiles.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1936469.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide and frequently arises in the setting of chronic liver disease, cirrhosis, and portal hypertension. Liver resection represents a cornerstone of curative-intent treatment, but its role is uniquely influenced by the need to balance oncologic radicality with preservation of functional liver parenchyma. Over the last two decades, minimally invasive liver surgery has progressively expanded from selected laparoscopic minor resections to complex laparoscopic and robotic hepatectomies, challenging the historical dominance of open surgery. This narrative review critically examines the evolving roles of open, laparoscopic, and robotic liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma, emphasizing patient selection, technical considerations, scenario-based platform choice, and comparative outcomes. Particular attention is given to hepatocellular carcinoma-specific challenges, including impaired liver function, clinically significant portal hypertension, future liver remnant adequacy, recurrence risk, and the need for parenchymal-sparing strategies. The review also discusses distinct clinical scenarios, including small solitary tumors, posterosuperior lesions, central or deeply located tumors, multifocal disease, and recurrent HCC. Current evidence consistently suggests that minimally invasive approaches are associated with reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications, and shorter hospital stay compared with open surgery, while maintaining comparable oncologic outcomes in selected patients. Laparoscopy remains the most established minimally invasive platform, whereas robotics may offer technical advantages in complex resections through improved dexterity, three-dimensional visualization, and enhanced suturing capability. However, available evidence remains largely retrospective and influenced by selection bias and institutional expertise. Platform selection should therefore be individualized according to tumor anatomy, liver function, technical complexity, and center experience, with the goal of maximizing oncologic benefit while minimizing functional liver loss.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1936605.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive and treatment-resistant malignancy characterized by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that promotes disease progression and poor clinical outcomes. Increasing evidence suggests that NOTCH signaling is a key regulator of GBM progression, governing both tumor cell plasticity and immune evasion. In addition to its roles in development and stem cell maintenance, NOTCH signaling modulates interactions among glioma stem-like cells, immune cells, and stromal components. NOTCH signaling in both tumor and stromal compartments modulates immune cell fate decisions, antigen presentation, and inflammatory cytokine expression. This suggests its potential role as a key modulator of immune crosstalk within the TME of GBM. Moreover, dysregulation of the NOTCH signaling pathway may lead to an immunosuppressive TME, enhance tumor heterogeneity, and restrict responses to conventional therapies. Recent investigations also reveal the epigenetic and non-coding RNA patterns that reinforce aberrant NOTCH activity in GBM. Understanding the multifaceted interactions among NOTCH signaling, oncogenic pathways, and immunomodulatory mechanisms could provide insights into the molecular pathogenesis of GBM progression. Here, we discuss the pleiotropic and context-dependent functions of NOTCH signaling in GBM, with particular emphasis on its implications for tumor-immune interactions and its potential as a therapeutic target to address immune escape and treatment resistance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1936986.abstract: Synchronous bilateral primary breast cancer (sBPBC) accounts for 2.9%-3.9% of newly diagnosed breast cancers, while cases with discordant histologic subtypes are exceptionally rare. We report on a 59-year-old woman with synchronous left-sided invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and right-sided invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC). The patient underwent bilateral breast-conserving surgery with sentinel lymph node biopsy, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and endocrine therapy. No recurrence or metastasis was observed during the 12-month follow-up. To place the present case in the context of the existing literature, we comparatively reviewed seven previously reported cases of synchronous bilateral IDC and ILC. The comparison illustrated considerable heterogeneity in the clinicopathological characteristics, molecular profiles, nodal involvement, treatment strategies, and clinical outcomes. These findings support independent characterization of each breast lesion and individualized treatment planning based on the features of both tumors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1937448.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning framework that combines semi-automated segmentation, intratumoral habitats derived from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and multiscale peritumoral radiomics to predict high-grade prostate cancer (HGPCa) before surgery. This retrospective dual-center study involved 274 patients, comprising 208 from Center 1 for development and 66 from Center 2 for external test. The clinical and imaging variables included patient age, serum PSA, fPSA, PSAD, maximum tumor diameter, PI-RADS scores, and anatomical zone distribution (PZ vs. TZ). The development cohort was randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 145) and an internal validation cohort (n = 63). Intratumoral habitats were delineated using semi-automated segmentation and unsupervised K-means clustering, while peritumoral radiomic features were extracted from concentric 1-, 3-, and 5-mm shells. Predictive classifiers were optimized through machine learning algorithms, particularly a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for the habitat signature. A combined clinical-radiomics nomogram was constructed, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) employed to enhance model interpretability. Subgroup analyses were performed to assess the discriminative performance of the combined nomogram across the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ). The combined nomogram exhibited superior diagnostic performance, achieving AUCs of 0.914, 0.903, and 0.797 in the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. The MLP-based habitat model showed good discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.896, 0.897, and 0.782 across the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. Among the peritumoral regions, the 5-mm shell demonstrated the best discriminative performance. SHAP analysis identified Habitat 1 Shape Sphericity as the most influential feature. Subgroup analysis demonstrated the discriminatory ability of the combined nomogram in both the PZ (AUC: 0.796) and TZ (AUC: 0.753) subgroups. The integration of semi-automated segmentation-based habitat analysis and peritumoral radiomics provides a promising approach for preoperative risk stratification of prostate cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1937565.abstract: Tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) is a life-threatening oncologic emergency well-characterized in hematologic malignancies but considered rare in solid tumors. In breast cancer, TLS has been documented only in sporadic case reports, and the evolving treatment landscape-including CDK4/6 inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, novel endocrine agents, and antibody-drug conjugates-may introduce previously unrecognized TLS risks. The only prior review on this topic was published in 2021 and has been superseded by numerous new cases. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from January 2000 to June 2026 for case reports and case series describing TLS in patients with breast cancer, following PRISMA guidelines. TLS diagnosis was verified against Cairo-Bishop criteria. Data on patient demographics, tumor characteristics, precipitating factors, laboratory abnormalities, management, and outcomes were extracted and analyzed descriptively. Twenty cases of TLS from 20 publications were identified, with one additional case of successful TLS prevention. All patients had stage IIB-IV disease, with the majority (90%, 18/20) having stage IV disease; liver metastases were present in 55% (11/20). Precipitating factors included endocrine therapy (n=4, 75% mortality), HER2-targeted therapy (n=4, 50% mortality), chemotherapy (n=6, 50% mortality), radiotherapy (n=2, 50% mortality), PI3K inhibitor (n=1, survived), immunotherapy-chemotherapy combination (n=1, survived), and spontaneous TLS (n=2, 50% mortality). Overall TLS-related mortality was 50% (10/20). Endocrine therapy-associated TLS-predominantly aromatase inhibitors-carried the highest mortality (75%, 3/4). The only surviving patient in this group achieved long-term remission following supportive management. TLS in breast cancer, though rare, carries a high mortality rate approaching 50%. Notably, endocrine therapy-particularly aromatase inhibitors-emerges as a previously underappreciated TLS trigger with disproportionately poor outcomes. With the expanding use of novel targeted and endocrine agents in advanced breast cancer, clinicians should maintain heightened vigilance for TLS, especially in patients with high tumor burden and hepatic metastases. Early recognition and prompt intervention are essential to improve outcomes. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261429658.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1937938.abstract: Health inequities in cancer care persist, indicating that advancing equity requires not only understanding inequities but also transforming how cancer research is developed and conducted. Although equity-oriented and community-engaged approaches have advanced important principles for research, there is limited understanding of the conditions and processes required to translate these principles into practice within cancer care systems, including how research agendas can be collaboratively developed to reflect community and health system needs. This Perspective describes the co-design and implementation of a provincial Health Equity Workshop in Alberta, Canada, as a practice-based example of how a cancer care system operationalized Patient-Oriented Research principles to support equity-oriented research agenda development. Guided by Patient-Oriented Research and informed by the Health Equity Implementation Framework, the initiative involved a twelve-member working group comprising people with lived experience of cancer, representatives of community organizations, health system leaders, and researchers who co-designed and facilitated a two-day workshop involving 43 participants. Reflections from the initiative highlighted relational, organizational, and practical conditions that shaped equity-oriented engagement, including trust-building, shared leadership, compensation and resource supports, institutional commitment, and attention to system-level barriers affecting participation. The workshop demonstrated how co-design can embed equity from the earliest stages of research agenda development by bringing together diverse forms of expertise to shape what research is needed and how it should be conducted. This Perspective offers practical insights for researchers, health systems, and community partners seeking to advance equitable cancer research and care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1938611.abstract: Glioblastoma CNS WHO Grade 4 (GBM) is associated with poor prognosis and high recurrence rates despite the current therapeutic approaches. Conventional imaging, in particular Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), is primarily used during follow-up to detect tumor recurrence but has limited ability to distinguish recurrence from therapy-related changes, such as tissue necrosis and postoperative scar tissue. Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor-specific serological biomarkers, such as miRNAs, provides a gene expression signature for early identification of GBM recurrence. This pilot "proof-of-concept" study investigated the potential of circulating tumor-derived miRNA in whole blood samples for early detection of tumor recurrence. In a previous whole-transcriptome screening (NGS) study, whole-blood samples (n = 33) from seven patients and tumor biopsies (n = 4) were used to identify biomarkers. Corresponding to tumor surgery and recurrence, miRNA expression was examined in pre-surgical blood samples and tumor tissues. In whole blood, we investigated whether a pattern could be identified indicating post-surgery downregulation, consistent with reduced tumor burden, followed by a return to pre-surgery levels at recurrence. We identified 1-19 miRNA species per patient (a total of 72 miRNAs) showing this pattern. In this manuscript, we present the qRT-PCR validation results. The 45 most promising miRNAs identified by NGS study were selected and quantified using qRT-PCR. In addition, miR-21 was included as a promising candidate reported in the literature. To address challenges in miRNA normalization, five normalization strategies and unnormalized raw Ct values were compared. Two normalization approaches (median DCt normalization and unnormalized raw Ct values) showed no systematic bias. Depending on the normalization method, the agreement between NGS and qRT-PCR ranged from 23.6 to 27.9%. Although the concordance between NGS and qRT-PCR was low at the individual-patient level, qRT-PCR identified a common set of 24 miRNAs differentially regulated across patients. Notably, miR-424-3p and miR-362-5p were shared by five of seven patients, followed by miR-1307-3p and miR-22-5p, each shared by four patients. Interestingly, miR-21 did not show the predefined recurrence-associated pattern in any patient. Blood-based miRNA profiling may complement imaging in longitudinal monitoring of GBM patients, although clinical benefits have not been confirmed, and validation in a larger independent cohort is required.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1938736.abstract: Objective Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Conventional biomarkers alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP) have diagnostic limitations, particularly for early-stage disease. This study investigated the expression profile of ORC1 in HBV-related liver disease and its association with HBV infection, disease progression, and prognosis. Methods 178 participants were recruited: 124 HBV-positive cases (49 HBV-HCC, 33 HBV-cirrhosis, 42 chronic hepatitis B) and 54 HBV-negative controls (35 non-HBV-HCC, 19 hepatic hemangioma). Tissue ORC1 was detected by immunohistochemistry, and serum ORC1 was measured by ELISA in a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum. Logistic regression identified factors associated with high ORC1 expression. ROC curves were used to evaluate the discrimination of tissue ORC1, AFP, and DCP for HBV-HCC, and the correlation between ORC1 and tumor diameter was analyzed. TCGA-LIHC data were used for external validation. Results Tissue ORC1 was significantly upregulated in HBV-positive patients, and HBV infection was independently associated with high ORC1 expression (P<0. 001). ORC1 expression increased progressively from chronic hepatitis B to cirrhosis to HCC. In a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum, tissue and serum ORC1 were moderately correlated (Spearman rs=0. 554, 95% CI 0. 085–0. 822, P = 0. 021). Tissue ORC1 showed moderate discrimination between HBV-HCC and HBV-LC (AUC = 0. 64) and between HBV-HCC and CHB (AUC = 0. 66). ORC1 expression was not significantly associated with tumor diameter ( P >0. 05). High ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC (HR = 1. 7, P = 0. 0026). Conclusion ORC1 upregulation is independently associated with HBV infection and increases with disease progression in HBV-related liver disease. Although tissue ORC1 showed only moderate discrimination for HBV-HCC, high ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC. These findings suggest that ORC1 is primarily a proliferation- and progression-related marker in HBV-related liver disease.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1939245.abstract: To investigate the expression levels of estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) in endometrial carcinoma (EC) and their correlations with standardized clinicopathological parameters in a single-center surgical cohort. Retrospective clinical and pathological data of 78 EC patients receiving primary surgery at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of Kiang Wu Hospital between Jan 2016 and Aug 2022 were collected. ER/PR expression was quantified via immunohistochemistry (IHC) using the Allred scoring system. Dichotomous receptor positivity (Allred 0-2 negative/3-8 positive) and continuous total Allred scores were analyzed separately. Fisher's exact test or χ² test was used for categorical comparison; Kruskal-Wallis H test with adjusted post-hoc pairwise tests and Wilcoxon rank-sum test were applied for ordinal Allred score data. Exact P values, test statistics and degrees of freedom were reported for all analyses. The overall cohort included 71 endometrioid carcinoma (EC) and 7 non-endometrioid carcinoma (NEC) cases. ER and PR positive rates were significantly higher in endometrioid lesions (97.2% and 94.4%) than non-endometrioid subtypes (57.1% for both, P = 0.018/P = 0.018). Continuous Allred scores of ER and PR declined significantly with worsening tumor differentiation (all adjusted P 0.05). Reduced ER and PR expression correlates with poorer tumor differentiation and advanced FIGO stage in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma; PR loss is independently associated with lymph node metastasis. This study only identifies crude cross-sectional correlations without survival or multivariable adjustment data, so ER/PR may merely serve as auxiliary morphological markers reflecting tumor aggressive potential, rather than standalone indicators for prognosis or individualized hormone therapy guidance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1939329.abstract: Acute leukemias require rapid subtype identification to guide timely treatment. Differentiation of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), acute monocytic leukemia (AMoL/M5), and acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL/M3) often relies on specialized tests that may not be immediately available. This study evaluated differentiation only among patients already confirmed to have one of these three diagnoses, rather than screening an unselected population with suspected acute leukemia. This multicenter retrospective study included 9,398 newly diagnosed, previously untreated patients with established APL/M3, AMoL/M5, or ALL between May 2019 and May 2025 at four tertiary hospitals in China. Relapse, remission, follow-up, and non-initial disease episodes were excluded. Twenty-four routine hematological parameters were evaluated. One center served as the development cohort with five-fold stratified cross-validation, while three independent centers were reserved for external validation. Ten machine-learning algorithms were compared. Performance was assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and F1 score. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) supported feature selection and interpretation. An 18-feature random forest model achieved a development-stage cross-validated AUC of 0.93 and external AUCs of 0.89, 0.87, and 0.90. Overall sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, accuracy, and F1 score were 0.78, 0.90, 0.81, 0.91, 0.81, and 0.79, respectively. SHAP identified leukocyte, erythrocyte, and platelet indices as the most important features. A Streamlit application was developed for clinical evaluation. Using a development-derived APL alert threshold of 0.0966, APL sensitivity was 99.02% in development and 96.32%-97.94% across external cohorts, with PPVs of 54.34% and 35.58%-84.25%, respectively. External validation showed center-specific calibration shifts, indicating that predicted probabilities should not be interpreted as universally calibrated absolute diagnostic probabilities. Among patients already confirmed to have APL/M3, AMoL/M5, or ALL, this explainable model enabled low-cost preliminary differentiation using routine hematological data. It may support subtype prioritization and confirmatory testing but cannot replace standard diagnostics, identify other diagnoses, or screen unselected patients. Prospective multinational and workflow-based validation is required before routine implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1939651.abstract: Uterine sarcomas represent a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies whose management remains clinically challenging. They account for approximately 3%-5% of all uterine malignancies. Undifferentiated uterine sarcoma (UUS) is a subtype of uterine sarcomas. SMARCA4 is a tumor suppressor gene that is aberrantly altered in approximately 5%-7% of human malignancies. SMARCA4-deficient UUS is a highly aggressive, undifferentiated mesenchymal neoplasm associated with a median overall survival (OS) of 7 months. During tumorigenesis, loss of function of either SMARCA4 or SMARCA2 is frequently observed; however, concurrent loss of both genes has been reported to be synthetically lethal and is therefore considered unexpected. In this case report, a 52-year-old Chinese woman with early-stage UUS and SMARCA4 and SMARCA2 co-deficiency underwent surgical resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and achieved a disease-free survival (DFS) of 32 months. This case suggests that patients with UUS harboring SMARCA4 and SMARCA2 co-deficiency may derive a survival benefit from early diagnosis and surgical resection. However, owing to the extreme rarity of UUS with co-deficiency of SMARCA4 and SMARCA2, conducting a high-level phase III randomized controlled trial to validate this observation remains impractical.
