doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940047.abstract: Objective To systematically evaluate published nomograms developed for patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) treated with radiotherapy, focusing on prognostic performance, core predictive variables, and implications for future model development. Methods A systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library identified studies published between 2010 and 2025 that developed new nomograms for LACC cohorts treated with radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. Data extraction included study population, predicted outcomes (overall survival [OS], progression-free survival [PFS], or disease-free survival [DFS]), model performance (C-index), validation methods, calibration, and predictor variables. Predictor patterns were summarized primarily by frequency of inclusion across nomograms, with β-coefficients used only for exploratory within-model descriptions. Results Nine studies met the inclusion criteria; eight developed nomograms for OS and three evaluated disease progression outcomes (PFS or DFS), with two studies evaluating both outcome categories. Reported C-indices ranged from 0.68 to 0.835, indicating moderate to good discrimination. Lymph node status, FIGO stage, and tumor size were among the most frequently incorporated predictors, while histology and SCC-Ag were also recurrently included. Validation in independent cohorts remained limited. Graphical calibration was commonly reported, whereas quantitative calibration measures and decision-curve analyses were inconsistently reported. Conclusions Nomograms for LACC treated with radiotherapy generally demonstrate moderate-to-good discriminative performance and frequently incorporate lymph node status, stage, and tumor size. However, methodological heterogeneity, incomplete validation, and evolving treatment paradigms limit their immediate generalizability. Future work should focus on robust external validation, recalibration, and evaluation in contemporary treatment cohorts before clinical implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940160.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are associated with a wide spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), reflecting enhanced immune activation. Pancreatic involvement is rare and typically presents as asymptomatic hyperlipasemia or diffuse inflammatory changes. Focal or multifocal mass-like presentations are uncommon and may mimic pancreatic malignancy, posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We report the case of a 48-year-old woman treated with Pembrolizumab and Paclitaxel for axillary recurrence of triple-negative breast cancer. After four cycles, FDG PET/CT demonstrated a complete metabolic response at the initial tumor site but revealed new multifocal hypermetabolic pancreatic lesions. Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed multiple pancreatic masses, raising suspicion of metastatic disease or dissociated response. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration at two concordant pancreatic sites showed neutrophil-predominant inflammatory infiltration without malignant cells, consistent with immune-related pancreatic injury. The patient subsequently developed symptoms of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, which improved after concomitant initiation of pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy and corticosteroid tapering, with the relative contribution of each not clearly distinguishable. Follow-up imaging demonstrated complete resolution of pancreatic lesions. This case highlights a rare mass-forming (pseudotumoral) phenotype of ICI-related pancreatic injury (ICI-PI), presenting as multifocal FDG-avid pancreatic pseudomasses. Such findings may represent a major pitfall in PET/CT interpretation under immunotherapy, particularly in the context of otherwise favorable oncologic response. Histopathological confirmation is critical to distinguish immune-mediated inflammation from metastatic disease. This observation supports the concept of organ-specific immune dysregulation driven by ICIs and expands the radiological spectrum of pancreatic irAEs. Multifocal FDG-avid pancreatic lesions occurring during immunotherapy should raise suspicion for immune-related pancreatic injury (ICI-PI), especially in the absence of systemic progression. Early recognition is essential to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment decisions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940160.title: Multifocal FDG-avid pancreatic pseudomasses mimicking metastases during pembrolizumab for axillary recurrence of triple-negative breast cancer: a case report of immune-related pancreatitis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940169.abstract: Cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, yet current liquid biopsy approaches provide limited information regarding the anatomical distribution of metastatic disease. Circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, and extracellular vesicle (EV)-based assays have substantially advanced molecular characterization of cancer but generally do not reveal the tissue sites where metastatic progression is occurring. Here, we introduce the concept of Spatial Liquid Biopsy, a proposed next-generation framework that utilizes circulating tumor-associated EVs as molecular maps of metastatic disease. We hypothesize that EVs released from metastatic lesions may carry both tumor-associated signatures and tissue-associated extracellular proteins reflecting interactions with the local metastatic microenvironment. By integrating tumor-associated EV enrichment with multiplex profiling of organ-associated surface markers, Spatial Liquid Biopsy seeks to identify composite tumor-associated/organ-associated EV signatures that may provide greater spatial specificity than either marker alone. If experimentally and clinically validated, these signatures may enable minimally invasive inference of metastatic organ involvement and longitudinal assessment of metastatic disease evolution. This framework represents a conceptual expansion of liquid biopsy from detecting circulating evidence of malignancy toward generating spatial information that may complement imaging and guide personalized cancer surveillance and management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940480.abstract: Deep angiomyxoma (DAM) is a rare, locally infiltrative mesenchymal tumor of the female pelvic and perineal regions that is often misdiagnosed because of nonspecific clinical and ultrasonographic findings. We report two cases of pelvic-perineal DAM initially interpreted as paravaginal hematomas. One patient underwent ultrasound-guided aspiration and thrombin injection before progressive enlargement prompted further evaluation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated marked T2 hyperintensity, internal swirling structures, and extension along pelvic floor tissue planes, raising suspicion of DAM. Both patients underwent surgical resection with histologically negative margins (R0). Histopathology confirmed DAM with estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor positivity. Following multidisciplinary discussion, both patients received six cycles of individualized postoperative gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy. No radiological recurrence was observed at 11 and 12 months, respectively. Persistent or enlarging hematoma-like pelvic-perineal masses without a clear precipitating factor should prompt consideration of DAM and further MRI evaluation. MRI is useful for suggesting DAM and delineating tumor extent, whereas definitive diagnosis relies on histopathology. The benefit of routine postoperative endocrine therapy after R0 resection remains uncertain.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940599.abstract: age and ovarian reserve markers are commonly used in clinical practice to predict ovarian response to controlled stimulation for assisted reproductive techniques in infertile patients. In oncofertility, some reports suggest the predictive performance of these markers may be lower in specific subgroups. We evaluated the performance of a prespecified age + log(AMH) model for predicting metaphase-II (MII) oocyte yield in women undergoing oocyte cryopreservation before gonadotoxic treatment. This retrospective single-center cohort study included consecutive oocyte cryopreservation cycles performed before gonadotoxic treatment between January 2015 and January 2025. MII yield was modelled using negative-binomial regression with age and log-transformed AMH as predictors. Regression coefficients were estimated in the current cohort. Model performance was assessed using calibration measures and patient-level bootstrap internal validation, with all cycles from the same woman kept together during resampling. Analyses were performed overall and by cancer type. Threshold-based underestimation analyses and the incremental value of antral follicle count (AFC) were also explored. A total of 179 oocyte cryopreservation cycles performed in 167 women were included. The model showed good overall calibration using aggregated out-of-bootstrap predictions, with calibration-in-the-large of 0.00 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.09) and calibration slope of 0.98 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.15). Mean prediction error was -0.10 MII (95% CI -0.97 to 0.80), indicating minimal average directional bias. Mean absolute error was 4.12 MII (95% CI 3.53 to 4.76), and root mean squared error was 5.94 MII (95% CI 4.92 to 7.00). Substantial underestimation, defined as observed MII yield exceeding predicted yield by more than 4 MII, was more frequent in hematologic malignancies than in solid tumors (31.8% [14/44] vs 12.6% [17/135]; risk difference +19.2 percentage points, 95% CI + 4.4 to +34.1; Fisher's exact p=0.006). This finding remained consistent in the one-cycle-per-woman sensitivity analysis. Adding AFC did not improve predictive performance in the complete-case analysis. age and AMH are useful tools for counseling regarding the expected mature oocyte yield, including in our subset of oncofertility patients. As we found substantial underestimation of mature oocyte yield to be more frequent in hematologic malignancies, the results should be interpreted cautiously in this subgroup.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1940599.title: Age- and AMH-based prediction of mature oocyte yield in oncofertility is well calibrated overall, but substantial underestimation is more frequent in hematologic malignancies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941008.abstract: SMARCA4-deficient non-small cell lung cancer (SD-NSCLC) is a highly aggressive molecular subtype. This malignancy is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, carrying a dismal prognosis and also demonstrating poor responsiveness to traditional treatment. Beyond its primary site, the disease can exhibit unusual metastatic patterns such as metastasis to oral soft tissues. We report a unique case of a 61-year-old male heavy smoker with molecularly confirmed SD-NSCLC who experienced rapid metastatic progression to the right gingiva and neck lymph nodes shortly after radical surgery and initial chemo-immunotherapy. This clinical scenario exemplifies primary resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), where pre-existing genetic or microenvironmental barriers hinder initial therapeutic success. To overcome this resistance, a salvage multimodal strategy was implemented, integrating ICIs with etoposide/cisplatin (EP) chemotherapy and low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT). Remarkably, this regimen achieved significant regression of the bulky metastatic lesions and has maintained sustained disease stability for over 15 months, with the patient remaining clinically stable as of the latest follow-up in June 2026. This case may hint the potential role of LDRT as an immunomodulatory component to overcome primary resistance in SD-NSCLC, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for patients who experience disease progression following first-line chemo-immunotherapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941099.abstract: Lipoblastoma-like tumor (LLT) is a distinctive adipocytic neoplasm most commonly arising in the vulva of women. Lingual involvement is extremely rare. Herein, we present a case of LLT occurring in the tongue and review the relevant literature. The patient was a 41-year-old female who presented with a mass on the right lateral border of the tongue for 6 months. Microscopic examination revealed the typical features of LLT. Immunohistochemically, the tumor was positive for CD34 and vimentin, with partial positivity for CDK4 and S-100, and negative for Rb, p16, and MDM2. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) demonstrated no DDIT3 rearrangement or MDM2 amplification. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) detected no significant genetic alterations. The tumor was completely resected, and no recurrence was observed at 19 months of follow-up. Given the rarity of lingual LLT-of which only three cases, including ours, have been reported-this report expands the current knowledge base and emphasizes the need for accurate diagnosis and long-term patient surveillance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941311.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here we integrated a 60-case clinical MPN cohort, the GSE174060 Affymetrix Human Transcriptome Array 2.0 microarray dataset, immune deconvolution, exploratory feature prioritization, the GSE228995 mouse single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset, human-sample validation, and functional perturbation assays to investigate whether cuproptosis-related metabolism is associated with total calreticulin (CALR) abundance and Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT)-related inflammatory signaling. GSE174060 included 36 samples: 6 essential thrombocythemia (ET), 11 polycythemia vera (PV), 9 primary myelofibrosis (PMF), 4 secondary myelofibrosis (SMF), and 6 healthy control (HC) samples. Clinically, CALR-mutated cases were enriched for thrombocytosis and distinctive megakaryocytic abnormalities, while inflammatory and fibrotic features tracked with higher interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). Microarray-based transcriptomic analyses identified an MPN-associated cuproptosis-related and immune-response program, and consensus clustering separated samples into exploratory transcriptomic clusters. Within this expression-derived partition, post hoc multi-algorithm feature prioritization recurrently retained FDX1 and CALR among genes associated with the Cluster 1-versus-Cluster 2 transcriptional contrast. Single-cell analyses localized Calr and Fdx1 across hematopoietic and immune populations and highlighted inferred JAK-STAT-associated communication potential. In human MPN samples, FDX1 and total CALR protein and mRNA levels were increased and accompanied by STAT5 phosphorylation and elevated inflammatory mediators. Functionally, FDX1 knockdown reduced total CALR abundance, STAT5 phosphorylation, cytokine release, sensitivity to copper-dependent cytotoxicity, and proliferation, whereas FDX1 overexpression showed the reciprocal pattern and was partly counteracted by ruxolitinib. These findings support an association between FDX1 perturbation, total CALR abundance, STAT5-associated signaling, and inflammatory output in MPN, but do not establish direct regulation of mutant CALR or mutant CALR-MPL signaling.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941438.abstract: The molecular chaperone HSPA8 is classically recognized for its role in protein homeostasis, and while its upregulation correlates with poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), whether HSPA8 exerts non-canonical functions beyond chaperoning remains unknown. Through integrative transcriptomic profiling, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), isoform-specific rescue experiments, and in vivo xenograft models, we investigated the functional and mechanistic role of HSPA8 in TNBC pathogenesis. We unveil a paradigm-shifting function for HSPA8 as a modulator of alternative splicing of the PP2A regulatory subunit gene PPP2R2D, promoting exon 2 retention to favor the full-length PPP2R2D-2 isoform over the truncated PPP2R2D-1. These two isoforms exhibit functionally distinct roles: only PPP2R2D-2 possesses pro-survival activity, whereas PPP2R2D-1 lacks this function. Specifically, PPP2R2D-2 rescues HSPA8 depletion-induced apoptosis by modulating the mitochondrial pathway (BAX/BCL-2/cleaved Caspase-3) and restores in vivo tumor growth. Strikingly, this splicing axis also correlates with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, characterized by altered M1/M2 macrophage marker abundance. These findings uncover a dual mechanism that simultaneously drives intrinsic survival signaling and is associated with alterations in the tumor immune microenvironment. They transcend the classical chaperone paradigm by establishing HSPA8 as a non-canonical splicing modulator, and the HSPA8-PPP2R2D-2 axis emerges as a critical vulnerability in TNBC, offering a novel therapeutic angle that concurrently targets tumor cell survival and microenvironmental immunosuppression.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941568.abstract: Soft tissue sarcoma (STS) is a rare but aggressive mesenchymal malignancy that accounts for less than 1% of all adult cancers. Head and neck soft tissue sarcomas (HNSTS) are infrequent malignant tumors arising from mesenchymal and neuroectodermal tissues in the head and neck region with a poor prognosis, and recurrence is predominantly local. There are few targeted management guidelines. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman with postoperative recurrence of HNSTS. The patient was diagnosed with high-grade soft tissue sarcoma of the scalp in February 2025 and treated with surgery. In June 2025, the patient was diagnosed with recurrence, and was subsequently treated with combination therapy consisting of the anti-angiogenic inhibitor anlotinib and radiotherapy. In December 2025, after nine cycles, the patient showed a complete response (CR) to therapy. This indicates that radiotherapy combined with anti-angiogenic targeted therapy may produce synergistic effects in patients with HNSTS and provide directions for future clinical decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941783.abstract: Long-term head and neck cancer survivors are few, but always exposed to a risk of mandibular osteoradionecrosis (ORN) despite the use of appropriate dose-volume constraints in today's radiotherapy. Here, ORN development is approached from another look, in an attempt to explain its complexity. Early ORN is best defined by length of the mucosal defect (<2 teeth long) and radiological assessment of the depth of areas of bone resorption (lysis below the level of the inferior alveolar canal) in the radiotherapy volume. Technical improvements have greatly reduced the incidence of ORN, but a lifelong risk remains and requires long-term follow-up. Pathogenic hypotheses have evolved over time from the "radiation-trauma-infection" triad to the 3H theory of "hypoxia-hypocellularity-hypovascularity", and then radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone. ORN is a dynamic process combining interacting causal factors that worsen each other over time: (a) radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone and its related radiotherapy technical parameters; (b) periodontal disease/dental trauma and their related questions on optimal timing of pre- or post-radiotherapy extractions and how many teeth; (c) infection/oral microbiota and their related mechanically inaccessible bone sequestra (residual bacteria); (d) vascular factors from capillary network destruction to artery stenosis of irradiated branches and the carotid trunk. Symptomatic medical care focusing on comorbidity parameters and devitalized tissue removal is not sufficient to protect patients against ORN. These new insights should help to treat early ORN through concomitant control of these causal factors and best dental care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941788.abstract: Prostate cancer remains one of the most frequently diagnosed malignancies and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among men globally. Its development is driven by a complex interaction of genetic susceptibility, molecular alterations, hormonal signaling, environmental exposures, and lifestyle-related factors. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on the etiological mechanisms and evolving therapeutic landscape of prostate cancer. A systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Eligible studies included original research, clinical studies, translational studies, and experimental investigations evaluating prostate cancer etiology, molecular mechanisms, risk factors, biomarkers, or therapeutic interventions. The review included 29 studies encompassing epidemiological cohorts, clinical studies, genomic analyses, tissue-based investigations, and preclinical experimental studies. Evidence demonstrated that prostate cancer etiology involves multiple interconnected pathways, including androgen receptor signaling, DNA repair alterations, genomic instability, chromatin remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and inflammatory mechanisms. Genetic variants, including single nucleotide polymorphisms and polygenic risk scores, were associated with disease susceptibility, aggressiveness, treatment response, and toxicity outcomes. Therapeutic advances included optimization of androgen deprivation therapy, novel androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy, radiotherapy personalization, bone-targeted therapies, PSMA-directed radioligand therapy, and emerging immunotherapeutic approaches. Biomarker-driven strategies, including genomic classifiers and molecular signatures, showed potential for improving risk stratification and individualized treatment selection. Prostate cancer is a biologically heterogeneous disease requiring integrated approaches that combine molecular understanding with clinical decision-making. Recent advances in precision oncology have expanded therapeutic options beyond conventional treatment paradigms, enabling more personalized management strategies. However, further research is required to improve representation of diverse populations, validate biomarkers across different ethnic groups, and optimize the clinical implementation of emerging targeted and immune-based therapies. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261435105.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1941793.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the most lethal solid tumors, with 5-year survival near 13% despite decades of incremental change, and current management continues to be organized around anatomic resectability and a chemotherapy backbone applied largely without regard to tumor biology. This article advances the thesis that the dominant paradigm underperforms because it treats a systemic, molecularly convergent, multi-compartment disease as though it were a local one. We first summarize the real advances of the past decade-in surgery, systemic therapy, molecular profiling, and immunotherapy-and then identify five interlocking failure points that persist despite them: (i) selection by vessel anatomy, judged on imaging criteria that are read inconsistently and that classify inaccurately even where read consistently, and applied to splanchnic veins without accounting for their baseline variability and tumor-associated thrombosis; (ii) occult metastasis and the resulting limits of local cure for the systemic majority, evidenced by the gap between complete resection and durable survival and by early distant recurrence; (iii) the addition of radiotherapy, which improves local control without extending survival; (iv) chemotherapy chosen without reference to a validated prognostic classical/basal-like distinction, although prospective subtype-directed regimen selection has not yet improved outcomes in randomized testing; and (v) a sequential, non-integrated structure in which systemic and immune therapy are deferred and no definitive path exists for the roughly 80% who are not surgical candidates. We then propose a multimodal, biology-guided framework that answers each failure point, with every component graded on an explicit evidence scale: corrected tumor-suppressor gene therapy matched to lesion type, a systemic backbone combining renin-angiotensin system-pathway inhibition with immunogenically sequenced chemotherapy and personalized neoantigen vaccination, in-situ immune conversion of an accessible tumor by cryoablation with local priming and natural killer (NK) cell delivery, and front-end biological patient selection. The framework is conceptual rather than product-specific; we specify its rationale, its integration in time, a staged first-in-human development program, and the studies required to test it. The objective is to convert local disease into systemic benefit-a step the current paradigm is not designed to take.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1942174.abstract: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) combined with pembrolizumab has become the standard treatment for high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer, increasing the need for prompt recognition of immune-related adverse events (irAEs). We report a rare case of severe gastrointestinal irAE complicated by hepatic portal venous gas (HPVG) during pembrolizumab-based CCRT. A 72-year-old woman with FIGO 2018 stage IIIC1r cervical squamous cell carcinoma developed persistent diarrhea and anorexia during treatment, followed by sudden hematemesis after the first brachytherapy session. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed diffuse gastric mucosal necrosis, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated HPVG, intramural gastric gas, and diffuse gastrointestinal wall edema without evidence of intestinal ischemia. Gastric biopsy showed marked intraepithelial lymphocytic infiltration predominantly composed of CD8-positive T cells, consistent with pembrolizumab-induced gastrointestinal irAE. High-dose corticosteroid therapy and supportive conservative management resulted in rapid clinical and radiological resolution, avoiding surgical intervention. This case highlights that gastrointestinal irAEs may mimic conventional CCRT-related toxicities, delaying diagnosis. Furthermore, HPVG should not be considered synonymous with intestinal necrosis. Careful integration of clinical, radiological, endoscopic, and pathological findings is essential to distinguish immune-mediated gastrointestinal injury from ischemic disease and to guide appropriate management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1942222.abstract: For advanced EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKI) therapy is the primary treatment, but drug resistance and side effects reduce its effectiveness. Integrating Chinese and Western medicine is a key focus in cancer treatment. This study evaluates the clinical benefits of combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with EGFR-TKI, summarizing TCM syndromes and medication traits. We searched six databases for relevant clinical studies. A meta-analysis assessed progression-free survival (PFS), disease control rate (DCR), and adverse reactions, with subgroup analysis by EGFR mutation type. A TCM syndrome network was created to examine syndrome distribution and core prescription patterns. TCM combined with EGFR-TKIs significantly improved PFS (HR = 0.70, 95%CI 0.65-0.76, p < 0.00001, I² = 0%), benefiting patients with Exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation equally (p = 0.75). The combination therapy increased DCR (RR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.01-1.40, p = 0.04), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 89%), and reduced targeted-agent-related adverse reactions. Qi-Yin and Lung-Spleen deficiency were the dominant TCM syndromes, managed via Qi-tonifying, Yin-nourishing and spleen-strengthening regimens. Integrating TCM with EGFR-TKI enhances tumor control and treatment safety in advanced NSCLC patients with EGFR mutations, showing consistent efficacy across various mutation types. This approach, which considers clinical syndrome differentiation and medication patterns in Chinese medicine, offers evidence-based guidance for personalized treatment. This review was performed following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261398486, identifier CRD420261398486.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1942370.abstract: With improved survival among people living with HIV (PLWH), non-AIDS-defining cancers have become increasingly prominent. Women living with HIV (WLWH) remain underrepresented in ovarian cancer trials, leaving limited evidence on the tolerability of standard therapies, including chemotherapy, anti-VEGF agents, and PARP inhibitors. These patients also face unique care barriers beyond biological uncertainties. This retrospective review included five WLWH diagnosed with ovarian cancer (June 2022-March 2024). Three received anticancer treatment; one refused chemotherapy and was lost to follow-up; one had biopsy only. We collected data on demographics, HIV history, tumor characteristics, treatment exposure, adverse events (CTCAE v5.0), CD4+/CD8+ counts, and HIV RNA, focusing safety and immune analyses on the three treated patients. Median age was 51 years; four had stage III-IV disease. No treatment-related deaths, persistent HIV rebound, or AIDS-defining events occurred. During first-line paclitaxel/carboplatin, one patient developed grade 3 neutropenia managed with G-CSF, but later developed significant thrombocytopenia on niraparib requiring dose reduction and hospitalization. Among two patients receiving bevacizumab, CD4+ patterns diverged: one showed a transient decline (387 to 259 cells/μL) with concurrent nedaplatin; another maintained stable counts (150 to 200 cells/μL). One patient had transient, self-limited HIV RNA elevation concurrent with disease progression, which resolved spontaneously. This series provides real-world observations that platinum-based and targeted therapies may be delivered to selected WLWH with close monitoring. The heterogeneous CD4+ responses highlight the need for individualized immune surveillance rather than attributing changes to any single agent. Integrated oncologic-HIV care and attention to socioeconomic barriers remain critical for this underrepresented population.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1942820.abstract: Approximately 35% of patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) progress to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), highlighting the limitations of PSA as a stand-alone monitoring biomarker. This study aimed to construct a peripheral blood mRNA-based prognostic model for progression to mCRPC, evaluate the prognostic value of the identified biomarkers, and explore the biological role of the top-performing gene in prostate cancer cells. Single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE288878) were analyzed to screen for mCRPC-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs). A prospective cohort study was conducted on newly diagnosed mHSPC patients who received first-line androgen deprivation therapy (ADT)-based treatment, from whom peripheral blood samples were collected for transcriptome sequencing. The intersection of DEGs from GSE288878 and our cohort defined the gene signature. Following random splitting of the dataset into development and validation sets (7:3), we used an Elastic Net-regularized Cox model to derive a prognostic model for mCRPC-free survival. TCGA prostate cancer samples were used to analyze the association between biomarker genes and progression-free survival (PFS). In vitro experiments investigated the biological role of the gene with prognostic significance in blood and cancer tissues. Five candidate genes (SLC25A39, GRB10, SELENBP1, SLC6A8, and YBX3) were identified as closely associated with mCRPC. We constructed a prognostic model, with an AUC for predicting 1-year mCRPC-free survival of 0.89 (0.80-0.97) in the development set and 0.83 (0.62-1.00) in the validation set. We identified elevated SLC6A8 expression in peripheral blood as an independent risk factor for progression to mCRPC. In the TCGA database, elevated SLC6A8 expression in prostate cancer tissue was identified as an independent risk factor for shorter PFS. Pharmacological inhibition of SLC6A8 significantly suppressed CRPC cell proliferation, decreased glycolytic metabolite levels, and downregulated glycolysis-associated gene expression. The prognostic model effectively predicted progression to mCRPC in patients with mHSPC receiving first-line therapy. SLC6A8 may serve as a prognostic biomarker and promote prostate cancer progression through enhanced glycolysis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1943135.abstract: Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MNs), which develop following cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy, remain one of the most significant clinical challenges in modern hematology due to their aggressive clinical course and poor survival outcomes. The traditional paradigm regarded the development of t-MNs as a consequence of de novo genetic damage induced by anticancer therapies. However, recent data concerning genomics and clonal evolution have fundamentally transformed our understanding of the biological origins of the disease. Current evidence demonstrates that low-level, clinically silent hematopoietic clones are present in the peripheral blood or bone marrow years prior to disease onset in a substantial proportion of t-MN cases. The pathogenesis of t-MNs is therefore being reconceptualized, not merely as the emergence of de novo treatment-induced mutations, but rather as the expansion and progression to malignant transformation of pre-existing silent clones under selective pressure. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) is a dynamic biological process characterized by the acquisition of a proliferative advantage by specific cell populations, resulting from somatic mutations accumulated by hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) throughout life. A clinically defined subgroup of this process, including CH of indeterminate potential (CHIP) and clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance (CCUS), are defined as the presence of somatic mutations with a variant allele frequency (VAF) of ≥2% in genes associated with myeloid malignancies. Both are recognized as clinically meaningful pre-cancerous states, differentiated primarily by the presence of unexplained cytopenias in CCUS. The presence of CH by itself is insufficient to drive malignant transformation. The observation that only a small fraction of individuals harboring CHIP or CCUS ultimately develop myeloid neoplasia indicates that clonal progression is not solely dictated by the presence of a mutation, but rather by the biological characteristics of the clone, the specific mutation type, clone size, environmental stressors, and the bone marrow microenvironment. The fundamental paradigm has thus shifted from simply asking "which patients have CH?" to determining "which silent clones possess the potential to evolve into aggressive myeloid neoplasms in the future?" The concept of the "power of silent clones" provides a novel biological perspective in t-MN risk stratification, establishing a foundational framework for the future development of personalized surveillance, early intervention, and targeted preventative strategies. Deciphering CH enables precise risk stratification and helps intercept myeloid malignancies before clinical onset.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1943176.abstract: The 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting presented substantial new data on antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in lung cancer, highlighting the ongoing expansion of ADC-based strategies from later-line treatment toward first-line combination regimens. This focused narrative review summarizes and discusses the efficacy and safety findings of ADCs targeting TROP2, HER2, Nectin-4, PD-L1, c-Met, B7-H3, DLL3, SEZ6, and other emerging targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with particular attention to emerging ADC plus immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations in the first-line setting. Taken together, these findings highlight an expanding ADC landscape in lung cancer. However, many of the emerging strategies remain supported primarily by preliminary conference-reported or early-phase data and therefore require confirmation in mature peer-reviewed studies and adequately powered randomized clinical trials.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1943424.abstract: Aberrant promoter DNA methylation represents an early molecular alteration in oral carcinogenesis and has emerged as a potential source of molecular biomarkers for oral cancer. Although RNF152 has been implicated in cancer-related molecular dysregulation, its promoter methylation and expression status have not previously been specifically investigated in oral premalignant lesions (OPML) or oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression were evaluated in paired tumor/lesion and matched adjacent normal tissues from 30 patients with OSCC and 30 patients with OPML, together with oral mucosal tissues from 15 healthy controls. Matched saliva and serum samples from the patient cohorts were also analyzed to evaluate RNF152 methylation as a potential liquid biopsy marker. Quantitative methylation-specific PCR (QMSP) and quantitative real-time PCR (QRT-PCR) were performed, and associations with clinicopathological characteristics, diagnostic performance, and the relationship between promoter methylation and gene expression were investigated. RNF152 promoter methylation was detected in 36.7% of OSCC tumors and 70.0% of OPML lesions, whereas no promoter methylation was identified in oral mucosal tissues from healthy controls. Promoter methylation was also detected in matched saliva and serum samples from both patient groups. Reduced RNF152 expression was observed in 33.3% of OSCC and 30.0% of OPML tissues. Methylation-associated RNF152 expression loss was identified in 13.3% of OSCC and 30.0% of OPML patients. Among methylation-positive cases, concomitant RNF152 expression loss was observed in 36.4% of patients with OSCC and 42.9% of patients with OPML. Continuous promoter methylation levels were not significantly correlated with tissue gene expression in either cohort. RNF152 promoter methylation demonstrated good discriminatory performance for distinguishing OPML from healthy controls (AUC = 0.867, p < 0.001), whereas its discriminatory performance for OSCC was statistically significant but more modest (AUC = 0.683, p = 0.047). This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression in oral premalignant lesions and oral squamous cell carcinoma. RNF152 promoter methylation showed greater diagnostic potential for OPML than for OSCC, whereas its performance in liquid biopsy specimens was limited. The incomplete concordance between promoter methylation and gene expression suggests that promoter methylation may contribute to RNF152 downregulation in a subset of cases but is not the sole determinant of its expression. These findings support further evaluation of RNF152 as a candidate component of multimarker epigenetic panels rather than as a standalone diagnostic biomarker. Validation in larger, independent cohorts is required to determine its clinical utility.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1943496.abstract: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS) and sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (SEF) represent a molecularly related spectrum of ultra-rare soft-tissue sarcomas characterised by recurrent FUS or EWSR1 rearrangements and frequent MUC4 expression. Despite sharing recurrent molecular alterations, their clinical behaviour differs markedly, positioning them at opposite ends of a biologically related spectrum with distinct clinical trajectories. This study aimed to characterise the clinicopathological features, molecular profiles, treatment approaches, and outcomes across this spectrum. We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients with LGFMS or SEF at a national EURACAN-designated sarcoma reference centre between 2013 and 2024. Clinicopathological characteristics, molecular findings, treatments, and outcomes were collected and analysed descriptively. Twenty patients were included: 11 (55%) LGFMS, six (30%) SEF and three (15%) hybrid tumours. MUC4 was positive in 13 cases (65%). Molecular analysis was informative in 19 patients (95%), with FUS or EWSR1 rearrangements in 16 (84%). FUS predominated (63%); EWSR1 rearrangements were confined to SEF (21%). Nineteen patients (95%) underwent curative-intent surgery. Local recurrence occurred in two (10%). Distant metastases developed in three (15%), all with SEF or hybrid histology. Metastatic progression was early (median 6 months), associated with high-risk histological features and EWSR1 rearrangement. SEF accounted for the only disease-related death; median overall survival was not reached, with 95% of patients alive at last follow-up. These findings highlight the divergent clinical behaviour across the LGFMS-SEF spectrum and support closer surveillance of high-risk tumours.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1943604.abstract: Alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) is a rare type of soft tissue sarcoma; ASPS originating in the central nervous system is even rarer. Previous literature has generally described it as having an indolent course with a favorable prognosis following surgical resection. This report presents a case of a 31-year-old woman with primary intracranial alveolar soft part sarcoma (PIASPS) that exhibited the opposite characteristics, demonstrating high invasiveness. The patient underwent gross total resection during the initial surgery, and postoperative histopathological examination and immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of PIASPS. Rapid local recurrence occurred just over two months after surgery; the tumor exhibited abnormally high proliferative activity, with an initial Ki-67 index of approximately 65%, which rose to 75% following recurrence. Molecular testing also revealed a complex mutation profile, including a BRAF p.V600E mutation, a TP53 p.D281E missense mutation, a TERT promoter mutation, an NBN truncating mutation, an HGF nonsense mutation, and an RPSAP52-HMGA2 fusion; these molecular events may have contributed to the rapid tumor recurrence, although their individual and combined effects require further functional validation. Following recurrence, the patient underwent a second surgery, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and concurrent oral anlotinib; however, the patient died two months following the completion of radiotherapy, with an overall survival of eight months. Characterized by rapid early postoperative recurrence, sustained high proliferative activity, and complex molecular features, this case challenges the traditional perception of PIASPS as an indolent tumor. This case suggests that a high Ki-67 index combined with molecular subtyping may help identify potentially aggressive subtypes; its value in guiding decisions regarding adjuvant therapy may be further explored in future studies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1943827.abstract: To systematically compare the key outcomes of endoscopic ultrasound-guided gastrojejunostomy (EUS-GJ) versus surgical gastrojejunostomy (SGJ) for the palliative treatment of malignant gastric outlet obstruction (MGOO). A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA statement. Databases including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from inception to December 2025 for comparative studies of EUS-GJ and SGJ in treating MGOO. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Eight studies involving 760 patients were included. Pooled analysis showed no significant differences between EUS-GJ and SGJ in technical success (RR = 0.98, P = 0.08), clinical success (RR = 1.08, P = 0.07), obstruction recurrence (RR = 0.48, P = 0.05), or re-intervention rates (RR = 1.48, P = 0.61). However, the EUS-GJ group demonstrated significant advantages, including a shorter length of hospital stay (MD= -3.57 days, P<0.001), a quicker time to first oral intake (MD= -2.88 days, P<0.001), a shorter time to resume chemotherapy (MD= -16.05 days, P<0.001), and a lower overall adverse events rate (RR = 0.44, P = 0.008). For the palliative management of MGOO, EUS-GJ showed no statistically significant difference in primary efficacy endpoints compared with SGJ, but it might be associated with faster recovery and improved safety. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261308316.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1944330.abstract: Intrathyroidal thymic carcinoma (ITTC) with neuroendocrine differentiation is rare, and evidence for definitive radiotherapy in nonsurgical patients remains limited. A 70-year-old woman with a 1-year history of a neck mass and hoarseness was diagnosed with ITTC with neuroendocrine differentiation based on histopathological, immunohistochemical, and imaging findings. After declining surgery and systemic chemotherapy, she received definitive radiotherapy: 60 Gy in 30 fractions to the planning target volume, followed by a sequential boost of 6 Gy in 3 fractions to the gross primary tumor and involved lymph nodes, for a cumulative dose of 66 Gy in 33 fractions. No grade ≥3 acute treatment-related toxicities occurred. At approximately 2 months after radiotherapy, the sum of target-lesion diameters decreased from 54 mm to 42 mm, a 22.2% reduction. With no new lesions or unequivocal progression of non-target disease, the overall response was classified as stable disease according to RECIST 1.1. This case documents early radiographic tumor reduction following definitive radiotherapy for ITTC, although longer follow-up is required to assess the durability of disease control and late toxicity.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1944586.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly used as bridging or downstaging therapy before liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but biomarkers of posttransplant recurrence in this setting are lacking. We evaluated the association between pretransplant plasma soluble programmed death-1 (sPD-1) and posttransplant outcomes after pretransplant ICI therapy. We enrolled 105 HCC patients undergoing LT, including 51 receiving ICIs and 54 without prior ICI exposure. Pretransplant plasma sPD-1 and sPD-L1 were measured by ELISA. The primary endpoint was 2-year recurrence-free survival (RFS). Associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. Pretransplant sPD-1 was higher in the ICI group than in the non-ICI group (P < 0.0001). Within the ICI-treated cohort, patients who experienced recurrence had higher sPD-1 than those who did not (P = 0.0002), whereas sPD-L1 did not differ. At an internally derived exploratory cutoff of 2073 pg/mL, high sPD-1 was associated with lower 2-year RFS (7.7% vs. 76.3%; log-rank P < 0.0001; HR, 4.42; 95% CI, 1.75-11.17). As a continuous variable, each doubling of pretransplant sPD-1 was associated with an increased risk of recurrence in the unadjusted analysis (HR = 1.51, 95% CI 1.25-1.82; P < 0.001). The association remained significant after adjustment for AFP, tumor number, and maximum tumor diameter (adjusted HR = 1.51, 95% CI 1.20-1.89; P < 0.001). Elevated pretransplant sPD-1 is independently associated with increased posttransplant recurrence risk in HCC patients receiving ICIs before LT. This association remained after adjustment for AFP and pretransplant tumor burden, and appeared distinct from MVI status, ACR occurrence, and the timing of blood sampling. sPD-1 may serve as a complementary biomarker for risk stratification, but external validation is required.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1944703.abstract: Genetic variation in DPYD can result in reduced fluoropyrimidine (FP) metabolism and increased risk of severe toxicity. This DPYD test implementation pilot aimed to establish a feasible workflow for DPYD ordering sample collection and FP dose modifications at the University of Florida Health Cancer Institute. Following education on the clinical utility of DPYD testing, a consensus was reached with the University of Florida Health gastrointestinal oncology clinic on an implementation workflow. Novel clinical decision support (CDS) tools were developed including pre- and post-test inline warnings in chemotherapy treatment plans, clickable dose modification buttons, and a pharmacist-facing alert upon medication verification. Primary outcomes were feasibility metrics including rates and timing of test ordering and sample collection, genotype turnaround time, and clinician response to CDS tools (e.g., FP dose modifications). DPYD was ordered for 201 patients between July 2024 and March 2026. Most (180/201) orders were placed prior to chemotherapy in FP-naïve individuals, and 85% (153/180) were also collected pretreatment. The average genotype turnaround time was 5.0 ± 2.7 days. Results were available prior to chemotherapy for 80.3% (114/142) of all patients who received a FP-containing regimen and for 93.2% (110/118) of those with DPYD ordered and collected pretreatment. Nine patients had a deleterious DPYD variant; all who newly initiated a FP-containing regimen received a 50% dose reduction. DPYD test implementation with customized CDS tools to support test ordering and FP prescribing in an academic oncology clinic is feasible, with the majority of results returning prior to chemotherapy. Integrating new and unique processes into already established workflows helps achieve timely test ordering and sample collection.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1945521.abstract: Background Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma (PPC) is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive extragonadal trophoblastic malignancy in males, with no established standard treatment. Cytotoxic chemotherapy alone generally yields limited therapeutic benefit, while the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains poorly defined. Case presentation Here, we report a 41-year-old man who presented with a six-month history of cough and was found to have a large right upper lobe pulmonary mass with multiple brain metastases. Histopathological examination revealed typical trophoblastic differentiation, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse positivity for HCG, CK7, GATA3, and SALL4, whereas TTF-1 and Napsin A were negative. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) was markedly elevated (> 10, 000 mIU/mL), and no gonadal primary lesion was identified, confirming the diagnosis of primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma. Intervention/outcome The patient underwent multimodal treatment including radiotherapy, EMA/CO chemotherapy, EMA/EP combined with sintilimab, and third-line therapy consisting of nab-paclitaxel, bevacizumab, and penpulimab. Despite intensive treatment, the disease progressed rapidly with new intracranial and systemic metastases. Throughout the disease course, serial β-HCG measurements closely paralleled radiographic findings and provided timely guidance for therapeutic decision-making. In addition, we reviewed previously reported metastatic male PPC cases and performed an exploratory survival analysis, which suggested that patients receiving ICI-based therapy tended to have longer overall survival than those treated without immunotherapy. Conclusion Although these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, this case highlights the highly aggressive nature of male PPC, emphasizes the diagnostic and monitoring value of dynamic β-HCG assessment, and supports further investigation of chemoimmunotherapy as a potential treatment strategy for this rare malignancy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1945549.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. Chemotherapy is central to the management of advanced or metastatic disease and is also used in perioperative settings, but outcomes vary substantially. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an inexpensive and readily available marker of systemic inflammation; its prognostic association in chemotherapy-treated CRC warrants focused evaluation. This study adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to July 15, 2025. Studies evaluating pretreatment NLR in relation to overall survival (OS) or a secondary progression- or recurrence-related time-to-event outcome, including progression-free survival (PFS), disease-free survival (DFS), or recurrence-free survival (RFS), in chemotherapy-treated CRC patients were eligible. Study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were independently conducted by two reviewers. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Thirty-eight studies (41 cohorts; 11,346 patients) were included. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.54-1.84; P < 0.0001) and poorer progression- or recurrence-related survival (HR = 1.61, 95% CI 1.43-1.81; P < 0.0001). The direction of association was generally consistent across exploratory subgroups defined by treatment category, age, geographic region, and NLR cut-off. Leave-one-out analyses did not identify a single study that changed the direction of either pooled association. Between-study heterogeneity and evidence of small-study effects warrant cautious interpretation. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer survival outcomes in chemotherapy-treated CRC. NLR may be a readily available prognostic biomarker, but heterogeneous populations, variable outcome definitions and cut-off values, inconsistent covariate adjustment, and possible small-study effects currently limit its use for clinical decision-making. Prospective validation and methodological standardization are required before routine application. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251136904.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1945631.abstract: Ewing sarcoma tumors are defined by chromosomal translocations fusing EWSR1 to ETS family genes, most commonly FLI1. The resulting EWS::FLI1 fusion oncoprotein drives tumorigenesis while simultaneously generating unique metabolic and molecular dependencies that may be exploited for Ewing sarcoma-specific therapies. Through analysis of the Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap, Broad Institute), we identified that Ewing sarcoma cell lines exhibit selective sensitivity to loss of genes regulating selenium metabolism compared to other cancer lineages. Ewing sarcoma cells are similarly sensitive to knockout of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), a selenoprotein that suppresses ferroptosis, a form of regulated, iron-dependent cell death characterized by the lethal accumulation of lipid peroxides. Using pharmacological inhibitors and targeted degraders of GPX4, as well as genetic knockout approaches, we demonstrate that Ewing sarcoma cells are selectively vulnerable to GPX4 loss or inhibition. We further identify ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) as a modulator of ferroptotic sensitivity in Ewing sarcoma, with FSP1 expression level serving as a determinant of the magnitude of ferroptotic response. Together, these findings establish ferroptosis as a targetable vulnerability in Ewing sarcoma, define GPX4 and FSP1 as key regulators of ferroptotic sensitivity in this disease, and provide a mechanistic rationale for therapeutic strategies targeting the ferroptosis defense axis in Ewing sarcoma tumors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1945673.abstract: Sonidegib, a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor, can induce clinical and imaging remission in locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (BCC). Residual deep tumor may persist after malignant dermoscopic and ultrasound features disappear. This case series assessed the utility and limitations of 20-30 MHz high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) for confirming complete imaging remission after sonidegib. Three patients with nodular BCC received sonidegib 200 mg daily (October 2024-May 2026). Two achieved complete imaging remission, defined as resolution of malignant imaging features with residual non-malignant hypoechoic areas allowed, and underwent surgical resection with histopathological correlation; the third declined surgery. Baseline ultrasound was unavailable, so findings were compared with the earliest 3-4-month follow-up. Response involved lesion shrinkage and loss of intratumoral blood flow. Serial imaging showed gradual resolution of hypoechoic nodules with vascularity on HFUS and blue-gray nests with arborizing vessels on dermoscopy, leaving avascular scar-like structures. Preoperative HFUS residual hypoechoic areas were correlated with histopathology, which showed chronic inflammatory infiltration (case 1) and mild dermal fibrosis (case 2), with no residual tumor. The third patient's malignant features regressed after six months. In this small case series, HFUS monitored deeper tissue changes after targeted therapy. In two histopathologically confirmed patients, complete imaging remission on HFUS plus dermoscopy corresponded to pathological complete response; however, given the small sample and histopathological confirmation in only two patients, this is a possible correspondence rather than evidence of true predictive capability. Post-treatment hypoechoic areas may reflect inflammation, fibrosis, or residual tumor, limiting specificity. Imaging-based complete response should be confirmed by biopsy or excision when feasible. Surgery remains the gold standard; non-surgical patients require close follow-up.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1946212.abstract: Older patients with lung cancer receiving thoracic radiotherapy have heterogeneous outcomes that are not fully captured by conventional clinical descriptors. We evaluated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted three-dimensional (3D) thoracic body-composition analysis of pretreatment radiotherapy simulation computed tomography (CT) could identify candidate body-composition imaging markers associated with overall survival. This exploratory retrospective single-institution study included 88 patients aged 70 years or older who received thoracic radiotherapy for lung cancer between 2019 and 2021. Thoracic skeletal muscle and intermuscular fat were segmented using an AI-assisted workflow followed by expert review and Hounsfield unit-constrained refinement. Twelve knowledge-informed candidate groups were evaluated using conventional Cox regression. After marker selection, the selected marker pair was assessed in continuous form using bootstrap optimism correction, repeated five-fold cross-validation, and Uno's C-index. Penalized and alternative model-family analysis were performed as exploratory sensitivity analysis. During follow-up, 28 deaths occurred. In an 18-case internal technical validation subset, the raw AI contours achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.930 for thoracic skeletal muscle and 0.723 for intermuscular fat. For Group 12, intermuscular adiposity index (IAI) and attenuation-weighted thoracic muscle fraction (TMF) were the variables that met the univariable screening criterion; the resulting two-marker model met the discrimination threshold without problematic collinearity. When modeled together, IAI values above the cohort median (hazard ratio [HR], 2.78; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.25-6.18; P = 0.012) and TMF values above the cohort median (HR, 3.77; 95% CI, 1.52-9.32; P = 0.004) were associated with poorer overall survival. In continuous form, the selected marker pair had an optimism-corrected Harrell's C-index of 0.751 (95% CI, 0.661-0.849), a mean repeated cross-validation C-index of 0.753 ± 0.112, and Uno's C-index of 0.737. These performance estimates were conditional on prior marker selection. AI-assisted analysis of routine radiotherapy simulation CT identified IAI and TMF as candidate body-composition imaging markers associated with overall survival in this clinically heterogeneous cohort. The findings are exploratory and require independent evaluation in larger, clinically characterized cohorts before clinical use.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1946625.abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy plus cytoreductive surgery represents the standard first-line therapy for ovarian cancer (OC), which yields robust early therapeutic responses in most patients. However, platinum resistance is a formidable clinical hurdle, and how macrophages mediate drug resistance within the OC tumor microenvironment remains poorly understood. We cultured SKOV3 OC cells and THP-1 monocytes, induced THP-1 differentiation into M2d tumor-associated macrophages. Stable apolipoprotein E (ApoE) -overexpressing SKOV3 cell lines were constructed via lentiviral transfection and puromycin screening. We established nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models with mixed tumor cells and M2d macrophages, administered cisplatin treatment and collected tumor tissues after sacrifice by cervical dislocation. RNA was extracted from tumor samples to conduct RT-qPCR for gene expression detection. Tumor tissue sections were prepared for HE staining, TUNEL apoptosis staining, and Western blot analysis to detect ApoE and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway protein expression. Using nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models, we demonstrated that M2d-type tumor-associated macrophages (M2d TAMs) promote platinum resistance and elevate tumoral ApoE levels. In OC xenografts with stable ApoE overexpression, cisplatin-induced apoptosis was profoundly repressed, resulting in reduced cisplatin sensitivity, while this inhibitory effect was not observed in the empty vector control group. Mechanistically, ApoE activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade to counteract cisplatin cytotoxicity by suppressing cell death and sustaining pro-survival signals. Overall, this study reveals that M2d TAMs induce platinum resistance in OC cells via exosomes carrying ApoE.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1946625.title: Regulatory mechanism of M2d tumor-associated macrophage-derived exosomal apolipoprotein E on platinum resistance in ovarian cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1947593.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity and signaling redundancy limit the efficacy of monospecific antibody therapies in solid malignancies. Here we used our platform of glyco-humanized polyclonal antibodies (GH-pAb), to investigate whether targeting multiple tumor-associated antigens provides integrated anti-tumor activity. GH-pAb (hereinafter XON7) were generated by immunization of double-knockout pigs with human tumor cells. Antigen specificity of XON7 was assessed using a human proteome array and validated by ELISA. Anti-tumor mechanisms were evaluated in vitro on 2D or 3D-cultures. Efficacy was tested in vivo in cell or patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX), in chicken chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model, and in orthotopic/metastatic triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) models. XON7 demonstrated tumor-restricted binding across tissue microarrays without detectable staining in matched normal tissues. Mechanistically, XON7 induced potent cytotoxicity across a wide tumor panel through complement activation, apoptosis, and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis. Proteome profiling identified predominant reactivities against solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), annexin A2 (ANXA2), and cytoskeleton-associated protein 4 (CKAP4), all broadly expressed tumor-associated surface proteins. Immunodepletion experiments revealed that concurrent targeting of these three targets was required to maintain the full anti-proliferative activity of XON7, supporting a multitarget-dependent mechanism. XON7 also induced released of high-mobility group protein box 1 (HMGB1), a hallmark of immunogenic cell death. In vivo, XON7 inhibited tumor growth in CDX and PDX models, and markedly reduced metastatic dissemination in orthotopic and intravenous TNBC models. In a CAM model, XON7 synergized with PD-1 blockade, enhancing tumor control and promoting macrophage polarization toward a M1 phenotype. By simultaneously engaging non-redundant tumor pathways and reshaping the tumor microenvironment, XON7 may overcome key resistance mechanisms of solid tumors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1947939.abstract: As research in molecular biology continues to advance, the classification of endometrial cancer has gradually shifted from traditional histology toward risk stratification based on the integration of molecular subtyping with clinicopathologic factors. Molecular subtyping has not only transformed our understanding of the biological heterogeneity of endometrial cancer but also provided new evidence for prognostic assessment and treatment selection. However, the maturity of clinical evidence and the translational therapeutic value vary across molecular subtypes. This review systematically summarizes the molecular characteristics and clinical significance of the POLE ultramutated(POLE-mut)subtype, mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) subtype, p53 abnormal (p53-abn) subtype, and no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype, with a focus on evaluating whether different molecular features can be further translated from risk stratification into specific treatment decisions. Centering on key issues such as de-escalated therapy for the POLE-mut subtype, the predictive value of immunotherapy for the dMMR subtype, intensified therapy for the p53-abn subtype, and further risk stratification of the NSMP subtype, this review analyzes the clinical basis and limitations of existing evidence and further discusses the challenges that tumors with multiple molecular features pose for classification and treatment decision making. Building on this, the paper compares how major international guidelines integrate molecular information with clinical and pathologic factors and analyzes real world implementation barriers such as testing standardization, result interpretation, and healthcare accessibility. Finally, it outlines the potential value of emerging technologies, including liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence, and multiomics, in dynamic risk assessment and precision therapy. This review aims to trace the continuum of evidence from molecular discovery to clinical action, clarifying which clinical decisions can be supported by existing molecular markers and identifying questions that current evidence cannot yet answer, thereby providing guidance for the precise application and clinical translation of molecular subtyping in endometrial cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1947958.abstract: Obesity increases the risk and progression of at least 13 types of cancer. Although the epidemiologic links between excess adiposity and these cancers are well documented, the biological mechanisms linking obesity to carcinogenesis and tumor progression remain incompletely understood. White adipose tissue in obesity is a source of inflammatory and immunosuppressive signals that act systemically, driving metabolic, inflammatory, and immune dysfunction whose consequences differ across tumor types. As adipose tissue expands and adipocytes enlarge, the blood supply becomes inadequate, leading to hypoxia, fibrosis, lipolytic stress, macrophage recruitment, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These obesity-induced perturbations generate endocrine, cytokine, lipid, and metabolic signals that act systemically, within the tumor microenvironment (TME), and/or cell-intrinsically to activate oncogenic and tumor-promoting pathways. The same signals reshape innate and adaptive immunity, promoting tumor-permissive macrophage states and myeloid-derived suppressor cell expansion, while the effector arms weaken as antigen presentation, natural killer cell and T cell function all decline. This review synthesizes current evidence linking obesity-associated inflammation and immune dysregulation to cancer initiation, progression, and treatment responses across multiple obesity-related cancers. Emphasis is placed on adipose tissue inflammation, myeloid cell biology, T cell immunometabolism, endocrine-inflammatory crosstalk, and the relationship between obesity and immunotherapy. Finally, we discuss translational opportunities for preventing or intercepting obesity-related cancers, including weight loss achieved through lifestyle, surgical, or pharmacologic approaches, with an emphasis on GLP-1 receptor agonists given their substantial efficacy, rapid clinical uptake, and potential to reshape obesity-related cancer prevention and survivorship strategies. Defining the metabolic, immune, and inflammatory phenotypes that drive obesity-associated cancer risk and progression will be essential for developing more precise, mechanism-based strategies for prevention, treatment, and survivorship care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948193.abstract: This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261289724.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948199.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a molecularly heterogeneous disease. This study aims to explore whether endocytosis pathway-associated genes and immune checkpoint-related features were linked to GC subtypes and prognosis. Public transcriptomic datasets from TCGA and GEO were analyzed. ssGSEA was applied to predefined endocytosis-related gene sets, and NMF was used to identify molecular subtypes. Survival, tumor microenvironment features, tumor mutation burden, microsatellite instability, and differentially expressed genes were evaluated. A three-gene prognostic model was developed and assessed through retrospective internal and external validation across public cohorts for prognostic association only. Two endocytosis-related subtypes were identified. The Group 1 subtype showed higher pathway activity, more immunosuppressive microenvironmental features, higher expression of selected immune checkpoint-related markers, and poorer survival. The Group 2 subtype showed lower pathway activity and more favorable outcomes. A three-gene signature (NRP1, SERPINE1, and MISP3) stratified patients into higher-risk and lower-risk groups across retrospective cohorts. Higher-risk cases were associated with worse overall survival and enrichment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition- and immune evasion-related pathways. This retrospective cross-cohort validation suggests that the prognostic signal was not restricted to a single dataset, but it does not demonstrate prospective clinical validity, analytical validity, or readiness for clinical implementation. Endocytosis-related molecular patterns may be associated with distinct biological and prognostic features in GC. The identified subtypes and prognostic signature should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings that warrant further prospective, functional, and assay-level validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948429.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is incorporated into the long-term integrative management of advanced prostate cancer in China, but evidence linking treatment duration with survival remains limited. Because treatment duration accumulates during follow-up, classifying patients by their final recorded treatment duration can misallocate pre-threshold observation time and bias survival comparisons. We evaluated the association between cumulative continuous TCM treatment exceeding 6 months and all-cause mortality in a single-center retrospective cohort of 242 patients with metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma at diagnosis who received continuous TCM from diagnosis. Follow-up continued through May 1, 2024. Treatment exceeding 6 months was modeled as a time-dependent exposure in Multivariable Cox regression, with sensitivity analyses addressing an alternative threshold, disease-severity adjustment, influential observations, and loss to follow-up. During follow-up, 147 deaths occurred. Median overall survival was 53.0 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 44.0-61.0), with 3- and 5-year survival rates of 64.0% and 43.4%, respectively. Cumulative continuous TCM treatment exceeding 6 months was associated with a lower average hazard of all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.269; 95% CI, 0.186-0.389; P < 0.001). The association attenuated over time: adjusted HRs at 1, 2, 3, and 5 years were 0.098, 0.192, 0.286, and 0.471, respectively. Sensitivity analyses yielded estimates in the same direction. These findings define a duration-survival association among TCM users and support prospective, multicenter evaluation using detailed longitudinal treatment records.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948667.abstract: Bone disease is a common manifestation of multiple myeloma. Although anti-resorptive therapy is recommended by guidelines, implementation can be variable. We sought to evaluate practice patterns for myeloma bone disease management and to identify opportunities for harmonization. An online survey was distributed to clinicians who see patients with multiple myeloma at medical centers affiliated with the Big Ten Cancer Research Consortium. Anonymous responses were collected regarding self-reported demographics, as well as practice patterns regarding preferred antiresorptive agent, dosing, duration of therapy, therapy modifications, vitamin and mineral supplementation, dental restrictions, and management at relapse. A total of 100 responses were collected from 11 different academic institutions and their community-affiliated sites. Respondents were predominantly physicians (74%) working in an academic setting (77%), with variable time practicing independently and number of myeloma patients seen per year. Most respondents (89%) reported using zoledronic acid as the preferred agent, with every 4 weeks as the most common frequency (for zoledronic acid 70%, denosumab 64%), with most administering therapy for 2 years (72%). Most clinical scenarios did not affect anti-resorptive choice at diagnosis, except for severe renal insufficiency. Dental recommendations were heterogeneous. There was low utilization of biomarkers to guide management decisions. Our survey suggests that at the time of diagnosis, most clinicians administer appropriate supportive care for myeloma bone disease. Further study is needed to help unify practice patterns in the relapsed setting, when dental care is suboptimal, and when it is appropriate to tailor such therapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948751.abstract: Anemia represents a frequent and clinically burdensome complication in patients with primary lung cancer receiving platinum-based regimens, yet robust risk stratification tools that integrate multidimensional clinical data and undergo external validation remain scarce. This multicenter study sought to develop and externally validate a machine learning-based predictive model for CIA in this population. A total of 3,434 patients with primary lung cancer were retrospectively enrolled from two geographically distinct institutions, with 3,097 assigned to the training/internal validation set (7:3 split) and 337 retained as an independent external validation set. Variables with missing rates exceeding 30% were excluded, and remaining missing data were imputed using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE). Thirteen candidate predictors were preselected via univariate screening and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Nine machine learning algorithms were developed and comparatively evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The primary outcome was defined as hemoglobin levels < 100 g/L (CTCAE Grade ≥ 2) recorded during the first two cycles of chemotherapy. Among the nine candidate models, LightGBM achieved the highest discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.871 (95% CI: 0.852-0.891) in the training set, 0.797 (95% CI: 0.763-0.831) in internal validation, and 0.684 (95% CI: 0.626-0.742) in the external validation set derived from Linfen Central Hospital. Calibration and decision curve analyses consistently demonstrated superior agreement and net clinical benefit for LightGBM across all three datasets. SHAP-based interpretation identified lymphocyte count, D-dimer, alanine aminotransferase, total bilirubin, sex, and albumin as the six most influential predictors, with D-dimer, female sex, and outpatient admission positively associated with anemia risk, whereas lymphocyte count, liver function indices, and albumin showed inverse associations. The LightGBM-based model developed herein demonstrates acceptable and moderate predictive performance, satisfactory calibration, and potential clinical utility across geographically diverse populations, offering a preliminary risk-stratification tool for early identification of lung cancer patients at elevated anemia risk prior to chemotherapy initiation. However, given the modest external validation performance, cautious interpretation and further refinement are warranted before widespread clinical deployment.
