doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948772.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are distinctive toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and have been reported to correlate with clinical outcomes in several cancers. However, whether this association also exists in patients with esophageal cancer (EC) receiving ICIs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between irAEs and clinical outcomes in this population. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the association between irAEs and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for PFS and OS, whereas odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were pooled for ORR and DCR using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and immortal-time bias were also assessed. 14 studies involving 1, 546 patients were included. The occurrence of irAEs was associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.63), OS (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.46-0.64), ORR (OR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.58-10.12), and DCR (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 2.40-6.20). The 95% PIs were 0.16-1.24, 0.44-0.66, 0.19-82.57, and 1.42-10.44 for PFS, OS, ORR, and DCR, respectively, crossing the null value for PFS and ORR. Subgroup estimates were generally similar in direction but remained exploratory. No eligible survival estimates using landmark or time-varying approaches were available for the comparison between patients with and without irAEs. In patients with EC receiving ICIs, the occurrence of irAEs may be a prognostic marker of favorable outcomes. However, wide PIs for PFS and ORR indicate that these associations may vary across future studies and immortal time bias may overestimate survival associations. This observational evidence derives mainly from East Asian patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is primarily applicable to these patients. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and require prospective validation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261346294.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1948986.abstract: Introduction Patients with advanced solid tumors and severe hepatic dysfunction have limited systemic therapy options due to impaired drug metabolism and increased toxicity risks. This population is often excluded from clinical trials, leaving a critical treatment gap. This study evaluates the feasibility, safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of S-1, an oral prodrug of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), plus cisplatin in these patients. Methods Between September 2016 and November 2023, 61 patients were enrolled into four cohorts based on hepatic function per NCI-ODWG criteria: normal (Cohort 1), mild (Cohort 2), moderate (Cohort 3), and severe dysfunction (Cohort 4). Primary endpoints were safety and 5-fluorouracil pharmacokinetics; secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR) and 3-month clinical benefit rate (3M-CBR). Results On Cycle 1 day 15, patients with severe hepatic dysfunction (Cohort 4) had lower 5-FU C max and longer T max than those with normal hepatic function (Cohort 1) (p<0.05), though 5-FU AUC remained comparable across cohorts. Safety in Cohort 4 were similar to those in Cohorts 1–3. No grade 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred. In Cohort 4, 22.2% achieved a partial response, 40.7% derived clinical benefit, and 22.2% maintained progression-free survival ≥6 months, providing preliminary evidence of clinical activity in this population. Conclusion Patients with severe hepatic dysfunction had similar 5-FU AUC and toxicities to those with less severe hepatic dysfunction, and preliminary evidence of clinical activity was observed with cisplatin + S-1. These findings provide prospective preliminary evidence that this combination may be feasible in selected patients with severe hepatic dysfunction, a population frequently excluded from clinical trials. Larger studies are needed to further define its safety, pharmacokinetics, and clinical activity in this population. (Clinical Trial Registration: NCT03519074. Retrospectively registered 08 May 2018).

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1949600.abstract: With accumulating evidence confirming that postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy improves survival outcomes in patients with left-sided breast cancer, the long-term cardiotoxicity risks associated with radiotherapy have attracted widespread attention. The deep inspiration breath hold (DIBH) technique increases the distance between the heart and the breast target, effectively reducing radiation dose to the heart and coronary arteries. However, the resource-intensive nature of DIBH and substantial heterogeneity in therapeutic benefits among patients pose a major clinical challenge: how to accurately and efficiently identify patients suitable for DIBH. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding DIBH patient selection, and integrates available strategies with clinical workflows to construct a three-tiered decision-making framework encompassing feasibility assessment, indication evaluation, and clinical benefit assessment. Given the existing gaps in high-level prospective clinical evidence, three primary research directions are proposed: (1) conducting large-scale multi-center prospective cohort studies to validate the generalizability and clinical practicality of selection strategies; (2) developing an individualized normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model integrating multi-dimensional risk factors to guide precise decision-making; and (3) implementing prospective clinical trials of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted selection platforms to accelerate the clinical translation of intelligent selection tools. This review synthesizes current evidence on DIBH patient selection, constructs a hierarchical decision framework to provide a reference for clinical practice, and delineates directions for future research.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1949729.abstract: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the oral mucosa classified as a potentially malignant oral disease. However, its risk of malignant transformation remains controversial because of heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and methodologies across studies. To assess the malignant transformation rate of non-dysplastic OLP through a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal studies. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261295782). PubMed, Embase, and grey literature were searched. Longitudinal observational studies including patients with histopathologically diagnosed OLP, without epithelial dysplasia at diagnosis, and reporting malignant transformation rates were included. The review focused specifically on longitudinal evidence evaluating malignant transformation in patients meeting these eligibility criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. Twenty-four studies, comprising 13, 143 patients and 230 cases of malignant transformation, were included. The pooled malignant transformation rate was 1.56% (95% CI: 1.14-2.12%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 74.8%). Subgroup analyses showed no significant differences according to study design, geographic region, or diagnostic criteria. Meta-regression identified the male-to-female ratio as a significant moderator, while sample size and follow-up duration had no significant influence. No evidence of publication bias was observed. The malignant transformation rate of OLP was very low, with a pooled estimate of 1.56%, supporting continued surveillance. Future research should focus on standardized diagnostic approaches and reliable risk stratification models to improve understanding of malignant transformation in OLP and ensure better population representation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261295782, identifier CRD420261295782.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1949729.title: Malignant potential of oral lichen planus without epithelial dysplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1949803.abstract: Background Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common in patients with glioblastoma, but their association with progression-free survival (PFS) remains incompletely characterized in molecularly defined populations. We examined these associations in patients with IDH-wild-type glioblastoma. Methods This single-center observational study included 64 adults with newly diagnosed IDH-wild-type glioblastoma who completed the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) at a median of 35 days after resection (range, 30–38 days), before postoperative adjuvant therapy. Scores ≥10 defined positive screens. Separate multivariable Cox models estimated associations with PFS, adjusting for age, Karnofsky Performance Status, and gross-total resection. An independent exploratory analysis compared neurotransmitter- and stress-related receptor expression in paired primary and recurrent tumors from 105 patients annotated as having IDH-wild-type glioblastoma in the Glioma Longitudinal Analysis Consortium (GLASS). Results Compared with scores below the respective screening thresholds, greater anxiety symptom burden [GAD-7 score ≥10; adjusted hazard ratio 1.92, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08–3.42] and greater depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 score ≥10; adjusted hazard ratio 4.22, 95% CI 1.72–10.35) were associated with shorter PFS. Supportive continuous-score analyses showed consistent associations. In the independent GLASS cohort, recurrent tumors showed higher adrenergic, serotonergic, dopaminergic, and GABAergic receptor-family scores, higher CRHR1 expression, and lower AVPR1A expression. Conclusion Greater postoperative anxiety and depressive symptom burden was associated with shorter PFS in IDH-wild-type glioblastoma. Prospective studies with repeated symptom assessments, more complete clinical data, and matched molecular sampling are needed to evaluate these observational associations and the separate, hypothesis-generating molecular findings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1949803.title: Association of postoperative anxiety and depressive symptom severity with progression-free survival in IDH-wild-type glioblastoma

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1950737.abstract: Cancer treatment-related oral mucositis (OM) is one of the most common adverse effects of cancer treatment and can substantially impair patients' quality of life. Its effective management depends heavily on patients' continuous self-management. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the intervention components, delivery modes, and existing limitations of self-management support interventions, thereby providing evidence to inform the optimization of intervention strategies. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. Seven databases, including PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and WanFang, were searched from inception to May 10, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were charted using a standardized form and summarized using descriptive numerical and content analyses. A total of 7,132 records were identified, and 16 studies were ultimately included, comprising 9 quasi-experimental studies, 6 randomized controlled trials, and 1 mixed-methods study. The interventions were primarily hospital-based and nurse-led, with some incorporating digital tools or written materials. Reported outcomes generally included OM-related clinical outcomes, quality of life, self-management-related outcomes, and nutritional status, although the direction and magnitude of findings varied across studies. Existing studies have reported potential improvements in OM-related and self-management-related outcomes following self-management support interventions. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of heterogeneity in study designs, intervention components, and outcome measures, together with the absence of critical appraisal. Further well-designed studies using standardized outcome measures are needed to strengthen the evidence base.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1951000.abstract: Hepatic portal venous gas (HPVG) is an uncommon radiological sign whose clinical importance depends on the underlying disorder and the patient’s physiological state. Only two cases of HPVG following transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) have been reported. We describe a rapidly fatal episode in a 71-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and biopsy-confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma. Selective TACE involved lobaplatin infusion, followed by 10 mL of an iodized oil-raltitrexed emulsion and 1 mL of epirubicin-loaded drug-eluting microspheres. Constipation and abdominal distension developed approximately 21 h after TACE. Severe abdominal pain and vomiting followed at 37 h. Emergency CT at approximately 38 h showed peripheral branching HPVG, bowel dilatation, and intraluminal fluid. At approximately 39 h, the patient developed impaired consciousness, hypotension, and bradycardia. He died despite resuscitative treatment approximately 40 h after TACE. Lactate, a repeat leukocyte count, blood cultures, and other microbiological samples were not obtained after the acute deterioration. Sepsis therefore remained an unconfirmed possible mechanism. The combined embolization regimen represents a procedural exposure, not a proven cause. Progressive abdominal symptoms after TACE should prompt urgent evaluation for bowel injury, infection, biliary complications, and circulatory deterioration.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1951000.title: Case Report: Rapidly fatal hepatic portal venous gas following transarterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1951068.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer (MBC) still remains incurable after advances in the field of systemic therapy. Sacituzumab govitecan (SG) is an antibody-drug conjugate that works against TROP-2 and clinical studies have shown its effectiveness in patients who have received multiple lines of treatment prior to its administration. However, the number of real-world studies is still limited in this field. The present study was performed retrospectively in one center and aimed at evaluating 48 women with MBC treated with SG in the period of December 2022 until March 2024. Clinical characteristics, toxicity of the treatment (CTCAE v5.0), pathology of progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were studied. The median age of the patients was 50.5 years, with 68.8% of them having triple-negative breast cancer and 31.2% having positive hormone receptors and negative HER2. The percentage of the women having metastases in their central nervous system is 31.2%. Three was the median number of treatment lines undertaken prior to the trial. According to the data obtained in the course of the study, median PFS and OS are equal to 3.9 and 9.85 months respectively. At the same time, the percentage of the patients experiencing Grade 3-4 side effects is equal to 39.6%, with neutropenia being the most characteristic for SG use. Dose adjustments were made for 41.7% of the patients and 12.5% had to stop treatment. Overall, SG demonstrated clinical activity in this real-world cohort, although Grade 3-4 adverse events and treatment modifications were relatively frequent, highlighting the importance of close monitoring and supportive care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1951255.abstract: Early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a clinically and biologically distinct subtype of gastric cancer characterized by unique molecular features. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify EOGC-associated hub genes using an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning framework. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between EOGC and late-onset gastric cancer (LOGC) were analyzed using functional enrichment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and random forest algorithms. Immune infiltration was characterized using CIBERSORT. Candidate hub genes were validated using an independent external cohort, clinical specimens, single-cell transcriptomic datasets, and in vitro functional assays. A five-gene logistic regression model was established and evaluated using ROC-AUC, calibration analysis, and bootstrap resampling. Transcriptomic analysis identified 227 DEGs, and WGCNA identified seven co-expression modules, with the green module showing the strongest association with EOGC. Machine learning identified five hub genes: CCR7, CD1D, PTGER2, PIK3CG, and EBI3. The combined model showed good discriminatory performance in the training, internal validation, and independent external validation cohorts (AUC = 0.909, 0.859, and 0.802, respectively). Bootstrap resampling yielded AUC estimates of 0.908, 0.852, and 0.789, respectively, supporting model stability. All five genes showed higher expression in EOGC and were validated at the mRNA and protein levels. Immune profiling and single-cell analysis revealed an immune-associated molecular phenotype and distinct expression patterns across immune cell subsets. Silencing the hub genes suppressed gastric cancer cell proliferation and migration in vitro. We identified five EOGC-associated hub genes and revealed an immune-associated molecular landscape. The five-gene model represents an EOGC-associated molecular signature distinguishing EOGC from LOGC rather than a stand-alone clinical diagnostic tool. These findings provide insights into the molecular and immune biology of EOGC and may inform future studies of molecular stratification and treatment-related outcomes.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1951947.abstract: Urinary toxicities are common following prostate radiotherapy and can impair quality of life. New biomarkers are needed that can predict the risk of urinary toxicity following MRI guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MR-SBRT) to assist with selection of the most appropriate radiotherapy treatment approach. We aimed to identify urine miRNA biomarkers of radiation-induced urinary toxicities. Ten patients undergoing MR-SBRT were enrolled on a prospective biorepository protocol and urine specimens were collected before, at the final fraction and 2-4 months following radiotherapy. RNA was isolated and microRNA sequencing was performed followed by qPCR for confirmation of microRNA expression changes. Differences in microRNA expression were assessed with regard to timepoint, cancer risk category and urinary toxicity. Both sequencing and qPCR showed that expressions of miR-26a-5p and miR-95-3p decrease during MR-SBRT and increase during early follow up. miR-204-3p and miR-192-5p changed differently in patients with and without urinary radiation toxicity. Expression of miR-375-3p was lower in patients with higher risk category (NCCN unfavorable intermediate to high risk or recurrent/metastatic) at all timepoints and decreased during and after MR-SBRT, especially in patients with a lower risk category (NCCN low to favorable intermediate risk) of prostate cancer. Urine microRNA analysis is feasible and may identify biomarkers linked to radiation-induced urinary toxicity and prostate cancer severity. The findings of this pilot study are limited by the sample size and should be prospectively validated.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1952158.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by VHL-HIF pathway alterations, lipid remodeling, abnormal angiogenesis, and marked immune heterogeneity. These features create a highly vascular yet unevenly perfused microenvironment in which vascular dysfunction, hypoxia, stromal barriers, and myeloid clearance influence whether cell death becomes immunologically productive. Although immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and HIF-2α inhibitors have improved outcomes, primary and acquired resistance and discordant responses among lesions remain common. Bulk PD-L1 expression, immune-cell abundance, and cell-death-related transcript signatures do not resolve this heterogeneity. Following current nomenclature, regulated cell death (RCD) is the mechanistically preferred umbrella term; we retain programmed cell death (PCD) in the conceptual label because it remains widely used in the RCC oncology literature, while requiring RCD execution-level evidence for mechanistic claims. Single-cell and spatial multi-omics studies increasingly show that the identity of the dying cell, execution of the death program, accessibility of death-derived material, and the recipient immune cells operate as a coupled local system. We define a PCD-associated immune niche as a spatial tissue state in which representative, non-exclusive immune-routing axes can direct tumor-cell death toward cDC1-mediated cross-presentation and adaptive antitumor immunity, TAM-dominant efferocytosis and tissue repair, or intermediate mixed states. This Review focuses predominantly on ccRCC, evaluates ferroptosis, apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, and PANoptosis, and briefly considers emerging RCD modalities for which ccRCC evidence is less mature. We further propose composite spatial biomarkers and mechanism-guided combinations that link cellular source, execution evidence, immune routing, and clinical outcome.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1952158.title: Spatial architecture shapes programmed cell death-associated immune niches and therapeutic resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1953570.abstract: Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT) is the standard consolidation therapy for multiple myeloma (MM), but its widespread implementation is constrained by the high cost and limited availability of conventional laminar airflow rooms. The air-flow bed, a single-bed unit equipped with high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filtration providing class 100 (ISO class 5) air quality, represents a more accessible and cost-effective alternative. In this retrospective cohort study, we compared the efficacy, safety, and costs of ASCT performed in air-flow beds (Group A, n=91) versus conventional laminar airflow rooms (Group B, n=60) in 151 MM patients treated between 2022 and 2026. Multivariable regression models were adjusted for potential confounders. Sepsis was analyzed descriptively because of the small number of events. Platelet transfusion requirements were analyzed using negative binomial regression. Engraftment outcomes were comparable between groups. Group A showed significantly lower rates of mucositis, diarrhea, and nausea/vomiting, and no sepsis events occurred in Group A compared with four cases (6.7%) in Group B. Pathogen detection rate was lower in Group A than in Group B (5.5% vs. 15.0%, P = 0.050). In negative binomial regression, air-flow bed use was independently associated with a lower number of platelet transfusion units (IRR = 0.50, P<0.001). Higher CD34+ cell dose was also independently associated with fewer platelet transfusions (IRR = 0.94 per 1×106/kg increase, P = 0.003). Sepsis occurred exclusively in Group B (4/60, 6.7% vs. 0/91, 0%). With only four events and complete separation between groups, multivariable logistic regression was not statistically reliable. This finding is therefore reported descriptively and no adjusted effect estimate is presented. Median total costs were significantly lower in Group A (¥121,738 [approximately $16,908] vs. ¥137,506 [approximately $19,098], P = 0.0002). No transplant-related mortality occurred in Group A, whereas one patient (1.7%) in Group B died. These findings suggest that air-flow beds may represent a safe, effective, and economically viable alternative to conventional laminar airflow rooms for ASCT in MM. Because protective environment and transplant era were strongly intertwined, these observational associations should be interpreted with caution and regarded as hypothesis-generating. Prospective validation in randomized controlled trials is warranted to confirm these observations.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1953767.abstract: In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), EGFR and HER2 mutations are generally considered mutually exclusive events, with a co-occurrence probability estimated to be less than 1%. Patients with either EGFR or HER2 mutations tend to exhibit low PD-L1 expression levels. The simultaneous presence of both EGFR and HER2 mutations accompanied by high PD-L1 expression is exceedingly rare. This study reports a female patient who was admitted to the hospital after a routine physical examination revealed a right lung nodule and was diagnosed with "right lung adenocarcinoma (cT2aN2aM1c1, IVA; EGFR 21 L858R mutation; HER2 exon 8 mutation; PD-L1 TPS 60%)." The patient was immediately started on first-line third-generation EGFR-targeted therapy (Furmonertinib), but disease progression occurred after just 4.4 months (malignant pleural effusion and pericardial effusion). As the patient refused repeat biopsy, treatment with an ADC drug (Trastuzumab rezetecan) was initiated. Disease control was achieved after only one cycle of treatment, and the regimen was continued thereafter. The progression-free survival has exceeded 5.3 months, and at the time of writing this report, the disease remained well-controlled. This paper presents the first report of this rare and therapeutically challenging combination of molecular pathological features-concurrent EGFR and HER2 mutations with high PD-L1 expression in an NSCLC patient. When standard first-line third-generation EGFR-TKIs proved ineffective, the successful use of an anti-HER2 ADC drug to control the tumor demonstrates its potential clinical value. However, whether all patients initially presenting with this pathological molecular subtype will achieve consistent efficacy remains to be further investigated.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954104.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) provide durable tumor control in some patients, but resistance can develop through tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental mechanisms. This narrative review examines the metabolic and immune conditions under which ferroptosis may enhance ICI responsiveness or resensitize selected ICI-refractory tumors. Radiotherapy (RT) increases oxidizable phospholipids and can repress SLC7A11, the light-chain component of system xc-. ICI-activated CD8+ T cells provide convergent interferon-γ signaling. Tumors can resist this pressure through GPX4, FSP1-CoQ10, mitochondrial DHODH, NRF2-dependent programs, and iron-export pathways. Recent preclinical studies have tested RT with ferroptosis-directed interventions and ICIs. These studies include functional evidence of ferroptosis dependence in radioresistant lung cancer and resensitization of LKB1-deficient, primarily ICI-refractory tumors. The findings support a preclinical rationale for combination therapy, although their causal strength varies. Reversal of clinically defined acquired ICI resistance remains unestablished, and the clinical RT-ICI studies reviewed here did not measure ferroptosis in patients. The immune effects also vary by cell type. Tumor-cell ferroptosis may support immunity, whereas lipid peroxidation in CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, or polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells can impair antitumor responses. Translation will require functional validation, cell-resolved biomarkers, achievable drug exposures, and evaluation of RT dose, fractionation, and sequence alongside normal-tissue and immune-cell safety.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954263.abstract: Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is a first-line chemotherapeutic agent that achieves a complete remission rate above 90% in newly diagnosed acute promyelocytic leukemia, with indications expanding to multiple hematological malignancies and solid tumors. However, dose-dependent cardiotoxicity-manifesting as acute QTc prolongation and malignant arrhythmia, as well as chronic myocardial hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis and progressive heart failure-remains a critical clinical barrier that limits its therapeutic window, and no approved targeted cardioprotective regimens are currently available in clinical practice. This narrative Mini Review proposes an integrated mechanistic framework centered on the oxidative stress-inflammation positive feedback loop, which complements the conventional view of two independent pathogenic pathways. In this framework, ATO-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired Nrf2 antioxidant defense initiate oxidative stress as the upstream trigger; ROS subsequently drives inflammatory activation via NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome pathways, while sustained inflammation in turn aggravates oxidative damage by suppressing Nrf2 activity and disrupting mitochondrial homeostasis. This proposed self-amplifying loop exhibits spatiotemporal heterogeneity. It appears incompletely established in acute electrophysiological injury, but may serve as a potential mechanistic contributor to chronic structural remodeling. Based on this framework, this work summarizes dual-target cardioprotective strategies that preserve ATO's anti-tumor efficacy, and evaluates translational biomarkers for early risk stratification. Collectively, this review provides a mechanistic foundation for precision cardioprotection and clinical safety optimization of ATO-based chemotherapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954263.title: Arsenic trioxide-induced cardiotoxicity: insights into the oxidative stress-inflammation positive feedback loop, translational biomarkers and targeted cardioprotective strategies- a narrative review.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954382.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common malignant tumor in the head and neck region. In locally advanced patients, neoadjuvant chemotherapy centered on cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil often leads to primary/acquired resistance, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 50%. Tumor microenvironment (TME) immunosuppressive remodeling is the core cause of chemotherapy failure. Adipokines secreted by cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) are the key mediators that link metabolic disorders, immune polarization and chemotherapy resistance. The adipokines leptin, adiponectin, chemerin, resistin, and GDF15 signal through pathways such as JAK2/STAT3, PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and PPARγ to bidirectionally regulate the polarization phenotypes of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), CD4+/CD8+ T cells, and NK cells. Pro-cancer adipokines induce M2-type TAMs, MDSCs expansion, Th2/Th17 polarization, and effector T cell exhaustion, constructing an immunosuppressive microenvironment, upregulating DNA damage repair, drug efflux, and anti-apoptotic genes, and reducing cisplatin/5-FU chemosensitivity. The tumor-suppressive adipokine adiponectin promotes M1 macrophage and CD8+ effector T cell infiltration, reverses immunosuppression, and sensitizes chemotherapy. This article systematically reviews the origin and classification of adipokines, the polarization patterns of immune cells in the OSCC microenvironment, the molecular pathways by which various adipokines regulate immune polarization, and the complete mechanism by which immune polarization mediates chemotherapy resistance. It summarizes the value of clinical markers and targeted reversal strategies, points out current research bottlenecks, and looks forward to the translational prospects of metabolism-immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy, aiming to provide new metabolism-immune targets for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in oral cancer.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954486.abstract: Frailty and low handgrip strength are established markers of limited physiological reserve, but it is uncertain whether their prognostic meaning differs between oncologic and non-oncologic surgery. We examined whether oncologic indication modifies the associations of preoperative frailty and baseline handgrip strength with early postoperative outcomes. This secondary analysis used a prospective cohort conducted at participating surgical centers between January 2023 and June 2025. Frailty was classified using the Fried phenotype, and handgrip strength was measured at admission. The primary outcome was prolonged length of stay (LOS >10 days); secondary outcomes were any postoperative complication, major complications, and log-transformed LOS. Effect modification was evaluated using interaction terms in multivariable logistic models adjusted for age and sex. Because no prolonged stays occurred among fit patients in the non-oncologic stratum, categorical frailty models used Firth penalized logistic regression. Among 222 clinically characterized participants, 118 (53.2%) underwent oncologic surgery. Prolonged LOS occurred in 41/118 (34.7%) oncologic and 7/104 (6.7%) non-oncologic patients. The complete-case primary analysis included 216 patients and 45 events. In an additional ordinal main-effects model, increasing frailty [odds ratio (OR) 2.91 per category, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.57-5.38], lower handgrip strength (OR 0.95 per kg, 95% CI 0.90-0.99), and oncologic indication (OR 8.97, 95% CI 3.47-23.19) were associated with prolonged LOS. However, categorical frailty-by-oncology interaction was not supported (global p = 0.341), nor was handgrip-strength-by-oncology interaction (p = 0.739); the joint interaction test was not statistically significant (p = 0.525). No convincing effect modification was observed for complications or continuous LOS. Oncologic surgery was associated with a substantially higher early postoperative burden, while frailty and handgrip strength retained prognostic relevance. No clear evidence of multiplicative interaction by oncologic indication was detected, but clinically meaningful effect modification cannot be excluded. Physiological reserve assessment should therefore be considered across elective abdominal surgery rather than restricted to the oncologic setting.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954599.abstract: Mismatch repair deficiency defines an immunologically distinct subgroup of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, but its relationship with CD163-positive macrophage infiltration in early-stage disease remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between MMR status and quantitative CD163-positive TAM infiltration, together with secondary clinicopathologic and exploratory DFS analyses. This single-center retrospective cohort included patients with surgically treated FIGO 2009 stage I-II endometrioid endometrial carcinoma and available formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor tissue. Immunohistochemistry for MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6, and CD163 defined MMR status and quantified macrophage density. CD163-positive TAM density was analyzed quantitatively as the principal measure, with a cohort-median low/high categorization retained for secondary phenotypic analyses. Median regression evaluated the association between MMR status and continuous CD163-positive TAM density, whereas logistic regression was used for the secondary binary TAM analysis and the composite adverse pathologic endpoint. Exploratory DFS analyses included single-marker and combined Cox models, formal MMR-by-TAM interaction testing, and comparison of models with and without continuous CD163-positive TAM density. Among 254 patients assessed, 236 were included. MMR protein expression was retained in 172 tumors (72.9%), whereas 64 (27.1%) were classified as dMMR. CD163-positive TAM density was higher in dMMR than pMMR tumors (median, 76 vs 47 cells/HPF; P<0.001), and high TAM infiltration was more frequent in dMMR tumors (44/64, 68.8% vs 71/172, 41.3%; P<0.001). After adjustment for age, FIGO stage, tumor grade, tumor size, and deep myometrial invasion, dMMR remained associated with high macrophage infiltration (adjusted OR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.19-4.18; P = 0.008). High macrophage infiltration was associated with grade 3 histology, deep myometrial invasion, LVSI, and the composite adverse pathologic feature; the association with the composite endpoint persisted after adjustment (adjusted OR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.01-3.14; P = 0.047). During follow-up, 26 DFS events occurred. In exploratory Cox analyses, dMMR was associated with DFS (adjusted HR, 2.76; 95% CI, 1.25-6.10; P = 0.012), whereas continuous CD163-positive TAM density was not (adjusted HR per 10 cells/HPF, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.97-1.12; P = 0.281), and addition of CD163-positive TAM density did not significantly improve model fit beyond MMR status (likelihood-ratio P = 0.279). The dMMR/high-TAM phenotype retained an exploratory association with DFS in the conventional model (adjusted HR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.02-4.81; P = 0.044), but the association was attenuated after additional adjustment for adjuvant therapy (HR, 2.04; 95% CI, 0.93-4.52; P = 0.075). IHC-defined dMMR was associated with increased CD163-positive macrophage infiltration, and higher TAM infiltration was associated with adverse pathologic features. DFS findings were exploratory and did not establish incremental prognostic value of CD163-positive TAM infiltration beyond MMR status; larger externally validated cohorts are required to assess prognostic relevance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1954599.title: CD163-positive macrophage enrichment is associated with mismatch repair deficiency and adverse pathologic features in early-stage endometrioid endometrial carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1955295.abstract: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1955295.title: Relevance between patients' clinical factors and 4D-CT lung ventilation heterogeneity for evaluating the adoption of functional avoidance thoracic radiotherapy with a large patient database.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1955408.abstract: Mushroom-derived polysaccharides are widely promoted as anticancer immune modulators, but interpretation is weakened by imprecise product identity, chemically non-equivalent preparations, and extrapolation across evidence levels. This critical narrative review evaluates beta-glucans, heteropolysaccharides, polysaccharide-protein complexes, crude fractions, modified derivatives, and multicomponent extracts as preparation-specific adjunct candidates. Receptor-level evidence is strongest for general fungal beta-glucan systems, particularly Dectin-1/Syk/CARD9 signaling and conditional complement receptor 3 cooperation; direct transfer of those mechanisms to individual mushroom preparations requires product-specific causal testing. Selected animal studies support myeloid remodeling, dendritic-cell and natural-killer-cell effects, and T-cell activation, but route, exposure, product characterization, and model limitations constrain translation. Human evidence remains heterogeneous: historical randomized PSK studies reported benefit in specific adjuvant chemotherapy settings, a later phase III lentinan trial was negative for overall survival, and small maitake, Agaricus, and pleuran studies mainly report immune surrogates. Direct clinical evidence with checkpoint inhibitors, therapeutic antibodies, or cancer vaccines is not established. The field should therefore move from species-level claims to product-level development with authenticated source material, orthogonal structural analysis, contaminant control, mechanism-linked potency, route-specific pharmacokinetics, tumor pharmacodynamics, and randomized testing against contemporary standard care. Mushroom-derived polysaccharide immunomodulators remain plausible research candidates, but neither the class nor unstandardized mushroom foods or supplements are clinically validated substitutes for established cancer treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1955408.title: Mushroom-derived polysaccharides in cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, human evidence, and translational priorities.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1956034.abstract: Background Prophylactic gastrostomy is widely used during definitive chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced head and neck cancer (LAHNC), yet some patients remain tube-dependent long after treatment. Whether prolonged dependence carries prognostic weight of its own, or simply mirrors tumour burden and performance status, is unclear. We examined predictors of time to feeding-tube independence and the association between persistent dependence and overall survival (OS). Methods We reviewed 213 consecutive patients with LAHNC treated at a single institution (2015–2022) with definitive chemoradiotherapy to 70 Gy and prophylactic PEG/RIG placement. Nine patients with an inconsistent extraction date were excluded, leaving 204. Time to independence was analysed with Kaplan–Meier estimates and cause-specific multivariable Cox regression, treating death as a competing risk, with a Fine–Gray sensitivity model. Dosimetric variables and baseline Karnofsky performance status (KPS) were modelled continuously. To avoid immortal-time bias, OS was assessed with landmark analyses at 3, 6 and 12 months. Patients were classified by tube status at each landmark, with adjustment for KPS, T and N classification, smoking history and age. Results Median time to independence was 3.2 months. Any smoking history predicted slower independence (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.42–0.84; p=0.004), and higher KPS predicted faster independence (HR 1.02 per point, 95% CI 1.01–1.04; p=0.006). Higher middle pharyngeal constrictor dose was associated with slower recovery (HR 0.98 per Gy, 95% CI 0.96–1.00; p=0.048), and oral cavity dose showed a similar trend (p=0.067). In unadjusted landmark analyses, patients still dependent had worse OS at 6 months (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.01–3.13) and 12 months (HR 2.53, 95% CI 1.30–4.91). After adjustment, the association was attenuated and non-significant at 3 months (aHR 1.35, 95% CI 0.76–2.42) and 6 months (aHR 1.48, 95% CI 0.81–2.70), but persisted at 12 months (aHR 2.20, 95% CI 1.05–4.58; p=0.036). Conclusions Early tube dependence largely reflects baseline disease burden and performance status. Dependence persisting to one year, however, identifies patients with worse survival that these factors do not explain, and they may merit closer follow-up. Smoking history and middle constrictor dose are potentially modifiable contributors to slower recovery, supporting structured smoking-cessation care and dysphagia-optimised planning. Prospective validation is warranted.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1956522.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) outcomes have improved with proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, anti-CD38 antibodies, and transplantation, yet a subset of patients with high-risk MM (HRMM) continues to relapse early and die prematurely. Immune effector therapies (IET)-B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)- and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D)-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR-T) and bispecific antibodies-have transformed the treatment of relapsed/refractory MM. However, their benefit in HRMM remains incompletely defined. This review describes how HRMM is defined in the IET-era distinguishing baseline biological/genomic risk, clinical high-risk phenotypes, and IET-specific adverse predictors. The International Myeloma Society/International Myeloma Working Group consensus integrates adverse cytogenetics and beta-2 microglobulin, whereas functional high-risk disease, extramedullary disease (EMD), plasma cell leukemia (PCL), high tumor burden, inflammation, and prior BCMA exposure identify aggressive disease in relapsed patients. Across pivotal trials, CAR-T therapy, particularly ciltacabtagene autoleucel, and selected bispecific antibodies retain activity in high-risk cytogenetic subgroups, whereas EMD and PCL remain associated with inferior responses and short progression-free survival. Emerging dual-antigen and trispecific engagers, along with novel targets such as FcRH5 and CD70, aim to overcome antigen escape. Prospective, biology-informed studies are needed to achieve durable disease control in HRMM.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1956522.title: Reshaping the definition of high-risk disease in the immune effector therapy era in multiple myeloma.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957030.abstract: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based adaptive radiotherapy (ART) has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing inter-fractional anatomical and physiological changes during treatment. By incorporating on-treatment imaging, ART enables treatment plans to be adapted to the anatomy of the day, with the potential to improve target coverage and reduce dose exposure to organs at risk (OARs). However, routine implementation remains constrained by the limited image quality of CBCT, uncertainties in dose calculation, labour-intensive workflows and the lack of reliable criteria for determining when adaptation is clinically necessary. This review summarises the development, current status and future prospects of CBCT-based ART, with particular emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted automated delineation and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems. CBCT is widely available on modern linear accelerators and remains the most practical imaging basis for ART in many centres. Nevertheless, poor soft-tissue contrast, noise, artefacts, field-of-view truncation and unstable Hounsfield unit values limit its performance in target delineation and dose reconstruction. Recent advances in image-quality enhancement, deformable image registration and synthetic CT generation have partially addressed these limitations. AI-based auto-segmentation models, including convolutional neural networks, Transformers, generative adversarial networks and diffusion models, have demonstrated increasingly favourable geometric accuracy and workflow efficiency. Automated decision-making systems can advise clinicians whether treatment-plan adaptation is required and how it should be implemented according to each patient's circumstances, representing a prerequisite for more efficient ART. Current research has mainly focused on two approaches: adaptation triggered by predefined dosimetric thresholds, and artificial-intelligence-based models that learn from prior knowledge and predict potential dosimetric changes for the current patient based on previous experience. Both approaches have their respective strengths and limitations, but require further refinement, including the systematic exploration of decision thresholds. Moreover, the realisation of fully automated adaptive radiotherapy will require the integration of additional systems, including automated treatment planning and automated QA. Overall, CBCT-based ART assisted by AI is technically feasible and may improve dosimetric quality and treatment efficiency. Future progress requires improved CBCT-specific algorithms, integrated automated planning and QA, multicentre validation, standardised safety frameworks and stronger evidence of clinical benefit.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957407.abstract: To evaluate 5.0-T ultra-high-field multi-parametric diffusion MRI (mp-dMRI) combined with histogram analysis for assessing the pathological grade, stage, and adverse pathological factors in prostate cancer (PCa). This retrospective study included 138 patients with histopathologically confirmed PCa. All patients underwent preoperative 5.0-T MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) sequences. Histogram parameters were extracted from parametric maps of the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), mean diffusivity (MD), mean kurtosis (MK), true diffusion coefficient (D), perfusion fraction (f), etc. using 3D Slicer software. Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or the independent-samples t-test, as appropriate. Spearman's rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate the relationships between histogram parameters and both the ISUP grade group (ISUP GG) and pathological T stage (pT). Logistic regression was used for variable selection and model construction. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Among the 138 patients, most histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between clinically significant PCa (csPCa) and clinically insignificant PCa (ciPCa). For distinguishing csPCa from ciPCa, D_90th percentile achieved the highest AUC among single parameters (0.756). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified ADC_mean, MD_Minimum, D_90th percentile, and f_Maximum as independent predictors across the DWI, DKI, and IVIM sequences. The combined model comprising these four parameters achieved an AUC of 0.809. After internal validation using bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions), the resulting AUC was 0.808, indicating good model robustness. Further correlation analysis showed that multiple histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f also demonstrated mild to moderate correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage. D_RMS and MD_skewness exhibited the strongest correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage, respectively (r = -0.458 and r = 0.443, both P < 0.001). Finally, among the 60 surgical patients, multiple histogram features of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between patients with and without EPE, SVI, PSM, and PNI. Quantitative histogram parameters derived from 5.0-T ultra-high-field mp-dMRI show promise for the non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and adverse prognostic factors in PCa.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957469.abstract: Programmable messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms can encode tumor antigens or immunomodulators, enabling coordinated antigen delivery and immune modulation. Yet the literature spans cancer vaccination, delivery engineering, immune biology, and adjacent infectious-disease research, making its structure and evidentiary boundaries difficult to discern. We mapped this cross-domain corpus to clarify its development, organization, and relevance to cancer-associated immune escape. We searched the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus on July 29, 2026, for English-language Articles and Reviews published since 2006. The strategy combined programmable or therapeutic mRNA, cancer, and immune-escape-related concepts. R-based analyses summarized the number of publications (NP), total citations (TC), and collaboration patterns; BERTopic modeled titles and abstracts after entity-aware preprocessing. Independent two-author review supported the five topic labels and characterized the outliers, and robustness was assessed across alternative clustering configurations. The dataset comprised 756 publications (NP = 756). Annual output increased more than fourfold in 2021 and reached NP = 182 in 2025. China (NP = 291; 38.49%) and the United States (NP = 146; 19.31%) accounted for nearly 58% of corresponding-author publications. Sichuan University and Frontiers in Immunology ranked first in institutional and journal output, respectively. Nature had the highest retained source-record citation total (TC = 2,326). BERTopic assigned 745 publications to five topics, while 11 of 756 records remained outliers (1.46%). The topics represented mRNA delivery and immunomodulatory cancer-vaccine research (52.1%), SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in oncology and immunotherapy settings (23.6%), therapeutic mRNA cancer-vaccine platforms (13.3%), tumor-antigen discovery and immune-subtype stratification (8.6%), and mRNA-vaccine immunogenicity during autoimmune immunosuppression (2.4%). Publication activity in the retrieved cross-domain corpus expanded rapidly after 2020. The corpus included both direct cancer-mRNA research and adjacent platform or immune-response literature. By distinguishing these components and identifying thematic connections among delivery, antigen selection, immune context, and collaboration, the analysis provides an evidence-navigation framework for prioritizing systematic reviews, mechanistic studies, and clinical evaluation. The map does not itself establish therapeutic efficacy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957728.abstract: Background KRAS-mutated ultra-low rectal cancer is associated with poor response to conventional neoadjuvant therapy, making sphincter preservation particularly challenging. In addition, effective rehabilitation strategies for severe low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) remain limited. Case presentation A 55-year-old woman with KRAS-mutated ultra-low rectal adenocarcinoma experienced insufficient tumor regression after multiple lines of chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, and immunotherapy, complicated by oxaliplatin allergy. After referral to our center, she received bevacizumab plus XELIRI combined with traditional Chinese medicine therapies. Following five treatment cycles, the patient underwent laparoscopic radical rectal resection with transanal specimen extraction and Bacon-type pull-through reconstruction. Pathological examination demonstrated negative proximal, distal, and circumferential margins, no metastatic involvement among 12 examined lymph nodes, and a final pathological stage of ypT2N0. The patient subsequently developed major LARS and underwent a four-week rehabilitation program centered on electroacupuncture at the Baliao acupoints. Assessment was conducted using the LARS score, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center Bowel Function Instrument (MSKCC-BFI), and EORTC QLQ-C30 scales. The patient’s bowel movement frequency decreased from over 30 times per day to approximately 10 times, and remained stable at 7–10 times during the 6-month follow-up. Conclusion In this patient, an individualized conversion strategy was followed by R0 sphincter-preserving resection, and postoperative bowel function improved temporally during and after multimodal rehabilitation that included electroacupuncture. This observation provide preliminary evidence in support of this treatment approach. However, high-quality studies are still required to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy of this treatment regimen.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1958227.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) impairs the health of China's working-age population and causes substantial socioeconomic costs. National long-term epidemiological data integrating trend segmentation, risk attribution and medium-term forecasting for domestic EOCRC remain insufficient. This study analysed China's 33-year EOCRC burden (1990-2023), identified trend inflection points, quantified modifiable risk-attributable burden and predicted epidemic trends to support tiered prevention strategies. Data on EOCRC burden among Chinese residents aged 15-49 were derived from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023. We analyzed absolute cases and age-standardized rates of incidence, mortality, DALYs and prevalence. Joinpoint regression detected segmented nonlinear trends, and Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models projected burden for 2024-2040. Dietary, metabolic and behavioural risk-attributable burden was quantified. From 1990 to 2023, national EOCRC mortality and DALY burden decreased continuously, whereas incident and prevalent cases increased significantly. Gender and age gradients existed: males and residents aged 45-49 carried the highest disease burden with slower improvement. Low milk and whole grain intake were the leading risk contributors, while high processed meat and high BMI showed rapidly rising attributable burden. All four burden indicators presented multi-stage trends and rebounded after 2020. ARIMA forecasts indicated age-standardized mortality and DALY rates would keep decreasing by 2040, yet male-dominated burden gaps remain prominent. China's EOCRC presents divergent long-term burden trends and stable age-sex disparities. The high burden in the 45-49 age group supports prioritizing this population for further screening evaluation, and male-oriented lifestyle interventions may help curb growing incidence and alleviate youth colorectal cancer burden.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1958689.abstract: Intracranial sarcomas are particularly rare primary central nervous system malignancies. Here we report the complete oncologic course of a patient diagnosed with a primary intracranial CIC-rearranged sarcoma with subsequent intracranial spread. A 36-year-old female patient with a prior history of melanoma presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset headaches and paresthesia. After workup demonstrated an intracranial lesion, she underwent gross total resection, with pathology showing primary intracranial sarcoma. She completed adjuvant radiation with an excellent local response. Unfortunately, she developed distant intracranial parenchymal lesions, managed by further resection, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy. One year after initial diagnosis, she presented with profoundly altered mental status with both local and distant intracranial failure, and she passed away a few days later. CIC-rearranged sarcomas are very rare malignancies and should be managed by a multidisciplinary team. While aggressive local failures are reported in these malignancies, here we report an anomalous pattern of rapid distant intracranial spread.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1958780.abstract: The combination of targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and locoregional treatment has established conversion therapy as a viable strategy for China Liver Cancer Staging (CNLC) stage IIb/IIIa hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, upon meeting the criteria for tumor resectability after successful conversion, it remains controversial whether surgical resection (SR) provides superior survival benefits compared to continued medical treatment (CMT), and the optimal timing for surgery is still undefined. We retrospectively analyzed 363 CNLC stage IIb/IIIa HCC patients who met strict tumor resectability criteria after a conversion regimen of lenvatinib, anti-PD-1 antibodies, and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). Patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 255) and an internal validation cohort (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized to balance the baseline characteristics. Survival outcomes were compared and prognostic nomograms were developed using Cox proportional hazards regression. After 1:3 PSM, the training cohort comprised 63 SR patients and 189 CMT patients. The SR group demonstrated significantly better median overall survival (mOS, 32.1 vs. 24.3 months; P 90 days from meeting resectability criteria to surgery, and a pre-operative AFP to baseline AFP (at the time resectability was met) ratio > 1, were significantly associated with worse OS. For CNLC stage IIb/IIIa HCC patients achieving tumor resectability following conversion therapy, SR is significantly associated with improved survival outcomes compared to CMT. Based on our exploratory findings, surgery within 90 days of meeting resectability criteria may be considered a beneficial strategy, provided that the pre-operative AFP level does not exceed the level observed when resectability was initially achieved.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959029.abstract: Pancreatic hamartoma (PH) is an exceedingly rare benign non-neoplastic lesion of the pancreas. Owing to its nonspecific clinical and radiological features, it is prone to misdiagnosis. Among its various subtypes, functionally active pancreatic hamartomas with distinct endocrine activity have only been sporadically reported in the literature as individual cases. We report the case of a 58-year-old female patient whose initial presentation was characterized by paroxysmal behavioral abnormalities during nocturnal sleep, manifesting as sudden agitation, arm-flinging, and purposeless stereotyped movements after sleep onset. During these episodes, the patient exhibited a confusional state with subsequent complete amnesia for the events, a clinical phenotype highly suggestive of REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) or frontal lobe epilepsy. In-hospital monitoring revealed refractory nocturnal hypoglycemia. Imaging studies identified a mass in the pancreatic tail, and the patient underwent laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy. Postoperative histopathological and immunohistochemical examination confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic hamartoma, composed predominantly of islet cells (approximately 90%) with associated islet cell tumor-like hyperplasia. Following surgery, the patient's nocturnal hypoglycemia and sleep-related behavioral abnormalities resolved completely.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959152.abstract: Metastatic dissemination and therapeutic failure, the major determinants of breast cancer mortality, are fundamentally driven by epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and its phenotypic plasticity. This review comprehensively interrogates the regulatory logic of EMT plasticity in breast cancer, decoding the intricate interplay among transcription factor cascades, epigenetic landscapes, non-coding RNA circuits, and microenvironmental cues that collectively sustain tumor cell adaptability. We further delineate the translational frontier, summarizing recent advances in pharmacologically targeting EMT core regulators and discussing the promise and pitfalls of plasticity-modulating therapeutic paradigms. Ultimately, by integrating evolving knowledge from basic and translational research, we present a cohesive framework aimed at bridging mechanistic understanding with clinical decision-making, with the goal of refining precision therapy for breast cancer patients.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959240.abstract: The process of chronic gastritis transforming into gastric cancer (GC) follows the classic Correa cascade, with persistent inflammation driving the stepwise transition from normal gastric mucosa through superficial gastritis, atrophic gastritis, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and ultimately carcinoma. Among these stages, intestinal metaplasia and dysplasia occurring on an atrophic mucosal background are widely regarded as the most common gastric precancerous lesions (GPL) because of their pronounced carcinogenic risk. Chronic inflammation can induce epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), thereby accelerating gastric malignant progression. In the GPL stage, the inflammatory gastric microenvironment commonly induces partial EMT (pEMT); importantly, this state is partly reversible and may be amenable to intervention to slow disease progression. As lesions advance, epithelial cells more fully undergo EMT, acquiring greater motility, invasiveness, and metastatic capability, which increases susceptibility to malignant conversion. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key molecular regulators in the transition from chronic gastritis to GC through EMT modulation. This review comprehensively discusses inflammation-driven EMT activation and functionally classifies pro-EMT oncomiRNAs (e.g., miR-21, miR-155) and anti-EMT tumor-suppressive miRNAs (e.g., miR-200 family, let-7 family, miR-34a), delineating a complex crosstalk network among inflammation, miRNA, and EMT. We further evaluate miRNAs as non-invasive biomarkers for early detection and prognosis of GPL and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the miRNA-EMT axis, including nanoparticle- or exosome-based delivery systems, miRNA antagonists, and miRNA sponges. Nevertheless, clinical application of circulating miRNAs remains limited by insufficient assay standardization and validation, incomplete target specificity, off-target effects, suboptimal delivery efficiency, and a lack of large-scale clinical evidence. By integrating molecular mechanisms and transformation status of miRNA-EMT axis in GPL, this review provides new insights for precision prevention and targeted intervention in gastric carcinogenesis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959542.abstract: Paraptosis is a form of non-apoptotic cell death characterized by cytoplasmic vacuolization and swelling of the mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Recent studies have demonstrated that inducing paraptosis in cancer cells can circumvent apoptosis resistance and synergize with other forms of cell death and tumor immunity, providing a novel strategy for anti-tumor therapy. The underlying mechanism of paraptosis involves ER stress triggered by inducers, leading to the swelling of the ER and mitochondria. This subsequently alters the cytoskeleton and disrupts molecular processes, such as calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis, ultimately causing cytoplasmic vacuolization and cell death. Unlike other forms of programmed cell death, paraptosis is caspase-independent and is marked by mitochondrial and ER swelling, along with extensive cytoplasmic vacuolization, without nuclear pyknosis or cell membrane rupture. Various natural compounds, chemical agents, and nanomedicines have been shown to induce paraptosis, which also holds potential in immunotherapy by promoting immunogenic cell death (ICD) and systemic anti-tumor responses. Thus, in cases where cancer cells evade and develop resistance to conventional pro-apoptotic therapies, paraptosis induction offers an alternative therapeutic approach. A comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying paraptosis and its targeted induction may facilitate the development of novel cancer treatments. This paper explores the impact of paraptosis on cancer cells, the mechanisms by which different drugs induce paraptosis, and the potential applications of paraptosis in cancer therapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959542.title: Paraptosis, a new type of cell death that can be applied to cancer treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959731.abstract: We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. We explore how increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability post-GKRS could potentially interfere with the lymphocyte anti-trafficking effect of natalizumab and result in new central nervous system (CNS) inflammation distant from the radiation site. Comprehensive analysis of the patient's chart, brain and spine imaging, serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles was conducted. We compiled a graphical representation of treatment changes, radiologic findings, and GKRS initiation within one timeframe. We conducted a structured literature review to support the discussion of this case and hypothesize possible pathophysiological mechanisms contributing to clinical and radiological findings. Seven months after GKRS, follow-up brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple gadolinium-enhancing lesions in both cerebral hemispheres, and repeat imaging one month later revealed new gadolinium-enhancing lesions, correlating with the patient's clinical relapse. Alternative causes of disease progression, including radiation-induced demyelination, radionecrosis, opportunistic infections, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and development of anti-natalizumab antibodies, were explored and considered less likely. The patient was switched to ofatumumab with subsequent clinical and radiological stability. Given extensive new inflammatory lesions far from the GKRS site, it seems unlikely that the sole mechanism was radiation-induced neurotoxicity. We hypothesize that late delayed radiation side effects caused by GKRS may have enabled peripheral lymphocytes to enter the CNS, counteracting the effects of natalizumab on blocking lymphocyte trafficking through the BBB and possibly contributing to MS relapse.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959750.abstract: Background Nigeria bears one of the world’s largest burdens of HIV, with ongoing expansion of antiretroviral therapy (ART) significantly improving the survival of people living with HIV (PLHIV). This epidemiologic shift has changed the pattern of morbidity and mortality toward chronic conditions, especially HIV-associated malignancies (HIVAMs), including both AIDS-defining malignancies (ADMs) and non-AIDS-defining malignancies (NADMs). Despite their increasing significance, the national burden, patterns, and systemic challenges related to HIVAMs in Nigeria remain poorly understood and characterized. Methods We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, cancer registry reports, and grey literature published between January 2000 and December 2024. Searches were carried out in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, African Journals Online, and Google Scholar, complemented by national reports from the National Agency for the Control of AIDS, the Federal Ministry of Health, and the National System of Cancer Registries. Eligible sources reported cancer occurrence among PLHIV or HIV prevalence among cancer patients in Nigeria. Findings were synthesized narratively due to significant heterogeneity across study designs and outcomes. Results Seventy-three sources met the inclusion criteria, and these were primarily hospital-based and retrospective studies. ADMs remain the most common cancers among PLHIV, notably invasive cervical cancer, Kaposi sarcoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with notable regional differences. Expansion of ART has been linked to a decline in Kaposi sarcoma incidence, while the burden of cervical cancer remains high, driven by persistent oncogenic HPV infection and limited screening coverage among women living with HIV (WLWH). Emerging NADMs, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, breast cancer, and ocular surface squamous neoplasia, reflect improved survival, aging, chronic immune dysregulation, and co-infections like Hepatitis B and C. Across these cancers, late-stage presentation and poor outcomes are common, largely due to fragmented HIV–cancer surveillance, inadequate pathology and radiotherapy capacity, limited molecular diagnostics, high out-of-pocket treatment costs, and weak integration of HIV and oncology services. Conclusion HIV-associated cancers pose a major yet often overlooked public health issue in Nigeria. Enhancing integrated HIV–cancer surveillance, increasing prevention and early detection efforts through ART programs, upgrading diagnostic and treatment facilities, and utilizing digital and molecular innovations are essential for decreasing preventable cancer-related morbidity and mortality among PLHIV in Nigeria.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959750.title: Burden, patterns, and challenges of HIV-associated malignancies in Nigeria: a narrative review

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1960445.abstract: Despite the expansion of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) services, contemporary Total Body Irradiation (TBI) practices remain insufficiently characterized in many healthcare settings. This study aimed to establish a national baseline for TBI practice to support benchmarking, standardization, and quality improvement. A cross-sectional online survey was distributed between May and June 2026 to seven Saudi centers that provided TBI services. The questionnaire collected data on service capacity, patient populations, dose fractionation, treatment techniques and delivery, planning methods, and quality assurance. A census sampling approach was used, inviting Radiation Oncologists, Medical Physicists, and Therapists. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics in Python (v3.11). All seven centers responded. One center (C) submitted two responses covering conventional extended source-to-surface distance (SSD) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) practices. Commissioned between 1980 and 2020, the TBI programs manage an estimated 386 annual cases (range: 12-120). Fractionated TBI (10-12 Gy, six twice-daily fractions) predominated. The extended SSD opposed-beam technique remained in use at six centers, with the umbilicus as the most common prescription point. At two centers, extended-SSD TBI was used alongside Intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT)-TBI (VMAT and Tomotherapy. IMRT-TBI-based centers reported volumetric target-coverage objectives of 90% and explicit organ-at-risk (OAR) dose planning constraints, particularly for the lungs and kidneys. Treatment planning for IMRT-TBI involved treatment planning systems (TPS), whereas extended-SSD techniques used varied planning approaches, including in-house spreadsheets, pre-calculated templates, and, in some cases, TPS-assisted planning. In vivo dosimetry was performed at all centers. The absorbed dose-rate at the prescription point ranged from <10 to 30 cGy/min for conventional techniques. Three centers planned their initial implementation of IMRT-TBI within three years. The ability to control OARs was the main driver, while linear accelerator availability and staff training were key barriers. Although conventional extended SSD TBI remains the most widely used technique, TBI practice is transitioning toward IMRT-based delivery. National practice guidelines based on existing international recommendations may help standardize care, address implementation barriers, and support the delivery of high-quality TBI services across treatment centers.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1960540.abstract: The aims of this study were to explore the longitudinal trajectories of core symptoms in survivors with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and to analyze their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and unmet supportive care needs. This longitudinal study enrolled 271 HCC survivors undergoing TACE in China. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at three time points-24 h (T1), 7 days (T2), and 1 month (T3) post-TACE-using four validated instruments: the MD Anderson Symptom Inventory-Chinese Version (MDASI-C), the Tumor Symptom Measure for Primary Liver Cancer (TSM-PLC), the Quality of Life Instrument for Liver Cancer (QOL-LC V2.0), and the Short Form of Survivors' Unmet Needs Scale (SF-SUNS). Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to extract discrete symptom clusters, and network analysis was used to calculate strength centrality (rs)-an index quantifying the sum of absolute edge weights connecting each symptom to all others-to identify core symptoms. Five symptom clusters were identified at T1: Fatigue-Cognitive, Post-embolization, Somatic, Emotional, and Hepatobiliary-Specific. The Post-embolization cluster was present only at T1, whereas the remaining four clusters persisted at T2 and T3. However, the core symptom shifted over time: nausea at T1 (rs = 1.154), lack of appetite at T2 (rs = 1.229), and sadness at T3 (rs = 1.107). HRQoL was lowest at T1, improved at T2, and declined at T3, with all pairwise comparisons significant (all p < 0.001). Unmet needs were highest at T3, with all time-point differences significant (all p < 0.001). The largest gaps were observed in information provision, care continuity, and emotional support. Greater symptom severity was significantly associated with poorer HRQoL at all time points (all p < 0.01). During the first month post-TACE, the sequence of core symptoms transitioned from nausea to lack of appetite and then to sadness, suggesting time-specific supportive care strategies-including antiemetic prophylaxis, nutritional support, and psychosocial care. Routine assessment of unmet needs may help reduce symptom burden and optimize long-term HRQoL for these survivors.
