doi:10.3390/cancers18203351.title: Evaluation of the Diagnostic and Prognostic Potential, and Correlation with the Tumor Immune Microenvironment of a Six-miRNA Signature Associated with Platinum Sensitivity in Patients with Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203352.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pathological response to neoadjuvant treatment in rectal cancer may differ between the primary tumor and regional lymph nodes, and the prognostic implications of this discordance remain incompletely defined. We evaluated oncological outcomes according to combined pathological tumor-nodal response patterns, with particular emphasis on complete primary-tumor regression with residual ypN-positive disease. Methods: A total of 215 patients with nonmetastatic rectal adenocarcinoma who received neoadjuvant treatment followed by curative-intent resection were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were classified as ypT0N0 (n = 34), ypT0N+ (n = 13), residual primary tumor/ypN0 (n = 119), or residual primary tumor/ypN+ (n = 49). The primary endpoint was time to recurrence (TTR). Kaplan-Meier, Cox, Firth penalized Cox, competing-risk, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: Median follow-up was 70.0 months. Recurrence occurred in 2/34 (5.9%), 6/13 (46.2%), 17/119 (14.3%), and 18/49 (36.7%) patients, respectively. Estimated 5-year recurrence-free probabilities were 90.1%, 53.8%, 81.6%, and 46.3%, respectively (log-rank p < 0.0001). Compared with ypT0N0, recurrence hazard was significantly higher for ypT0N+ (adjusted hazard ratio 7.56, 95% confidence interval 1.49-38.40; p = 0.015) and residual primary tumor/ypN+ (adjusted hazard ratio 7.10, 95% confidence interval 1.64-30.83; p = 0.009). In an analysis restricted to patients with baseline cT3N1 disease, the association for ypT0N+ remained evident (adjusted hazard ratio 6.34, 95% confidence interval 1.19-33.79; p = 0.031). Competing-risk analyses were concordant, and all documented recurrences in the ypT0N+ group involved distant metastasis. Conclusions: In this cohort, residual ypN-positive disease despite complete pathological regression of the primary tumor was associated with an increased risk of recurrence. Given the small number of patients with ypT0N+ disease, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger independent cohorts.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203352.title: Pathological Tumor-Nodal Response Patterns After Neoadjuvant Treatment for Rectal Cancer: Prognostic Impact of Residual ypN-Positive Disease.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203353.abstract: Background: The four molecular subtypes of endometrial carcinoma defined by The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) can be reconstructed from multi-omics data, but these data contain about 460,000 features for 369 patients, the subtypes are imbalanced, and feature selection easily leaks test-set information. Methods: We developed POISE-X, a leakage-controlled, imbalance-aware benchmarking pipeline with an interchangeable metaheuristic search engine. Using RNA-seq, miRNA, DNA methylation, copy-number, mutation, and clinical data from 369 TCGA-UCEC patients, we compared 19 optimizers under nested five-fold cross-validation, with in-fold prefiltering to 2505 candidate features and a macro-averaged F1 fitness function. Results: Performance differed across optimizers in a Friedman test on fold means (p=1.989×10-6). No selected panel exceeded logistic regression on the full candidate pool, which reached a macro-averaged F1 of 0.902; the compact configuration chosen by our selection rule, POISE-GWO, retained 443 features with a macro-averaged F1 of 0.880, and the selection rule itself scored 0.881 under leave-one-fold-out evaluation, and an ANOVA-ranked panel of 450 features reached 0.886. These results held without clinical variables and, in the two searches tested, for parsimony weights of 0.8-0.99. A surrogate of the clinical molecular classification built from POLE exonuclease-domain mutation, mismatch-repair deficiency, and TP53 mutation reached a macro-averaged F1 of 0.924, higher on average than every multi-omics model. Conclusions: In this cohort, wrapper search therefore compressed the feature set without adding discriminative power, and the selected panels reconstructed an existing classification, not a new treatment-relevant signature. POISE-X is a framework for benchmarking feature-selection strategies; any selected panel requires external validation before clinical use.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203353.title: A Leakage-Controlled Benchmark of Metaheuristic Multi-Omics Feature Selection for Reconstructing TCGA Molecular Subtypes in Endometrial Cancer.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203354.abstract: Aim: Estrone (E1) is of particular interest as most breast cancers are diagnosed after menopause, the period in which E1 becomes the dominant estrogen. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly invasive cancer that lacks hormone receptors for estrogen (ER), progesterone (PR), and HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor-2). TNBC management remains clinically challenging despite recent advances in targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches. This study investigated the effects of the estrogen hormone estrone sulfate (E1S) on cancer cells. Here, E1S engages in non-classical biased G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) signaling in TNBC MDA-MB-231 cells, estrogen receptor-positive MCF-7 breast cancer cells, and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cells, which express estrogen, progesterone, and androgen receptors. Methods: We performed sialidase and colocalization assays in breast MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cells. An epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) transition, a tunneling nanotube assay, and a scratch wound assay were conducted to elucidate the cellular behaviors of E1S. We used a RawBlue reporter macrophage cell line to measure NFκB activity using the secreted embryonic alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) assay, and we measured cellular viability and metabolic activity using the AlamarBlue assay. Results: E1S induced NMBR/MMP9/Neu1 signaling in MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, PANC-1 and RawBlue cells. E1S increased E-cadherin expression, reduced N-cadherin and vimentin expression, decreased tunneling nanotube density, and reduced scratch wound migration. E1S increased SEAP activity, suggestive of increased nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) and activator protein-1 (AP-1)-mediated transcription. E1S treatment did not affect cell viability and metabolic activity in triple-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cells using the AlamarBlue assay in a dose-dependent manner. Conclusions: E1S binding to GPER potentiates a biased heterodimerization with the GPCR neuromedin B receptor (NMBR) to activate matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9) and neuraminidase 1 (Neu1), a signaling paradigm with previously established receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) and Toll-like (TLR) receptors. Biased, temporal GPER signaling has significant implications for breast and pancreatic cancer cellular behavior, which may be leveraged to inform therapeutic strategies for aggressive forms of breast and pancreatic cancers. This research study is mechanistic in nature and may have potential translational implications.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203355.abstract: Background: Accurate evaluation of bone marrow involvement is important for staging and treatment monitoring in pediatric neuroblastoma. This study evaluated flow cytometry for detecting neuroblastoma cells in bone marrow aspirates. Methods: In this prospective exploratory correlative analysis, samples from 28 children were assessed through flow cytometry and cytomorphology; available histopathological and iodine-123 metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy results were compared. Neuroblastoma cells were identified as nucleated CD56+CD45-CD36-CD71- events. Results: Flow cytometry detected neuroblastoma cell populations across a broad quantitative range, including low-level populations. Agreement between flow cytometry and cytomorphology was 90.0% (Cohen's κ = 0.56). In 16 paired aspirate-level records with at least one positive result, flow cytometric and cytomorphological percentages showed a positive Pearson correlation (r = 0.878, p < 0.0001), although this association was sensitive to one high-value observation. Agreement with histopathology was 92.1-94.8% (κ = 0.59-0.64), whereas agreement with MIBG scintigraphy was slight to fair (κ = 0.12-0.23). Conclusions: Flow cytometry provided rapid, quantitative detection of neuroblastoma cell populations in bone marrow aspirates. It should be considered complementary to cytomorphology and histopathology, as repeated examinations, the limited panel, and the lack of an independent reference standard preclude definitive estimates of diagnostic performance.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203356.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) remains a leading cause of cancer death in Chilean women. Gallstones are present in >90% of GBC cases, but few individuals with gallstones develop cancer, suggesting additional factors are needed. To determine whether obesity increases the risk of progression from gallstones to high-grade dysplasia (HGD) and GBC, we used data from the Chile Biliary Longitudinal Study, 2016-2025, comprising women with ultrasound-detected gallstones in high-incidence regions of Chile.We measured body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) at baseline and up to two follow-up visits. We used Cox proportional-hazards models with age as the time scale to quantify associations of time-varying BMI and WHtR with HGD/GBC risk. During a median follow-up of 4.8 years, 116 of 4711 women developed HGD/GBC. Time-varying BMI was not significantly associated with HGD/GBC risk (p-overall = 0.11; p-nonlinearity = 0.20). In contrast, time-varying WHtR showed a non-linear association with HGD/GBC (p-overall = 0.02; p-nonlinearity = 0.02). Baseline WHtR and BMI models showed similar patterns of associations. Based on longitudinal WHtR trajectories among cases and lag sensitivity analyses, preclinical disease-related weight loss is unlikely to fully explain the observed associations. In conclusion, central obesity measured by WHtR was non-linearly associated with HGD/GBC risk in this population, suggesting that central adiposity may impact the progression from gallstones to HGD/GBC.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203357.abstract: The efficacy of somatostatin analogues (SSA) in Grade 3 (G3) neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN) remains controversial, and registry data rarely permit a formal separation of NET G3 from neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC). We analyzed 519 patients with G3 gastroenteropancreatic (GEP) NEN recorded in a national neuroendocrine tumor registry (data export 3 April 2025; 464 de novo G3, 55 transformed G3); bronchopulmonary primaries were excluded. A Ki-67 > 55%, entered as a time-varying indicator, served as a surrogate for NEC. Outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models with all treatments and the Ki-67 > 55% indicator entered as time-varying covariates. Among 410 patients with classifiable Ki-67, 256 (62.4%) ever had a Ki-67 > 55%. Ki-67 > 55% was associated with worse progression-free survival (PFS; HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.06-1.84; p = 0.016) and overall survival (OS; HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; p = 0.006). SSA use was not significantly associated with PFS (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.85-2.04; p = 0.215) or OS (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.54-1.56; p = 0.744). After adjustment for Ki-67, transformed G3 was associated with worse OS (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.02-2.51; p = 0.040). SSA therapy was not associated with improved survival in G3 GEP-NEN. As this is an observational analysis subject to confounding by indication, these estimates do not establish a lack of biological efficacy of SSA. A Ki-67 threshold of 55% identified a prognostically distinct subgroup and explains why transformed G3 appears indolent: after adjustment, it was associated with worse overall survival. This finding rests on 55 patients with 29 deaths and is hypothesis-generating.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203358.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent form of RCC and is defined by loss of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) function and dysregulated hypoxia signaling. Hyperactivation of the mTOR pathway is also frequently observed. These factors increase anabolic and protein-synthetic demand leading to proteotoxic stress. To survive under these conditions, ccRCC cells rely on adaptive endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress responses and autophagy to maintain proteostasis. Regulated in Development and DNA Damage Response 1 (REDD1, also known as DDIT4) is a key stress response protein that integrates hypoxic, metabolic, and ER stress signals to regulate mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) complex 1 (mTORC1) activity and redox homeostasis. REDD1 can either suppress tumor growth through mTOR inhibition or promote survival by facilitating oxidative stress tolerance and autophagy depending on the specific context. In ccRCC, REDD1 expression is driven by VHL loss and HIF stabilization. Yet, mTORC1 activity frequently persists due to dysregulation of upstream repressors such as TSC1/TSC2, direct activating mutations in mTOR, and enhanced growth factor signaling. This paradox underscores the complex interplay between REDD1 and the oncogenic signaling landscape of RCC. Here, we review emerging evidence positioning REDD1 as a pivotal link between hypoxia, mTOR signaling, and ER stress in ccRCC and discuss how therapeutic modulation of this pathway through ER stress inducers, proteasome inhibitors, and p97/valosin-containing protein (VCP) inhibitors may overcome adaptive resistance and improve patient outcomes.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203358.title: REDD1 in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Linking Stress Adaptation, Proteostasis and Therapeutic Resistance.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203359.abstract: Background: Accurate pretreatment prediction of pCR is critical for stratifying patients with LARC and selecting candidates for organ-preserving approaches. However, pCR is a postoperative pathological endpoint, whereas watch-and-wait strategies are based on cCR. Despite a rapidly expanding literature encompassing gene expression signatures, MRI radiomics, deep learning, and multi-modal fusion models, no prior systematic review has comprehensively evaluated predictive performance across all modalities using contemporary meta-analytic techniques for diagnostic test accuracy. Methods: Systematic review and random- effects meta-analysis of studies developing or validating predictive models for pCR in LARC treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) were conducted. Summary AUC was estimated using logit-transformed random-effects models. Heterogeneity was quantified by I2 and τ2. Subgroup analyses were performed according to model modality and validation strategy. Publication bias was assessed with Egger’s linear regression test. Sensitivity analyses were performed using leave-one-out cross-validation. Results: Forty-three studies with 67,302 patients were included. The pooled AUC across all models was 0.874 (95% CI: 0.855–0.892), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 94.3%, τ2 = 0.247). Deep learning models showed the highest pooled AUC (0.919, 95% CI: 0.877–0.948), with MRI radiomics (0.885, 95% CI: 0.852–0.911), multi-modal (0.875, 95% CI: 0.813–0.919), gene expression (0.855, 95% CI: 0.797–0.898), and clinical factors (0.820, 95% CI: 0.788–0.849) showing progressively lower pooled estimates. External validation cohorts had a lower pooled AUC (0.864) than internal validation (0.884). Significant publication bias was detected (Egger’s test p < 0.001). Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis confirmed robustness of the overall estimate. Conclusions: Deep learning and MRI radiomics models demonstrate promising diagnostic accuracy for predicting pCR after nCRT in LARC. However, the predominance of retrospective, single-center designs with limited external validation represents a critical translational gap, and the lack of studies in the total neoadjuvant therapy era limits generalizability. Prospective, multicenter validation studies incorporating standardized endpoints and class imbalance-appropriate metrics are urgently needed.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203360.abstract: PM is a locally aggressive tumor associated with asbestos exposure. Despite legislative efforts to regulate asbestos use, its incidence continues to rise in some parts of the world. Chemotherapy and immunotherapy have improved survival in PM patients, but overall survival remains poor. MTAP loss is frequent in PM and may influence tumor behavior, resulting in a poorer prognosis. MTAP-deficient tumors exhibit unique metabolic vulnerabilities that have stimulated the development of targeted therapeutic strategies in recent years with promising results. The aim of this review is to analyze the prognostic and predictive value of MTAP in PM patients, as well as the outcomes of drugs with potential activity against this target.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203361.abstract: We evaluated molecular selection stability and external prediction beyond age, sex and broad pathological stage in resected stage I-II lung adenocarcinoma. Models were developed in 228 patients from two sources and frozen before evaluation in four historical cohorts containing 778 patients. The primary comparison added pathway scores using elastic-net Cox regression. Secondary analyses examined a gene model, 200 development bootstrap resamples, alternative modeling specifications and locally updated baselines. Prediction error was measured by the integrated Brier score over 1-3 years (IBS); negative molecular-minus-clinical differences (ΔIBS) favored molecular models. Evaluation intervals used 2000 paired bootstrap resamples. The pathway model retained no molecular terms. The final gene model retained 16 genes, whereas both source-held-out fits and 159/200 development resamples retained none. Penalties of 0.5, 0.15 and 0.05 were selected in 160, 38 and 2 resamples. Alternative specifications changed gene retention from 0 to 61 and pathway retention from 0 to 5. Frozen gene-model ΔIBS ranged from -0.0034 to 0.0055 across cohorts. Its equal cohort mean was 0.0016 (95% CI, -0.0012 to 0.0042), compared with -0.0008 (-0.0024 to 0.0007) after cross-fitted local baseline updating. The clinical model predicted a 3-year mortality of 19.6% in Japan and 22.6% in Moffitt, versus observed values of 9.1% and 28.6%. Molecular selection was unstable, and incremental performance depended on specification and population. The results characterize these learning procedures and their limited development sample; broader transcriptomic prognostic value and contemporary clinical utility remain unestablished.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203362.abstract: Architectural innovation is widely assumed to improve the cross-institutional generalization of tumor segmentation models, yet this is rarely tested. We compared three architectural families under an identical, leak-safe protocol in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) segmentation. Convolutional (nnU-Net ResEnc-M), state-space (U-Mamba Bot) and transformer (SwinUNETR) models were trained on HCC-TACE-Seg (n = 103) with identical patient-disjoint five-fold splits, then applied without adaptation to 3D-IRCADb (n = 15) and LiTS (n = 118). We assessed discrimination, case-level failure concordance, lesion-volume dependence, calibration and selective prediction. Internal performance differed (Dice 0.685, 0.662, 0.479; Friedman p = 0.022) but external performance was low and largely convergent: the convolutional and state-space models were formally equivalent on both external cohorts (pre-specified margin ±0.05 Dice), whereas the transformer was inferior on LiTS (0.222; p < 0.0001) and inconclusive on 3D-IRCADb. Case-level Dice was highly concordant across all pairings (Spearman ρ = 0.84-0.96; 0.67-0.81 on LiTS after adjustment for lesion volume), the same cases failing across architectures. Lesion volume predicted performance in all six architecture × cohort combinations; lesions < 5 mL failed completely in 61-76% of cases and formed 1.9% of the development cohort against 31.4% of LiTS. Neither liver-mask constraint nor ensembling recovered performance. Deferring the 30% least-confident LiTS cases raised Dice to 0.516 (0.450 when only empty predictions were removed). Under a single-source, TACE-treated HCC training regime, cross-dataset failure of liver-tumor segmentation was governed primarily by lesion size rather than by architectural family; confidence-based selective prediction offers a deployable mitigation.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203363.abstract: Gliomas are the most common brain tumours in children, adolescents, and young adults. In children, paediatric-type low-grade gliomas (pLGG) predominate, while IDH-mutant low-grade gliomas (LGG) become more common in young adulthood. While outcomes with complete surgical resection are excellent, many pLGG patients with residual or unresectable tumours experience significant long-term functional impairment despite conventional medical treatment. IDH-mutant LGG have an unfavourable natural history, with high risk of malignant transformation. With the emergence of precision medicine, targeted therapies have offered hope as more effective treatments. For pLGG, favourable short-term outcomes have been demonstrated with MAPK inhibitors. Significant challenges remain, however, including designing treatment regimens that prevent regrowth, understanding mechanisms and biomarkers of response and resistance, and addressing treatment-related toxicities. Furthermore, pLGG manifest as a chronic disease, and it remains unclear whether targeted therapies can yield superior long-term functional outcomes relative to conventional chemotherapy. For IDH-mutant LGG, IDH inhibitors hold promise; however, it is unknown whether monotherapy will avert malignant transformation. Notably, adolescent and young adult patients have been excluded from many clinical trials, resulting in limited data on the efficacy and toxicity of pLGG-directed targeted therapies in this population. Clinical trials and patient care for LGG should be designed around tumour biology rather than patient age. Overall, the molecular era has transformed our understanding of LGG and facilitated the development of novel therapies. The next challenge is to translate new biological insights into patient- and tumour-specific treatment regimens that can improve long-term disease control and functional outcomes.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203363.title: Mutations to Medicine: Advances in Medical Management of Paediatric, Adolescent, and Young Adult Low-Grade Gliomas.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203364.abstract: Background/Objectives: The 2021 World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (WHO CNS5) integrates histological and molecular criteria for adult diffuse gliomas, but comprehensive molecular testing may be difficult to implement in resource-limited settings. This study assessed the feasibility of a sequential, marker-based approach for diagnostic reassessment and described its association with clinical characteristics and overall survival (OS) in adults from Colombia. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 68 adults with diffuse gliomas treated at two referral hospitals in Bogotá, Colombia, between 2015 and 2023. Molecular assessment used IHC, FISH, PCR, and Sanger sequencing according to the available tissue and diagnostic workflow. The study did not include comprehensive NGS or systematic assessment of combined whole-chromosome 7 gain/chromosome 10 loss (+7/−10). Results: The diagnosis changed after molecular reassessment in 51.5% of cases. The proportion classified as glioblastoma increased from 48.5% under the historical histologic classification to 66.2% under the WHO CNS5-based algorithm, whereas FISH-defined oligodendrogliomas decreased from 17.6% to 11.8%. OS differed among historical histologic groups (p = 0.03), but not among the WHO CNS5-based groups (p = 0.13). Female sex was associated with longer OS in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.02), while age was the only independent predictor in the multivariable analysis. Conclusions: Sequential molecular reassessment materially changed diagnostic categorization in this cohort and was feasible using locally available marker-based methods. However, the results are exploratory, limited by small molecular subgroups, incomplete molecular coverage, and the retrospective treatment context; they should not be interpreted as demonstrating improved treatment selection or survival after reclassification.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203365.abstract: Background: Maximal safe resection remains the cornerstone of glioma surgery, particularly in eloquent regions where oncologic gain must be balanced against functional preservation. While 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) fluorescence-guided surgery improves extent of resection in high-grade gliomas under general anesthesia, its role during awake craniotomy (AC) remains underdeveloped. We aimed to evaluate the oncologic and functional outcomes of 5-ALA-guided tumor resection during AC. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 2026 for studies reporting original data on AC using 5-ALA following PRISMA guidelines. Results: Across ten studies comprising 108 patients, fluorescence positivity was 79.2% in high-grade gliomas (Grade III-IV) and 24.1% in low-grade gliomas (Grade II), among the 83 patients with both grade and fluorescence data available (grade was not reported for 19 patients in one case series, and 6 patients in one cohort study did not receive 5-ALA and were excluded from grade- and fluorescence-stratified analyses). Gross total resection was achieved in 62.2% of patients with evaluable extent-of-resection data (56.5% of the full cohort), reaching 66.7% in the largest comparative cohort. Transient aphasia occurred in 32.6% of evaluable patients, while permanent aphasia and persistent hemiparesis were observed in 14.6% and 16.9%, respectively. In multiple studies, resection was intentionally halted despite persistent fluorescence when functional mapping identified an eloquent cortex, underscoring that mapping remained the decisive determinant of surgical boundaries. No study reported conversion to general anesthesia. Conclusions: 5-ALA-guided resection during AC appears feasible and clinically useful, particularly for high-grade gliomas in eloquent regions. Permanent neurological morbidity was observed in a minority of patients, within a range broadly consistent with awake glioma surgery generally, but the absence of a non-5-ALA comparator group means that functional safety relative to awake mapping alone cannot yet be established with confidence. Across the available literature, 5-ALA consistently enhances intraoperative tumor visualization, supports identification of residual fluorescent disease, and integrates well with cortical and subcortical mapping without clear evidence of increased permanent neurological morbidity. Although functional mapping remains the decisive determinant of the final resection boundary, the available evidence supports 5-ALA as a valuable complementary adjunct in onco-functional glioma surgery.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203366.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sustained drug-free status is an emerging milestone after atezolizumab plus bevacizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. We examined baseline host biomarkers associated with achievement of 6-month sustained drug-free status and evaluated a composite stratification score. Methods: This multicentre retrospective study included patients treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. The endpoint required systemic therapy discontinuation after complete response or no viable disease, followed by at least 6 months without viable or recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma and sustained normalization of initially elevated tumour markers. The PAN-DF score (preserved hepatic reserve, altered immune-inflammatory status, and nutritional-immune reserve for achieving drug-free status) combined modified albumin-bilirubin grade, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and prognostic nutritional index. Results: Among 655 patients, 25 achieved the endpoint; median post-discontinuation follow-up was 533 days. In the complete-case cohort (n = 473; 17 events), achievement rates were 0.0%, 2.9%, 3.7%, and 13.6% for scores 0-3. Each one-point increase was associated with higher odds of achievement (odds ratio 2.90, 95% confidence interval 1.51-5.55; p = 0.001), and the area under the curve was 0.719. The examined baseline tumour-related factors were not significantly associated with the primary endpoint, and the examined host-related factors were not associated with objective response. Conclusions: Selected baseline host biomarkers were associated with achievement of 6-month sustained drug-free status. PAN-DF stratified the observed probability of this outcome and may help identify patient groups with a relatively higher likelihood of a sustained drug-free state, supporting early multidisciplinary planning.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203367.abstract: Giant keratinocyte carcinomas, comprising basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) with a maximum diameter ≥ 5 cm, pose substantial clinical challenges. This structured narrative review distinguishes giant-specific findings from contextual evidence in advanced or high-risk disease. The synthesis uses a retained bibliography assembled from searches described in earlier drafts as covering PubMed/MEDLINE and PubMed Central from January 2015 to March 2026, supplemented by citation and guideline searching and a focused update reported through 4 September 2026. A record-level search and screening log is unavailable; historical selection counts cannot be independently reconstructed. The review protocol was not registered, and exhaustive coverage or full PRISMA compliance is not claimed. Sources were classified by design and directness, with descriptive consideration of methodological limitations. The retained set contains 51 sources: nine containing direct giant-specific clinical evidence and 42 providing contextual evidence. Direct evidence consists principally of case reports, retrospective or comparative studies and a giant-cSCC literature synthesis. It links giant BCC with prolonged lesion duration, ulceration, deeper invasion and reconstructive burden. Giant-cSCC outcomes vary substantially between reported series. Evidence for Hedgehog-pathway inhibition, PD-1 blockade and most molecular mechanisms derives mainly from conventional or advanced disease. Management requires multidisciplinary assessment integrating size, pathological risk, resectability and patient factors. Giant-specific molecular and therapeutic evidence remains limited, and contextual treatment effects should not be interpreted as effects established specifically in tumours ≥ 5 cm.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203367.title: Giant Keratinocyte Carcinomas: Clinical, Histopathological, Molecular and Health-System Factors with Therapeutic Implications-A Structured Narrative Review.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203368.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pericardial effusion may occur in patients with established cancer but may also represent the first manifestation of an occult malignancy. This study evaluated the diagnostic contribution of pericardial fluid cytology and pathological assessment according to previous oncological status, with particular emphasis on previously unrecognized malignancy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients hospitalized with pericardial disease between January 2021 and December 2025 at a tertiary cardiovascular center. The final cohort comprised 234 clinical episodes in 209 patients. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, procedural, cytological, and histopathological data were analyzed in relation to previous oncological status and malignant pericardial involvement. Results: Pathological assessment was available in 95/234 episodes (40.6%), with neoplastic involvement identified in 21/95 (22.1%). Neoplastic findings occurred in 13/33 (39.4%) evaluable episodes with known malignancy and 8/62 (12.9%) without a previous cancer diagnosis (odds ratio, 4.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.59-12.11; p = 0.004). Conversely, 20/33 (60.6%) evaluable episodes in patients with known cancer showed no neoplastic involvement. In all eight patients without previously known malignancy, pericardial fluid cytology provided the first pathological evidence of cancer; six (75%) had findings suggestive of a pulmonary origin. All presented with large effusions and hemodynamic compromise. Conclusions: Pericardial pathological assessment provides diagnostic information beyond previous oncological status. It can distinguish malignant from non-neoplastic pericardial involvement in patients with established cancer while also revealing occult malignancy when pericardial disease is its first presentation.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203368.title: Occult Malignancy Presenting as Pericardial Effusion: The Diagnostic Contribution of Pericardial Fluid Cytology.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203369.abstract: Background/Objectives: Resistance to cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy is usually attributed to DNA repair, drug efflux and apoptotic threshold. Chloride channels intersect these processes but are rarely considered as a group. This review asks whether chloride flux forms a coherent, targetable axis of treatment response and, if not, how the therapeutic direction differs by channel and tissue. Methods: PubMed was searched to 23 August 2026; all free-text searches were re-executed on 22 September 2026 and supplemented by controlled-vocabulary searches. Cited records were checked against NCBI E-utilities and screened for retractions. Claims were graded by whether pharmacological phenotypes were reproduced by genetic perturbation and by the available target-engagement and replication evidence. Results: The therapeutic direction is not uniform. In experimental models, LRRC8A- and LRRC8D-containing channels mediate substantial platinum uptake, and dose-stratified associations between their expression and outcome have been reported in head and neck cancer, supporting prospective evaluation as predictive biomarkers; contrary reports in ovarian, colon and breast models indicate that this direction is established for platinum uptake rather than for cytotoxic resistance in general. CFTR is an intestinal tumour suppressor and the only channel reviewed with an approved potentiator, yet its direction reverses in glioma, with a prostate report of CFTR-dependent cisplatin resistance pointing in the same direction. Conversely, ClC-3, ANO1 and CLIC1 are associated with resistance when gained, although CLIC1 is better supported as a determinant of drug response than of tumorigenesis. Sixteen modulators are compared by potency, assay format, selectivity/counter-screening and clinical status; widely used blockers are often poorly selective. Conclusions: Chloride transport is not a single therapeutic target class. Candidate chloride-channel blockers should be counter-screened against LRRC8/VRAC before combination with platinum therapy, and CFTR potentiation should not be generalised across tumour types. Conflicting evidence is reported alongside the directions it qualifies rather than set aside.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203369.title: Chloride Channels as Determinants of Anti-Cancer Drug Response: Why the Therapeutic Direction Reverses Between Channels and Between Tissues.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203370.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (r/r LBCL), yet primary resistance and relapse remain common. We evaluated how recent clinical and translational evidence refines established resistance frameworks and which knowledge gaps prevent the relative contribution of individual mechanisms from being determined. We conducted a structured narrative review of 14 selected clinical and translational studies addressing tumor-, product-, host-, and microenvironment-related dimensions of treatment failure, synthesized across four interpretive domains and compared with nine previous reviews. Durable benefit was associated with favorable tumor and immune transcriptional programs and greater CAR T-cell fitness, expansion, or persistence. Treatment failure was associated with tumor-intrinsic resistance programs, exhausted T-cell states, systemic inflammatory signals, and suppressive tumor-microenvironment features, including PD-L1-expressing macrophages. Antigen escape remained relevant, but incomplete serial CD19 assessment precluded conclusions about its relative contribution. Comparison with earlier reviews showed continuity rather than replacement, with LBCL-focused evidence adding biological resolution. Resistance and relapse after CD19 CAR T-cell therapy in LBCL are multifactorial. Prospective longitudinal studies integrating tumor tissue, apheresis and manufactured products, peripheral blood, and matched relapse samples are needed to validate predictive biomarkers and guide rational treatment strategies.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203371.abstract: Objective: To compare survival of patients with different histological types of locally advanced cervical cancer after treatment with radical surgery or radical radiotherapy. Methods: Data for United States residents diagnosed with locally advanced cervical cancer between 2000 and 2022 were extracted from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database. Overall survival and cancer-specific survival were compared using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. To minimize baseline differences, patients from each group were paired using propensity score matching. Results: Among the 1,363 patients with squamous cell carcinoma in the propensity score-matched cohort, surgery was associated with significantly better overall survival when disease was in stage IB3 (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.50-0.97), but not when it was in other stages. Cancer-specific survival did not differ significantly between the two treatments at any disease stage. Among the 576 patients with adenocarcinoma in the propensity-score-matched cohort, surgery was associated with significantly better overall survival in stages IB3 (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.28-0.77) or IIA2 (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.15-0.96) or IIB involving tumors < 4 cm (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.16-0.80). It was also associated with significantly better cancer-specific survival in stages IB3 (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29-0.90), IIA2 (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.76) or IIB involving tumors < 4 cm (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.07-0.62). Conclusions: Surgery may be associated with better overall survival than radiotherapy in stage IB3 squamous cell carcinoma. In the case of adenocarcinoma, surgery may be associated with better overall and cancer-specific survival than radiotherapy in stage IB3 or IIA2 and in stage IIB involving tumors < 4 cm.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203372.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, a key feature of cancer progression that enables tumor adaptation to stress and therapy, represents an emerging target in anticancer research through dietary and pharmacological modulation. Dietary strategies such as caloric restriction (CR), intermittent fasting, and nutrient-specific modifications are emerging approaches to target oncogenic metabolism. Preclinical studies show that CR reduces tumor burden and inhibits IGF-1/mTOR signaling, while restoring immune pathways. Complementary preclinical evidence confirms that pharmacological inhibitors of the IGF-1R and mTOR pathways independently expose metabolic vulnerabilities, while concurrent autophagy blockade alongside mTOR inhibition can further reduce cancer cell viability by preventing stress adaptation. Multi-omics analyses facilitate the identification of how dietary restriction and pharmacological interventions remodel the tumor microenvironment by altering immune infiltration and stromal interactions, and uncover metabolic dependencies, that represent actionable therapeutic vulnerabilities. These findings suggest that dietary and pharmacological metabolic modulation represents an innovative approach in anticancer research. Preclinical models demonstrate the capability of these interventions to suppress tumor growth and enhance therapeutic responses, while early-phase clinical trials currently establish their safety and biological feasibility. In this review, we aim to summarize findings from in vitro models, in vivo animal studies, clinical observations, and multi-omics analyses to assess the potential of diet and pharmacological mimetics in influencing tumor metabolism and the tumor microenvironment.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203373.abstract: EGFR-TKIs serve as standard first-line targeted therapy for EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Real-world data on the prognostic role of baseline HBsAg positivity and the risk of HBV reactivation during EGFR-TKI treatment remain limited, particularly in HBV-endemic Chinese populations. This retrospective single-center cohort study enrolled 580 consecutive patients with stage III-IV EGFR-mutant LUAD who received EGFR-TKIs between 2013 and 2026. Patients were grouped by baseline HBsAg status; Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox models adjusted for key clinical covariates were used to evaluate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). HBV reactivation was defined by EASL criteria, with virological evaluation available for 51 of 82 HBsAg-positive patients. Among all enrolled patients, 14.1% were HBsAg-positive. The HBV reactivation rate was 9.8% among evaluable HBsAg-positive patients, and reactivation was not independently linked to survival. After adjustment, baseline HBsAg positivity showed a borderline trend toward poorer OS (HR = 1.42, 95% CI, 0.99-2.04, p = 0.054) without significant PFS association (HR = 1.14, 95% CI, 0.80-1.62, p = 0.481). Liver metastasis independently predicted worse OS in HBsAg-positive patients (HR = 3.84, 95% CI, 1.65-8.94, p = 0.002). HBV reactivation was uncommon but warrants close monitoring during EGFR-TKI therapy. Baseline HBsAg positivity demonstrated only a non-significant trend toward inferior OS without affecting PFS. Routine HBsAg screening at diagnosis may facilitate risk stratification, and HBsAg-positive patients with liver metastasis require intensified surveillance.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203374.abstract: Background/Objectives: Longitudinal monitoring after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy primarily focuses on CAR-T-cell expansion. However, comprehensive immunophenotypic characterization of both CAR-T and endogenous T cells remains limited. We investigated longitudinal immune dynamics following tisagenlecleucel treatment using multiparameter flow cytometry. Methods: Nineteen patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies (11 diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and eight B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia) receiving tisagenlecleucel were prospectively enrolled. Serial peripheral blood samples collected during the first 28 days after infusion were analyzed for CAR-T-cell kinetics, differentiation status, activation and exhaustion marker expression, longitudinal phenotypic changes, as well as associations with treatment response and immune-related toxicities. Results: CAR-T-cell expansion predominantly peaked on day 7 after infusion. However, in several patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, delayed peak expansion was observed. At peak expansion, CAR-T-cells were enriched for a central memory phenotype and exhibited significantly higher HLA-DR and PD-1 expression than endogenous T cells. During follow-up, the proportion of central memory T-cells progressively declined, whereas the proportion of terminal effector T-cells increased, which was accompanied by reduced expression of HLA-DR, PD-1, and TIGIT. Despite the distinct activation profiles, CAR-T and endogenous T-cells displayed broadly similar differentiation patterns. Exploratory analyses further demonstrated higher absolute CAR-T-cell counts in patients who developed immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome. Conclusions: This clinically applicable approach provides immunophenotypic information beyond CAR-T-cell enumeration alone and may facilitate biomarker discovery and longitudinal immune monitoring in patients receiving CAR-T-cell therapy.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203375.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate and reproducible patient positioning is essential in breast cancer radiotherapy to ensure target coverage while minimizing exposure to surrounding healthy tissues. Conventional tattoo-based alignment remains widely used but has inherent limitations, including variability, potential setup errors, and negative psychological impact from permanent markings. Surface Guided Radiation Therapy (SGRT) using ExacTrac Dynamic (ETD) offers a non-invasive, real-time alternative that may improve workflow efficiency and patient experience. This study evaluated the accuracy and efficiency of ETD compared with conventional tattoo-based setup in breast-only radiotherapy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective comparative cohort analysis of patients treated for breast cancer at Shaare Zedek Medical Center between December 2022 and December 2024. Forty-nine patients (245 fractions) were positioned using SGRT with ETD, while a control cohort of 20 patients (100 fractions) underwent conventional tattoo-based alignment; all patients received breast-only irradiation (26 Gy in 5 fractions) in deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH), and all received daily kilovoltage (kV) imaging, which served as the reference. Six-dimensional pre-correction setup deviations and treatment preparation times were recorded. Because fractions from the same patient are correlated, the primary analysis was performed at the patient level (random-intercept model, equivalent to comparison of patient means in this balanced design), with patient-level (cluster) bootstrap confidence intervals, Bonferroni correction across the six axes, and rank-biserial effect sizes. Results: Setup errors were strongly clustered within patients (intraclass correlation up to 0.75). At the patient level, absolute setup errors did not differ significantly between cohorts on any axis (all p ≥ 0.11), nor did composite translational (p = 0.27) or rotational (p = 0.70) errors. SGRT showed a mean vertical offset of -5.1 mm relative to control (95% CI -8.9 to -1.3 mm; p = 0.013, Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.078). Clinically significant pre-correction deviations (≥5 mm) occurred in 52-65% of fractions in the vertical and longitudinal directions in both cohorts. Mean preparation-for-treatment time was shorter with SGRT (11.0 vs. 13.9 min; median 10.0 vs. 12.5 min; p = 0.036). Conclusions: Initial setup with ExacTrac Dynamic showed no statistically significant difference in setup accuracy compared with tattoo-based setup and shortened preparation time but was associated with a vertical offset. Pre-correction errors were large with both methods, so daily image guidance remains necessary. Because backup tattoos were placed in all patients and equivalence was not formally tested, these results support-but do not establish-tattoo-free daily setup. Prospective, multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings and assess long-term clinical outcomes.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203376.abstract: Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has historically been managed with systemic therapy, and local therapies have, in general, been avoided in the absence of symptoms directly related to a specific metastasis. Even if a specific site of disease, such as a local recurrence, had the potential to cause symptoms in the future, there was a bias against prophylactic palliation. It was well-established that most patients die of systemic progression. This approach is now under pressure from four directions. Retrospective case series have reported survival durations longer than anticipated in highly selected patients with low-volume, single-organ disease. A randomized phase II trial reported that metastasis-directed therapy prolonged progression-free survival. Biologic data indicate that the site of metastatic relapse is encoded in gene expression profiles already present in the primary tumor. Second-line systemic therapy has become substantially more effective, which lengthens the interval over which control of an untreated metastasis may become clinically important. We trace the oligometastatic concept from the 1995 Hellman and Weichselbaum hypothesis to the 2026 OligoPanc consensus definition of up to three lesions confined to a single organ, examine the criteria proposed for patient selection, summarize the surgical and ablative radiotherapy literature, and consider the trials that will determine whether this is a treatable disease state or a favorable prognostic phenotype. We conclude that induction systemic therapy, followed by response assessment that weighs the absence of disease progression, Carbohydrate Antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) kinetics, and performance status, is a defensible route to local therapy directed at the metastases and the primary tumor, and warrants prospective study.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203377.abstract: Resectable or potentially resectable stage II-III NSCLC encompasses heterogeneous clinical scenarios. The introduction of neoadjuvant and perioperative strategies has expanded treatment options while increasing the complexity of multidisciplinary decision-making and the need to reassess treatment pathways over time. We conducted a single-centre retrospective descriptive analysis of 101 patients with clinical or pathological stage II-III NSCLC discussed within our thoracic multidisciplinary team (MDT) between 2023 and 2025. Using MDT meeting records supplemented by medical records, we analysed decision-making trajectories and the main reasons for changes in treatment strategy. Three major decision points emerged: selection of preoperative treatment, reassessment of resectability and operability after preoperative treatment, and postoperative assessment of recurrence risk and feasibility of adjuvant treatment. Treatment pathways were modified according to disease response or progression, surgical feasibility, comorbidities, treatment-related toxicity, pathological findings, and postoperative recovery. Particularly challenging scenarios included heterogeneous stage II disease, borderline resectability, and discordant responses after induction therapy. Perioperative management of stage II-III NSCLC requires dynamic, longitudinal multidisciplinary decision-making rather than a single treatment decision at diagnosis. Integrated reassessment of clinical, pathological, and molecular disease characteristics, treatment response, patient fitness, and surgical feasibility may help individualise treatment pathways.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203378.abstract: Active surveillance (AS) is the preferred management strategy for localized low-risk prostate cancer. However, clinical debate persists regarding long-term oncologic safety beyond 10 years, the diagnostic reliability and false-negative risk of serial multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for biopsy deferral, and the prognostic magnitude of adverse pathological patterns such as invasive cribriform morphology. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive meta-analytic synthesis of long-term oncologic survival, dynamic imaging performance, multivariable progression predictors, and longitudinal patient-reported functional outcomes. Registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261479059) and conducted per PRISMA 2020 and GRADE guidelines, electronic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through January 2026. Twenty-nine prospective cohorts, randomized trials, and diagnostic imaging studies comprising 46,318 patients were included. Time-to-event survival outcomes were synthesized using Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) and random-effects inverse-variance models (REML). Diagnostic accuracy of serial mpMRI was modeled via bivariate random-effects meta-analysis (Reitsma approach). Multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and longitudinal EPIC-26 domain scores were quantitatively pooled. Across 10 cohorts reporting long-term outcomes (N = 24,987), pooled 10-year prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) was 98.9% (95% CI: 98.4-99.4%), demonstrating comparable oncologic efficacy to radical therapy. Pooled 10-year metastasis-free survival (MFS) was 96.2% (95% CI: 94.7-97.4%), and 10-year treatment-free survival (TFS) was 54.2% (95% CI: 48.1-60.3%; 95% prediction interval: 31.4-75.8%; I2 = 88.1%). Serial mpMRI demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 85.6% (95% CI: 74.2-92.6%) and a negative predictive value of 93.4% (95% CI: 89.1-96.3%) for PRECISE 1-3, supporting selective biopsy deferral while recognizing a 6.6% residual risk of missed occult high-grade disease. Invasive cribriform morphology in Grade Group 2 was the strongest independent multivariable predictor of progression (aHR: 12.67, 95% CI: 4.77-33.64; two studies, 1420 patients, 184 progression events). AS preserved baseline urinary continence (+3.0 points at 12 months) and sexual function (-2.0 points at 12 months) compared to profound declines observed after radical prostatectomy (-17.0 and -35.0 points, respectively). Active surveillance provides comparable 10-year oncologic safety to immediate radical therapy while robustly preserving quality of life. Sequential mpMRI facilitates selective biopsy deferral, though invasive cribriform histology and visible target lesions indicate aggressive disease phenotypes that require proactive definitive intervention.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203379.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver malignancy, often arising in cirrhosis. Its early non-invasive diagnosis and prognostic assessment remain challenging due to the limited availability of reliable circulating biomarkers, creating the need to establish non-invasive biomarkers that distinguish malignant transformation. This preliminary study aimed to: discover EV-associated miRNAs that differ among healthy subjects, patients with liver cirrhosis, and patients with HCC; validate selected candidates by ddPCR in an independent cohort; compare their abundance in plasma-derived EVs, whole plasma, and paired tumoral/peritumoral tissues; and explore their diagnostic performance for HCC versus cirrhosis and their associations with clinical outcomes. Methods: miRNA sequencing was performed on plasma-derived EVs from an exploratory cohort of 10 healthy subjects, 10 cirrhotic patients, and 10 HCC patients. Three candidate miRNAs, miR-98-5p, miR-130a-3p, and miR-1246, were subsequently quantified by droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) in an independent cohort of 29 HCC patients, 30 cirrhotic patients, and 20 healthy subjects using plasma-derived EVs, plasma, and paired tumoral/peritumoral liver tissues. Results: In plasma EVs, miR-98-5p and miR-130a-3p were reduced in HCC and cirrhotic patients compared with healthy subjects, whereas miR-1246 was increased in HCC compared with cirrhosis. In plasma, all three miRNAs were elevated in HCC compared with cirrhosis and healthy controls. Plasma miR-1246 showed the highest diagnostic performance to discriminate HCC from cirrhosis (AUC = 0.87). In tissue, miR-98-5p was upregulated and miR-130a-3p downregulated in tumoral versus peritumoral samples, whereas miR-1246 showed no significant difference. Higher plasma miR-130a-3p and miR-1246 levels were associated with improved overall survival, while increased miR-98-5p levels were associated with lower relapse rates. Conclusions: Among the three miRNAs, plasma miR-1246 showed the strongest diagnostic performance for distinguishing HCC from liver cirrhosis. Combination with miR-98-5p and/or miR-130a-3p did not improve discrimination. Thus, plasma miR-1246 emerged as the leading candidate diagnostic indicator in the HCC cohort, whereas the three miRNAs showed distinct potential associations with prognosis.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203380.abstract: Background: Peptides that selectively bind to cancer-associated proteins are attractive candidates for molecular imaging and targeted therapeutic applications. The urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR) represents a promising molecular target as it is highly expressed in several cancers and has been linked to cancer aggressiveness, invasion, and metastasis. This study applied an NGS-informed biopanning strategy against uPAR, combined with multi-assay downstream validation, to identify and prioritize candidate peptides. Methods: An optimized biopanning protocol incorporating additional selection controls was combined with next-generation sequencing to identify candidate uPAR-binding peptides from a phage display library. Selected peptides were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays, including flow cytometry and a quantitative plate assay. Results: Three peptide candidates were identified and selected for further evaluation with complementary in vitro assays. The optimized workflow incorporates measures to reduce, but not eliminate, enrichment of target-unrelated peptides, and includes complementary validation of the peptides in in vitro assays. Differences observed between the validation methods highlighted the importance of evaluating peptide candidates using complementary assays. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the value of combining an optimized phage display selection with next-generation sequencing and complementary validation assays for identifying candidate peptides. The identified peptides represent promising candidates for further optimization toward molecular imaging and targeted therapeutic applications.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203381.abstract: Objective: Osteosarcoma, the most common primary bone malignancy in children and adolescents, frequently metastasizes to the lung, with a five-year survival rate of about 20% after lung metastasis. This study assessed whether matrine suppresses osteosarcoma lung metastasis by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction through inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Methods: Using 143B, U2OS, and MG63 cells, we assessed proliferation, colony formation, and invasion; examined mitochondrial ultrastructure, membrane potential, and reactive oxygen species (ROS); and measured PI3K/AKT phosphorylation and mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis-related proteins by Western blotting. Direct binding of matrine to PI3K was verified by molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Rescue experiments used the PI3K agonist 740 Y-P, and efficacy was tested in subcutaneous xenograft and tail vein lung metastasis models. Results: Matrine inhibited the proliferation, colony formation, and invasion of 143B, U2OS, and MG63 cells in a concentration-dependent manner, with 143B cells being the most sensitive, and in vivo, it suppressed tumor growth and lung metastasis without obvious organ toxicity. Mechanistically, matrine caused mitochondrial swelling, cristae rupture, membrane potential loss, and ROS accumulation; upregulated FIS1, Bax, and cytochrome c; and downregulated Mfn1 and Mfn2. It directly bound to PI3K and inhibited PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. The PI3K agonist 740 Y-P only partially reversed these effects, indicating partial dependence on the PI3K/AKT pathway. Conclusions: Matrine suppresses osteosarcoma lung metastasis by targeting the PI3K/AKT pathway to induce mitochondrial dysfunction and may be a useful therapeutic agent.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203382.abstract: Background/Objectives: Comparative data on metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) versus systemic therapy in oligometastatic endometrial carcinoma (EC) recurrence are lacking. Methods: In this retrospective population-based registry study (Tumor Register Saxony-Anhalt, 2000-2025), we included 153 treated patients with distant-only oligometastatic EC recurrence (≤2 anatomical sites) after curative-intent primary treatment. Overall survival (OS) was compared between a strategy including MDT (n = 97) and systemic therapy alone (n = 56) using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW)-adjusted Cox regression. Subgroup, sensitivity and competing risks analyses were exploratory. Results: In the IPTW analysis (n = 145 with complete data), OS did not differ significantly between MDT and systemic therapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61-1.35; p = 0.622), consistent across sensitivity analyses. In exploratory subgroup analysis, MDT was associated with better OS in high-grade tumors (n = 51; HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.12-0.59; p = 0.001; Holm-adjusted p = 0.013), but not in low-grade tumors (HR 1.29; p = 0.339). Conclusions: MDT and systemic therapy showed no statistically significant survival difference in unselected oligometastatic EC recurrence; the confidence interval cannot exclude clinically relevant benefit or harm, supporting individualized decisions. The high-grade finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203383.abstract: Reliable and reproducible imaging-response assessment is essential for endpoint evaluation in glioblastoma clinical trials. The Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) criteria provide a rule-based framework for standardisation, but their implementation can still yield variable outputs between readers and across timepoints and trial sites. This partly reflects differences in lesion definition, measurement geometry, longitudinal tracking, and new-lesion adjudication. We externally evaluated an automated pipeline for auditable, RANO 2.0-aligned imaging-only response assessment using pre-existing segmentation masks. This retrospective feasibility and pilot evaluation used longitudinal glioblastoma magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies from the public single-centre LUMIERE dataset. Dataset-provided tumour segmentation masks were retained unchanged. An expert neuroradiologist visually reviewed the masks against the corresponding MRI images, and timepoints with segmentations clearly non-representative of tumour tissue were excluded. Deterministic rule-based processing performed lesion definition, admissibility-filtered measurement extraction, longitudinal tracking, new-lesion detection, and provisional response classification. Expert RANO imaging annotations and bidimensional measurements served as comparators rather than complete clinical RANO 2.0 adjudications. Analyses assessed agreement in the sum of products of diameters (SPD), longitudinal burden change, response classification, progression timing, new-lesion agreement, and failure modes, with patient-level clustered bootstrap resampling. Visual segmentation quality control excluded 57 timepoints across 42 patients, leaving 542 evaluable timepoints, including 506 matched to expert annotations. Across 84 expert-measured timepoints from 47 patients, the constrained maximum product of perpendicular diameters (Max-PPD-c) correlated with expert SPD (Pearson r = 0.753; Spearman ρ = 0.861), although the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) was 0.680 and the median absolute percentage difference was 36.8%. Overall, 73.8% of measurements were within ±50% of expert SPD. Across 31 consecutive pairs from 17 patients, correlations for longitudinal percentage change were r = 0.715 and ρ = 0.874. Per-timepoint four-class response agreement was 48.1% (κ = 0.173), whereas final-timepoint binary progressive disease (PD) agreement was 76.0%. Among patients with PD by both methods, the pipeline assigned PD earlier more often than later, although the median timing difference was 0.0 weeks and the paired comparison was not statistically significant (p = 0.068). New-lesion detection had a positive predictive value (PPV) of 22.3% and negative predictive value (NPV) of 89.0%. Conservative patient-level later-positivity estimates were 10.8% within 12 weeks and 27.0% within 24 weeks, without same-lesion verification. This study supports the value of a deterministic pipeline for standardising imaging-derived response outputs in glioblastoma clinical trials. Future work will focus on prospective multi-institutional validation incorporating clinical variables, non-enhancing disease assessment, and adjudicated outcomes.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203384.abstract: Renal cancer is a fatal disease and ranks among the 14 common cancers in the latest WHO ranking. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) prediction not only diagnoses the disease at early stages but also prevents patients from suffering pain and eventual death. This study aimed to construct and validate a model that predicts renal cancer using machine learning (ML) classifiers. Feature engineering techniques were used to refine the dataset, such as interaction feature generation, which categorizes the features according to values such as BMI, eGFR, and radiographic size. Binary clinical risk flags identify clinical risks according to the feature values, and correlation pruning removes the common and correlated features among various features. Three public datasets were collected, and the performance of seven machine learning classifiers was evaluated using the proposed model. The evaluation parameters included accuracy, precision, recall/sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). An Explainable AI method was used to visualize the importance of the model characteristics. Among all the algorithms, the Multilevel Perceptron (MLP) algorithm fits best for the prediction of renal cancer with 98%, 96%, and 100% accuracy, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAPs) are used to visualize the importance of all model features. The proposed model provides an efficient method and shorter computation time to predict renal cancer using clinical features.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203385.abstract: Background/Objectives: In recent years, the number of cancer survivors has increased. Psychological difficulties or disorders are frequent during survivorship (e.g., fear of cancer recurrence, anxiety, depression, and insomnia). Various interventions have been developed to address survivors' specific psychosocial needs. This rapid scoping review aimed to define the interventions that have been developed for adult cancer survivors by describing (1) the type of intervention, (2) their measured psychosocial outcome variables, and (3) participants' main characteristics. Methods: PubMed was searched for articles published between 2020 and 2025. The search strategy combined terms related to cancer survivorship, psychosocial outcomes, and interventions. Titles and abstracts were screened, and data were extracted using a structured form specifying study type, population, intervention, and outcome characteristics. PRISMA-ScR guidelines were followed. Results: Out of 1743 screened studies, 80 were included (67 studies, 13 systematic reviews/meta-analyses), representing approximately 7880 cancer survivors (from the n = 67). Nearly 45% of included studies were conducted in the United States, and most interventions were developed for breast cancer survivors (38.8%) or included a majority of female participants. Physical activity (22.39%), psychoeducation (17.9%), and cognitive behavioural therapy (16.4%) were the most common intervention types. About a third incorporated eHealth or telehealth. Two-thirds of studies (65.7%) reported predominantly positive effects on psychosocial outcomes. Few interventions included cultural adaptations and targeted minority or socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Conclusions: Most interventions for cancer survivors targeted breast cancer, female survivors in high-income countries. Developing and implementing culturally adapted and cost-efficient interventions, particularly for underrepresented survivor groups, remains a priority for future research and implementation.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203386.abstract: Introduction: Radical hepatectomy is the standard curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs). However, extensive resection may be contraindicated in patients with insufficient liver reserve or anatomically complex disease. Although ablation therapy is generally not recommended as a primary curative modality in current guidelines, intraoperative ablation may facilitate parenchymal-sparing, curative-intent treatment in selected high-risk patients. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 118 patients who underwent curative-intent hepatectomy for multiple CRLM. Patients were categorized into hepatectomy-only (Hx) and hepatectomy plus intraoperative ablation (Hx + Abl) groups, and propensity score matching (PSM) generated 29 balanced pairs. Overall survival (OS) and hepatic progression-free survival (HPFS) were compared using a log-rank test. Cox regression identified predictors of OS, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated tumor size associated with local recurrence after ablation. Results: Before PSM, the HX + Abl group showed higher tumor burden and Beppu scores, and demonstrated inferior OS and HPFS. After PSM, oncological outcomes were comparable. Perioperative outcomes, including major complications and post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF), were similar. Preoperative chemotherapy was an independent predictor of OS. Among 99 ablated tumors, local recurrence occurred in 12 lesions, and ROC analysis identified tumor size ≤ 15mm as the optimal cutoff predicting local recurrence. Conclusions: In selected high-risk CRLM patients, hepatectomy with intraoperative ablation had no statistically significant difference in OS and HPFS compared with hepatectomy alone without increasing major complications or PHLF.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203387.abstract: Background/Objectives: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by peritoneal dissemination and ascites formation. Kallikrein-related peptidase 5 (KLK5) has been linked to aggressive disease. Building on evidence linking KLK4–7 to keratin 19 (KRT19), we hypothesized that a KLK5–KRT19 axis contributes to tumor progression and investigated this potential axis alongside broader KLK5-associated tumor-cell, metabolic, signaling, and microenvironmental mechanisms. Methods: KLK5-overexpressing ovarian cancer models were characterized using functional assays (adhesion, migration, spheroid formation), KRT19 expression analysis, proteomics, and gene set enrichment analysis. The putative KRT19–KLK5 axis was further investigated in vivo, in silico, and by immunohistochemistry. KLK5-dependent tumor progression was assessed in vivo, including survival and ascites formation, with quantification of CXCL9 in ascitic fluid. Clinical relevance was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in an HGSOC cohort. Results: In vitro, KLK5 overexpression induced KRT19 expression and enhanced spheroid formation, whereas effects on adhesion and migration were limited. Proteomic analysis identified KLK5-associated alterations in cholesterol homeostasis, coagulation, and mTORC1 signaling. In the in vivo mouse model, KLK5 overexpression was associated with reduced survival and increased ascites formation, and KLK5 induced intratumoral KRT19 expression. KLK5 and KRT19 protein levels were positively associated in patient tumors and primary ascites-derived tumor cells. In ascites, KLK5 overexpression was associated with reduced CD3+ cell abundance and lower CXCL9 concentrations. Conclusions: KLK5 promotes HGSOC progression. Its association with KRT19 expression, altered cholesterol homeostasis and mTORC1 signaling, reduced CD3+ cells and CXCL9 in ascites suggests that KLK5 contributes to both tumor-cell and immune features of HGSOC.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203388.abstract: Background: Teclistamab plus daratumumab (Tec-Dara) was approved in March 2026 for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, but infections are frequent. We hypothesized that dual BCMA- and CD38-directed immune depletion causes infectious toxicity exceeding that expected from either agent alone. Methods: In the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS; Q4 2022–Q4 2025; all combination reports pre-approval), we compared reports listing both agents (n = 353) with teclistamab-only (n = 2774) and daratumumab-only (n = 19,230) reports. Interaction was quantified as Ω = RORcombination/(RORteclistamab × RORdaratumumab), where ROR is the reporting odds ratio, with sensitivity analyses addressing calendar period, sparse counts, comparator, and confounding. Results: Pneumonia (Ω, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.06–2.12) and influenza (Ω, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.20–5.77) were reported more often than expected. The pneumonia estimate increased against a myeloma-restricted background and after covariate adjustment, but was no longer statistically significant after excluding reports co-listing immunomodulatory drugs or proteasome inhibitors or with a relapsed-disease daratumumab comparator. Cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, and cytopenias were reported less often than expected, a reporting pattern rather than protection. A bone marrow failure signal rested on few reports and is hypothesis-generating only. Conclusions: Consistent with our hypothesis, Tec-Dara was associated with higher-than-expected reporting of respiratory infections, although confounding by treatment population cannot be excluded. Any new respiratory symptom or fever warrants same-day evaluation.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203389.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (lcWGS) is a promising approach for non-invasive cancer detection. However, most existing methods summarize millions of cfDNA fragments into handcrafted sample-level features before classification, potentially discarding informative patterns carried by individual molecules. We aimed to develop and benchmark a framework that learns directly from fragment-level signals. Methods: We developed FragMIL, a fragment-token multiple-instance learning framework that represents each cfDNA molecule as a learnable token integrating end-motif, genomic-position, and fragment-length information, and aggregates thousands of fragment tokens into a patient-level cancer score. FragMIL was evaluated on 934 samples from three public lcWGS cohorts (pan-cancer, lung cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma) using five repeated subject-level splits, a 288-configuration design-space benchmark, and comparison with four established fragmentomic approaches (coverage, DELFI, end motif, and fragment size). Results: FragMIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) in every cohort, with 0.963 ± 0.009, 0.802 ± 0.009, and 0.910 ± 0.015 in the DELFI/Cristiano 2019, LUCAS/Mathios 2021, and Jiang 2015 cohorts, respectively. End-motif encoding provided the strongest standalone discriminative signal, whereas the optimal fragment pool was cohort-dependent, with open chromatin region fragments performing best for pan-cancer detection and tumor-enriched fragments for disease-specific cohorts. Performance was retained across cancer stages and cancer types. Conclusions: Preserving molecule-level fragmentomic information improves cancer detection, supporting fragment-token learning as a promising framework for next-generation cfDNA fragmentomics.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203390.abstract: Background/Objectives. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are two of the deadliest adult cancers. High-dose acetaminophen (AAP) has anti-cancer activity when given in conjunction with CYP2E1 inhibitors to block liver toxicity. However, the administration of high doses of AAP presents practical challenges stemming from limited water solubility, making it difficult to create a concentrated treatment solution in limited volume. Propacetamol (PROP) is a water-soluble AAP pro-drug that has been used clinically as an IV AAP formulation for analgesia. Methods. We sought to investigate the pharmacokinetics, safety and anti-cancer activity of PROP in comparison to AAP using transplantable syngeneic models of TNBC and PDAC. Results. In vivo, PROP was rapidly converted to AAP within minutes of administration. PROP demonstrated enhanced effectiveness in suppressing tumor growth in the TNBC and PDAC syngeneic murine tumor models compared to AAP. The enhanced efficacy of PROP appears to stem from increased cellular uptake, leading to intracellular AAP concentrations that are 2.7-fold higher within 5 min compared to cells treated with unmodified AAP. PROP demonstrated enhanced modulation of intracellular JAK/STAT signaling, a key mediator of AAP anti-cancer activity, using both murine and humanized models. STAT3 and STAT6 inhibition by PROP led to modulation of macrophage polarization, likely contributing to its anti-TNBC and anti-PDAC activity. While parenteral administration is the preferred route of administration for PROP in anti-cancer indications, we also evaluated the safety and efficacy of oral PROP in comparison to AAP. High-dose PROP demonstrated improved safety following oral administration compared to AAP in the BALB/c murine model while maintaining anti-cancer activity in vivo. Conclusions. PROP, an AAP pro-drug, demonstrates enhanced intracellular delivery of AAP and in vivo anti-cancer activity compared to unmodified AAP, setting the stage for investigation as an anti-cancer drug across different indications.

doi:10.3390/cancers18203391.abstract: T-cell-engaging therapies have revolutionized care for relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. Transformed follicular lymphoma (tFL) has had limited representation in CAR-T or bispecific antibody trials. Thus, outcomes in this subgroup are not well-described. Furthermore, trials that include aggressive disease transformed from indolent lymphomas often report collective outcomes rather than results for individual histologic subsets despite biologic heterogeneity; this limits interpretability of results. Despite these limitations, there are consistent signals that tFL responds well to T-cell-engaging therapies. tFL has a unique tumor microenvironment, but it is not clear if or how this contributes to the favorable outcomes. More robust data are available for CAR-T compared to bispecifics in this population and differences in responsiveness between the two therapies are difficult to ascertain. More research is needed to better understand biologic interaction of tFL with T-cell-engaging therapies and response to therapy to inform future clinical trials.
